reviews.comment: I have had Dellachiesa twice and I can say he is one of the best professors in Gatton. This professor and I have a very good relationship and we still keep in touch, he cares about his students and wants them to succeed. Test heavy.
Love Dellachiessa! Great person, gives leniency to outside factors. Often uses jokes and is very informative in retaining concepts
Great professor and truly cares about student success. One of the best professors in Gatton.
good professor
AD is my favorite professor I've had at UK. He's entertaining and keeps lectures interesting, as well as having a super organized class. Definitely recommend for ECO202!!
Very enthusiastic and willing to help. Best professor I've had so far

Professor AD is very respectful and helpful. You can easily tell that he wants you to learn not just the material but also develop your intuition. Be sure to pay attention and take notes during his classes if you want an A.
Dr. Dellashiesa is awesome, extremely helpful, and he truly cares about his students. I definitely recommend taking eco202 with him.
Great professor and very helpful. Definitely take his class. He truly wants to see his students succeed.
Dr. A.D. is awesome! He doesn't make the class stressful and he is always available for help. He really tries to make sure students understand the material. I strongly recommend him
Professor Dellachiesa is passionate about what he teaches and teaches this class in a simple, clear, and informative way. He is one of the most caring and passionate professors at UKY.
prof AD. truly cares about his students and is dedicated to making sure they learn the material. He teaches in a very informative way and he is very approachable. He is a great professor.

Professor D. has been the best professor I have had at UK. He explains everything very clearly and looks for responses from the class to confirm that we understand. He also reviews for each exam thoroughly which helps a lot. Overall just an amazing professor.
Absolutely amazing professor! He is nice, very helpful, and he goes out of his way to help students. He also always respond to questions in a timely manner.

Everyone should be required to take this class! I misunderstood so many things about how the overall economy works and this course cleared them up. I didn't even know that I didn't know till I took this course
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The best thing about his class is that he gives you a notes packet to use, he has MANY practice exams, and you get 2 tries on every homework. The only con is that the exams are worth a large chunk of your grade, but they aren't too hard if you study. His lectures are easy to follow.

pros: caring, responds to emails quickly, gives generous curves, tries to help as best he can, provides note packet, provides several past exams for practice which are the most important study materials - your exams will be very similar 
cons: lectures can be confusing, notes are not always relevant to lectures, recitations not helpful

Professor Dellachiesa is a great person and professor. He likes to tell interesting stories occasionally, and he always makes sure that his students know whats important to remember during lectures and what will be on the exams. Theres homework for the first half of semester with more than enough time to complete and a total of 3 exams. 10/10
I highly recommend this class. You will be okay as long as you pay attention and attend his class
Dellachiesa is a great professor with clear lectures. He gives access to all old tests to help you study. If you pay attention, you'll do well. Take him.
AD is a great professor and he is extremely helpful during class and during office hours
Dr AD is awesome. He really cares and wants to make sure everyone understands the material. His class examples are also very funny.
AD. is an amazing professor. He makes attending a 9am class worth it!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: dr Delachiesa loves to teach and it shows. He is very caring and makes sure everyone has all resources needed to do well. You need to attend classes to do well.

This man is a blessing. He takes the time to cater to your needs as a student and is very understanding if you need help. He even mentioned that if any of us have jobs, kids, etc. that hes happy to work with us on deadlines. He also is very sweet in general and is there for all students.

Excellent work ethic and cares about students, and provides multiple opportunities. Challenges students to understand the concepts and material, not just how to do the math. I enjoyed the online lectures, and the material presented real-world applications. Presents information in a simple to understand manner that builds upon itself.
Professor Dellachiesa was not good. We only met once every 2 weeks. He would put out prerecorded lectures that were not at all helpful. Tests were hard and homework did not help.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Very smart and wants to talk with you to make sure you understand content. Lectures however were all over the place and though he gives a lot of practice exams, you never really know what to expect on them. Multiple times content not covered in class was on exams. Overall a nice guy, but you definitely have to work for an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor AD is very approachable and was always available for help. He is very supportive. He kept encouraging me to keep going even when I didn't think I could do it.

He's very kind and responds to emails very fast. There's only 1 weekly assignment that is sometimes not exactly like his lectures, but google will have the answers. He gives you access to past exams so you can study easily. If many do poorly on the exams he'll give you /a bunch/ of extra credit. Super sweet guy.

Gives opportunity for extra credit and if majority of students struggle on the exam, will give even more. Was very understanding during the pandemic and went from proctored exams on ProctorU to unproctored on Canvas. Also gives practice exams which are very helpful!
His notes packet is very helpful in studying. It makes taking notes much easier and the class easier to follow along with. He also provides a lot of practice exams.
Dellachiesa is a great guy and even a better professor. IMO, every econ student should take a class with him at least once.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Great teacher, great guy. Very responsive helping to solve problems. This is a high quality online course.

I took this class online, and I found that compared to other online classes the assessments reflected course material more and it was more meaningful work instead of busy work. also, Professor Dellaciesa was very quick to respond and very helpful with any problems I had.

I loved having Dellachiesa as a professor. He did a great job of explaining things and gave great examples. He always covered things thoroughly and I never felt like his exams were unfair. He was also always willing to help if you needed it. I also think he did a great job transitioning in to online.

This guy actually seems like a pretty kind and genuine dude, but is just terrible as a teacher. Doesn't explain things well, has very poor handwriting on the board, and overall doesn't do a good job of getting his message across to students. It is evident that he has great knowledge of the subject matter, but just struggles in presenting it

Took his ECO391 class and it was ridiculous. He thinks his class is more important than all your other classes. You have to go to class if you actually want to pass and even in doing that, he is not very thorough with his teaching.

He tries to make the class as interactive as possible. The beginning of class he goes over what you covered last time, what youre going to go over today, goes over it, then recaps what was covered. The way the class is laid out even the more complicated material is digestible. You do need to study for the test & do the hw. Extra credit available.

Taking ECO391 online was an awesome choice. He is a really fair and great professor! The final is cumulative but he uses repeat questions from exam 1 & 2 to make it easier. I would 100% recommend taking him.

Dr. Dellachiesa is a very nice guy and does care about his students. I don't love stats so I can't say this class was boring or not. The only thing I didn't love was that he tried to call on people in a 300+ lecture which just doesn't work well all the time. My advice is go to class, recitation and study a bit for the exams and you should pass.

Professor D. has been the best professor I have had at UK. He has the ability to keep you interested in the class. He also uses simple analogies to relate the content to real world topics. Overall just an amazing professor
Dr. Dellchiesa is probably the best Economics professor the I have encountered.

Best professor that I have ever had. Too bad I just met him now! He is incredibly engaging and passionate. For the first presentation, he scheduled office hours with groups to look over their ideas and projects and offered feedback and direction. He was very helpful.
Amazing teach, really liked the way he taught. A great guy and someone who wants to see you succeed and will do anything possible to help you if you are willing to put the time. Awesome awesome guy

Definitely my favorite professor this semester. He truly cares about his students. As long as you put forth the effort and go to class, you should get an A. Do whatever you can to take Dellachiesa. Even if it's an 8AM. He's the best

Sweetest professor ever! He really wants students to do well and does his best to offer up opportunities for extra credit! He does a lot of iClicker questions he uses for attendance and extra points, they end up helping your grade a lot!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Dellachiesa is probably the friendliest professor I've ever had. He is very down to earth and understanding. The guy enjoys just talking to you out in the hall and he really wants to you succeed. Class is easy too. I wish I could take more classes with this professor!

This is a very interesting class. Alejandro was very relatable and explained things well. Class requires some studying, but if you go to class you should get an A or B. He also dropped one of our three exams.

Alejandro is such a nice professor. He really cares about his students and wants you to succeed. He is really helpful when answering questions. The class itself was more difficult than 201 in my opinion but still manageable. He dropped our lowest exam score this semester so I didn't have to take the final which was awesome.

Really test heavy class, about 80% of total grade. He's a really good professor though, and explains material clearly. Tests aren't too bad if you take the time to study the material and attend class. Attendance taken some days by reef polling.
This professor was probably one of the best I've had on this campus. I was stuck with taking ECO202 at 8 AM but his lectures inspired me to get up every TR.
Dr. Dellachiesa is a great economics teacher and educator.  He really cares about his student's learning experience. UK is so lucky to have an educator like him.
Best teacher I've had at UK. Always willing to help and kept students interested with jokes and relating topics in class to things we could understand.

He is kind, funny, caring, and easily approachable. That being said, his class diverges from the textbook and homework a ton.   You are not graded on attendance, but if you want to do well, you have to attend. He uploads his slideshows, but they are not that descriptive. If you attend his class and stay involved with him, you can get an A or B easy
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Dellachiesa has got to be one of UK's best teachers. He really cares if you're having trouble with the assignments and provides extra time out of his day to help you. His tests are a bit tricky but, he really tells you what you need to study and how you need to study it. Definitely would take again

His power point slides were bland and boring. He whispers when he lectures and everyone talks over him. He taught in a lecture hall and there was no way to ask questions. He made typos and errors when we did math.  He would always work the math on the bored, which was very helpful. But the way he solved the problems was not the most efficient way.
His exams are significantly harder than the other professors' exams. He will help you if you go to office hours, but nothing can really prepare you for whatever BS he is going to throw on the exam.

I did not like 241. The lab manuals were not descriptive enough so figuring out exactly what to do was harder than needed. You are also expected to learn python code by yourself to make your graphs, so good luck if you don't have prior experience. Thankfully, labs are not graded too harshly, and mistakes will only cost you like 3-5% of your lab.

Dr Brown has been one of my favorite professors. I think his lectures are great, home work is done through Expert TA, and his exams are reasonably challenging. He is a caring person and very supportive.

Labs & manuals make 0 sense, have no direction, use incredibly vague sentences that are hard to follow("you must have many many graphs"), like he is trying to confuse us. When the professor comes in he never helps, could not answer any question I asked and always left me more confused. The labs are structured for 3 people but got put to group of 2.

The lab manuals gave almost no direction, and you are expected to know how to code even in the first lab. The experiments are fine, but you have to hope you have good group members, or you're basically screwed. Your experience will mainly be based on your TA and how they grade your labs.

Dr. Brown is hardly even in your class as it is taught strictly by a TA. Your grade will depend on your TA and knowledge in coding. You are expected to learn python all on your own throughout the course and manuals can be very vague. Completing the OneNote will secure you at least a 6/10. Labs are fun but most work is done outside of class.

Max Brown teaches PHY 241 except I only saw him twice the entire semester. Instead, I had the TA Tanner Jackson who taught the class the entire semester and he was great. Whether you pass this class or not depends on the TA that you will get. Only take this class if you need to take it. There was a lot of work that needed to be completed.

Dudes an absolute mess. His exams are SIGNIFICANTLY harder than other sections, and his section is also unfairly harder than other sections. His weighting is more difficult, his grade lines are higher, and don't even think that he cares about it for a second. Please please avoid this guy, he is the WORST.

This class is very poorly structured. The lab manuals seem to be written in a way that is purposefully confusing. The TA's have been instructed to not give students straightforward answers. This leads to great frustration on both ends. I spent ten hours a week on this one hour course. I highly recommend you take Physics elsewhere, such as KCTCS.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lab is hard, and the manuals are indeed unclear. The hard parts of the lab are mostly the coding bits. They take a while, but a TA is usually there to help in class. And if you email him, Dr. Brown will make time for you. If you have a decent group and a decent TA you will be fine.
He is so kind.

For 231, he will help you when you go to his office hours and explain things well. HOWEVER, his tests are so unnecessarily hard compared to all the other physics tests. If you can do the homework without AI, you should be fine, but if you even slightly don't understand math or physics, or don't have experience in the subject, don't take him!

Dr. Brown is probably one of the best professors I have ever had at UK. I took him for PHY232 and it is a hard class but with him, it was doable. You do a lot of group work in class which was helpful in learning the material with other people. You can tell he really wants you to learn the content, and he is very easy to talk to.

Former teacher here: Dr. Brown is terrible at teaching. Expected us all to know how to use Python programming language. For those who never had that exposure beforehand, you're screwed. Ironically, the Computer Science department doesn't even assume you've had programming experience before enrolling as a CS major. "Backward" best describes the lab.

Although this is a one-hour class I often found myself spending 4-5 hours outside of class completing the lab reports. This is largely because of how unclear the lab manuals are. They seem to purposefully be written in an obtuse way, and the grading criteria are non-existent. Often your grade comes down to what your TA arbitrarily deems important.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Your experience depends on your TA. They grade your work, and I think mine was a pretty tough grader, which was a little frustrating. In terms of things Dr. Brown controls, the lab manuals felt unclear at times, but you can easily figure it out. I also felt that assignment expectations, like for the midterm presentation, were not always clear.

Weird how other reviews expect Brown to supervise 6+ hours of lab classes M thru R. Good TAs and groupmates help but it's up to you to understand. JUST ASK. Ask multiple TAs or peers. Ask at the Physics Learning Center or Open Lab. Ask Brown. Brown is super knowledgeable and explains very well. You can usually find him at Open Lab. HE IS THAT GUY.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Is basically never in lab, your grade in this class honestly depends on how good your TA and group is. Chat GPT and Gemini will save you if you aren't familiar with coding.

Dr. Brown came to only 2 out of 12 labs throughout the semester. When he did come, he walked around for a couple minutes and then left. I'm thankful I had a good TA because if I didn't I don't think I would've learned anything. The labs also don't relate to the lectures majority of the time. You learn more coding than you do physics.

For PHY 241 lab, Max Brown did not even show up to 90% of classes. Classes were led by TAs, but when Brown did show up, he wondered around, talked to the TA, then left. We best knew him through his very badly written lab directions, which sometimes the TA told us to ignore. He never really taught us anything.

I only know who he is because he showed up to a singular lab for 5 minutes halfway through the semester. His lab manuals are very ambiguous and how you do in the class mainly depends on your TA. However, when you ask questions or go to office hours he is always nice and helpful.

His manuals are SO unclear but if you have a good group and a good TA, you can figure it out. Really dependent on your group and TA as prof brown is barely in the labs. You're gonna have to figure out python pretty quickly and that'll prob be the hardest part. Use the TAs and anyone you know to get help on that.

This lab was honestly my least favorite class of the semester. It was python based and I didn't have any prior coding experience so it was extremely difficult to pick up on and I felt like I couldn't contribute to the lab group. Brown would sometimes come in but was very unclear if you asked him a question. I like Brown as a professor otherwise.

Overall, really good professor. He is more than willing to help if you're struggling. Yes, the class is difficult but that should be expected with any physics course. He gives multiple opportunities to raise your grade as well.

He only showed up for 1 lab for 5 minutes. How you do in the class entirely depends on your TA. Make sure you get a good group to work with! Labs don't have a ton of directions and can be really tough and if you have the Python coding labs, I'm so sorry. If you need help after class go to Physics learning center. Finish the notebooks in advance.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The grading of the homework is extremely unfair and different from other classes, I finish a homework while answering every question the highest grade was a 82%. Went every day to lectures and saw the numbers decrease every day. Said students who show up get extra credit and never ended up doing that pray for the best in this class.
He explains things very well in different ways to help you any way possible. He is willing and able to help all you have to do is ask. He was very good and I was glad to have him.

Physics lab sucks and it's taught by the TAs.  Also all the labs are group work, and the groups are assigned to you.  You would rarely see the professor, and grading was always really strange.  The feedback was minimal on lab reports, so when you got a 16/20 you could never figure out why it was so.  Lab sucks and you just gotta get thru this one
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
Dr. Brown is easily the best physics professor I've had at UK. If you make any effort at all he'll acknowledge it. He offers credit for late work pretty much all semester, large bonuses for TCE completions and is available in his office like 24/7. 
Physics or engineering majors should seek him out.

The professor didn't care about grades, he just wanted us to understand the topics. Instead of droning on we were tasked with active learning. He begged us to ask questions and alwasys had an interesting physics video to show us. His passion for learning/physics and high capacitance (lol) made him extremely inspiring for me.

Dr. Brown knows what he is talking about but tries to teach in a complicated and very confusing way for no reason. Homework problems are atrocious, you will need lots of help to get started on them. Helpful outside of class but can be passive aggressive about your ability to succeed. Avoid at all costs.

I never saw Dr. Brown, so it's important to get a decent TA; mine was a critical and very slow grader. Lab manuals were used during each class; however, these manuals were often vague. Microsoft Excel and LoggerPro expertise were never given, which were both very important for labs. Also, random groupmates were assigned. I got lucky with mine.

This class is all about the TA lottery because seeing this professor is like seeing a unicorn. The class is disorganized and the excel sheets you use have stuff from previous years on them. You are placed into a group randomly and if you get a bad group you just have to deal with it. You have to give a final presentation and your graded as a group.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Brown tries to get students to think critically about topics, and at times this turns a 200 level course into a 300 level. HOWEVER, if you do the work and ask him for help, you will never find a professor who cares more about their students and thoroughly explains complex concepts. He is also a mentor of SPS, so physics majors should find him.

The physics 2 lab is taught by TAs, so hopefully you get a good one (get Guopeng Xu if you can). You likely will see Dr. Brown once or twice during the semester, but he creates all the lab manuals which are generally pretty vague. If you can take PHY231 and lab separate semesters, I would recommend it as the lecture typically lags behind the lab.

Lectures were rough. He taught in a confusing way and refused to work out full practice problems in class. He encouraged students to ask questions, but often would refuse to answer them. Tests were very hard and not reflective of any practice materials. You have to be able to understand physics on your own to do well in the class. Avoid if possible

Dr. Brown does his best to explain things in different ways and encourages students to ask questions. He's very positive and puts a lot of effort into the course. My only complaint is that exams aren't reflective of homework, worksheets, etc. However, he drops the lowest midterm exam, which is helpful.

Professor Brown seems like a really nice guy, but for his class you have to eat, sleep, and breathe physics. His grading scale doesn't match the other professors and neither do his test they are much harder. If you want an A you have to have no life. The practice exams are NOTHING like the test. Avoid at all cost and save your tears.
Absolutely terrible at teaching. Every other physics professor made their grading scale where an 80 is an A and Dr. Brown refuses to do that. DO NOT TAKE

Don't take this class if you don't have to. It is a massive waste of time and the labs are confusing. You probably will never see Dr. Brown over the semester and signing up for this class is like playing the TA lottery. Prepare to have very little help during lab times and to get marked off for things you didn't know you were being graded for.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Never had Brown as an instructor since he makes his TA's (if you have trouble understanding very broken English, good luck) do everything for him including teach. The labs he designs are pretty bad, but to be fair I went to an in person lab once and he was there, and he was very helpful. I think if this course was in person it would be better.
None of the labs make sense at all highly confusing.
Overall you will never see him, all of the lab sessions will be done by his TA's. He makes simple lab assignments extremely hard and confusing. Avoid him!

Super kind. I took his intro to organizational communication class over the summer. The slides he put out were very lengthy but easy to understand and he breaks down each concept nicely. He was very kind when I had questions regarding the textbook he assigned, which I believe was not very necessary to the class
He is great! Minimal work. Just show up to lectures, and you will do great.

Chandler is the sweetest person ever. He is so understanding of the situation if class needs to be missed. The class is fairly easy; all tests are open-note online. Participation is required, but I enjoyed going every week!!

Amazing Professor!! Definitely take his class, he cares a lot about students being successful, and is super flexible to make sure you are! If you show up and engage in lectures, you will do well! I would recommend him to anyone!
he was super chill and understanding and made all the lectures engaging and easy to follow. attendance isn't required and there is a textbook but i never read it and got an A.

One of my favorites in the department. She is a new lecturer so still figuring out how to expand on powerpoint material but pose any questions to her and she's very knowledgeable and willing to help. The factor that decides your grade is the lab which is out of her control. Your TA and section # make or break your chance for an A, so best of luck!

One of my favorites in the department. She's a new lecturer so still figuring out how to expand on powerpoint material but pose any questions to her and she's very knowledgeable and willing to help. The thing that decides your grade is the lab which is out of her control. Your TA and section # make or break your chance for an A, so best of luck!

Has weekly inquizitives but will give you an extension if you ask her before it's due. Does reviews the lecture before exams, and they are super helpful - might be the only reason I did well on exams. Responds to emails quickly and overall is just a sweet and caring teacher.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Leibold has a great personality, but her teaching style is very monotone, which leads me to have trouble paying attention in class. There isn't much homework for the class, but there is in the lab. Attendance isn't mandatory which is really nice.

Dr. Leibold is so great! She is very understanding and caring. The material isn't too difficult and attendance isn't mandatory which is nice. Make sure to attend lab though and know your stuff well prior to exams, otherwise your grade will most likely suffer.

Dr. Sandmeyer is a very knowledgeable professor. You really need to pay attention in class; you will be lost if you don't pay attention. He does sometimes ramble, and that will sometimes interfere with class. If you are lost or need additional information, go to his office hours. his office hours are very helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment:
He is very charismatic and knows how to keep your attention. Be prepared when answering questions-- whatever you think is right, you are wrong. Very book heavy, and the class is like math with words. 

I would not take the class again, but Prof. Sandmeyer is a real teacher and knows how to teach very well. Prepare to learn, and cry.

He is very intimidating. Even if you read the assignments, as I did, i did not feel comfortable at all speaking up. And when I did, or when others did, he would tell them they were wrong and ask them many more questions. Then he would get mad and talk bad about his students when we wouldn't speak up in class. 
Very unapproachable in a group setting
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: My experience with Dr. Sandmeyer was very different than what other ratings would suggest. There is a lot of reading. But, Sandmeyer is also very patient and flexible with his students. He really cares about the material, and it brings him joy to inspire thought in his students. If you show effort, he will work with you and you will succeed.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Discussion posts were a bit annoying but there's only 3 of them. The quizzes aren't hard, a lot of the times you can CTRL + F to find the answers w/ out reading. The tests were pretty similar to the quizzes so study those, they help. The final essay seems hard at first but it was not at all. He's nice too, idk why there are a lot of poor reviews.

loves to hear himself talk. so boring except ~first two weeks. test questions are at times too specific for how long the readings are. gets monotonous at times, and just reads off slides. comes off as full of himself, at times talks over students halfway through a sentence. however, he can be engaging at times and the workload wasn't too bad

Take PHI 336 in the spring. He usually doesn't teach it then. This class was comically bad. If you're going to be all over the place, you need to be a lenient grader. His lectures and quizzes were incomprehensible. Impossible to please. I started to hate a subject I used to love. I had all As and a few Bs until I took him.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Test heavy

reviews.comment: all over the place in lectures. contradicts himself. does not provide information in a way that good notes can be taken. a lot of readings. he seems to try and tell you how to think about the information. in review sessions, he does not give answers but "facilitates discussion". is very vague about the material, yet expects very precise answers.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Very passionate about his classes, and wants to encourage you to get excited about the material, too. Very understanding and helpful if you ask for it, but get ready to read a ton of articles and write lots of papers! Really enjoyed his class, but sometimes hell get carried away and talk about the lesson until class time is up.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Caring

reviews.comment: He will take SEVERAL days to respond to your email, and you might need to follow-up. There's a quiz with each reading (all posted, no textbook), and I send my condolences. There was a dispute about questions almost every class, because he words them so weirdly. Reading quizzes should be straightforward, and sometimes he had to correct his own quiz.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Compared to others I know who have taken Food Ethics with another professor, this class is very difficult. My friends who are taking this class with other professors have no exams and we had two. He requires you to do six hours of community service which no other professor in this course requires. His class is way to lecture heavy.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I was so excited to take this class. However, he took this subject and made it basically incomprehensible. His lectures had nothing to do with the long readings he assigned, and were basically him rambling for 50 minutes. His exams were multiple choice and asked specific questions about readings you werent allowed to have in front of you.

Dr. Sandmeyer has a brilliant way with words. He can explain difficult philosophical concepts in plain English. This means that attending the lectures is a MUST. I also read quite a bit in this class. Over all I found it very enjoyable, and would absolutely love to take more with him. Just read and do what he asks of you and you will be fine!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He is pretty great. You do have to read and take notes in order to keep up with the material, but he's really caring and he always wants to help his students. Warning: he does get a bit confusing and can get off topic, it's PHI after all, but I think he really tries his best to make sure everyone understands. Up to you if you take advantage of that
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: Since it is a philosophy class there are a lot of dense readings, but he takes the time to go over the material through lectures and in-class discussions. He makes available time outside of class to discuss any material you don't understand. You must keep up with the material to pass. Dr. Sandmeyer is caring and will work with you.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I'm in the food ethics class and Dr. Sandmeyer is a little scattered with what he's trying to talk about, but overall is an alright teacher. The projects are difficult and can't be procrastinated and the reading assignments must actually be read. The content is kind of tough but he genuinely tries to explain things in a way people can understand.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. Sandmeyer is a great professor. He takes something that could be very boring and makes it fun and enjoyable. I have no interest in majoring in philosophy but I sure had a great time in his class. He is very humorous and I always looked forward to his class!

Dr Sandmeyer is an extremely engaging professor. He is sometimes longwinded but will stop to explain a point you don't grasp at first. He never failed to make efforts to help his students understand the topic we were discussing. This was NOT an easy class, but it was an interesting class. He raises the bar and expects you to rise with it as well.

Sandmeyer is a great professor. He is welcome to questions in class. WONDERFUL if you go to his office hours. And is really good at explaining. If you don't understand, the TAs basically review in recitation. but GO TO CLASS. You WILL get behind. Theres a lot of information in a Logic class and you NEED to be there
Despite going a bit quick with the material, he's not that bad of a professor. He clarified the material well and he really welcomed asking questions in class. Recitation was more helpful though
He attempts to explain the material, but goes way too fast & assumes you'll understand it right away. Prepare to learn EVERYTHING in recitation.

I loved Dr. Sandmeyer. Logic isn't an easy subject to teach but he does it very, very well. He is super helpful and always makes sure to remind you of available times for tutoring. He is entertaining as a lecturer and an A in the class is definitely possible if you just show up and don't get behind on what he is teaching each class.

I'm seeing a lot of harsh comments on here so I thought I had to post. PHI 120 was a great class, and he teaches it very well.  Show up, pay attention (which I know is rare at UK) and this class is easy.  I had an A no problem and I honestly didn't study a ton outside of class.  Sandmeyer's powerpoints were great and he is an excellent teacher.

Tough class as an entry level course. Bob takes a tough subject and explains it as best he can. He and the TA's will always help - he has extra study sessions before exams. You can print the lectures and take notes on them. He's serious when he says you need to study approx 5 hours a week on top of class time. HW can take lots of time and effort.

The material is difficult and I feel like he does his best to explain it but he often speaks too quickly. His tests are hard but the TA's are allowed to give a lot of partial credit. He often calls people out during class to answer questions so don't sit on the ends of rows!

he can occasionally be vague or unclear, but if you pay attention in class, do the hw and really try to learn the rule, the class is very manageable. the TAs are extremely helpful. he will have pop attendance quizzes everyday when you are learning the info for the second exam. overall, this class is not nearly as bad as people make it out to be

Bob Sandmeyer is a nice man. He is a little scatter-brained but who isnt these days. The material he teaches is hard but he tries to help you understand it. The TAs are helpful and if you go to office hours Bob will be happy to help you. All in all the course was hard but he is a nice man.

Bob Sandmeyer is the worst professor I have ever had at UK. He doesn't prepare for class (and blames it on how busy he is). He gets mad at you for being late, but then shows up only to say he forgot his notes, or your papers. It's unlikely you'll understand anything he says, because he is so full of double-negatives
worst teacher ever! very very unhelpful. confused me more!

Everyone scared me to death when i signed up for this class last semester when they said it was hard but it's really not.  It can be difficult but I didn't think it was as near impossible as they made it out to be.  The TAS are super helpful.
Good teacher.  A little scattered, but good. Difficult course, but not too bad of a teacher.
good guy and easy grader. attendance is mandatory. he always said there would be pop quizzes which would make you read the textbook but never gave any quizzes out.

Honestly, the class is just painfully boring and everyone on here is lying about how great he is. He is a normal guy who tries to make unfunny jokes, and makes the class more unbearable. Also, don't buy the book because you don't use it, and its all common sense. He wrote the book and will threaten pop quizzes that have never happened.
Great professor! DO NOT BUY THE TEXTBOOK!
Good guy, easy to pay attention to
Super cool and funny guy, his class was always engaging. Highly recommend!!

Dr. Crowder is an amazing professor. He is very flexible with grades and deadlines and very approachable, so if you ever have any questions he will gladly answer them. Attendance is mandatory and the class is a little boring but he's such a good professor he almost makes up for it. Literal king

He is really flexible and kind just don't take it for granted. You need to show up for class. Yes you get excused absences but use them wisely also his work is very simple and easy just set aside 30 mins and you will finish it with ease.

Dr. Crowder is a great person! Though WRD 110 is a more boring class, Craig finds a way to make every “lecture” engaging and useful to develop better communication skills. Grading is straight forward, and leniency is available with good reason. It's clear to all students that he is genuinely passionate about your education and well being. Take him
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Great guy but he does grade a little hard. You do need to show up to class and turn your assignment in on time. If you do those things and your assignments are done well you should get an A.

Dr. Crowder is just a gem of a human being! He truly cares about his students in and outside of the classroom. He is a very progressive person who is relatable and makes genuine connections with everyone. There's no final for this class and the assignments are fairly fun if you choose to make them so. I hope to take him again for technical writing!
Crowder was super sweet, genuinely cares about every single one of this students, and his class was very easy to pass if you showed up and did as you were told. Understanding about absences.

Hes honestly just such a nice dude, and hes always there to help. Hes been the most understanding/caring professor Ive had yet. The WRD110 lectures might get a little boring, but he does what he can to make them more interesting.

Mr. Crowder is a phenomenal teacher and person who really puts in the extra effort for his students in everything he does. The class work and homework is very easy for his WRD 110 class, and as long as you show up to class, you will do well. Overall, if you have the opportunity to take this class with him, do not hesitate to do so.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: Best professor I've had at UK so far. Very passionate about what he teaches which made me passionate about my work in the class, and outside of the class. I learned a lot from Dr. Crowder that I will take with me for the rest of my life (not necessarily from the course content, but from Crowder himself). Another plus his class is super easy. 100/10
Genuinely cares about his students and gives good feedback because he wants everyone to succeed.
Best teacher I've had to date; truly cares about his students. Made me want to show up to class and learn.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Crowded is great! He expects a certain level of participation and ability but he also gives great feedback
One of my favorite professors ever. Genuinely cares how his students are doing. Such a fun class and an easy A.

Absolutely amazing. The most amazing and genuine man - he wants you to learn and pass, but most importantly he wants you to be a good person. He will talk to you, help you, work with you, and be a teacher beyond the bounds of the classroom. It helps that he's an awesome teacher and gives amazing and engaging lectures. 20/10 would recommend
Very chill, wants you to pass

Craig is a great guy and even better professor. While he requires a little more of you than most WRD111 professors, you will gain a lot from his class. Lectures are long but he keeps them fun with stories, jokes, and dry wit, which I enjoyed. He's always there to explain something better to you and genuinely cares about his students. I'll miss him.
Professor Crowder was very nice. He is very helpful and gives great feedback on your assignments. He is a fair grader.
Really helped me when I met with him during office hours.  Can be a hard grader, especially if you don't do something he asked you to do.

He was a great teacher! He was always very clear and was always willing to help. Attendance was mandatory but his class was fun, so it wasn't like you had to dread going to each lecture. His gives readings but I never read and got an A. I wouldn't bother buying the online handbook or the textbook assigned. Great teacher!

Craig has a passion for teaching and it really shows. He really cares about everyone and wants everyone to do the best they can. He is very helpful and is diligent in answering any questions you have. He puts a lot of work into teaching so he expects you to put some work into the assignments. He makes dry material interesting. Take him if you can!
He is really helpful and keeps the student best interest in mind. As long as you follow his rules and pay attention he is fun.
Mr. Crowder is both an awesome teacher and guy. He loves what he teaches, and he is very good at portraying that to students. I recommend him greatly for anything that he teaches.
I'm in my fourth semester at UK, and Craig is still one of my favorite professors! He has a great way of presenting the material without making it too dry. He's hillarious.
Awesome guy, and very good at helping students meet deadlines. The class is easy if you pay attention and work with Crowder.
Fantsastic English teacher. If you really want to become a better writer, this is your man.
He was awesome! I hated english and dreaded taking this class and he was great! Extremely helpful and grades easy. Just do your work and you are fine! Also will give you extensions if you need it.
i missed alot of class and had troble with the essays.  still a fun class tho.
Mr. Crowder is a nice, fair man. He'll give you extentions on your papers and trys his best to help you succeed. Just be sure to read the assignment very carefully or you will lose points.
Mr. Crowder helped me a lot with my papers.  Visit him during his office hours, and he'll give you great advice on writing.

Means well, I didn't love his lecture style, but at this point in math you can figure it out on your own or online pretty easily. He gives old exams and quizzes, this is the meta. Not a tough class at all. He's also super easy to reach outside of class should anything come up

Very nice and caring professor. The majority of the class is graded based on assignments, quizzes, and participation. No tests, only quizzes (about once a week), and the final is optional. Sometimes the lectures can be hard to pay attention to, but helpful for the quizzes. Practice quizzes are the same layout as the actual quizzes.

For MA214, he is a decent lecturer, does mostly examples during class. Not much homework, not many quizzes. Post many reviews/practice/old material before each quiz/exam. This is the MA214 professor you want!

Truly, neither I nor my peers can figure out why his ratings are so low. For Calculus 4, he did a great job and made nearly 1:1 copies for practice quizzes/exams, which helped tremendously. Hotchkiss is quite caring and even allows students to make up an exam or quiz. This is the Calculus 4 section you want. Homework is through WeBWorK- quite fast.

It's really hard to follow as he teaches very quickly. Too many iClicker questions that take up a lot of class time. It's difficult to fully understand him, as he is very soft-spoken and has to use a microphone in a small classroom.
Very annoying voice. hard to follow. Don't recommend

Sometimes it is hard to hear him, but if anyone had a question or needed more information, he would always go back. The course is written very well. The work is the same across the math department, so the number of quizzes and homework isn't his fault.
He seems like a nice guy but most of the content from class was learned on my own. Half of the class is just Iclickers and the homework has little to do with what was taught in class.
He's incredibly hard to understand him, felt bad at first. He's so unhelpful when it comes to questions, he teaches way too fast and also assigns so much homework, quizzes every single week.

Felt kind of bad for him but I genuinely learned nothing and found it really hard to stay on top of quizzes. You barely go over any content and do little to no practice in class. He is hard to understand, moves very quickly, and makes frequent mistakes.

Made mistakes constantly during lectures, which would throw off an entire problem. Whenever someone asked a question, his answers were confusing and unhelpful. I did learn in this class, but I don't think it was because of him.

RUN. dude could not teach for the life of him. Kids would ask questions and he never could answer. He has premade problems worked out, but always did them wrong and a student had to point them out. I did better in the class when I quit going.

This guy is NOT good at teaching. Lectures are practically pointless. He moves through material much too quickly and just reads off the slides, there's no deeper explanation of concepts. Calc 3 would've been much easier with a different professor. I had to rely heavily on recitation and outside resources to get through the class.

I had Hotchkiss for MA 213. I got an A in calc 2 and figured this course would be similar. WRONG. And it's not just because of the different material. Students have to correct his mistakes almost every lecture. I started performing better on exams when I stopped attending lectures. Hope that your TA is good because mine is the only reason I passed.
Terrible teacher and always ask you to have name card on table 24/7

Professor Hotchkiss is absolutely horrible. During the lectures you have to constantly correct him, he just talks to his iPad, and he does not explain anything. If you are looking to teach yourself MA 213 I suggest you take him. We had to switch to paper attendance because people stopped going to his lectures.

I feel like he doesn't even truly understand the math himself because he cannot explain for the life of him. He is actually the worst professor I have ever had. He goes through slides and some problems but instead of explaining, it feels like he is just doing problems by himself.

Actually one of the worst teachers I've ever had. Even though all he does is copy from his notebook with the answers he still makes so many mistakes students correct him on every class. Does very very little explaining on the math we are learning. This is a tough class and do not make it tougher on yourself by taking him. Very nice person tho

This is genuinely the worst math professor I have ever had. He mumbles through slides and does not offer any explanation of what is happening, just barely gets into how to do problems. Also I had him for CALC3 / MA213.

He doesn't explain what he teaches. He goes over the notes so quick that it's hard to keep up and doesn't offer any explanation of the notes, only thing that's good about his course is the webwork homework assignments and that's because they take the highest score and you can actually learn from them. The text book online and The Study carried me.

Hotchkiss was a very sweet guy and would listen to any questions during office hours. His lectures were not beneficial. It is all just examples where no purpose is explained. If we did less examples and more explanation of why we are doing certain problems, I think that would be better for the class. Exams are almost the same as previous ones.

He makes many mistakes during lecture which gets you off course of the entire problem you've done. He also prioritizes doing more examples rather than slowing down and explaining certain topics. Attendance is based off an in-person location locked question so you have to be there for attendance to work.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I was not a fan. His lectures are not easy to follow and he just works out problems without telling us the why. I said in a feedback form to use desmos more, because it was used once up to that point, but I never saw a graph since. He is a nice person, and I think his lectures could be good if he explained things instead of only writing out math.

Dr.Hotchkiss is by far the worst "teacher" I have ever had in my academic career. Does not explain any of the content in simpler terms, he copy and pastes the textbook definitions and reads them off in lecture. I learned every concept in this class through YouTube and outside resources. Class Average for every exam was never over 60%.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Hotchkiss has this interesting system for tests, the first 3 tests are super easy, and then they got so much harder, he goes off notes and only uses maybe 4 problems as examples, he doesnt go over things that are on the dezmos and you spend alot of time just trying to understand how to type the problem in.

This is a fairly easy class and Dr. Hotchkiss gives lectures that greatly help with the homework assignments and worksheets. You need to go to class but if you do, you should easily pass. He is available during office hours and drops a lot of assignments, so you don't need to panic over one missed assignment or failed quiz.
Dr. Hotchkiss did as great job instructing this class because it is an introductory class. Your worst two test grades are dropped.

He was very sweet, but the class was very hard to stay focused in, but maybe that's just math. The content was very easy to get near-perfect grades without studying on exams. His lectures were very hard to follow. Not very engaging.

He is awesome! Even though he is pretty heavy on the note side everything was very transparent on what would be tested so you knew how to prepare for the quizzes. He was very passionate on making sure everyone was comfortable with the material and able to truly understand the content. If you have the chance to take his math class... DO IT!

Attendance is not mandatory, but that changed a few weeks into class unexpectedly. Homework was easy, and professors were accessible through Piazza if there were questions. Test reviews I skipped so I could study alone, but he was accommodating when I needed a make up test take day.

reviews.comment: Linnen has excellent and engaging lecture and always is willing to take time after or outside of class to help you understand core concepts or just entertain half backed theories regarding evolutionary biology. She wants you to learn first and foremost and will bend over backwards to help you do that.

I loved Dr. Linnen. She is so good at teaching material. Her exams are challenging, but she also gives a lot of opportunities to earn points elsewhere if you aren't the best test-taker ( I'm not ). If you can, I would highly recommend taking one of her courses.

Literally the best! I was dying in all my other classes, but Dr. Linnen's lectures and style of teaching was a breath of fresh air! Highly highly recommend! Got a 99% on the final thanks to being allowed to have a 4-page (2 front and back) cheat sheet (goes for all of her exams)! Final wasn't cumulative either! Take her if you can!!

Literally the best! I was dying in all my other classes, but Dr. Linnen's lectures and style of teaching was a breath of fresh air! Highly highly recommend! Got a 99% on the final thanks to being allowed to have a 4-page (2 front and back) cheat sheet (goes for all of her exams)! Final wasn't cumulative either! Take her if you can!!

TAKE DR.LINNEN!!!! She is so passionate about this material, and truly inspires you to do well in this class. The exams are hard, but she lets you use 2 (front & back) cheat sheets on each one. Also the final was not cumulative. You will have to put lots of work into the class, but I would highly recommend her if you need to take 303!!

One of the most positive and understanding professors I've had. Multiple extra credit opportunities and extensions during semester. Exams are super tough, but you get a 2 page cheat sheet and they're only 55% of your grade. Offered lots of time to meet outside of class and always answered emails quickly. Get ready to work hard but would recommend

One of the most impressive and kind professors I've had. She is always looking for ways to improve the class and she truly cares about her students. If her office hours don't work for you, she's very quick about responding to emails and making another time to meet. Some concepts are tricky, but nothing crazy if you go to class and study enough.

About half of class meetings are lectures and half are in-class "labs" done on computers. Have to write a lot for this course but it's broken up in between assignments. Great class to take if you're interested in genetics or evolution, especially research in these areas.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--So many papers

reviews.comment: Linnen is incredible. Her exams consist of exactly what you would expect, and practice exams are extremely similar to the real exams. She moves too quickly during lecture to take notes, so I strongly recommend just listening and going back to Echo360's later when creating your cheat sheets (two per exam, front and back). you will learn so much!!

Dr. Linnen is one of the most impressive professors I have encountered while at UK. Not only is she prestigious scientist with published work to prove it, she also cares her students and their success on her exams. Her exams are VERY HARD. As is the material. But she does a great job of explaining the concepts in depth. You'll learn a lot.

Dr. Linnen is an amazing evolutionary biologist and the most impressive professor I've ever had. Her tests are extremely tough and you have to work for the grade. Word to the wise, she talks way too fast to take notes, WATCH THE ECHOS, and take diligent notes on those and you're guaranteed to do well on the exams.

Catherine is an amazing evolutionary biologist and is great at what she does, but do NOT blow off her exams. I received a 66 on the first exam and had to work HARD to bring my grade back up to an A. Her exams are very difficult but doable and here's how: listen in class, and don't take notes until after lecture. Gives you time to absorb info.

Dr. Linnen is a highly respectable professor who obviously cares about her students and evolutionary biology. Her exams are somewhat difficult, however, watching echoes/ taking notes from powerpoints should equip students with enough information to perform decently. The final grade also takes into account recitation, lecture, and quiz grades.

Dr. Linnen is a nice and intelligent lady. She got her PhD from Harvard, which sounds and is very impressive. However, I do not believe that the degree from Harvard accurately represents how good she is at teaching. She goes very fast and skims through her lecture, the quizzes are all from the textbook, and the exams are extremely tough!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Tests are tough--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Linnen is a great person and decent professor, but her test are ridiculously hard. reviews.comment: Extremely tough exams. impossible to get above a 75 in the exam without rewatching her lectures twice.
Catherine Linnen is so bomb. All these people are haters.
BIO GOD

reviews.comment: By attending her lectures and preparing for reading quizzes, you will understand the basic evolutionary concepts and vocabulary well. However, her exams are very difficult. You will need to study extensively for her exams! Her grading system is set up so that the recitation provides you with a means of compensation for exams. But STUDY.

The textbook is GREAT, but I found the quizzes focused on matching exact verbiage, where even one word or comma mattered. It felt more like searching than learning. The primary project is a large (1/3-grade) fill-in-the-blanks PowerPoint that I found of little developmental value. Responses were difficult to obtain, and grades were often delayed.

- I do not feel like 3 books should have been required for this class at all.

- His canvas is practically nonexistent in its organization.

- 1 hour 15 minutes of extremely monotone and unenthusiastic talking which makes learning very difficult.

reviews.comment: Dr. Davis jammed all of the coursework into the final few weeks of class, your grade is based off a few assignments, and he barely teaches any history. reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: RUN RUN RUN as far away as you can from this class and especially from this professor!!! He is extremely unorganized; He is extremely unclear when it comes to any homework assignments, and often has to change the date because he fails to put clear instructions on canvas.

All I have to say about Dr.Davis is that he crammed all assignments in the month of April like we had one thing due April 3rd than read a book in the span of 3 classes then a reader responds paper due of April 16th suppose be due earlier than what was supposed to be 2 more reflection journals and then your final project.

All he does is yap at the front of the class and then randomly springs a test on us, he doesn't give out study guides or post his lecture notes. His tests are harder than they should be for a level 100 class

Professor Davis only taught through lectures which at times were incredibly difficult to hear from any point in the lecture hall and only using PowerPoints for images made it so he couldn't post notes for later review, in general I would learn more from recitation than class.

Dr. Davis is intelligent but the way he teaches the material is not productive and makes the class way harder than it had to be. It is almost all verbal which was hard to keep up with. I wouldn't recommend this class for those who aren't great at history. Your grade is defined on papers and the midterm/final. Way too hard for a 100-level course.

reviews.comment: Dr. Davis knows his stuff, but his lectures are hard to follow; not a level 100 class. Your success in the class is determined by what TA you get. reviews.comment: THIS IS THE WORST CLASS I HAVE EVER TAKEN! Way too much work for an 100 level course. You are also only allowed to have 4 unexcused absences before you are dropped from the class. Keep track of them so that you are not randomly dropped from the class after the midterm. Be prepared for reading quizzes too; or save yourself and never take this class!

This is the worst class I have ever taken. It is so much harder than it needs to be! So many readings, multiple papers, pop quizzes, midterm test, final project AND final exam. reviews.comment: He is knowledgeable, helpful, very interesting subject matter. 10/10 would recommend. Why doesn't he have a chili pepper?

reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Dr. Davis is a good professor. He knows an excessive amount about South African history. Every question he was asked, he could answer well. The class does require a lot of reading. He gives quizzes on the reading, but only a few (like 4 or 5) through the semester, and he warned us before each one. All in all, I recommend him. Interesting content.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Prof. Davis definitely knows what he's talking about, but has absolutely no idea how to teach it.  His lecture slides have almost nothing on them and it is extremely difficult to take notes in lecture. Also an excessive amount of reading, probably close to 100 pages per week, and this is a core level class! Way too difficult for the course level.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: He is tough, but if you show you are interested in the content and at least attempt to keep up with the readings you will do well. Usually requires more than 1 book but are fairly cheap. Group projects are huge chunks of grade, but usually gives option to make it a larger chunk of grade and then makes midterm/final optional. Occasional pop quizzes.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Professor Davis definitely know his stuff. However, Davis's teaching style unreasonable. Davis doesn't include nearly enough context to his teaching slide, this makes it nearly impossible to take quality notes while he lectures. All in all, Davis knows his stuff, but he definitely doesn't know how to teach it.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: Its clear Davis knows his stuff when it comes to South Africa, but as a teacher he is absolutely horrendous. He is constantly giving extra group projects or assignments not put onto the syllabus,  and expects way too much for a level 200 course. I honestly can't believe he has gotten so many good reviews, everyone I've talked to dislikes him. AVOID
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: Great class, Dr. Davis is extremely knowledgable in the history of South Africa. Sometimes goes off topic but all of his stories are very interesting. If you like history you will love this class, if you don't i would advise not to take it. Attendance is mandatory and be prepared to read every class.  Pop quizzes, no written test, group projects.

I loved the fact that he was very enthusiastic about what he teaches and he is very knowledgeable, so I learned a lot from this class. You get to write 4 papers but the books that you get to read are fun and helpful to understand Africa better. Also I loved that we don't have group projects. If you work hard, your efforts will be paid back.

I learned so much from his class. Reading is a part of nearly every class and there are reading quizzes at least once a week. The class is set up so that if you don't do the reading and pass the quizzes you can't pass the class. You also need to read really closely because his questions are sort of obscure.
Dr D is da bomb. Took a tough course but learned alot. Don't be intimidated by his smarts and engage with the material.  Rewrite rewrite rewrite
Pretty nice guy, however, his expectations are way too high. Workload is ridiculous!

She will post what is on the exam but not explicitly give a study guide. Her hand writing is atrocious. Homework due almost everyday. No feedback on exams or quiz's unless you go to her office, which she can then come across as rude and not the most helpful. Does give lots of extra credit if you respond to weekly emails. Tough but fair, can be mean

Lectures are nothing like what you will be tested over. The material conveyed in class, and that is given through homework, and guided reading does not prepare you for quizzes or exams. Questions do not feel welcome, and office hours are not much help if you are genuinely confused.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: She is clearly knowledgeable about the subject, but I found her teaching style very difficult to follow. It was challenging to understand key concepts and very poor handwriting on the board. Office hours,  often felt discouraging and I felt uncomfortable asking questions and left feeling more confused.

Ton of extra credit which was really nice. Terrible hand writing so if u miss class youll have no idea what the notes are trying to explain. Hard to get below a B because of how much extra credit she gives you, and she usually curves the tests because the MC can be very hard.

I was surprised to see Professor Davis had a low rating for 403. She is incredibly intelligent and hardworking, and I've found her class enjoyable. She's one of those professors who makes learning not suck. Assignments are not incredibly time-consuming, exam review modules are very reflective of exam material, and TONS of extra credit is offered.

She can be very rude and sarcastic at times. Very hard to get ahold of over email and you have to book an appointment to see her after class (there is a 3 week waitlist). If you have any technical issues better figure them out yourself or she will give you a zero for it 2 weeks later when she thinks you have forgotten.
This is the worst professor I have had in three years at UK

Does not provide rubrics for her projects but will tank your grade without providing any feedback. Don't even bother trying to make an office hours appointment because she'll be be booked 3 weeks in advance. I am a 3.7 gpa student and she is killing my grade with her outrageous grading style.
This might be the worst class and professor combo I have ever taken in my three years at this school.
Does not care about external situations. If you are sick, she likely not respond to any of your emails while simultaneously just giving you zeroes. Offers absolutely no leeway for absences.

Prof. Davis receives FAR too much hate. While I will say her teaching is hit or miss, I cannot think of anyone more knowledgeable in the field she's teaching. She's super nice, very conversational, and has lots of meeting availability. She does have a "no bs" personality, but as long as you are polite and attentive, she's awesome. Highly recommend.

TAKE DAVIS for 301! People who hate on her are the people who want to be able to do well without going to class or putting in the effort. I'm not good at accounting but her study guides are exactly like the exams, she's straightforward with what you need to know. As long as you try & she sees you're trying you'll pass.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Take a different professor. You teach yourself everything. Assignments almost everyday, sometimes lengthy, and what little she goes over in class barely helps. She is EXTREMELY rude and condescending when asked a question, to the point I am surprised a student hasn't recorded it and put it on the internet. There are some extra credit opportunities.

I LOVE OLIVIA DAVIS! She is so amazing and helpful. If you put in the work and attend class, you'll get an A. She is super helpful during class and at office hours. ALSO her SI is ACCOUNTING. The SI is just as helpful as Davis and is such a good teacher as well. couldn't be happier with Davis & the SI. Davis is the best acc prof out there

301 TAKE DAVIS! Content is difficult but she makes it very do-able. One of the BEST accounting professors in Gatton. People talk bad ab her bc she doesn't let students email her (which is rly the only con to taking her) but just talk to her ab whatever it is even after the fact and she's pretty understanding. + extra credit for showing up to class!

She is a terrible professor. She refuses to answer questions and is blatantly rude to students. You will have to teach yourself everything because she barely goes over anything. She reads directly from the lecture slides and relies off wiley to do everything for her, except for the tests (extremely difficult). Not sure what she's getting paid for.
She's not awful but she is kind of rude and goes too fast in her lectures. Take another prof if you can

She isn't great at all. Basically you will have to learn through wiley homework and the textbook. She doesn't teach at all, and even gets things wrong during lectures. Won't let you email her at all, and in general just mid. I wouldn't take her, but if you do all assignments and decent on test 70% and above, youll be fine.

The WORST prof I ever had!!! She does not teach at all, you have to teach yourself. And she doesn't give enough time for you to study/prepare for your exam. This course is my only and also the first C :)

She is THE worst teacher I ever had. Does not teach, classes are a waste of time. She is also extremely rude and not willing to work with students. If you asks questions she makes you look like an idiot and answers in a condescending manner. She does not curve tests because she has a "Standard to uphold." She is the rudest teacher ever.
Professor Davis is a very good teacher. She wants to see all of her students succeed, and if you put in the work, you will

Professor Davis is amazing!! I took her twice and wish I could take her more. She teaches difficult subjects so the classes aren't easy but she really does care about you and wants you to learn. Take her !!! Gives lots of extra credit too
The rudest teacher I have ever had. She is extremely unfair and shows favoritism. She does not teach either!!! avoid her at all costs. you won't fail but having her will make you hate accounting

I usually don't rate professors. Prof. Davis on the other hand is horrible and deserves a bad rating. She is incredibly rude, condescending and difficult to communicate with. She sent out a message the weekend before finals stating she would no longer be answering questions. Who does that right before a cumulative 150 question final? AVOID HER.

She is one of the worst prof. I've had. Condescending, rude, unapproachable and entitled. Vague in her expectations and you must study everything for the exam because she is not clear on what will be on the exams. She does not respond to emails, and she doesn't teach. You will have to teach yourself.

She is one of the rudest teachers and does not respect her students at all. Its a typical accounting class and you will not get an awful grade. However, if you arent the smartest kid in the room she makes you feel absolulty stupid. Dont ask any questions because she will make you feel worse. The rudest teacher I have ever had.
Her personality is the reason I don't like audit

Spends too much time talking about community service. Purposely puts her exams an hour after a Finance exam that nearly all of her students also have to take. Shes rude and has a way too short temper. Literally acts like child. Maybe she needs to get herself together before she continues teaching accounting.

I've had Davis for 301 and 302, and she is hands down one of the best accounting professors I've had. She REALLY knows what she's talking about. She expects you to come to class already having reviewed the chapter material, which can make the lectures hard to follow if you don't work out of class. She is also a AMAZING professional resource.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Olivia is one of the smartest accountants you will meet. her class is difficult but if you pay attention, attend office hours, do the extra credit, and try more then most people do, you will be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Davis is very knowledgable about Accounting. That being said, she expects that students know as much as her and can often be condescending/talk to you like you're stupid. Go to class, she tells you a lot about what will be on the exams.

Dr. Davis was very professional and clearly cared about her students doing well in the class. She was funny and made the class interesting by having real life examples. If you do the work, go to class, and study what she tells you you'll do well in the class

I took Olivia for ACC301. I was terrfied to take the class, however, Olivia Davis calmed my nerves. Her lectures are very helpful and she is clear on what to study for exams. She really cares about her students and wants you to do well. Tests are easy if you study what she tells you.
For audit Olivia was awesome because she had a real life story for every definition we learned. I took her in the summer so she got to know each of us better. I've heard she's tough for 302.

olivia is friendly and has a lot of experience in actual public accounting. she's a great connection to have. with that being said, her intermediate classes are extremely difficult. the exams are really really hard to finish within the time frame given. it's an extremely hard class but passable. she gives a lot of extra credit and curves every exam
Reads straight from slides and very few problems are done in class. Tests are very difficult and she is very vague with how to prepare for them. She is also very condescending to students. Good luck
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: All the opinion below are corrected. But she offer many extra bonus credit. Looks like she don't want to lose this job. This is her first semester to teach. So we may give her another chances rather than let her go.

Davis is knowledgeable about accounting, but a horrible teacher. Her lectures are lazy and straight from the book, she berates students for being wrong, but will blame students for not understanding the content. She is too emotional, rude and sassy. You are better off buying the book and teaching yourself.

Definitely one of the worst professors I've had. Context: 4 years of Chemical Engineering and in my second year of Accounting. Doesn't explain the material well, just reads off of power points. Constantly condescending toward students. If you attempt to ask her questions at office hours or email, she will tell you it was covered in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Note: This course is difficult no matter who you take it with, but it is more difficult with Davis. Her lectures are just her reading off the provided power points and she is not approachable to ask questions. She often criticized and degraded the class by calling us "not smart enough" or advising the entire class to drop. Do not take Olivia Davis.

New professor at Gatton, NABA advisor. Ton of auditing experience, therefore able to explain the PowerPoints very well . Loves to talk to students, grading for test and quizzes are fair. Go to class, do the homework, you should be fine. I highly recommend her ACC 403, but I heard she isn't as at teaching regular accounting.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Caring

reviews.comment: This class is laid back. The lectures involve reading and commenting on various pieces, sometimes with writing exercises between. Dr. Carter tells lots of personal stories, thoughts, and jokes --- it can get boring, but his love for this subject is infectious. You'll need access to a printer. Always read the assigned example pieces!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Hilarious--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: You will buy several books read and write a ton for the class. He is a not a great professor but a nice person. If you are not an English major I really would rethink taking this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I love this man so much. He randomly sings in class all the time, it's great. My only problem would be that the TA grades everything and he was a VERY hard grader. In the end, it's usually fine because he gives a lot of feedback for the final portfolio. If you are interested in reading/writing I would definitely recommend his class!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Lectures are drawn out and mandatory. You will be graded on three essays by a TA, along with said TA's teaching a mandatory recitation. Be careful to stay in MLA format, though your grade ultimately is determined by the toughness of your TA.

Had him for ENG 107. His lectures seemed unrelated to the topics. Few assignments (all graded by TA's) so be sure to really try on them. Kinda strict abt participation in lecture and pop quizzes on the daily readings. Overall easy course, if you get good grades on the 3 papers, its an easy A.
