Not a history person, only took this class for a core requirement but im so glad that dr. myrups class is the one i picked. he truly cares about his students and does a great job of emphasizing learning rather than just memorizing things and makes lecture funny and interesting. only thing is that i didnt know my grade until the end of the course
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Hilarious

reviews.comment: One of the greatest teachers that I have ever had. Dr. Myrup is good at what he does and he loves doing it. He is a master of his craft and for me it felt like a gift to be able to sit in his class and watch him teach. He is also very energetic and fun, and his exams are fair and nothing to stress over. Excellent teacher and class!

Dr. Myrup is an AMAZING professor. He is super chill with due dates and will work with you and not against you. His lectures are great. He does not waste your time. You can tell he really loves his job. You'll need to know how to skim readings. He is passionate about what he teaches. Show up to class, do the readings, and try and you will do well!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Myrup is a great professor. He is very passionate about what he's teaching. He also genuinely cares about his students and cares more about the quality of the work rather than when it's turned in. I will say there is a hefty amount of reading, however as long as you look at his weekly emails you can get away with not reading.

Dr. Myrup is a great history professor, he would kind of act out the stories he was telling which I enjoyed. He is a very nice guy who will put in the time to meet with all of his students if they need help or have questions. The worst part of this class is the discussion sections and the readings which are not that bad.

Very few professors are as enthusiastic as Dr. Myrup. His lectures are fantastic, although he tends to choose obscure IDs for exams (some are merely brushed over in class), so beware. I also didn't like how ambiguous the recitation grade was. It consisted of quizzes, attendance, and "engagement", but I didn't know my actual grade till the very end.

Dr. Myrup is such a great professor, I would recommend him to anyone. I took his class for a core credit, and while you have to take notes and do the readings to do well, Dr. Myrup and his TAs are very lenient and forgiving with grading. You can tell from his teaching that Dr. Myrup loves what he does and wants his students to do well! Hes a king!

Professor Myrup is the best professor I've had in college yet. He is always willing to work with you and make sure you understand and comprehend the content. He's very big on creativity and allows you to have lots of flexibility with his assignments. He explains everything in lecture thoroughly and makes it entertaining even when he isn't trying!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Fantastic Prof super nice, easy to talk to and lenient grader.

I took Dr. Myrups class and honestly had a rough semester and wasnt going to pass and planned on retaking his course in the summer. He called me to reach out and worked with me to retake his course separately to avoid any fees and to replace my grade. He truly loves what he does and cares for his students 12/10 man.

Dr. Myrup is easily one of the best professors in the History department, if not one of the best professors at UK. His lectures are engaging and he structures them so it's like he's telling a story. He makes himself very accessible outside of class and is willing to stay late (i.e. past 5-6pm) and seems to genuinely care about how you are doing.

Dr. Myrup is the best professor this university has by far. He is incredibly caring and understanding and will let you turn things in later if life gets in the way. His lectures are funny, his assignments are creative and inspiring, and the readings are thought provoking. Take his class, you won't regret it ever.

Dr. Myrup encapsulates everything a professor should be. He truly cares about every student. He will help you with anything you need. He is a great teacher in every aspect. He is also one of the nicest and funniest people you can meet. I truly enjoyed his class and the discussions we had in class. He is exactly the kinf of teacher you want to take.

Even though the course matter was very dense and high paced, I loved Dr. Myrup and I believe he is everything a college professor should be. He is literally the nicest guy and really knows what he's talking about. He is super laid back as well. However, he doesn't use canvas which can make it a little difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Even though the course matter was very dense and high paced, I loved Dr. Myrup and I believe he is everything a college professor should be. He is literally the nicest guy and really knows what he's talking about. He is super laid back as well. However, he doesn't use canvas which can make it a little difficult. Take one of his classes if you can!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Absolutely the best professor I've had at UK. I'm not a history major, but he makes me want to take every class he teaches.

Professor Myrup is the prime example of what a college professor should be. He is easy going, caring and works hard to make sure he knows all of his students and what they need to be successful. His lectures are entertaining and he tries to get everyone involved and having a good time.

Dr. Myrup is the perfect model of how a professor should engage with his students. If you're not wanting to read, however, I would highly recommend you take another class. There are readings from the course packet, books, and electronic readings. Also, there are two 7-8 page papers to write throughout the semester. His exams are writing heavy.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Myrup is a very able teacher. Extremely lecture heavy, so regardless of the relatively small impact attendance has, it is very recommended. Grade based on two papers at 20% each (one creative, one research), midterm (essay and IDs) at 15%, final at 25%, and attendance/readings/quizzes at 20%. Really, really worth taking, and easy to work with.
Best professor ever. Enough said! Expect to read a decent amount, but he is always super helpful

He is one of the most respected history professors in the department, and there's a reason why. His lectures are so much fun and interactive, and overall he is a fantastic person who does his best to make sure the student is doing well.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Good guy

Dr. Myrup is a great prof who works hard to make his lectures entertaining! He gives the usual amount of history reading and really has a passion for the subject. He genuinely cares about his students and their lives outside of his class. If you can you should take him!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Dr. Myrup is an excellent teacher. His course is lecture heavy so if you miss class you are going to miss content. He has a midterm test and a final test. He gives three readings each week and a quiz on Friday. There are also two papers. He is animated and keeps you very engaged in class time. Very approachable. Loved him!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Myrup I have ever had in my 4 years at UK. His classes are some of the hardest history courses I have taken at UK, but he is organized, sticks to the syllabus, tells you what he expects. He's also understanding and will work with you on due dates, etc. A must take at UK! Great professor and an even better person.

Dr. Myrup is incredible at lecturing (VERY intelligent man). YOU MUST ATTEND CLASS & DO THE READINGS or you will not pass. He is very helpful and friendly. His lectures are very interesting. The exams are VERY hard (you must memorize 70+ IDs for the midterm & final & there are also essays). The creative writing assignments are super fun! Take him!

Dr. Myrup is the best teacher I've had so far at the University of Kentucky. He is extremely helpful and the lectures were well structured and he stays true to the syllabus. There's a decent amount of reading and the tests are lengthy, but nothing too bad. I would definitely recommend Dr. Myrup and I will be taking another class of his.

I took his class based on the rating on this site and was not disappointed! He is the best professor I've ever had in my college career. He is willing to help you in any way he can. He loves what he teaches and you can tell. He is flexible with deadlines. He cares about his students and it shows. TAKE HIS CLASS YOU WONT REGRET IT!

Dr. Myrup is my favorite professor at UK. He has an amazing way to grab your attention in lectures. He has your best interest at heart and will go out of his way to help you do well. If you like history at all- please please please take his classes (I took 3)!

I have nothing but great things to say! So sweet, understanding, and helpful. He is always welcoming students to office hours for help on exams, readings, and papers. With that said, you need to study at least 5 days in advance for his exams. IT IS ALL SHORT ANSWERS/ESSAYS so you need to know your stuff and stay on top of your readings. Take him!

One of the best professors I have ever had. He is willing to help you in any way possible. His lectures are very organized and easy to follow. Make sure you take time out of your schedule to go to his office hours.
Excellent in every way. Took his class because of the ratings on this site and did not regret it one bit; best professor ever.

One of the greatest professors at Uk. I will always be on the lookout for any class he is teaching because he is phenomenal. He has an interest in the topics and makes every lecture interesting. Loved being in his class and can only hope I have the pleasure of being in his class again.

Hand's down the best professor I have had in college. He will go out of his way to help you with problems that you have in the class and is very understanding. Two decent length papers but flexible topics along with two big exams. Need to study for exams and do weekly reading but overall great class.

Dr. Myrup  is one of the nicest and most approachable professors at UK! He's always energetic in class and talks fast but pauses for questions. At the end of the lecture, he ties everything together into a bigger picture. The class consists of 2 papers, a midterm, final, and discussionquizzes. Quizzes are an easy A--do the readings each week.
Loved his class. Taking him again next semester!

He has a lot of passion for this topic, and it shows. He has a little bit of an unconventional lecture style in that he will write up the key words for the lecture every day on the board and just start talking. He gives study guides for exams and papers are pretty easy to write. Wikipedia was a good tool to fill blanks you may have from lectures

Great person, great professor. Dr. Myrup was clear, flexible, and wants his students to succeed. He makes class entertaining by switching it up. Also helped me improve as a writer. Probably my favorite teacher I've had in college.

Professor Myrup is the best professor I ever had in my entire academic experience. His course is not easy, but because he is such an avid and skilled professor, the learning process becomes easy. He is of the highest and finest teaching quality and professionalism and I am grateful that I had the experience to learn with him!
Mr. Myrup is a great professor!

Myrup is one of my favorite professors at UK! His lectures are incredibly organized and interesting. You have to take notes while he talks, but you get used to it quickly. He clearly loves the subject and loves to teach. His exams can be hard, but he tries to help you out beforehand. Also, he is very understanding about deadlines. Love his class!!

He is the best prof I have ever had! He is more than just an amazing teacher, but a nice, genuinely kind person. I am taking his class on Brazil next semester just because I enjoy his lectures so much! Going to class is enjoyable and informative! Take his class if possible!

Hands down one of the best professors I've ever had! Very helpful, understanding, answers questions clearly and thoroughly. He makes lecture interesting and go by very quickly. Speaks quickly but pauses for questions. Write down all the key terms! There is a  quiz each week but it's super easy as long as you read. Everyone should take this class!!

By far the BEST professor at UK and an even better person.  He is humble, enthusiastic, understanding, and helpful.  His class is very entertaining and not difficult at all.  He wants to see his students succeed and goes out of his way to help you.  TAKE HIM!!!

Professor Myrup is a great teacher and an even better person. he is willing to work with you and meet anytime you need. He also understands we all have other classwork to do and is flexible with his due dates on papers and projects.

Professor Myrup is literally one of the best teachers on this campus! He is so much fun and enthusiastic about what he teaches that you can't help but to pay attention! I absolutely loved him and if you ever need help he is always there!

Best history professor at UK. Very nice person, and also understands his students. His lectures is basically a 50 min story. He speaks very fast, but pauses every 10 mins to allow his students to ask questions. Puts up 10-20 terms on the board (key terms), which will be on his test. Overall: TAKE HIM!

The best, most approachable, likeable professor employed on UK's campus.  He is a real class act and his classes are a pleasure to take, they are hard but unlike many classes you actually leave the class with knowledge you didnt have before.
Best professor I've had at UK. Extremely helpful. Nicest man you'll ever meet!

Great prof! He talks really fast but as long as you know how to take notes by being focused on key points you'll be fine. He's a fine prof. he makes the class and topics interesting. Tests are like any history test, key terms and essays. The reading is necessary.
Really nice man.  Really humble and actually understands students.  Not a typical arrogant academician.  He'll go out of his way to help.  He's an excellent professor.  Take Him!
The MOST helpful and accessible professor in the history department.  Definitely recommended.

Don't listen to anyone saying he teaches good. He gives you a little push, and then directs you to the textbook for the other 80% of the material you have to learn on your own. Engineering Deciphered is what got me through his class. Do not take.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: A good lecturer and person, but there are some critical flaws. Tests are an extreme time crunch, & you get essentially no equations for an equation heavy class. I never went in to review my tests, but from what I heard the tests are strictly graded where you have to do exactly what he wants, even if you get the answer right, to get full points.

His class is difficult to pass. His homework is online through Wiley. His tests are incredibly difficult, about 5 questions and they were far more complicated than anything we worked on in class or in the homework. He doesn't return the exams, so you have to go to his office hours. When he asks questions in class, he wants a specific answer.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great at teaching, but exams are impossible. They have more questions than the once-per-week homework and are arguably more difficult/take more time to do. On top of that he grades like he wants you to fail. Drop him for the sake of on time graduation.

Really good at teaching, but leaves details out on purpose to make you read the textbook. Exams are super fair but his grading is the opposite. Fails you if you get below a 60% average on exams. Didn't think that would apply to me but here I am. On par with Hansen.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Makes the class very hard, but not so hard that you don't learn anything. Homework usually isn't too obnoxious and really helps you learn. Lectures are useful and well-planned. Exams usually have low averages, though. Lots of extra credit opportunities and ways to improve your grade. Be ready for homework to be due on Saturdays.

Dr. Tag is honestly one of the best lecturers that you will have at UK. He is well-knowledged and commands respect, but if you pay attention and do things the way he wants you to, you will easily pass the course. You will hear a lot of scary things about Tag before you enter into statics but if you respect him and do things his way, he is great.

Best professor in my tenure at the university. In an engineering program already lacking in quality professors, Tag is head and shoulders above the rest. Fair warning, while being the best professor I have ever had, he is simultaneously the hardest professor I have ever had. Be ready to actually LEARN and UNDERSTAND the topics covered.

Took Thermo II with Tag in spring and failed despite real effort. Retook it in summer with a different UK prof, didn't go to a single lecture, barely studied, and got a high B. Summer exam averages were in the 60s. Sure, Tag might be able to teach, but what does it matter if he can't grade fairly? He's failing solid engineering students.

Very good lecturer, very harsh grader. Exams are brutal with barely any partial credit. It's in the syllabus that if your exam average is below 60%, you automatically fail. That kind of built-in failure rate says a lot. For a junior-level class, it felt like a weed-out course.
Just go to a different school to take thermo he is the worst professor I've had in my college career

I didn't always like Dr. Taghadossi at first, but he grew on me over the semester. If you follow his instructions from day one and stay consistent, you'll likely get an A or B. I thought I did that on the first exam—I didn't. I didn't agree with everything he did, but this was the first $2000 course where I felt I got my money's worth.

Tag is a very knowledgeable professor, however, he fails to communicate clearly with students. He refuses to "reteach" any material if you don't understand, and is very useless when it comes to homework help. His exams are extremely hard, and he grades very strictly. To the point where even the right answer doesn't guarantee you any points.

I could not name a singular professor as knowledgeable as him. Yes the course is hard, but he gives so many examples and gives you every tool you need to succeed. Amazing worked out examples and lectures, as well as homework! I failed the first exam as you have to get used to his style, but its nothing you can't come back from. Amazing professor.

Tag is the kind of guy you love/hate. He's a super good professor/lecturer, but God bless you. You will have a strong relationship with God by the end of his thermo 2 course. Regardless it's all for the better.
The definition of "fair", and a fantastic teacher that pushes engineers to excellence in very difficult subject matter!
High quality but high difficulty; probably the best lecturer UK Mech E has but don't expect a cakewalk

Farzad is a really great lecturer and teaches you exactly what you need to know; however, his tests were EXTREMELY difficult. I studied for days and would still only get a C. You will most likely fail the first exam and I did but somehow I managed to survive. This class will test you hard. Just suffer through it, I came back from a 5 on the test.

Tag is a good teacher who knows his stuff and teaches it well, but his exams are incredibly difficult and he gives very little grace in grading. Taking thermo from Tag will likely lower your GPA, but better prepare you for thermo 2 than any of the other professors.

Horrible class design. Made the 1st half 10x harder than the second half causing half the people to drop the class by the third exam. After the three exams class gets 10x easier and at the end offered extra credit for teacher course evaluations.
Horrible Professor who makes the first half of the class 10x harder than the second half for no reason. Then offers extra credit for Teacher evaluations at the end of the semester.

This class will test your ability as an engineering student. The first 8 weeks there are 3 exams. Make sure you attend class and pay attention. Dr. Taghaddosi tells you EXACTLY how to study for exams, and if you follow his guidance throughout the semester you will succeed. The rest of the semester is group projects which are graded more leniently.

A lot of students hate him but he just wants you to know the material. Just study HARD for the first three tests and you'll be alright. The rest of the semester is projects that he grades somewhat leniently.

He has some tough exams but his lectures are probably the best I have had in terms of being able to understand the content. I got a 20% on my first exam and ended with an A in the class. Do all of the assignments because one of them might be worth extra credit at the end of the course. He usually curves or gives a extra credit question on his exams

Dr. Tag is super informed about the subjects he teaches, he cares about student success and wants to help students learn. Although sometimes, when he makes you do your own work, ppl think this is him being an ass. His tests are very difficult and not always extremely well written, they will challenge your content knowledge. Good guy, tough tests.

No partial credit on exams. Asks at least one random obscure question every exam. Being in this mans office is beyond intimidating. The material is not even that difficult and he somehow makes it difficult. Just take thermo at a different university if possible. If not, just hope you get lucky a semester and hope you have other options.

The worst professor at UK. The worst professor I've ever had. Possibly the worst professor period. If you need to add a semester to avoid him, do it. He should not have a job, but tenure is what it is I suppose.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The class is broken up between the first half and the second half of the term. In the first half, there are 3 exams, and to even be able to continue with the course you must average 60% of the three. He is very tough and strict during this half. The second half is all projects and lectures. He lightens up A LOT. Grades easier and offers bonuses.

Highest Quality ME professor at the University of Kentucky. Be prepared to work hard to receive the grade you want. It is all worth it because you will understand and appreciate the material more than if taken with an easy professor.
He expects a lot out of students but does give them tools to succeed. Definitely need to be willing to work hard and improve to be successful in his class.

One of my favorite professors at UK. Presents content in a clear and understandable way, with no more than 15 slides per 50 minutes lecture. Asks a lot of you, but you learn the content well. He knows most of the names in his classes and will call on you. If we could have him for every class we might graduate a dozen people but they'd be top notch.

Dr. Taghaddosi is very polarizing. Yes he asks a lot from his students, but you'll come out a better student who will truly understand the subject. I've had him 4 times and like him. He does truly care about the student's success. He is professional, but personable. He takes some getting used to. You'll come to realize he's one of the best at UK.

Dr. Taghaddosi does an excellent job of breaking down the material that at times can seem super complex. Statics is a fundamental course of ME. Dr. Taghaddosi is a pro at creating intuitive slides that highlight the big picture items that need focused on.
Run as fast as you can. Not worth your GPA. Loves his students, but his grading criteria is psychotic.

Avoid. AT ALL COSTS. He will belittle you, demean you, grade unfairly, test on things unrelated to what he's taught, and you will likely not pass. He has constructed his courses meticulously to make it as hard as possible for a student to pass. I don't know how he's kept his job here. I have never met a student who's had a positive opinion of him.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Took this class twice with him. He is a smart professor and knows his stuff but he is ruthless when it comes to grading. His lectures are not very good at all but talking to him in office hours/after class he can explain things very well. He wants you to pass but his grading is unnecessarily ruthless. I had to drop twice. Avoid if possible.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: this professor is one of the best i have had in college. he is very approachable and genuinely cares about student success. thermo 2 is a hard class, but he made it very easy to take on and was very good at explaining topics.

Had him fall 2021 semester and dropped my C because he basically told me to. Teacher grades very hard on accuracy, all exams that I took were all Free Response Questions instead of every other EM221 class that was 2-3 FRQ and about 10 Multiple Choice. His exams are a week and a half before the common hour exams. Good speaker but poor teacher.

Dr. Taghaddosi is the best teacher I've had while pursuing mech engineering at UK. I had him for Themo 1-2 and Mech Systems. He has very high expectations but genuinely wants students to succeed. He makes everyone aware of how much effort they need to put into his class to succeed. If you expect to do less than what he asks you will struggle.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Yes, the material he teaches is difficult, and he expects you to understand what you are doing. It isn't enough to be able to plug values into an equation. But he clearly cares about his students, and is more than willing to help you understand concepts that you don't have a grasp on if you go to him.
Truly does not understand that his class is not the only class students take. Not forgiving at all. Tests are hard and have a big time crunch.

He has high expectations for all of his students and if you make an effort with him, he will return it in kind. I will not sugar coat it, you will do more studying and homework than most of your other classes. You do not get a grade with him, you earn one! He also offers a lot of extra credit to help offset the increased difficulty! (+9% overall)
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: He has earned a reputation for a tough professor, and it is rightfully so. Be ready to be engaged and paying attention during lectures or you won't pass. Quiz every week and two homework that will take a couple of hours. Exams worth 73% of the class. Work plenty of practice problems and take good notes and you will do fine on exams. Toughbut doable
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: In my experience, exams were worth 73% of the overall grade in this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: This is my third time taking Farzad and I hated him after my first two classes with him, but this class went surprisingly smooth. Usually, he likes to trick people on exams with content they've never seen before, but the material was so easy he couldn't surprise you with anything. MATLAB can be somewhat of a challenge, but it wasn't on exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: You'll go through the lectures and wonder why I rate him 1 star, but then you go to the homework and exams and it's like you're taking a 10 credit hour class. He will take any opportunity he can to make you lose points on exams and assignments and accuse you of cheating. I've had him for two classes so far and I aged 20 years due to the stress.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr. Taghaddosi has earned his reputation is a tough professor. His exams are difficult and has grading can be ruthless. That being said, he makes every effort to make sure his students are prepared. Pay attention, take notes, do the homework + book problems. If you can't pass his class, you shouldn't be an engineering major anyway. Great professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr. Taghaddosi has a well-deserved reputation as a difficult professor. He works his students hard, he expects a lot out of students, and you will not pass if you do not put in the most effort possible. That said, if you do make it through his class with a passing grade, you WILL know the material forwards, backwards, and sideways.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: This man-child was very disrespectful to his students. He held such a high standard of his students, but would never uphold these standards for himself. Grading in the course was not fair. Taghaddosi is a borderline perfectionist and your grades will reflect. DO NOT TAKE HIM
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Worst teacher I have had at UK. His teaching is mediocre at best and his superiority complex makes him unbearable. Be prepared for no grading criteria and cutthroat grading. As a senior in Mech E, this will be my first C and not for lack of effort. Went to office hours and he called my work "incomprehensible" and failed to answer a simple ?

No clear grade criteria Changes assignment details after assigning so you have to rework Feels like you're fighting a losing battle Doesn't post averages on scores because they're so low but he wants you to feel like you're the only one struggling

Absolutely ruthless professor. It doesn't matter if you're an extremely diligent and hardworking student, he will fail you over a fraction of a percent. Some things are nice about him, like his grade replacement policy, but if you expect to get an A and you're not a prodigy look elsewhere. Also, being in his office is the most intimidating thing.
He is the literal worst.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--So many papers

reviews.comment: A tad too professional, but a fairly good teacher
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Clear grading criteria--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Hardest Statics Professor, but not in a bad way. I am an A student and barely made it out alive holding onto my 4.0, but you learn so much more in his section I would do it again even if i got a B. He can seem abrasive and likes to say "refer to syllabus" but you're an adult. If you're a snowflake, avoid him at all costs.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: As someone who had to deal with him in the class more than one semester, he is terribly rude and his behaviors are not according to the university rules. He thinks that he is way higher than students and lets himself to easily insult them and assistants. He has no knowledge of solid mechanics. Avoid him unless you have no choices.
-hard grader -really good professor

He is very polarizing. I have had him 3 times, and I am now a senior. Looking back at all my professors, he is the best. Some people will not like him and not do well. Those are generally the types that do not pay attention in lecture, do not read the text, or put forth the effort. Take him if you are fine with discipline and a challenge.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: His grading criteria is extremely unorthodox. 5% of your grade depended on answering one question correctly when called upon in class. If that wasn't stressful enough, he would also give you a 0% on your entire homework grade (worth 12% overall) if your tests didn't average a 60% or above. Doesn't care if his students are successful or not.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Participation matters--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Very smart man, and he knows it. Has difficulty teaching the most basic engineering arithmetic, and his students struggle because of it. Expect a high drop rate, as my class started with 35 kids and ended with a mere 8. Callous to student success and the worst professor I have encountered in my entire college career. Avoid his classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: If you have the option to not take Farzad , I strongly advise you do that. The way he grades his exams in my opinion is just not fair. I have had him for 2 classes so far and both of these classes have been the worst class experience that I have had since I have been at UK. I have no respect for a professor who is unwilling to help his students
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr. Taghadossi seems callus but he is actually very caring. More than any professor I've had he took the time to ask me how I was doing with the material, and he even went out of his way multiple times to ensure I had help. He wants you to try hard and he gives chances to come back from a bad test grade, but he will not pass you for effort alone.
The language barrier makes him hard to listen to, which isn't really his fault, but it's still there. A pretty tough grader, I'd recommend looking elsewhere for this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: Class is somewhat difficult, but he curves when necessary and provides plenty of opportunity to rebound from a poor test performance. He's definitely not a professor who lets half the class fail, but you will have to work to get a high grade. He understands it's stressful and tries to alleviate some of that stress. Positive experience.

Seems really intimidating in class but is a really nice guy who truly wants his students to succeed. Going to office hours and asking questions really helps, exams are fair and often have a bonus question. Is strict on his rules but his rules are fair and easy to follow. If you put in effort and show respect he is excellent and very knowledgeable.

He's a great lecturer. His class is split into groups and the homework is to be divided however you like. Lecture attendance is mandatory and he has a quiz every week. If you follow his in class examples and do your homework, then the tests will be a breeze as they are simply extensions of that work. I think he's excellent and would take him again.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: He is a very good lecturer,  he cares about his students and doesn't want anyone to fail. As long as you study you will do fine on the tests and exams. This is the second time I have had him in class and would take him again.

see... I just had the guy and he's a really cool teacher and he cares. He's a little intimidating at first and has an accent but once you get used to it everything is fine. HW does not have to be done in groups and tests are exactly what the homework is. Take the guy and if you pay attention you'll be fine
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: One of the worst professors I've had. He works unclear/incorrect examples in class, and by examples I mean example, because we almost never make it through more than 1 per class. (1hr 15 minutes). HW is done in groups for some reason, and tests for the most part are unrelated to the homework. Weirdly he seems like he really cares, but he's horrible

I think he is a very good teacher, but he is hard to get use to because of his accent. If you need help he is very willing to help as long as you try to help yourself. His test are not that hard and he also gives one bonus question which helps alot. Over all as long as you got to lecture you will be fine.

Bad professor. Will ask you questions and will expect a word for word explanation that matches his or he believes it's wrong. That counts against your grade by the way. Smart guy, but that is exactly his problem. Don't take him unless it's absolutely necessary.

Good professor, and a super smart guy, and he knows it. His lectures give a good understanding to the topic, but to complete homework you will have to teach yourself some. Test are not the hardest in the world, but you better study. He has this thing where he tries to embarrass students in class for a participation grade, very counter productive.

Worst professor I've had at UK. Works problems in class that are impossible and he doesn't even know how to solve them. The homework is extremely difficult, and he's very unhelpful in office hours (he blew me off when I went to ask questions). All in all do your best not to have him as a professor. You'll thank yourself for it.

Brilliant guy.  Really knows his stuff.  Asks a lot of his students but tends to ease up when grading.  Expect hard homework.  Slightly easier test/quizes.  If you want to slide through he won't work.  If you want fair, he will work.  Only negative thing I can say is seems to have a little bit of a complex about being the smartest guy in the room.

Best lecture I've had at UK. Very clear and will answer any questions a student has in class. Will force participation in class- he'll ask you a question and stare at you until you answer, but this works out really well as it creates discussion among the class and forces you to learn the material. Very friendly. Really want to take him again!
She was very informative and passionate about the class. I learned a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment:
She does not give study guides
She does not give much homework so if you do bad on a major assignment (which is very likely given the way for formats her exams), you will not finish with a good grade in the class
difficult to take good notes
15-40 page readings before every class
30-60 minute videos to watch before every class
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I liked the professor. She's really passionate about her teaching which is nice because not everyone is.

I had her for HIS 499. She's a hard grader, and she will nag you over email until you respond. She's very smart, and she projects that onto you. You'll learn a lot from her, and the 20-page paper at the end of the semester is your only real 'exam'. Just put in the work and you'll be rewarded.

Get ready to do 2-3 reading everyday for homework and watch a one hour long lecture that she will ask questions on. Very hard grader on papers and tough on projects. Nice lady that can seem like a chill professor at first but as the course went on she got more picky on the way we did our work.If you're a history junkie and love to read it's for you
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Dr. Chassen-Lopez is a phenomenal professor. She is insightful, engaging, and ready to challenge her upperclassmen with her readings and assignments. I took her twice for upper level history classes and she absolutely prepared me for my graduate studies in GWS.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Respected

reviews.comment: Great professor, but is kind of difficult when it comes to assignment requirements. There are some quizzes and a group project but overall she has great lectures. I agree with some reviews don't get on her bad side or youll regret it
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Dr. C-Lo is a great professor! She tells a lot of interesting stories and is passionate about what she teaches. There were readings for every class, two papers, two exams, and a skit. As long as you do the reading and attend/pay attention in class, youll be fine.

Dr. C-Lo is a good teacher, but the assignments aren't great, she makes students do skits and things to "make the content more interesting." She taught the Mexican Revolution well, but lots of reading. Two shortish papers and an easy midterm. Not the easiest grader. Don't get on her bad side. Brought us authentic Mexican food.
I've had her twice and love her! She is great at teaching.

A very educated and well-traveled lady and brings her experiences into the classroom.  Always has a smile on her face and makes you feel like you can do the work when you talk to her - very encouraging.
Took her for SPA 201 and it was great! I learned so much and am taking her again next semester. She's a native spanish speaker and does have an accent.

She is SO SWEET! I loved her class so much. I was such an easy class, especially if you've taken Spanish before! I would absolutely take another class if she taught it. The homework is pretty easy, and she's always willing to help you if you need it!
LOVED HER. Actual angel on earth I will sing her praises she was so kind to us who were butchering her language and made it just a safe place to be wrong, and grow.

TAKE FAB!! She is so caring, sweet, and funny. She's a very approachable prof and exams are so easy as long as you pay attention to the review slides. She is very good at explaining things that you're confused over, and she makes the class super doable even if you have no spanish background.

Attendance is graded each week & participation is included in this grade. Fabiola is an amazing professor who makes sure you understand and feel prepared for the exam. There is an oral and written portion on each exam but you go over the content for each part so much it is a breeze. Highly recommend this queen!

The content can be hard to grasp at times but he taught it well. There is math involved and stumped many students. He does extra credit but its not worth alot but helps alittle. Overall, really liked the content.

RUN AND RUN FAR AWAY. DO NOT TAKE BIO 304 WITH HIM. Doesn't TEACH material that shows up on the exams well. Lecture slides only really make sense to him. iClicker matters! Made content way more difficult to learn than necessary. Hardest class I've ever taken (4.0 student/valedict), even with the fairly simple lecture concepts. Exam averages = 50-60

Dr Famulski is incorporates practice questions during the lecture, although he doesn't give nearly enough time to answer them. Sometimes he overcomplicates things, but for the most part he does a good job explaining and not just reading off the slides. You definitely need to watch lectures to understand his slides and exams are all word problems.

I really enjoyed him; you can tell he did the majority of the organization and grading in his joint class with Dr. Morris: he had a lot of office hours & explained questions well during class time. He was nerdy in an endearing way, and explained concepts well and thoroughly. The only problem I had was pacing; the ends were sometimes rushed.

WORST TEACHER I HAVE EVER HAD! Dr. Famulski makes genetics way harder than it needs to be. I have never struggled in a college biology or stem class until I took genetics. If you have the option to not have him as a professor, take it! He is really bad at explaining at lectures and somehow doesn't care that the averages are failing grades.

One of the hardest professors at UK. Didn’t matter how much you studied cause he designed the exams to make you fail. Yes, genetics is difficult, but it really shouldn’t be as difficult as he made it. Got a C in this class but took advanced genetics after this class (BIO 404) and got an A, make it make sense.

Every exam question is very tricky and the average grade on the exams is a failing grade. He does not curve exams and 90 to 100 is an A. He teaches the content very briefly and poorly you must review it yourself and dedicate whole nights/days to studying for his exams. Do not take this class unless you are required to or you are a genetics guru.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: A professor should not be able to hide under the umbrella of a subject being hard. As a professor it is your responsibility to cultivate you teaching ability, listen to your students, address issues, etc. Students put themselves in your hands with the expectation that you care about us just as much as we care in taking that class.

Dr. Famulski made this class so much harder than it needed to be. His lecture slides rarely even had any words on them and he would zip through explaining diagrams. His tests almost always had errors, and he will never throw away questions, even if everyone gets it wrong. Stick with Miravito on this one.

You can tell that Dr. Famulski cares about his students but there were some key issues with the course: exams frequently had many errors and questions were often designed to trick you (occasionally to the point that no one would answer some correctly) and his rubrics for projects were unclear. The lectures were somewhat disjointed as well.

He is nice, but it was hard to understand his disjointed explanations during lectures and there was a lot of information in the lectures that wasn't necessary. The exams were also full of typos, errors, and purposely misleading questions. The class was harder than it really needed to be.

Don't take Famulski. He's a nice man which makes me feel bad for hating his class as much as I did. If you aren't EXTREMELY smart, you'll feel like you're drowning. I dreaded exams because they just made me feel stupid. He's very easy to reach outside of class, but this class has to be your only priority if you want to have any hope at succeeding.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. F is a great professor. He is very easy to contact outside of class and genuinely wants you to succeed. His class is difficult, because it's genetics, but not impossible if you are willing to put in the work. He makes lectures fun and he seems to really love what he does. He tends to make typos on tests and practice exams, but that's it.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Genetics is insanely hard no matter what. This class was extra hard. Dr. Famulski was a new professor when I took the class, so he was inexperienced in writing exams which made them next to impossible. Clarity of grading policy might also need a bit of work, but I feel this will improve over time. He is a very nice person and was open to concerns.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Caring

reviews.comment: Hardest class I've taken. He is a great lecturer and kind/passionate man (but that is about the only positives). The exams were impossible and unrelated to class lectures (averages in the 50s and highs around 70) ,he constantly contradicted the syllabus, and he even curved midterm grades, and then REVOKED the curve. RUN! Fast. Do not take!?!?!?!??!
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--TEST HEAVY--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: He's a great guy, super nice and wants to help. The major assignments are your speeches. He does good at making sure you're not nervous and adapting if you choke up. I recommend taking him!

He is very philosophical and you will find yourself wandering off. However, it is the easiest class. Everything is group projects and really fun if you get a good group. It genuinely is so easy and usually get out of class early. He is super nice and very understanding, but often wanders on about morgue topics at times.

Lecturer Frost is kind and forgiving, so long as you convey effort. His study guides were brief and perfectly on-topic, which helped lots before the 3 exams. He helps lots with the final project, so you can expect a solid grade. His enthusiasm towards communication is clear, and I grew to respect it as the course developed. Overall, an easy course.

Mr. Frost led a pretty easy class. He lectured for half the semester then it was mostly group work. Just show up. Don't miss class; it hurts you and your group. Mr. Frost wants everyone to succeed, and the exams are easy if you just use your resources. This class will require you to do a social experiment with your group outside of class time.

Super sweet always a smile on his face. He is very accommodating when late or need to miss class. he does lecture the first couples weeks then it just group work. Pretty easy and the quizzes and test are very easy when using the study guide. He even says his tests are not to trick you up.
Really nice professor, really wants you to do good! The assignments are easy and really just rely on how well you and your group decide to do the work. I would take him again!
I had a hard time as it seemed he wanted us all to agree on his opinions on political ideas, which I did not. I did well in the class, but it was hard for me to gain anything from it.
All group work, and it is pretty enjoyable if you like your group. Interesting guy, but I love him.

the class was fairly easy & you typically work in a specific group to finish assignments. there are a few exams throughout the semester that you should look at the study guide for. it definitely was not my favorite class but i didn't want to have to give speeches so this was a good alternative

Professor Frost is so kind and caring. He made the class really enjoyable and you honestly won't dread going unlike other classes. This class is made up of quizzes, exams, one paper, and an overall group assignment. He guides every single student to doing well and none of the assignments are too hard because of this.

He is a little awkward but he's fun to have in class. He lectures at the beginning of the semester but we focus on our groups a majority part of the semester. There are a lot of exams, quizzes, participation and a paper or two. Just go to class and have fun, the quizzes are short and the exams have some of the same questions as the quizzes.

Very sweet and personable. She is very easy to get a hold of for any questions. The class is very easy with only a few major assignments. Attendence does not matter, with class sometimes being cancelled for work days.
She is awesome!!!!

Super easy class, she's also very entertaining and easy to talk to. She doesn't really count attendance that often, just make sure to show up for speeches or in-class assignments. She usually posts when. Very easy grader. It'd be hard not to get an A.
Best teacher I've ever had, intentionally signed up for an 8 am just to take her class again.
Enjoyed Dr. Watson and am signed up to take her for 111 next semester.
Fallon is the best for CIS 111. Very easy grader. There is a lot of work and an annoying group project but she walks you through everything with very thorough instructions.
Fallon is the best for CIS 110!  We learned a lot but she is so chill. Gave lot's of extra credit. The work is pretty easy and she is not a tough grader. Will be taking her for CIS 111.
Best teacher I've had at UK. She is extremely caring and if you have any problems you can let her know and she will take care of you. I wish UK was filled with Mrs. Watsons.

I took this class online after taking CIS 110 in person and it was equally as good! Fallon is super easy to reach and answers questions well. There are a few papers but they are fun to do since the topics are pretty much up to you. The group project was more detailed but the instructions are very clear on all assignments.

Dr.Watson is one of the best English teachers I have ever had. She is so caring and loving about her students. I have a 110% in her class and i must tell you the extra credits are amazing.

She is very helpful when it comes to assignments and accessible outside which does come in handy in case of an emergency.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I loved having Fallon! Super chill and laid-back. Very heavy on public speaking, but offers heavily-weighted extra credit.

I highly recommend if you have to take CIS 110 take it with Dr.Watson she made this class super enjoyable to be in. The class revolves around mainly public speaking, two papers, and some group work. The grading was very generous and the public speaking was made very easy and in a comfortable environment. Plus no class on Fridays which was nice.

I loved Fallon! She is an easy grader but values your effort. She was easy to talk to and let us have Fridays out of class to do our weekly assignments. There are public speaking assignments but she always made everyone feel comfortable. The class isn't hard as long as you pay attention to directions which she was great at explaining. Super nice!

110 is basic material, so it's good to have a prof like Watson who brings the class to life! She loves cracking jokes but still gets down to business every session. Gives her students a lot of room to work on their own while also making sure grading instructions and expectations are clear. You'll get what you give in her class, so show respect!

She was so awesome! She was literally like so friendly to everyone! Her willingness to help everyone pass the class was so helpful but if someone pushed her patience, she would put her foot down. Absolutely would take her classes again!
Is very lenient on due dates as long as you're actually trying
SHES AWESOME. Take this class-everyone needs to have a teacher like her

I couldn't possibly summarize how amazing Dr. Watson is! She is truly one of the best professors I could ever ask for. She cancelled class every Friday to give us time to work on assignments, which was amazing. Dr. Watson is accessible, personable, and completely down-to-earth. Her lectures are both engaging and informational. I'd take her again!

She is the most caring, nicest person ever! She is so easy to work with. Take CIS 110/111 with her. The assignments were kinda like busy work but its an easy class to check off of UK Core. You will not regret taking her. She is willing to work with you for whatever reason. TAKE HER

If you want an easy gen Ed take Watson! She is so nice and easy. That being said you need to put in the effort and you cannot slack off. For our big paper it was 1500 words. So her class is easy if you are a good writer. She is so willing to work with you if you have any issues.  take her you wont regret it

I absolutely LOVED Ms. Watson! Both she and her class were definitely one of my favorites because she's very lenient with grading as long as effort is clearly evident, cancels class on Friday's, gives plenty of opportunities for extra credit, and explains her expectations for assignments very clearly so that you always know what to expect!
Greatest class to have as an incoming freshman. Did like 3 "hard" assignments and then never came back to class. Such a gem.

Such a super easy class. Few papers but easy. Put in some work, show up, and you will pass easily. Shes supper chill and always cancels class :) Im taking her again for cis 111 because she was so chill and amazing. Theres really nothing else to it. Supper easy, chill, and I love her as a professor.
This is one of the best classes I have taken. She is real and honest about speaking. If you show up, interact, and do the little bit of work she gives, it's an easy A.
Very personable and friendly, if you do your work you will do well. Very manageable workload.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: She is a top-notch person and a very laid back professor. She doesn't assign much work, and she is a fair grader on projects like the video tutorial and presentation. However, be wary of her paper grading.

I highly recommend taking this class with her. As long as you do the work and put an effort in, you will do well. She genuinely cares about her students and often says that she tries her best not to put any stress on us.

This class is an easy A if you put the work in. Everything is laid out in the beginning of the semester super clearly and she's always accessible to answer questions. She's also super understanding that we have lives outside of class and encourages us to do what's best for us

Dr. Watson is a very good professor! Shes very caring and obviously loves what she does. The class is easy and requires you to do some quizzes, and essay, and a speech. Theyre very easy and Dr. Watson gives great feedback. I had a great semester in her class!
Great professor. Very intelligent. Pushed my creativity. Best class of the semester.

Professor Watson was an amazing professor, highly recommend for anyone needing a com class. Much more laid back than the average professor, making it a million times easier to talk to her. Recommend her class 100 out of 100 times.
fallon is such a nice lady! few speeches and like two papers, show up and act like youre interested and you'll be fine

Such a great teacher!! She is a mom so she understands schedules and how hectic our lives are. Gives many out of class workdays and all quizzes are online and have unlimited attempts!!! There is no final in this class (CIS111) but be prepared to speak in front of the class a lot in this class!

Great professor. She cancels class all the time if you have a project to work on. Overall the best CIS 112 professor so take her if you can. Be prepared to do volunteer work outside of class, it's part of the curriculum. One group project to create 3 podcasts throughout the semester, but overall such an easy class.

As long as you give effort in your speeches, you'll get an A. The course wasn't designed by her, so the curriculum is really boring and seems like a lot of busy work. Most classes were spent preparing for speeches or listening to speeches. She's a cool person to talk to if you stay to chat on days she lets you leave early.

Definitely take Fallon for CIS!! She rocks. She is super understanding of any circumstances and is extremely flexible with the material and making everything achievable. She wants everybody to succeed and gives many out of class work days! She is super personable and funny. An overall awesome professor!

If you have to take CIS, TAKE THIS PROFESSOR! She is super understanding of students, flexible, and really laid back. She made this class fun! It's clear she wants all of her students to succeed and often doesn't require you to attend class for "out of class workdays." Highly recommend, but don't bother buying the textbooks.
She is really laid back but knows what to do. Very easy to talk to

I love this teacher. She really understands how students feel and tries to connect with them logically. She removes all the boring busy work put in front of us by the curriculum and lets us be creative and express ourselves on assignments. I would love to have her again and again.
amazing professor, super chill and understanding. very easy to get along with and makes the class work for her students. wish she taught more than just these 2 classes so i could take her again

This course was challenging for me, and the teaching style did not work well with how I learn. I felt the material was not always explained clearly, and I often had to rely heavily on outside studying. I passed, but it was a stressful class, so I'd recommend being prepared to learn a lot independently or avoid this teacher at all costs

This is a hard course, and you need to be locked in every class. Dr. Ferguson is a good professor, but he can be pretty blunt, and comes off as unfriendly/unapproachable at first. He is better once you get to know him. Exams are incredibly comprehensive and will test EVERYTHING you have learned in class (nothing will be left off of the exam).

Professor Ferguson grew on me throughout the semester. He's not a warm bubbly kind of guy. He's blunt but lightened up as the class went on. You will be in groups for practice problems that count as extra credit the whole semester. If you get a good group its great, if you dont it sucks and there's nothing you can do about it. ACC 302 is very hard
Amazing class. Great content. Get to know your fellow classmates through cool on campus scavenger hunts and hands on time at the campus farm. Professor super engaged and fun class.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: ACC 302 is a hard class, but Prof Ferguson presented material in a way that was easier to understand. His tests were hard, but not terrible. Attendance was mandatory if you wanted bonus points. He wanted all students to succeed. He seems intimidating at first and can be dry in emails, but very nice guy.

His lectures were not very helpful, I stopped attending and learned more by figuring out the content myself. Exams are worth a lot and he fortunately does give you a practice exam that is like the real one. He uses his own website instead of canvas which is pretty annoying. He also responds to emails by sending the response to the whole class.

Obnoxiously repetitive material. Lectures are incredibly boring. Homework is difficult and takes forever. The only redeeming quality is that exams are quite easy and pretty much directly from the homework and study guide. You can learn nothing and pass.
Hard to understand. Homeworks are insanely hard. Only reads from the slides that will not help you when you need help. Loses track of the lecture every 20 minutes.
Easy if you attend
Attendance is required but you get 5% extra credit. Exam questions are pulled straight from hw and study guide. Easy course if you review the homework.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The hw assignments are uploaded as weirdly structured pdfs so when you convert to word doc it is really annoying. BUT this class isn't that hard, he has a few extra credit questions and if  someone emails him about the class he will send his response to everyone. Attendance isn't mandatory but you get extra credit if you do. Tests look like hw.

Gave him a 3 just because the exams aren't tough, but Professor Cheng is really hard to understand, and always reads everything from the slides that are like 100 years old. Although we always appreciate the consistency he has with what he teaches. Nearly every homework and exam is almost the same as the last. He is a funny guy too, and respected.

He doesn't use Canvas so you basically don't know your grade till it's in the registrar. That said, the content is very easy and his other reviews are right. He's decent, but lectures are very boring. Go to class, though, since you get a ton of extra credit for going and sometimes he just works through HW problems in class!

Highly recommend taking this class with Professor Cheng! Very caring for his students. His exams are almost identical to the homework questions. I can't see anyone who goes to class regularly and does their homework every week not getting an A.

His lectures weren't useful, but the class itself wasn't hard. I learned mostly from google. He requires a selfie for attendance. He showed up late to most classes and both tests. The tests are exactly like the homework, sometimes the same problems. If you can do the homework, you'll get an A.

Having taken a few of Dr. Cheng's courses before and knowing the impressions of him beforehand, I can say that he seems to have improved over the years. His lectures are dry but cover interesting enough material to stay engaged.
The projects can be rough to start, but if you're interested in computer graphics, its worth sticking with it.

The lectures are dry and hard to follow at times. The attendance policy was bizarre, but attendance will allegedly count as extra credit. Homework is straight from the slides, tests are straight from the study guide. I can feasibly imagine somebody learning absolutely nothing and still getting an A.

Overall the class is pretty easy and exams are the exact same as the study guide. However, the attendance policy is ridiculous. Everyday you have to take a selfie with a code on the board to prove that you were in class. If you miss two classes you lose 5% of your grade.

Dude was caring, but cared too much. Attendance policy is awful, required a selfie in class with a code on the board. If you miss 2+ days, you automatically lose 5% of your grade which just encourages not showing up later. Otherwise cares about students' comprehension and is generally good. Not a difficult class.

Lectures were long and hard to follow. Im not convinced he fully understood the material himself. But the exams are basically the same as the homework and he gives you practice exams that are basically the same as the real exams. And the homework holds your hand through the problems so it was easy. Certainly wouldnt take him for a harder course.

I'm just gonna be honest this guy is a terrible lecturer probably top two worst I've ever had. However this is one of the easiest classes I've taken; the homework is straight from the slides with one or two things changed and the tests are the same as the homework with minimal change. Bad professor but an Easy A

Dr. Cheng should not be teaching classes anymore. Lectures aren't about conveying content, they are digressions into minor details only he finds important. This man could spend 75 minutes talking about why he thinks 2+2  5. He does not follow a textbook whatsoever, do not take him unless you want to suffer for 16 weeks.

Dry and boring lectures. Reads off of slides for the most part. He does try his best to engage with the class by asking questions. Sometimes goes on hilarious rants about unrelated topics. Strict attendance policy, miss 2 classes and you lose 5% of your grade. Somewhat helpful in person and via email, can be rude at times. Easy homeworks and exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: He is an interesting person but his lectures not. Homeworks and projects are difficult but he is not a tough grader. Easy A if you spend enough time on it.
Classes are completely PowerPoint based and lectured. Decently easy homework/tests. Harsh attendance policy and the two tests are worth 30 percent each.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Not bad. He's friendly, funny (his weird, off-topic rants can be pretty entertaining), and his slides are pretty extensive. Homework is a lot like lecture examples. Homework and exams are fill in the blank and leniently graded. Attendance policy is a little unnecessarily rough, though - not much here I couldn't learn from the slides online.

Attendance is mandatory and super Draconian -- miss two classes and you lose 5% from your grade. He rambles a lot and isn't a very good lecturer. He often goes on tangents he doesn't know anything about like finance or politics. The class isn't super difficult, but he makes it as dull as possible.

Dr. Cheng is not an amazing lecturer. Classes are optional, but I still attended to make sure I never missed anything. The classes generally got off topic and he would lose his train of thought frequently. The homework and tests are fairly easy as long as you read the powerpoints, book, and work with friends to catch tiny details might have missed.

Dr. Cheng is an excellent lecturer, he's very funny. Attendance is not mandatory but highly recommended as he works example problems on the board, which helps with homework. He has lots of useful materials on his course page, though it would be nice if the course used Canvas instead.
I hate this class, it shouldn't be required for CS majors

He spends the entire class facing the board writing notes, hardly ever taking a break for students to catch up or ask questions.  He grades the homework very hard, which caused me to get my first B ever (after having As in 125 credit hours).  He's usually late for class, and usually holds us over by 4 or 5 minutes, which is infuriating.  Avoid him.
Funny and informative. "Resurrection of China"
Very funny, kind of hard to understand with his accent but does explain the material well. Tests were very similar to the homework.
Good teacher. TA are great. Turn up the mic, get better mic. Give him a raise.

Professor Garrett is an amazing teacher. He teaches at a high level. If you want to cruise through school this class isn't for you. If you want to learn he will be the perfect professor for you. Meet with him regularly and build a relationship. Very understanding as well.

reviews.comment: Awesome guy! I wasn't enrolled in the class due to my current class schedule it was impossible to formally enroll. I asked to just come and watch to learn more about trading and markets and he was more than happy to share his time and the class with me. He just asked not to take a student's chair and find an empty space and come ready to learn!
Fantastic professor, extremely knowledgeable and helpful for a career in finance

In FIN 490 for trading we did nothing in class for all of our meetings and maybe had 5 assignments all semester.  One of the tests was based on a reading we never went over and did a stocktrak assignment all semester. Didn't learn much from this class but we had some good guest speakers
bro moves way too fast. He is really knowledgeable, but can't teach at all. You will be learning finance on your own. Practice problems and examples are exactly like the test.

He rushes through slides and spends most of class going over practice problems but just goes to the answer without explaining how to do the problem. Goes through lectures acting like we have years of finance experience. Luckily the exams aren't too difficult because he uses the exact same questions we go over in class. Take a different professor.

Great guy but poor professor. He has lots of experience and knows what he is talking about but does a poor job teaching it. The only reason I ended with an A is because the exams were scaled very heavily. Don't expect to learn much in this course. TA's are your only help but even they didn't know the material and always cancelled office hours.

Is a really great guy and seems to want people to succeed in his class. I believe he is new and is still learning how to teach. Got a lot better throughout the semester. He curves the exams if needed and rounds your final grade if you are close to the next letter grade. He was new so id give him some slack and will probably do better next semester.

lectures dont do anything and are not mandatory and you can't hear or understand him anyways. you're just paying to teach yourself. exams are hard and even harder to prepare for. if you don't do a bunch of work outside the class you will not do well.

I'm sure he's a great guy, but the way that his exam review was always was nothing like the exam is actually incredible. For each exam, I studied the material so hard expecting to get at least a b and walk away with a 45/100. Says to attend office hours but they are cancelled almost every day. Do not take this professor unless you want to fail.

Beware that you will be teaching yourself a majority of this course if you take this professor. He only reads off of the lecture slideshow, so the lectures aren't helpful and are boring. Most people ended up skipping the class and working on the content on their own time. Also averages are pretty low for most exams, so expect a decent curve.

FIN 300 is difficult, but if you work hard, you will do fine. My best tips: read the textbook and learn how to do the problems. You will have to teach yourself most of the material, but tests have a heavy curve. Prof. Garrett is super helpful 1 on 1 and will give you great insight if you want to pursue a career in finance.

You won't have to go to class because all lectures are streamed online. He teaches like you already know the material, so you will have to self-teach most things. Very math heavy, so do the provided practice problems when studying. Three exams, with an optional final exam.

Bad lecturer but improved over the semester so by the end he was better. Class is math intensive, but he gives plenty of practice problems. Much better to talk to in smaller setting and does care to help and explain.

If you take FIN300 with him, you don't even need to go to class. All the lectures are posted online, and the way he talks makes it much easier to see what he said and what we need to learn. He did provide a heavy curve for exams, so as long as you put in the effort to teach yourself, you will be fine.

FIN300 was not a difficult class topic wise, however the lectures were entirely useless resulting in 99% self teaching after lectures and before exams. By far my worst professor I have had at UK. only positive is that there is a replacement exam.

Lectures are useless, homework and reading assignments don't correlate to exams. had to teach myself everything I know regarding his material, the finance tutor helped but hardly accounted for the lack of teaching
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: FIN300 is not an easy class; however, Professor Garrett is very nice and helpful. I have learned that if you have the drive to succeed, he wants to help you succeed. The TA office hours were beneficial, as were his office hours. If you are struggling, Professor Garrett is reachable. He doesn't hesitate to prepare you for the corporate world.

Great guy to talk to, will help you when you ask for it. I personally liked this class and him as a professor. He does just read from the slides and is kinda quiet, but that's improved from the start of the semester. He goes over practice problems after the slides and ends class early almost every time.

Garrett's lectures are very boring and difficult to engage with. 4 exams and he drops the lowest which is nice.Exams can be difficult if not prepared but no trick questions or unfairness in the exam itself. He seems like a solid dude, never had to seek help but I imagine he would be helpful in a 1 on 1 setting.

This class is extremely difficult. The Prof. Garrett is extremely nice and cares about you especially if you go and talk to him. But he can't teach at all, super quiet, and there's no point in going to the classes, reads slides word for word and does not elaborate on how to do difficult questions. Don't take this professor if you have the option.

I am in his FIN 300 class this year and it truly is the hardest class I have EVER taken at UK. He does not speak clearly and has a very hard time with his microphone. He mumbles when he talks and it is very hard to understand anything he is saying. The Exams are completely different then in class problems. Nice guy, but doesn't know how to teach.

he is a very nice professor but teaches like you already know everything and have super hearing abilities because he is SO quiet and doesn't speak up. exams are very hard, he curves them a lot though.

If you are considering taking this course with this professor, be cautious. Lectures barely cover any material covered on exams. reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very knowledgeable, but explains things like you already have a full-time job on Wall Street. Also talks like he's in a classroom of 15 people. Also, a weed-out class now because Gatton thinks finance has become a joke of a major.

You need subtitles for Prof. Garrett, even though i'm pretty sure english is his first language, his voice is just hard to understand over the microphone. Absolutely no joy in his voice and he uses slideshows that aren't on canvas.

Lectures hardly cover enough material for an exam. Doesn't feel like he wants to even be there, and I don't think I had a class that didn't finish early. Largely up to yourself to learn the course through the TAs, or just self teaching.
Great professor, very clear about his expectations and willing to help if you ask him.

The policy recommendations feel impossible. Tough grader is an understatement. Besides that, the lectures are pretty interesting, and the quizzes/exams are relatively simple. Read the book.

The policy recommendation assignments are definitely the toughest part of his class. I liked that the weekly homework assignments weren't that difficult on top of them. Lots of lecturing by him, but I was mostly able to keep up with everything.

His grading is very harsh. I felt like I was putting a lot of work into my assignments and still getting bad grades. I do feel like his lectures were engaging, and the material is easy to retain as long as you're paying attention. Like others have said, he takes forever to grade. That's really all I've got to say that's bad. He's approachable, but maybe a little awkward sometimes. I learned a lot in the class.

reviews.comment: Way too difficult on policy recommendation assignments. You will submit pages that are 8-10 pages long with a heavy amount of research and still receive poor grades. He is a very tough grader. He has four policy recommendations that he is considerably strict on grading. However, there are plentiful extra credit opportunities, one of which is attendance. He is not the friendliest, but very knowledgeable.

He is very passionate about what he teaches, so the lectures are good. There are four 10-page policy assignments and two exams which he is very tough on grading. He takes forever to grade assignments/papers and doesn't give many comments about how to improve and what exactly he is looking for. Very knowledgeable, but also tough.

He respects students and tries his best in my opinion to get you to understand material and wants you to ask a lot of questions.This course was particularly difficult so make sure you read the textbook and practice math. He takes a long time to grade assignments. He came through for me grading wise so I must commend him and recommend.

MGT 391 Her grading was not REMOTELY transparent. I literally had no idea what my grade was all semester. She's a nice woman, a little weird, but nice. DO NOT TAKE HER !!!!

literally never responded to emails, so unhelpful if you actually need him. would not take his section again.

Didn't care about his students and was bad at articulating the material.

Dr. Gaynor is respectful, approachable, and willing to help. However, his teaching style isn't always effective. Be prepared to teach yourself much of the material, as topics move quickly and class time often isn't enough to fully understand everything.

I think he did an amazing job for his first semester at the university and first semester as a professor. I think his grading was fair and that the amount of work helped to pad the grades from exams.
