He explains most concepts pretty well and goes at a good pace. Exam material reflected the lectures well and the homework was never awfully time consuming. He also grades very fairly. Overall, if you take the time to study and practice the material, you will be fine.

Dr. Owen is a great professor and a nice guy. His lectures can move very quickly, but he is good at explaining content and if you have a question, he can usually answer it very clearly if you ask outside of class. The exams are tough, but he is very generous with partial credit. He's also pretty funny and clearly cares a lot for his students.

Professor Owen isn't bad, the class is just very hard and he has a lot to cover. Really great person and fun/upbeat teacher, but the timing of the class is so crammed that it's hard to actually learn without a lot of time spent outside.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Owens is okay. He teaches content in a confusing way. But if you go to him he is willing to work with you. As a professor hes average but tries to make orgo fun haha! But as a person I totally respect him and he is such a nice guy! Read the book bc thats helps a ton and try you best! Plus its on a 15 or grading scale :))
Loved his class. As long as you do the extra work he gives you, then you will be fine in his class

Dr.Owen was nice but he is irresponsible, He broke his leg by slipping on ice then he got bad subs for weeks. He then flooded unit 3 with reactions to the point where you did not know what to do. He was a mask-czar and if you don't read ahead you will not like it ALOT. Don't take him, he has no interest in students' future, he will not curve EVER.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Many people struggle with orgo but Dr. Owen helps. USE THE LEARNING OUTCOMES AND TEXTBOOK. If you want an A in orgo you can do it. Owen's lectures are helpful and easy to follow. He is nice and holds office hours. The best resource is the textbook! Seriously do all the practice problems and redo homework! Use guided notes as extra problems!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Owen was thorough, detail oriented and passionate the entire semester I had him. He answered emails promptly and really cared about his students. Chemistry in general sucks but it was made manageable by him.

I absolutely loved Dr. Owen! As someone who struggled with general chemistry, he made learning organic chemistry so much easier. He is so kind and is always willing to answer your questions if you need help. He gives plenty of time in class to ask questions and does lots of practice problems! Would highly recommend Dr. Owen as a professor!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: Absolutely would recommend taking Dr. Owen, especially if you think chemistry will be a challenging class for you because he goes through the material slowly and tries to make sure students understand. Very helpful and nice in office hours and has a great OneNote notes packet to use in lecture as well.

Owen is a good professor he's very nice but his lectures are pretty boring. I had a B in the class until I studied really hard for the final and pulled off an A. I suggest actually using the e book and doing the practice questions. They helped me much more than the sapling homeworks. You can click in and watch the lecture at home for attendence

Tons of dad jokes, super nice. Takes time to explain examples well and take questions, even though the lecture is huge. Makes his notes and help accessible. The class is sometimes hard to make yourself pay attention, but it's a chemistry lecture so you can't really expect anything else.

Dr. Owen makes the best of what hes got. CHE105 is a lot of tough and diverse content, but he does his best in making it as understandable as possible. His office hours are great and hell break down the concepts behind the curriculum in a way that youll understand. Great lecturer as well, but his voice can put you back to sleep in the morning
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Really sweet and kind guy, just chemistry isnt fun. Has a really strong southern accent, so hes a little hard to understand at times. He knows chemistry isnt peoples favorite but he really tries to get students involved but he makes a lot of Dad level jokes. He does respond to emails very fast and is helpful during office hours too.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: A great professor. His classes are live-streamed online so if you do not feel like getting out of bed you can participate in class through the video. Despite having a large lecture class, he walks around to ensure individuals understand the content. He takes a while to explain the content, and we were behind for one of the exams.

Dr. Owen is pretty great; he ensures everyone has time to answer the in-class polling questions and explains things pretty plainly. Just be sure to sit near the front, especially for morning classes, because his voice is softer and can make you tired. Also, he got us behind by a small amount for one of the exams... but it wasn't by a big amount.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Caring

reviews.comment: Dr. Owen was a great professor! If you attend lectures, and take the time to learn the material on the homework, you will be fine. Showing up, paying attention, and filling out the notes during class helps tremendously. Would highly recommend Dr. Owen.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures--LECTURE HEAVY--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Dr. Owen is an amazing professor for CHE 105! He explains concepts very thoroughly and makes sure to do plenty of practice on iClicker. He doesn't go very fast, which means sometimes he gets behind, but overall, he is able to cover all the material for the exams. The exams are fairly easy, so as long as you study you'll be fine.

Joshua is a wonderful professor. Textbook isn't necessary for the class, though it is optional. There's lots of homework every week, but it usually isn't that bad. The lectures are always enjoyable. He gets you pretty adequately equipped to face the exams.
He was a pretty good teacher for a tough class. If you go in to see him, it will make the tests much easier.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: I had him for organic 1 and he was fine in lecture but his tests really didn't reflect the notes or practice tests. He is really awkward in office hours so I didn't like going... If I had to take him again I wouldn't be mad but I wouldn't be overjoyed.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: If you have him when there are common hour exams with Steelman, I've heard he's fine. When he gives his own exams, he tends to put questions that are worth a lot, that were never covered in class. I had him for 105 too and enjoyed him, but if organic is not your thing. good luck.
Boring lectures.
Best Organic Professor at the University of Kentucky and makes Organic as easy as he is allowed too
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: He is AMAZING! he makes chemistry understandable and is always open for questions!

Attend lectures and you will do fine. This class is standardized so much, it is honestly not that difficult. Dr. Owen is a great professor, who happens to make a lot of corny chemistry jokes. He takes a lot of extra time to do examples in class, and help students visualize the material.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Owens to me is definitely one of the better chemistry professors at UK! He provides his students with a course pack that can be purchased at Johnny Prints which is extremely helpful and always provides lots of well-explained examples. He has a bit of quiet, monotone voice and falls a little behind schedule sometimes but was overall pretty good!

He is kind of a quiet speaker, which causes me to lose interest easily. If you pay attention, he explains things pretty well and draws pictures which helps. With any prof for chem 105, you'll have to teach yourself some material outside of class to really get it. He uses a course packet from johny print which I really like.

Prof Owen is great! I definitely recommend him. He can be a little behind schedule, but homework is always rescheduled accordingly. He's full of silly chem jokes, which helps to make the class more interesting. I would totally take him again.

I love prof Owen! Sitting in lecture listening to a professor read a slide is never truly entertaining, but he throws random jokes in there now and then and makes it tolerable. He likes to explain things so that the class is sure to understand them. I would definitely recommend choosing him for chem.
He is so montone and boring and continually uses football analogies. Not the worst chem teacher at UK, but not my favorite.

Chemistry can be difficult for people in general, but professor Owen is always sure to go into more detail for difficult content so students can preform better. The only fallback to this is that it sometimes results in his classes being behind more than others, which is can be annoying at times.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Good prof. Tends to be a little behind schedule, but not too bad. Super kind, and a little funny. Posts his notes after class, which is great. Easy class, especially if you study from the Tro textbook. Everything comes right from there.

He's a really good guy, bit quiet however. I have severe hearing loss and even though I sat at the very front I had a hard time hearing him. Not a very animated speaker, can get hard to pay attention to after a while. Other than that, very clear about what was being said.

I am writing this review only because of the other reviews about the final exam for Che 230. The exam was like he said it would be. I don't know how anyone counted points to add up otherwise, probably didn't know enough to know what was new vs old. Owens grades fairly and is clear about exam content. Jeez, people, just go to class and red the book.

Owens spends lots of time explaining things which leads us to fall behind easily, but it isn't the worst thing a professor could do. However, he blatantly told our class the final would be 150 points and 100 of the points would be cumulative and 50 points would cover new material. In reality about 30-40 points were cumulative. Don't trust him....

Dr. Owen is kind of quirky but it makes him a good lecturer and he is great at dumbing things down. However, he is a stickler for directions and the exams are written so if you're right but the answer isn't in the box it will be counted incorrect. If you read your text, go to class, do the practice problems, and seek help you will excel.

Owen explains things well, often gives easy ways to remember concepts through cute acronyms.  I was not happy that he presented new material on the day before each test, especially before the final.  Also, it felt like he sped through the last three chapters.  I wish the course had been more evenly paced.  Sapling homework sucks.

Dr. Owen takes the time to explain concepts of organic chemistry. You can't memorize your way through this course. However, he ends up going a little slower than normal and has to pick up the pace at the end of the year. Exams are very fair. As long as you go to class and practice the problems in the book, you should get an A.

Definitely go to every class. I would also recommend taking CHE 297 the recitation class. You have to work hard for a good grade, but he takes the time to explain things to you. Take Owen if you can! A lot of times he'll stay after class to answer questions and allow people to ask questions in his office when it's not his office hours.

It's organic. It's hard. Owen makes it bearable and even fun. He's clear, well-paced,  and has a gift for teaching. He's adorable and funny. You'll love his quiet country accent as he explains, "Hydrogen is a lot like me, you know, it's weak, can't pull as hard as chlorine..." You'll never forget his wacky metaphors that help you understand.
You will likely get a good grade if you study hard and get the textbook early

He is very willing to help with various office hours, help sessions,  and will answer to his best ability question raised in class. He provides additional help videos. He goes along with the book. Reading it will always be your best bet and do as many practice problems. Partial credit available. No curves but class grading scale and A was 100- 85.

Dr. Owen is honestly one of the best professors I have ever had. Period. He goes out of his way to make sure that you know the content and is willing to help whenever he can. I would not have done well in the class if it wasn't for him. Still you will have to put in a lot of work to get a good grade. Only gave a 3 for Easiness because it is Organic.

Dr. Owen is somewhat of a rambler during lectures. He gets through what he needs to and does examples forever. He sometimes will bring up something while doing an example but he mumbles it and says "well that's not important" and keeps going. Overall, he's pretty good. You'll live on partial credit on his tests
CHE 105 was tough for me because I'd never had chemistry before. Owens is extremely helpful in class and gives lot of examples. As long as you study hard for this class you should be fine.

Dr. Owen is super nice, don't get me wrong. He just has a hard time making his point and is really notorious for falling behind on schedule. He covered material for exams the morning before them. That was unacceptable. If you stay on top of things, you can get an A. Just don't expect a high one.
So so nice and, very interested in chemistry and tried to make it as easy to understand as he could but was often flustered and made mistakes on example problems.

He's a little out there when it comes to stories and analogies he makes and he definitely gets flustered when people start moving around near the end of class but overall he understands what he's teaching and tries to make it as clear as possible, although sometimes it may not seem that way.

He is such a helpful teacher! He introduced concepts so smoothly that it was easy to go back, read the textbook and immediately be familiar with the material covered. Practice all the old exams on the organic chemistry website, the suggested problems on his syllabus and read the textbook well to get good grades on his exams.

Dr. Owen is a great guy and extremely helpful when approached. That being said, his lectures are sort of all over the place and you are wasting your time trying to take notes. The class is difficult but that should be expected for organic.
It seems sometimes that he just has no idea what he's doing, his analogies are just awful. His lectures are  of little use but he's genuinely caring.

Great teacher! I really enjoyed his chemistry lecture. It's important to go to class and time manage well for any Chemistry course. There is a lot of work and memorization, but if you work hard and attend lecture, the class isn't difficult at all. He made things easy to understand and was always willing to answer questions. We also laughed a lot :)

He is a really really nice guy but I just didn't understand his lectures, they didn't really help me in chemistry. I basically taught myself... he is new but still...not beneficial if you've never taken chemistry.

I dont think its Josh's fault. He tries hard to teach and reach everyone, but the truth is that you pretty much have to teach yourself. This course should be called "Time management 600", because the amount of sheer memorization and the girth of homework assignments under the frustratingly picky web-based system leaves you with nothing to spare.
He is a wonderful TA.  He's so helpful; though I think I drove him crazy with all my questions.  He's so adorable too!

She responds to emails and is present on some lab days. Getting a good TA is super important just like gen chem. The class itself is super easy if you put in effort and work with others. Almost everything is graded for completion and understanding, not accuracy. Final is definitely harder than CHE 231, just try to not lose points during semester.
She is amazing and understanding. Your TA makes or breaks the course just like the gen chem labs.

This is a breath of fresh air compared to Gen Chem labs, the postlabs only take an hour at most and the answers to both the pre and post labs are usually in the lecture slides on Canvas. The experiments themselves can be lengthy, but aren't hard, if you have a good TA. I did see Dr. Patwardhan once in lab and she seemed very sweet.

I have never seen her in person. The class is taught by TAs. You work alone in the lab, but if you get a good TA, it makes the class tolerable. The content is laid out pretty clear. You show up to lab, complete assignments, and do a post lab. The TA grades everything, so grading might be more harsh for some depending on what TA you have.

Just an average, dull math class. The material is boring, which isn't her fault, and recitation attendance is weighted as an exam. Does offer extra credit, not a phenomenal lecturer, but you'll be prepared for the exams, and she does give out multiple practice exams.
She is a very nice lady. Cancels class A LOT. I do not learn much in actually lectures, but learn a lot in recitation. Class is pretty easy.

She is nice and explains the material clearly and efficiently breaking down each step over and over with various problems which I find valuable in a math teacher. Sometimes her kids would be in class but they were not distracting they were cute. I loved how she gave us multiple practice exams that were EXACTLY the same format as the exams!

As someone who is not good at math Dr. Paullin made it very easy to learn new content and did a great job reinforcing the material. Her lectures were very easy to follow and she always did a good job reviewing different units.

Professor Paullin is a very good teacher. Her notes and lectures are very detailed and easy to learn. She's understanding and open to answering questions. The only reason I have this grade is because of missed quizzes and I didn't understand some material at the time. I recommend choosing her as a professor if you can, she's great!

Dr. Paullin is a great professor. I don't understand math easily, so I didn't particularly enjoy this class, but Dr. Paullin did not make me hate showing up. She's very kind and often stayed after class to help students with questions. Recommend!

Although she posts notes, it is really important you go to class to learn the material. Recitation is also very important. Tests get progressively harder so really try to do good on the first two exams.

Calc is hard all around and she can't change the way the department organizes the course but she does a good job communicating with students and explains problems clearly in lectures. I would definitely recommend her for MA 123!

Really nice lady. When she lectures she sometimes tends to write a little too much which can be confusing at times. This class is pretty hard but she helps by using days to go over homework and review for exams. Make sure you go to class if you want to pass. But overall good professor and very easy to approach if you need help.

I truly enjoyed MA123! That's coming from someone who isn't the best at math! I can tell that Dr. Paullin loves what she does, and wants others to love it too! She is caring, passionate, and very knowledgeable in the subject! She explains content well; shows what she's doing and how! I highly recommend her! She is beyond outstanding!

Paullin is a nice and cooperative professor. the material directly aligns with the homework which aligns with the tests. she gave many many many resources for help on homework/tests so i always felt very prepared. there is some amount of homework but it is spaced out well so its not overwhelming. overall a good pressor and good class!

Lectures are easy paced. Homework is much more difficult than what she teaches in class. Exams are your only shot at getting a good grade no matter how well you do on homework. DOES NOT RESPOND TO EMAILS. Ive read she responds fast but, she never responded to me all semester.

Shes a very nice teacher but the lectures dont go with the homework. The exams are pretty simple if you understood the material and you can do retakes if needed. Lots of homework but being a math class it makes since. She emails back very quickly and will answer any questions you have!

Professor Paullin was very understanding during this crazy semester. However, like many professors, I do not think she is great at teaching online. (Of course, this switch is not her fault.) It was really hard to grasp concepts through the recorded lectures and it was often that the knowledge checks didn't reflect the videos. Exams were difficult.

Paullin is a very nice lady and I do respect her, but her lectures and the hw do not correlate at all. Not only is there no point of going to class but the lectures are so dull down that there is practically no reason to pay attention in class when you could easily learn more by looking at the textbook (which is free btw). Don't take this class!

Professor Paullin is a very nice professional professor, but the way she presents the subject doesn't correlate to the homework that is assigned. Also, if you fail your first exam better just to drop out of the course because there isn't a lot you can do to redeem those points. Overall, I wouldn't take the class. My final rating is a: 4/10

Dr. Paullin is a really kind & intelligent woman. You can tell she has a lot of experience. However, the lectures often don't really help with the homework. If the content of this class is new to you, you will likely struggle on the HW. She offers lots of resources though. 3 exams, a final, participation & HW (hardly count) are the only grades.

If you listen and follow along with her lectures during class you should be able to pass. Online homework is always more difficult than what was learned in class and what will be on the exam but as long as you finish it you get credit for it. Exams are pretty easy and straight forward. Should not be difficult to pass this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Prof. Paullin is a god awful teacher. Her lectures do not correlate with the WebWork she assigns. She does the most basic level in class then our homework is senior level calculus. The only reason to attend class is for participation points, but honestly why even show up when she is wasting our time.
Paulin is not good at explaining content and makes it seem way harder than it needs to be. She only seems to care about sounding smarter than her students.

Professor Paullin has been really nice to students that take her class. The only complaint is that she goes over material too quick in lecture and the concern in the classroom is that there's not enough desk space. Other than that, the big lecture is great if I want to stay unnoticed. She only goes over the material but never gave any bookwork.

Her examples in class are very clear and make sense, but the homework is much harder so the lectures are not much help with that. She does not answer emails so if you really need something you should go see her in person. Theres not much to be graded on so you should make sure you have an A for homework and quizzes
Not the best math teacher but also not terrible. I felt this class was harder than it needed to be.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: really doesn't teach at all. going to class doesn't help. I have been going to the study in order to pass. the only reason I go is for attendance. DO NOT TAKE HER IF POSSIBLE.

Prof. Paullin isn't necessarily a bad teacher; it's the fact that she doesn't actually teach anything relevant in class that makes me give her a bad grade. I think I speak for many when I say she hasn't taught hardly anything that has shown up on the homework.
Class is not super interesting, but it is calculus. As long as you do all the homework, pay attention in class, and ask or help when you need it, you'll end the class with an A.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr. Paullin is great at explaining how to do problems in class, and what we go over is a reflection of the homework problems. STUDY FOR EXAM 3! It is the hardest of all the exams. Reef is done in class for participation and attendance. Homework almost every other night, not due till 8am of next class day.
Paulin is a very good teacher! she teaches slow and does alot of examples that are on the tests. four tests all are easy except exam #3. If you do your work you will get an A or a B.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: For someone who isn't good at math, this class is hard. In lecture, the problems aren't really explained, but are just copied down onto a projector to write into your notes. She usually gives you the reef answers to get your attendance points, but I would've done better in the class if the concepts and problems were explained better.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--TEST HEAVY--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Dr. Paullin is seriously the best teacher for math at UK. If you get the chance to take her do it---unless you hate going to class, are a d -bag who talks the whole time, or hates great lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Would take again

reviews.comment: Dr. Paullin is a very caring professor and her lectures are very helpful. If you go to class, take notes, and do the homework you will do fine on exams and the class. Lecture and recitations are required and attendance counts toward your grade. She also asks REEF/iclicker questions throughout her lecture but she basically always give you the answer
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: If you have a bad understanding of math like I do, then avoid her. Does not explain well at all. Doesn't explain her answers at all, just writes and writes.
Calculus is tough and so was this class. Study past exams because they are very similar. She takes attendance through Reef polling so you have to come to class.

This is a very basic math class that is an easy A if you pay attention in class and do your homework. The practice exams are also the same exact thing as the exam you take so do the last 2 she has online and you'll ace all the exams.

Paullin is such a sweetie!!! MA109 is extremely easy, but you have to go to lecture. You're allowed 5 skips, and she uses REEF for attendance. Overall, her examples are pretty clear cut, and if you review the old exams, you're guaranteed an A. I'll be taking her for calc!! Take her.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: While it is easy to skip class seeing as she posts all the notes online, attendance ends up mattering. Although the entire lecture is just copying notes which could be easily done on your own time, she is very kind to answer questions or explain further into detail during class.

Dr. Paullin is a very good choice for a math professor. She is knowledgable and explains things simply. I knew a lot of the material before entering this class, but she helped reinforce certain concepts just because of the way she explains them. Exams are incredibly easy.

She's super awesome, really helpful and she tries to explain everything.  She is really funny and realistic about people's understanding level and will answer any questions and explain it until you get it.

Hated this teacher, mostly because she didn't help me ever and when I asked her questions after class she acted like I was an idiot. My recitation teacher was even worse. I just did homework in the recitation because we did nothing but worksheets that count for nothing. Pointless class and even more pointless to have a recitation for it.
Dr. Paullin was a great professor. Calculus may suck but she makes it a little better. Study the old exams a day or two before the exam and you should get an A.

She's such a sweetie. If you go to her for help she'll help you. Texts and quizzes aren't hard and she uses clickers for attendance and participation points but she's not too strict at all. I would definitely take her again. Her clearness isn't always on but if you ask enough questions she'll try to answer them

Pretty clear cut information. Homework is all assigned at the beginning of the semester, so you always know when it's due, but the date may be moved back sometimes. All homework is online. Past exams are online and they're super helpful. I studied them really well and ended up doing well on exams.
You won't regret taking her as a teacher, and the exams are pretty easy if you study past exams

I freaking loved having Professor Paullin in class! I sat in the front row and she talked to us pretty often and she's actually really funny if you do get a chance to talk with her! She teaches so clearly that she only has to go over it once. If she does not teach something, she tells you to goto the study and it works out. She makes everyone laugh

The class itself is hard, but his notes are extremely clear and he will always stop to answer any questions. The class is very homework heavy but he grades leniently and gives good feedback. I even submitted some homeworks in late but emailed him and received full credit. But... no notes or material are uploaded to canvas so taking notes is a must.

The best professors I have ever known to teach Linear Algebra. He is very good at understanding students and focuses more on how the student should study so that if they apply in other courses too then it will be helpful. Amazing teacher.

Dr. Ye is a very nice professor. He is very easy to understand and explains concepts in class very well. Class consists of going over a theorem for 15-20 minutes, and then examples the remainder. Sometimes he gets excited and makes mistakes, but he is very passionate about his job and cares for students.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Ye is completely fluent in English - he has a slight accent, but it's a nonissue. He gives good lectures and thoroughly answers any questions students have. Homework can be tricky and is time consuming, but fair. Exams are fairly straightforward, though not easy. Dr. Ye is very accessible outside of class and is super nice and helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Prof Ye slightly difficult to understand at beginning but if you pay attention you can clear his subject. His assignments are simple programs based on lectures. Sometimes he is not fluent in English, but you can approach him during office hours. Many feel his midterm and finals are tough and lengthy but I found it easy, depends on how you study.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Group projects--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Prof. Ye is one of the good teachers in the department. Any failure to "understand him" can only refer to the material. He's been in North America since grad school and exceeds many native speakers in fluency.

Don't let anyone else misguide you - his English is very good.  He can speak off-script, unlike many foreign professors.  Tests are a lot of problems to do in 50 minutes.  The difference between an A and a B on each test is whether you can do a 10-point derivation question at the very end so be ready for that.  Do the homework.

Dr. Ye gives good notes during his lectures and plenty of examples, but he doesn't usually do problems exactly like the homework, so you actually have to understand the material for those assignments. The class was very consistent throughout the semester. Like most other calculus classes, you really get out of the class what you put into it.

very hard course, very hard to understand due to he like skip step of prove on class, But, his homework will cover what he skip. Strongly Recommend no to take his course, othwise you will regret to take a useless course!

He speaks very good english so don't be turned off by his name. The class itself is difficult but I would say he teaches it as good as anyone else could. For this class getting a good TA is more important than worrying about how good the professor is.

Very hard to understand. Knows the subject very very well but will skip steps in his example. If you skip steps on the exam you basically fail. Hard to understand sometimes. Exams are graded very hard. If you miss a step in the beginning of the problem, no partial credit. Even if you get the right answer, if you don't show all you work it's -20 pts

Dr. Qin was good at explaining material and was very organized, but despite being accessible outside of class she was not accommodating, understanding, or flexible. She often rushed through lectures not leaving ample time to explain some concepts. Posted lecture notes but deliberately not until after homeworks were due where you would need them...

Lectures are pretty vague, wouldn't recommend taking unless you are fully capable of teaching some of the material to yourself. Super sweet lady though, always happy to help especially if you go to office hours. Lots of homework but tests are manageable and no quizzes.

Dr. Qin occasionally overcomplicates mathematic methods. She had a shaky start but gradually improved a bit. I found that with recitation and online supportive notes, I was able to get through with my decent background with calculus. If you don't have good fundamentals or struggle to teach yourself supporting topics, I would not recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I really liked this professor she did a great job preparing us for exams and she always had the highest averages as far as I know, she isn't great at explaining things when you ask a question but that's her only downside. The textbook is online and she mainly just picks problems from it to explain on the board
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Qin did a great job at teaching content during lectures with example problems, coding examples, and formulas. Canvas was very well set up with amazing lecture notes that outlined clearly what was done during each class. Attendance was taken during each class. Dr. Qin is passionate about this class and I would recommend taking it with her.

She goes through slides quickly, and still doesn't have enough time to complete some of them. She does a good job of showing equations, but rarely explains how or why they work. I had to resort to YouTube professors to help me understand the content, and they made it seem so much easier than how Qin teaches it.

Her lectures are fairly easy to follow provide you pay attention and make more of an attempt to engage with the material than simply following along and noting formulas. She grades fairly (if not slightly generously) on tough assignments and gives very reasonable exams. Super helpful outside of class and quick to respond to emails.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: I was a fantastic calculus student prior to this class. I understood how to do every problem before exam time, yet it was 10x harder than every problem when I took the exam. In lectures we got through two example problems at best. I got a 50% on my first exam that was because of my TA. I ended up dropping out because exams were worth 90% of class

I sent many emails about HW/projects and she responded promptly (sent at 12:00am and responded 12:17am). I learned from the book and used her examples from class to reinforce what I learned. You might not understand right away but use HW and you will succeed. Workload gets rough around project due dates but otherwise good. Review Q's=exam Q's.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: She always managed to make things more confusing when answering a question during lecture. I found the way she explains topics very difficult to understand. She spent time on the wrong topics, there was a 5 minute portion of one lecture was dedicated to learning how infinity was a "sideways eight". The way she teaches is of someone learning english
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dr Jing always came to class prepared, made sure if students had any questions, was always available during office hours. In order to succeed in this class, I read the relevant sections ahead of class, used her notes she posted, always attended class. If you want to learn, take her course, if u want an easy A, take someone easy haha :p

If you are not 1000% confident that you can teach math to yourself, do not take her classes. Lectures are confusing and hard to follow when she tries to explain something, and when she is working out equations on the projector she makes mistakes and her handwriting is hard to read. Tests are extremely hard and are worth the majority of your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Doesnt speak English. Reads lectures off a paper does not explain.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Do not take Professor Jing Qin if you have never taken an advanced-level Calculus course before. Rather, do not take Jing Qin if you do not know calculus like the back of your hand. Upon entering the class, Professor Qin expects for all students to have a strong background in this course. If you wish to maintain a good GPA, drop this course ASAP!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Good Luck. Can't teach and as a student you cannot understand her. Unbelievably difficult and not caring about the success of anyone except her own. Dropped after the first test to try to get a different professor next semester which is very uncommon for me. Typically an A student but there is no hope unless you ready understand the content.
Would incorrectly do examples on lectures.

Not that she doesn't explain anything... she complicates everything even more (even the easy concepts). Doesn't care that much about students. The most chaotic and unorganized canvas page in the world. I had to teach everything myself. Boring lectures. And either makes a lot of mistakes in PPT or writes in unreadable handwriting.

This professor is not a good instructor. I stopped going to her lectures because I couldn't understand what she was saying and her lectures were very confusing. I am fortunate to have a good TA to help me in this class or I would be completely lost. The tests that she gives are nothing like tests from previous years.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: She is the worst teacher. She is unable to teach the subject and I had a difficult time following her lectures. I asked her questions outside of class and she only managed to confuse me more than she did in lectures .

Messes up consistently in lectures, answers to questions are not clear and are usually wrong. Recitations are also mostly pointless bc half of them happen after the HW for that topic is already due. You are encouraged to watch the prerecorded lectures, as well as to attending 3 lectures per week. Example problems are much easier than exams or HW.
She knows the material well but not how to teach it. You will have to teach yourself all of the information or find a secondary source to learn :) lectures are pointless

Her lectures are often completely incorrect and she doesn't even catch it until we point it out. The tests are worth 60% of your grade and she doesn't even prepare us for the test well at all. She basically goes over the bare minimum and somehow still doesn't make it make sense. I'm completely teaching myself at this point.
Worst Professor Ever. Do not take unless you want to ruin your gpa. I took Calculus in high school and still didnt understand. She is rude and not understanding. Her lectures are often incorrect.

I wouldnt take her if you want to do well in this class. She doesnt seem to know what shes talking about and makes many mistakes in her lectures, causing more confusion. She does not prepare us well for exams. I am now teaching myself the material because it works better than her style of teaching. She can also be difficult to understand.

Tatro is an amazing teacher / person. He's passionate about teaching and truly cares about his students in the classroom--and beyond. Learned so much / loved him a lot that I stayed for FIN 490 alongside other students. We need more professors like him at UK.

This is probably the best professor at all of UK. He genuinely cares about his students, and you will probably learn more about real world application in this class than all of your other classes combined. If you have the chance definitely take him.
Best teacher ever. The negative review is a complete lie.
This is the best professor at UK hands down. You will probably learn more about Finance and the Stock Market in this class than you will your 4 years at UK.

Professor Perry is a absolutely amazing professor. If you can take his class please do, his lectures are nice and easy to understand, he's more then happy to help you out and understand anything, he also throws in a few jokes which can be funny.

A nice old school professor who loves teaching calculus with a nice dry sense of humor. He keeps things lively when working through tough subjects and says things like "now that I'm done yapping" and "zippers of death" which cracks me up. Encourages class participation a lot, sometimes getting volunteers to work out equations on the board.
I like him. He helped make the transition from Pre-Calculus to Calculus 1 feel pretty smooth.
The calculus GOAT.
Great professor. Provided great lectures with amazing slides which explain topics step by step. Office hours were good.

Everything you read here about Professor Perry is true. He is a great lecturer, makes concepts as simple as they can be, and drills them repeatedly in order to help reassure you on them. TAs are also excellent. For a Calc 1 Course he's your best bet.
Great at teaching, he's just a sweet old man with a doctorate in Physics but amazing with teaching Calc 1. 10/10
He was overall pretty good but I learned more in the recitation for the class than in lecture. Overall he's kinda mid not the best and not the worst.
Just do the homeworks and study old exams and pray. Go to office hours, he will help explain stuff.

Honestly I love Dr. Perry. He tries to make his lectures fun but it is often extremely hard to make math fun. My only complaint with Dr. Perry is the WeBWork, webwork is 1000 times harder than anything that we do in class or on the exams, and my homework grade was the lowest amongst the three.

Professor Perry is a great lecturer to an extent. He can drag on a bit and the slides he uses can be very confusing. He does not post his completed notes on Canvas so make sure to be in lecture. He is an amazing person though and truly cares about his students and wants people to enjoy the content.
Perry is a great guy who knows his stuff. He is very caring and will work with you if you need help with something. Lectures were well organized and slides posted on canvas.

Dr. Perry is a great professor. He has plenty of expertise and qualifications, and it shows. His lectures are detailed and he works out several example problems. He also follows the textbook so you can use that for extra help. He likes to crack jokes to lighten the mood and is generally goofy and lighthearted. Lectures can be heavy, but manageable.

Dr. Perry is one of the kindest professors I've had. He gave many chances to boost your grade with extra credit/make ups and his slides were excellent. Homework was proof heavy, but exams were very straightforward. I'm only giving a 4 instead of a 5 because of the COUNTLESS typos he'd make. It was funny at first, but got annoying pretty quick.

Dr. Perry is a great man and professor. He has been very helpful to me and I feel that he really cares about his students. Calc 3 was really hard for me and I did not do as well as I wanted, but it was not the professors fault. I would recommend taking Dr. Perry and attending his office hours especially after exams.

Prof. Perry was very compassionate through the altered coronavirus semester, and he was completely understanding of the strange circumstances. He gave an option for asynchronous or synchronous class. Very caring and flexible teacher, knows the content extremely well, very fast replies, and amazing at answering questions.

Awesome professor, however his lectures go blindingly fast. He has a powerpoint with all of the theorems and notes on it (small font size) and at the same time he is working examples on the board expecting you to copy all of it down. Be prepared to write fast and not understand anything in lecture. You must go back over the notes on your own.

Perry is the best calc 3 prof but only because the others are terrible. He is a good guy, but the class was hard and lectures not very helpful for me. Not enough examples, and the few examples we went over in class are easy compared to tests /HW. Go to mathskellar/the study for HW help. Study ALL practices exams but exams are not the same.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Peter Perry is the best calc 3 professor you can take. He always made class interesting with his hilarious personality and math jokes. Very easy to talk to in office hours. Seriously wants to help students. It was easy to get A's on exams because of cheat sheets. Homework was hard at times but he was always willing to help. Highly recommend!

Dr. Perry is a serious gem in the UK math department. I would take him for every math class if I could. The way he goes through subjects in calculus is some of the best teaching I have seen in my time at UK. If you have any problems in this class, he will try to personally help you to succeed because he really cares about his students!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: The best professor for MA 213. Friendly, energetic, explains well, clearly cares about the material and his students. Not too much homework though it often has a few very difficult problems.
While the class material itself is difficult, Dr. Perry makes it as understandable as Calculus can be. His lectures are very helpful so I highly recommend going to lecture.
Very funny, very caring, very prepared. Best math teacher I've encountered at UK including recitation teachers, TA's and student tutors.

PETER PERRY IS THE BEST PROFESSOR YOU WILL EVER HAVE AND HE DESERVES MORE THAN 4 STARS HE DESERVES THE WORLD. HE IS EXCITED ABOUT THE MATERIAL AND KNOWS IT LIKE THE BACK OF HIS HAND I HAVE HAD HIM FOR CALCS 1-3 AND HAVE THOROUGHLY ENJOYED MY LEARNING EXPERIENCE BECAUSE OF THIS MAN

Dr. Perry is great. He really knows calculus and tries to make his lectures very easy to follow. His lectures are all available on his website. Calc 2 is hard no matter what, but Dr. Perry made it better. Actually do the homework and study the past exams and you should be fine. He has plenty of office hours but lots of people like to go to his.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Dr. Perry is a great professor! Lectures, especially calculus lectures, can be boring, but he tries to make them fun. Hes also very sweet: he will always take time to help you if you ask! Very enthusiastic and truly cares about his students. Calc 2 is a very difficult class, but Perrys exams are very straightforward and he is a fair grader!
Professor Perry was one of the best math teachers I have ever had. He was very clear, and brought a lot of energy with him to class.

I am not a math person. Dr. Perry has made me so much more comfortable with math. Any question or concern I had was addressed. He truly listens and he truly cares. You will not be able to pass the class if you don't do the work, but if you are willing to try and ask for help, he is definitely there. I recommend him to anyone and everyone!

He is a really great professor, but his slides are riddled with mistakes. He highly encourages participation during class, and it helps you learn the material a lot better. Look at previous exams to understand question style, but don't put too much into them the tests change drastically from year to year. Beware the bug question.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Professor Perry is very likable and teaches so students understand topics, not just get past them on tests. He really made me like math concepts and helps break down complex theorems. However, he does go extremely fast at some points, and skimps on practice problems. If you work the problems in recitation, however,  this shouldn't be a problem.

I would not recommend Perry for MA113 (I cannot speak for other classes).  He is funny and a good teacher overall, but his lectures are not helpful in this class.  The issue is that he focuses on teaching you theorems and real math, but the problem is that the tests demand that you just learn how to do problems quickly and easily.

Dr. Perry grades tests extremely strictly. If you get a problem correct but don't do it his way, you will not receive credit. 80 percent of your grade is based on exams. He covers complicated topics too fast in lectures and assumes everybody already knows how to do them. He rarely works out example problems and instead spends the time on theorems.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Peter Perry is a very unique professor; not in a good way. He spends too much time theorizing rather than actually going over the problems. His way of teaching is catered to those who already know what they are doing and absolutely love math. His lectures will make you cringe when he tries to add out of place humor. Tests must be done HIS way only.

2 MAJOR issues with Perry's teaching skills: 1. His lectures are proof-heavy. He spends maybe 5 minutes on how to do a problem, and 40 on the math behind why it works. Switch that ratio and class might be good. 2. His grading on exams is subjective. You are expected to do problems a specific way, though often those ways are not specified at all.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Everyone gives Perry good reviews because he tries to be funny but his lectures are terrible and now that they changed the whole math department you can't really prepare for tests that well. Do the practice exams, not the old exams. He's incredibly degrading when you talk to him one-on-one but the rest of the Calc 3 professors are much worse.

Goes on vacation for two weeks during one unit and not review the day of the test. However, he preaches "You are paying me to be here."  Plan on waiting 45 mins in line for office hours. When you finally get to talk to him he will put you down for using the term math incorrectly instead of helping you. Great guy. Every other calc 3 prof sucks more.

Everyone loves Perry because of his jokes but you learn the most in recitation. There are very few examples worked in class and he is not very helpful when questions are asked. Just get through the class and you'll be okay.

Awesome awesome guy. He's a total math nerd and he's very passionate about the subject he's teaching.  He's always available and has good office hours if you need help.  Subject matter is obviously a little difficult so that what makes the class hard.  He writes his own tests and always lets you use a cheat sheet, even for the final!

Easily the best professor I've had. He teaches the applications of the material as well as principles. He also really cares about the students and brings a lot of energy to class. We have 1 blackboard on each side of the room that not everyone can see, so he runs back and forth across the room working out problems on both boards at the same time.

Peter Perry: the man, the hero, the legend. He's the sole reason I'm getting a math minor. Lectures are engaging and the perfect balance between theory and application. In fact, I had him for MA 114 last year and chose to completely scrap and rework this semester's schedule in order to take him for calc 3. If you ever have the choice, choose Perry.
Probably the hands-down best professor I've ever had.

Mr. Perry is seriously the best teacher. I entered ma 213 as a hesitant freshman,  but after just a few classes with him i've never felt more confident in my decision. He's really enthusiastic about math and creating an equal opportunity for all his students. He's the guy to have for calc 3

What can I say about Dr Peter Perry in 350 characters or less? Dr (Simon) Peter Perry is the rock upon which I build my calculus knowledge. He genuinely cares about your knowledge of calculus. Does he throw the occasional chocolate into the audience to explain 3 dimensional motion? You bet. I would become a math major for this man.

I've taken Dr. Perry for both MA 113 and 114 and he is by far the best professor I've ever had. Calculus is required for you more than likely, and Perry is the man you want. He keeps lecture lively, and explains the concepts very thoroughly. He is also more than willing to help during office hours however class will usually suffice.

Dr. Perry is extremely passionate about his profession and his students success. If you need outside help, he WILL help you. His lectures are relaxed. Challenging, but class will cover everything you need to know. The process is as important as the final answer for tests, so seeing how he  works problems is a major help. Definitely take his section
As much as I don't like math he makes class very interesting. He provides lots of examples and help if you seek assistance.
One of the best professors I've ever had. It's very beneficial to attend lecture, and tests reflect lecture material. Take him!!
Best math teacher I have had to date.  I had him for 113 and liked him so much I took a CS night class to make room on my schedule so I could have Perry for 114.  He is the man.
Dr. Perry is great; take his section if you have the option.
I liked that he explained why we went about answering problems the way we did instead of just saying this is how it is.

I never actually had Dr. Perry as a professor. I had Dr. Readdy for MA 213. I went to his lectures when Readdy's didn't make sense. I soon learned to rely on Dr. Perry's lectures to clear up the confusion created by Readdy. Wish I would have taken his section.

Peter Perry is by far the best mathematics teacher I have ever had. He loves to come into class and teach everyday. He teaches all the material clearly and lets you know exactly how you need to put it on the test. Take his class.

On my first day of class I approached Dr. Perry and told him of some dates I would not be able to attend.  He bought me coffee and went through everything I would be missing on those dates.  He is an invaluable asset to the university.
Peter Perry is super energetic and always stops along the way for ANY questions. I loved this class.

Calculus is easy to me, but I still think the way he teaches is great.  He very obviously loves what he's doing, stops to see if anyone has questions, and is very approachable.  If you just copy the notes during class and spend about 30-45 minutes on homework, you'll be prepared for the quizzes and tests.  (Maybe longer if you struggle with math.)

Excellent teacher, and grades easily as long as you know what you are doing.  I got an A in the course without ever doing the practice HW problems.  I also learned everything I was supposed to, just from notes from lecture. Best math teacher I've ever had, take this guy.

Class seems easy at first, and you can get really good grades on quizzes and such, but if you do not show every single step exactly the way it was taught on the test you are SOL as I am.  If you get the right answer without showing all the work, you should get at least half.  Not so here.
This guy is so excited to be teaching math, its great.  Sure, you probably do not share his joy in taking derivatives, but he is a solid teacher, and he really wants people to do well in his class.
This was one of my favorite classes because he made lectures interesting and made me excited to learn which isn't normal for most classes.

Clint is so relaxed and lectures are more of a class conversation than lecturing. He is by far the best prof Ive had at UK. Take this class even if its just for an elective! When I took it we only met once a week for 2 hours but he usually let us out a little early.

Best class I've had at UK.  Quarles is funny, super smart, and teaches things that actually relate to real life.  Some occasional reading/notes for exams but no book needed.  Also be ready to get called out - everyone participates
Quarles is the coolest teacher at UK. Be prepared to get ragged on a bit but, class is so great
Dr. Qualls is exceptional. Quality teaching and communicating skills. Words do little justice to encompass the totality of an experience. Definitely. recommend

So the course was Intro Computer Science using Python. He was an awesome professor that is really down to earth about everything. Hes also really chill about his teaching style and general demeanor. The man showed up on the first day without shoes on. 13/10 would take again

I had him for computer science. Terrible teacher but cool guy. He didn't teach the content that was on the test. Told us final would be cumulative, it wasn't. I think he would be an okay professor if he was teaching in his field.
amazing
He is amazing! The best class I have taken!!!!

Dr Qualls is an amazing professor. He is super good at explaining things, and sometimes gives us extra interesting physics trivia. He's always nice and willing to answer questions, while making sure the student is relaxed. I didn't like EM before, but thanks to him I'm starting to like and enjoy it. You really should take class with him!

Dr. Qualls was really, really willing to meet with students and answer questions. He would always answer emails, he scheduled extra test review sessions, and he worked to make sure everybody understood everything. Plus, he was just COOL.

Dr. Qualls is probably one of the best professors I have had during my four years here at U.K. Not only is he very helpful if you reach out to him but he truly cares about students and loves teaching. I pity anyone that has to take PHY211 with anyone else, I'm sorry your professor won't be as amazing as mine.

Dr. Qualls kept class fun and interesting while making sure we actually learned the material. Easily the best teacher I've had so far in my college career. He was very helpful and usually available to answer questions. Really cared about students and went above and beyond to ensure their success.

Professor Rothgeb challenges his students to think outside the box and be creative. Good feedback is given during critiques. During office hours he is available and willing to talk with students. One of the best professors in the design school.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Mr. Rothgeb had favorite students, I was not one.  Those who kissed up to him, did things his way got A's, if not, he did not like you or your design.  He was mean and conceited.  During a trajic time he could have let me drop or fail, he gave me the F.  I will never forget this about him.  I was devoted and worked hard, just didn't kiss up.
Makes you think and work. Design is an intellectual and interactive field and he makes you do just that. Can be aggravating at times, but always manages to pull the best design out of you.
i just love mr. rothgeb! he is a cute little old man and funny too. he always gives good feedback on projects. very helpful. i recommend whoever is in interior design to get him as the professor

I love Terry!  He is so funny!  He does say "and so forth" a lot, but that's what makes him Terry.  Class is always laid back and really fun.  I spend 2 hours and 50 minutes every Monday, Wednesday, and Friday with him and I don't mind a bit!
Mr. Rothgeb is really funny and helpful. Also, we all loved the way he smelled! Hahaha...but he really knows his stuff and is a cute little old man so take him!

He's been at UK forEVER, but still great!  He's funny, or at least HE thinkgs he is, so laugh at his stupid jokes and score good karma points.  ;)  He's a good guy and gives you hints at how he'll grade things, so keep a good ear.  Look at him when he speaks, because otherwise you won't be able to understand him, lol!  Nice guy though!

He made getting an A in a daunting class attainable. He is pretty nice with the partial credit but he doesn't just give out good grades. You have to put a good amount of time in to do well but you will come out better for it. Love this guy!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Grading was harsh and expectations for projects were unclear. There was little guidance given, which made assignments frustrating to complete. Examples in class didn't always match the difficulty of homework, and grading felt inconsistent. He did allow exam corrections, but overall the class was unnecessarily difficult due to lack of direction.

I enjoyed professor Halls class. His lectures were a good mix of content and example problems. The homework can be challenging but the exams feel easier. Hall wants to see students succeed and be able to think like engineers. He made this class so much easier than I expected it to be.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Probably the best professor for statics. depending on the content, homework could take a long time but was designed to be much harder than the exams, making the exams feel extremely easy if you did the homework. Attendance was not mandatory but he offered an up to 2% grade bump if you attended all the classes. Hall is my goat

This professor made what I thought would be a miserable class pretty tolerable. Homework was probably the most difficult thing, where I would put in at least 8 hours a week outside of lecture. Besides that, exams were almost easier than the homework (in my opinion). Just remember to care in lecture, and put in some hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Someone said, "the worst kind of villains are the ones who say they do things for your own good," and Dr. Hall embodies that to his core. The lectures are good, but his homeworks take entirely too long (15-20 hours each) and that's why all my friends dropped the class. In office hours, he just told me things I already knew and didn't really help.

I have tried taking EM 221 with another professor at UKY and had a tough time in the class. Professor Hall was amazing! His lectures were straightforward, and he taught us as if we hadn't learned it prior. He highly encouraged questions and never made students feel less than for any question. I feel like I have a great understanding of statics now!
Statics is a hard class in general, and he does a good job teaching. If you can do the homework the exam should be light work
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class is just so difficult, and the homework took 5 hours every time for me to just get at most a 60%. He is a very good professor and is willing to help you understand the subject. Tests were also very hard!

The difficulty is not due to the professor just the class. He was very clear what you needed to understand, though the exams were very difficult. Averages for the exams were 52 and a 49, there was no curve, but it is an engineering weed out class. The workload was a lot, but the homework was very difficult. He was GREAT, Statics just sucks.
I absolutely loved her; she can be difficult and pesky, but I believe it is all for your benefit. If you show up, pay attention, and be intentional with your studying you will be successful
I really enjoyed her and her class, she gives all your materials needed to do well and makes it clear what is tested. It is a significant amount of content, but I liked how organized it was.

This course was pretty content heavy, although it didn't have to be. The things taught in class seemed like such easy topics but Dr. Aaron made them super complicated. I Don't think this is the worst class to take, but it is certainly challenging. BE PREPARED TO STUDY EARLY FOR EXAMS! Make sure to get on her good side.
There is a lot of material, but if you show up to the lectures and study you will do good. She taught me a lot and I really enjoyed the class.

as hard as this class was, i am glad i had her as a professor. very clear on what she expects from students on tests (esp. definitions) & will constantly remind you of important things to note. don't expect to get a quick response from emails though; she doesn't have set office hours. also, don't write notes DURING class, she'll go fast.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Clear grading criteria--So many papers

reviews.comment: Dr. Aaron is a great professor for animal science. Some students don't like her teaching style because she is paper only and no canvas. She is a tough grader and teaches a lot of material. However, she does care about her students if you actively participate and she will help you if you need it. I recommend Dr. Aaron but be prepared to study.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr. Aaron is possibly one of the most charismatic professors I have ever had. She does not let people just slide by, you have to put in work in her class. If you always do the assignments you should be set for exams, shes a tough grader but its because she really wants you to understand the material. I stop by her office anytime I have questions!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: I have never studied as much for an exam as I did for Dr. Aaron's final. Don't expect to breeze through this class, but she is a good, fun professor and will give fair exams. GO TO CLASS. There are little "quizzes" at the beginning, a right answer gets extra credit, a wrong answer is neutral, not turning it in gets 5 points off your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: While Dr. Aaron can be a hard professor, she genuinely cares for her students and wants everyone to do the best they can. She does not give out As to everyone, but doesn't make it impossible with a little work. A little bit old-school in her style of teaching, but always offers a practical approach for the information taught.

Dr. Aaron was possibly the worst professor I've ever had. Was never available to meet outside class, had no clear idea of what would be on exams and two binders full to study from. She was rude and condescending, but had plenty of time for her favorite students (who did well in the class). There was tons of homework which was severely graded.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: Dr. Aaron is not an easy professor to listen to. She sounds condescending and often times words things in a confusing manner. She grades hard and is extremely nit picky when it comes to homework and in class assignments. She gives a lot of handouts but reads off of her slides that you never get because she doesnt use canvas.
I really liked her and the class.

Dr. Aaron expects students to do their part, however, she is very willing to help if you don't understand a concept. She was new to teaching the class a couple years ago, but I think she is figuring out the better way to do things. Only bad part is MWF at 8:00am and takes attendance.

Has extremely long exams that almost entirely consist of long math problems and short answer.  Exams lasted 2 hours  every time for my class, were 12 pages long and they were extremely hard.  She gives out tons of packets and sheets that it is hard to  keep everything organized.  She also grades very hard. I do not recommend taking her.
Great professor. Very clear and interesting
So unclear on homework assignments, never know what half of the questions are asking me to find.
I should not have taken this course. I find it a waste of time and energy.

I agree with most of the other students. she spends most of the time teaching sta basics and totally forget to teach you SAS. If you go to that class get some Adderall you will need a lot of memory for all the material and formulas that she gives.
She spends so much time on the useless basics that she doesn't have time to cover the useful material
The worst teacher I have ever had....

I believe Statistics 570 is a 100% waste of time; not in the sense of subject but in the manner the material is presented.  If you are interested in learning statistics and a statistical analysis program (This course tries to teach SAS), then take another course on the main campus.  This class's "Lab" needs to be thought in a computer lab but isn't

I had a LOT of prior knowledge before taking this class, but I still managed to learn.  She occasionally teaches the wrong material, but pretty good for the most part. She also thinks she's incredibly funny.

Class was amazing and interesting. He doesn't want you to give perfect answers just honest and insightful ones. Assignments are not hard but do require intentional thought. He really wants to see you go above and beyond. Great Professor who does genuinely care about the success and well-being of his students.

Dr. Voogt is for sure one of the best professors I've had at UK! He's understanding and a great instructor. He shows a lot of care for his students as people and his lectures were always interesting to me. If you have the option to take him, I say you should. The workload was very light and even then he was quite lenient with deadlines. He's great.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Take him, he is so easy. You actually have to pay attention in class, and he will randomly call on you, but a great guy. Always understanding if you didn't do the homework.

Was an amazing professor and actually cared for his students! He knew all of our names and asked about our days and how things were going on the regular. Super relaxed grading, and we have less work in this honors 140 than in other honors 140. You do have to participate and share your thoughts, but all honors classes are like that.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: Dr Voogt was a great professor! His class was very engaging, my only complaint is having to read the passages before class and since this class is so chill I most of the time forget to read before class. The class was very interesting though and your grade is based off of your realization about yourself and being able to communicate your ideas.

There's nothing else to say about Dr. Voogt that everyone else hasn't said; Dr. Voogt is a fantastic professor in every aspect. If you are a freshmen reading this and you are taking Voogt for HON140, or any class for that matter, know that you are in good hands.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I loved Dr. Voogt. He led good discussions in class and is great about keeping the class interested in the work and does a good job showing that he cares about his students. I would take him again for another honors class. His class is participation & paper heavy but it isn't too hard if you do the readings. Would recommend.

Dr. Voogt is truly one of the best professors I've ever had. He knew every students' name, major, and hometown by the second week of classes. I felt very comfortable speaking up in the class and thought his discussions were very interesting. Definitely recommend!!!
Definitely take his classes! Cares about students and wants to see you do well. Could not say anything negative about him!

There is a lot of reading that has to be done before classes because he will pick people to talk about it. His lectures can drag on but as long as you are paying attention and get the main points you will do fine. The majority of the projects and assignments are opinion based. Your participation in class is for a grade and he will call you out.

Cannot say enough good things about him - I have now taken two of his classes and wish I could take more. Genuinely one of the deepest thinkers I have ever met, very understanding and kind, cares about his students, and all around a terrific professor. There is always a reading to prepare for class which gets frustrating, though. Tough grader.

I took this course for my minor, and honestly, it was one of the best courses I have taken while at UK. He kept the class interesting even while delving into frankly boring topics and cared a lot about how his students were doing. If I could take this class over again, i would just due to how amazing of a prof he is. Take his classes!!

Dr. Voogt is the best professor the Honors College has to offer! He is incredibly knowledgable in his field and really WANTS to share the information with you out of genuine interest and care. He is incredibly understanding and helpful + wants to see his students succeed. He sees students as people first and is overall a great person/professor.
I loved Dr. Voogt and would take his class again! He is very caring and knowledgeable. As long as you try, you can get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Get ready to read because before every class there is a reading assignment that has to be completed. He is a good professor though that I feel actually does care about his students. There are lots of papers for this class. And you HAVE to participate in the lectures or else you will get a bad grade. Speak up, he actually wants to hear your voice.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--So many papers

reviews.comment: Dr. Voogt was okay, the lectures were typically interesting however his sections of HON 140 include quite a lot of reading and writing papers. Even still, I would recommend him, especially if you're looking to get a lot out of this course!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: If you have the opportunity to take any of his classes, do it. He is by far the best professor I have ever had, and I hope for the opportunity to take his classes again. Some of the subjects are pretty deep, but he does it in such a caring way. He reaches out to students on a personal level, and is very helpful as not only a professor, but a human.

Dr.Voogt was very invested in the discussion and graded more based on participation. He is a relatively tough grader and it is easy to get confused on the wording, so ask questions! It is very easy to slack off in this class, so make sure you are coming to class and participating if you want that A. Overall very understanding and respectable.

Dr. Voogt leaves detailed feedback on papers and really cares about his students. We got into some pretty philosophical and heavy topics, but he handled them with care. He sometimes throws in some corny dad jokes which can be funny. The class challenged my thinking and perspective, despite being tedious at times.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: If you have the chance to take Holocaust with Dr. Voogt- do it. Best class I've ever taken. Voogt handled a atrociously difficult subject with incredible grace and empathy. He truly values student input and fostered a seriously kind and helpful learning environment. Learned so much from him in this class, even as a non-history major. Truly a 10/10.

I took the Holocaust course which was super interesting and disturbing. The grade is based on 4 papers, 3 quizzes, and participation in class. There are heavy readings every night, including reading two entire books and the majority of a third. However, these books are interesting and highly relevant to class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Good lecturer, very intelligent, although some lectures can be difficult to understand.

Dr. Voogt is passionate about all the content he teaches. He is a funny and down-to-earth professor. Never had an issue with him, although other students did regarding his workload. His HON 151 requires way more reading than necessary. An awesome, personable professor.

Dr. Voogt has been one of my favorite professors at UK! I took both HON 301 on Marxism and HIS 323 on the Holocaust. In HON 301, we read a lot for the class but it was typically really interesting. We did group projects, however, they weren't difficult and we all learned from those projects. Very funny and kind guy, creates a welcoming classroom.
Dr. Voogt is one of the best professors I’ve ever had at UK. He cares so much about his students and is very knowledgeable in his subject areas. Would highly recommend taking a Dr. Voogt class
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Voogt is a super nice person. I highly recommend him for Hon 140. He encouraged thinking about things from multiple different sides and always left thought-out feedback on papers. Participation in discussions is necessary, but he is very lax about things. From what I've heard of other Hon 140 professors, the workload is pretty much the same.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Very much discussion based & participation matters- readings were SO interesting though. Course covered a very heavy subject matter and Dr. Voogt dealt with it well, overall my favorite class I have taken so far in college.

He's not bad but there are other better HON101 professors. Lots of reading and expects you to participate A LOT in class (participation is v important). Sometimes he liked my submissions, sometimes he hated them
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Tough grader
