reviews.comment: I really enjoyed this class. I had to take it for core and found it to be relatively easy. You have to read quite a bit, but I you do it makes the reflection papers cake. Dr. King is pretty relaxed and really likes when people attend office hours. Highly recommend.

Dr. King is a very engaging teacher. The class is not hard but you have to go to lecture. I definitely recommend ANT160 to fulfill your core requirements if you want an easy class! There is rarely work besides reading and small reflection papers. The tests are a breeze and can be done in less than 15 minutes.
Worst professor at UK, also the TA's are absolutely horrible when it comes to grading.

Lectures are boring. She gets off topic and talks about herself quite often. Her tests seem easy, but she uses a lot of trick questions. You have to have her clarify what she means. It's important to have a good TA. She has a really weird grading system. She's not terrible, but I would not recommend.
Dr. King is a harsh grader on tests as well as papers. She asks tricky questions and takes off points for petty things. If you can stay away, do.

There is no actual textbook (which is nice), but she expects you to read different books based off other Anthropologists accounts. They can be really interesting! The class only offers 100 points so every tenth of a point matter. The tests are fairly easy, but you have to go to class and take notes to know whats going on.

Read the books! Her lectures can get a little long winded when she talks about her own research. Very nice and helpful. Knows this topic well. Do the readings and you'll be fine. Tough grader on papers.

I took Cultural Anthro just to see what it was like and I really enjoyed the class and her teaching style. I hardly ever read the text book and did fine on exams. BUT you have to read the two ethnographies to do well on the exams. If you go to class and stay open minded, you will do well.

Dr. King spends almost the entire lecture talking about herself and her fieldwork. At first, it was interesting but now I really wish I had a different professor. Dr. King even went so far as to make one of our exam questions about herself... I love cultural anthro, but I hated this class.

Her lectures often get off target. Check your work when you get it back, she messed up on mine. She often talks about her self and the kurds. Good Luck with her..   first day of class ask her about the usa being a salad bowl and not a melting pot.. :)

She often contradicts the textbook in lecture and exams, disagreeing with key concepts. Her lectures are often confusing and she easily gets of topic. I honestly did not learn much about cultural anthropology but now I am an expert in Kurdish culture...

I had two classes with her. She is more like an acquired teacher. The way she explains things, unfortunately you have to have her go back and clarrify. Always visit her during her office hours. She has favorite students and remembers that when grading (its been proven!). Always listen for words she repeats alot, those will be the terms on the exam.

This course gives a excellent cursory look at the troubled Middle East and dispells a lot of ignorance about the area and its occupants.  Dr. King's extensive research in the area provides for interesting class time and engaging dıscussions.  Your grade is dependent on good attendance and a thorough reading of the text book.

This class was way too hard.  The exams were awful and hard to study for considering all class time was devoted to Dr. King talking about herself and how amazing she is because she does research in Kurdistan.

This class was unnecessarily difficult.  The exams were ridiculously hard and the 'correct' answers would sometimes contradict the textbook.  Her lectures aren't lectures at all, so you never really know what to expect or how to study for her exams either. Good luck if you take this course with her -- you'll need it.

She has very clear expectations for in-class presentations as well as term papers, which she makes crystal clear -- AFTER the fact. Also, a very rigid view of what ethnography is -- compliance maximizes individual utility.
Professor has interesting research experience and perspectives to contribute to class discussions.

Graduate students, unless you are an existing member of the Diane "Go-to on Kurdistan" King fan club, consider avoiding. You will hear a LOT of monologues about Dr King and her work, but mainly about Dr King. Seminars are horribly dull, and she manages to sap any excitement out of the air. Infuriating.
No Comments
way to self centered. she spends hours talking about people she knows and people academics online. Way to boring a professor for such an interesting subject.

Dr. King is way too into herself to teach this course or any course at this university. I have had 4 Anthro professors and they were all saints compared to how she is. Her exams are unnecessarily hard and involve personal questions about her and questions that contradict the textbook. Please take my advice and avoid this professor.
Incredible teacher. Changed my life

She is a scholar, not a teacher. There is a large disconnect between her massive amount of knowledge and her ability to share said knowledge. Expect to teach the class to yourself or plan on having a lot of one on one meetings with her.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Extremely difficult and mind numbingly boring.  She obviously cares tremendously about the subject and if you ask for help she will give it. Classes are laboriously difficult to stay awake in, however. AVOID.

If you want to pass, look over your notes and do the readings she assigns. If you want to make above a C, you HAVE to read over your notes DAILY and go to her office to ask questions. Her class lectures are sporadic and her tests are the hardest I have ever taken. Biased towards guys and HATES undergrads. Thinks we are all morons. DO YOUR HOMEWORK.

Meticulous grader and a scholar of the "old school."  Do not think you can glide by in her classes because the work load is sometimes overwhelming, but you come away truly enriched.  You must do the work or you will fail.
Avoid, avoid, avoid. Heartless woman who hates undegrads.
Are you kidding? If you can avoid her -- do it. She hasn't got a clue.

Assignment feedback and guidelines were often unclear and lectures were usually unhelpful and confusing. Class is largely based on group work. That being said, the class is not hard by any means and is a solid choice for an easier 300+ A-S course.

Almost all group work with the same group. Feedback was confusing and we would often miss points and not know why. Class rarely takes up the whole time. If you don't have a laptop, you will probably have to do all the work in the lab. Compared to other upper-level A-S classes, not a bad workload. Great for DMD minors. Not a lot of grades.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Class was okay. He lets you out early most time periods but sometimes his homework was unclear in terms of feedback and directions which was very confusing. We were also not in line with the syllabus dates so it was confusing when he would make us present on days we were supposed to have work days. He is nice and sometimes has class remotely

The class is very difficult in terms of content. His exams are extremely hard, he makes them so that you don't finish the exam and nobody does finish them but he is a very easy grader.
