reviews.comment: She can be a little intimidating at first, but she truly cares and is passionate about what she teaches. If you take the time to get to know her, you'll find she's a nice person who wants her students to succeed.  Exams follow the study guide. Take notes, turn work in on time, and do what she says, and you will be fine. I would take her again.

She comes off a bit harsh at first, but she is a nice professor the more you get to know her. Attendance is mandatory as well as being involved in class. If you are not involved/show up, you will not pass the class. A lot of this class is roll playing. There is not a lot of homework and the exams are straight forward.

Dr. Spencer is excellent at her craft, and possible one of the best professors within UK's ISC Department. This class is neither easy or hard, but rather intense like you are working for a Creative Advertising Agency. You are in a consistent cycle of projects that grow and evolve upon each other. She is a mentor to all who wanted to be pushed there

Doesn't seem like she understands what she is teaching. Doesn't know the answers to the questions you ask in class. Confusing instructions. Crazy amount of work in short time periods. Takes months to grade, and an assignment that 10 other ones are based on. I don't know if shes ever given anyone 100%.

Unorganized. Confusing directions. Doesn't seem to understand the content as well as a professor should & can't teach it well. She doesn't accept late work at all, but will take over a month to grade your assignments. I feel like I could've learned just as much in this class without her teaching it. Just overall frustrating.

ISC 490, an easy online class to pass but had interesting material. Mainly project based. Spencer was able craft assignments that allowed you to demonstrate an understanding of sports industry without eing overly time consuming. Allowed multiple accommodations and very easy to contact. Would take her course again!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Contrary to belief she is not understanding at all

I have never had a professor that cares so much about their performance as an instructor. She had someone come in and ask us about how we were feeling about the class (all anonymous), and then made changes based on our feedback. I wish all professors were like her. She expects a lot from you, but she is a good person and knowledgable about ISC.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Spencer is very strict about attendance and late work, so keep that in mind. That being said, she is a kind and understanding person who is clearly knowledgable about the subject. You will need to buy the textbook because there are weekly reading response activities surrounding the chapters. Overall, not a bad choice at all for a professor!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I took her for 499(wasn't an option to choose from). She provides great feedback and is very willing to help you if you need it. She genuinely values you and wants to do what she can to help you do good in the course. 10/10 :)
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: She tried to make lectures fun for all of us. However, lots of memory retention is needed to get a decent score on the exams. There's about 300 total terms you need to know. However, the professor is very understanding, numerous extra credit opportunities, and gave great feedback on essays. Overall, a great professor and I would take her again.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Do not take this class if you are not a history major. It is very lecture heavy. I do like the professor she's so understanding about the exams and homework and always asking for our input to change things. This class for me was so hard to focus on because I just needed a core credit and didn't care about the history.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: She's very good as a professor and helpful. The class can be boring if you're not into the subject but she's does her best to make it fun. She's very understanding and willing to help, and you can get by with just showing up. She's gives readings every class, unit quiz's that arnt to bad, and you write 2 easy essays. She's there if you need help.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I love Dr. Mokros but not her class. Overall, she is a very understanding professor and very nice. However, this class is for people who are genuinely interested in East Asian history. If you are just looking to fill a core, choose something different.

dr mokros was amazing!! didn't think I'd like East Asian history but her passion for it made it interesting to learn about!! also a very caring professor. attendance is mandatory but nothing is graded too harshly.

Honestly one of the best professors I've had at UK. She's very sweet and extremely caring towards ALL of her students. There are 5 map quizzes throughout the semester, some were harder than others, but not terrible. There are 2-3 essays which are fairly easy as long as you keep up with readings. Lecture was never boring as she always made them fun.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I love Dr. Mokros down. One of the most personable and understanding professors I've had and always made lectures interesting. Extra credit stuff isn't really worth it because you don't get much, but it's fine. Great class
Dr. Mokros was great! She did a great job keeping up with her students and never let anyone fall behind. Was very understanding of my absences!

Dr. Mokros's HIS 355 was very fun and not too difficult of a course. The class is divided into 3 parts: lecture, roleplay game, and final exam prep. The roleplaying game was more fun than expected and easy to get into. Lots of reading is necessary to do well. Dr. Mokros herself was very helpful and accommodating when needed!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I really liked Dr. Mokros' class. Her lectures are interesting to anyone even slightly interested by the material, and the homework isn't too bad. She does assign a lot of reading, but a skim is usually good enough for class discussion. My only complaint is that her essay assignments don't have a lot of freedom and are pretty rigid.

Dr. Mokros is a quality professor. Her lectures are not always the most interesting, but as long as you go to class and do the discussions and readings, you should pass with an A. There were no exams in HIS296, just a few papers and a group project. Overall would recommend!

Her class was too difficult for the 200 level- it was my lowest level class and I worked hardest for it. Most of the test material is on her lectures, not powerpoints nor the readings. I went to her office hours several times and had a difficult time connecting with her and didn't see it improving my grade. Take an easier 200 level history class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: A lot of the class is based around the readings she has you do everyday, which are anywhere between 20 to 180 pages, plus a book. If you LOVE Chinese history, then definitely take this course. If not, it'll be the most boring class you've ever had.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: She gives great feedback for your papers, but she'll make you work for a decent grade. Her grading isn't overly harsh but defiantly a little harder than average, but showing up to class and participating helps a lot. As far as her lectures go, if you like Chinese History I am sure you'll enjoy but if not the class can will feel boring.

If you really love learning about East Asian history (China, Korea, Japan), this class will be beneficial. If you want an easy A, however, this is not the course for you. Finals week was stressful, because the final exam and essay were due on the same day. She will be strict on your grammar. Lowest essay grade was a B (hardest B I've earned).
Amazing professor! Very knowledgable and good at what she teaches. Important to attend lecture, but readings are interesting and good.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Respected

reviews.comment: Dr. Beth is an amazing person and professor. She helped me grow tremendously as a writer and academic overall. Although the class is difficult, she wants the best for you. Take advantage of office hours, she explains exactly what needs to improved. I was not expecting to have such a “boring” class be so fun. Take Dr. Beth.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: This class was very work loaded. It took more time then all my other classes combined. There was an assignment/paper ever other day. The teacher is fun but a strict grader. Her class goes over some hard concepts but she is very good about scheduling meeting and office hours to help.

Dr Beth cares a lot about her students and genuinely wants them to get better and gives them the resources to do so. She does grade harshly but she will give you the feedback you need to succeed and an opportunity to fix assignments. If you want to become a better writer and speaker, I highly recommend Dr. Beth!

She genuinely wants her students to become a better writer, which is why some of the assignments are tough, but I learned a lot. Writing is such a valuable skill, and I've heard some other sections of WRD110/112 are kind of a waste of time. If you want to be challenged and become a better writer, then I highly recommend Dr. Beth.

Dr. Beth is by far the best Professor I have had. She is straightforward and tells you her expectations on the first day of class. She doesn't have time for BS. She has everything laid out for the entire semester. She is the most organized professor. As well, she has helped me with my writing more than anyone has.

This class only has a few major assignments, but they all take a long time to complete. Her grading scale is odd( 95, 85, 55, 0), but she gives great feedback on what you need to change to get a specific grade. She is a super great person to talk to and she made me not mind going to class even though I hate writing and public speaking.

Dr. Beth is so sweet and was really good about creating an environment supportive of open discussion. She's a tough grader, and her assignments were usually a lot of work, but she always made herself available outside of class if you needed help. In sum, if you put in the effort, you'll learn a lot and do well.
Dr. Beth is a caring teacher who wants her students to succeed. The grading is tough at times but it is all in an effort to make you a better writer.

Dr. Beth is awesome! I wish I had met her earlier in my education career, as I would've taken her as much as possible. She's improved my writing so much Her class was pass/fail based, with a high bar for passing, but the feedback was great. It was heavy in writing, but that's expected in a Style for Writers class. Cannot recommend her enough.

Dr. Beth is intelligent and kind. Some of her assignments are very abstract, but she goes over them extensively during class, leaves times for questions, and works up to a concept with exercises and readings. She is super organized and lets you know about assignments in advance, but does not publish them until the concept is taught. Learned a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Beth requires attendance and participation. The work is extensive, but she grades papers fairly and as long as you put in the work you will be successful.

She really cares and wants you to be a good writer. The class is definitely a lot of work but she gives good feedback and will help you through your papers if you ask. I walked in knowing nothing about good writing.

reviews.comment: Work hard or die

reviews.comment: She is amazing. I had her for WRD 111 and she is currently my faculty advisor for WRD 399 which is an internship course. She is very patient with her students, she gives amazing feedback and as long as you do the work, you will be good.

She's an excellent professor and person in general, but her class is rather difficult. The content is interesting, but the accompanying assignments are rather vague and thus tend to be difficult. reviews.comment: Dr. Beth's class was extremely difficult. She doesn't give out rubrics, but she does have general guidelines for grading. Be prepared to stay up late working on essays and projects. reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: She will RUIN your GPA. I've done my best to keep up with everything but if you are three lines short on a paper she cuts half your grade ! She is unnecessarily difficult with no room to make up for things you did not understand.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: For some reason she seems to care so much about the design of documents. She weights the design part of a paper equally with the the actual writing in the paper. Great teacher but confusing grader. She doesn't use any online grade site so you never really know your grade.

She marked down for design on papers all the time. She'd give a D for design and an A for the actual content. I'd end up with a B or C on assignments. It was annoying as hell.   I'm writing a paper, I'm not creating a damn art project. She's nice but jesus, i dont care about being nice. I want a grade that doesnt ruin my gpa. A C doesn't cut it.

Dr. Beth is fantastic--that's why I'm taking the time to rate her. She's very easygoing and doesn't treat this like a traditional speech and comp class. We've done some outside the box assignments, but they aren't hard. There's not a lot of busy work, but you won't ever just listen to a lecture.

This class wasn't a lecture, it was mostly class discussion. Prof knows how to help students, and provides resources for writing good papers and speeches. Group projects are long but she gives ample time.
Lots of writing and speaking in class, but really not that hard. She is amicable to students and makes them feel comfortable in class.
Dr. Beth is a great professor. If you show up for class, do the work, and ask for help when you need it, you'll pass easily. Just don't blow off the class or the work!
I hate always writing papers. Everyday a new paper is due.

Excellent professor. Do not take if you're looking to get an easy A. Do take her if you actually want to become more prepared and would like to become a much better writer/public speaker than you were before. Class has a heavy load, but she was always willing to speak with me outside of class. Definitely recommended.

Awesome teacher! Had her for Intro to Women's Lit a couple years ago. It was a great class, the readings and lectures were fun. The tests were sometimes long and hard (that's what she said) but they weren't too bad. She cares about her students and is very helpful outside of class.

Lots of work, hard grader.  However if you go to class and pay attention she tells you exactly how she wants everything structured.  One time i went to her office hours with a rough draft and she told me EXACTLY how to fix it to get a good grade.  Keep up with your work, pay attention and skim the readings and you'll be fine

I have had two classes with Dr. Beth and she is by far one of my favorite! She is so helpful and I noticed a huge improvement in my writing! Be prepared for a lot of work and confrencing with her outside of class. I consider myself an average student and mostly do what I can to get by and I loved her class so I do recomend it!

She's awesome! She will tell you straight up that she's a hard grader, but she's always willing to conference and help you make your papers better! Her tests aren't too bad if you write down everything that is talked about during class. Do the work, read the books, and you'll be fine.

I liked her. There was more work than expected but she's really nice and occasionally funny, making for a decent class. I took the advice from the last comment and met with her before turning in each paper. I got an A on them all and she was always helpful. We did have a final exam so be sure to keep up with the reading & write down the key terms!

She is a really good teacher if you take advantage of meeting with her.  She grades hard, but if you meet with her before the paper is due, she helps you edit your paper so that you get a better grade.  I fully enjoyed this class, but it is definately not one that you are just going to fly by without doing work.
she is a good teacher she just grades really hard
No Comments

I loved Dr. Bacchus!! Very obviously knowledgeable and passionate about the subject she is teaching. Posts powerpoints on canvas but recitation attendance is mandatory. There is a lot of required reading, but I passed without reading. Exams and quizzes are all online.

Extremely biased class. You will learn nothing about international politics and you will be ostracized if you go against her views. The class focuses on white supremacy. If that's what you want out of a $4,000 class than this is perfect for you. Nothing you learn from this class will prepare you for a career after college.
Fun class to take. A good professor who helps students.

Dr. Baucchus was fabulous! If you are in a lecture/recitiation setting, difficulty is really determined by the TA. Dr. Baucchus is eager to engage with students about course material before and after lectures and is very entertaining. Would take again!

Dr. B is really passionate about what she teaches. Lectures were pretty boring, but Dr. B made the material engaging. All quizzes and exams were open note and online, but despite this, most people didn't get 100s on the quizzes. The class was pretty straightforward, and she posted the lecture slides on Canvas.
Best professor I have ever had! Incredible lectures, fair grader, great professor all-round. As long as you put in some effort and read the book, you should pass with flying colors.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I am honestly so inspired by Dr. B. She is super knowledgable & really knows what she's talking about. Her lectures are info heavy but very interesting. Extremely easy class as well. Honestly no reason anyone should not get an A. There are some required books, but not super necessary to read them. Class only meets MW and she cancels quite a bit.
Loved Dr. B! Her lectures were always interesting and she was always nice. The assignments/papers were straightforward and participation was crucial to the course.

Prof Shortslef is absolutely great! I had never had a class dedicated exclusively to Shakespeare, but she makes the content understandable if you don't know early modern stuff. Tests are easy if you read, and as long as you find a topic you can write about well, she'll give you good feedback on your essays. She appreciates folks who talk in class!

Dr. Shortslef is a fantastic professor. I have never enjoyed reading Shakespeare until this class! She is really approachable and kind, and is SO incredibly knowledgeable and passionate about what she's teaching; making class enjoyable and I never felt intimidated to ask questions, and she'll provide feedback on paper drafts. Highly recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Shortslef is so knowledgable and kind! The course was easy if you attened class, did the readings, and did the short writings weekly. She is so passionate about Shakespeare and it really shows in this class.

Dr. Shortslef is SUPER knowledgable about Shakespeare, and it was really sweet to listen to her excitement over the plays we read. You take 6 exams that can be difficult if you do not study properly. Two papers that she offers to help with in class, but can be graded a bit harshly. She is so kind and intelligent, I definitely appreciated her class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: All her reviews are true, but she changed halfway through the semester for me. Started grading things more harsh, and the final exam was extremely unfair. Closed book closed notes, identifying the speaker of random passages from 5 plays we read with NO hints. And she did not plan this until later. This class made me drop my English double major.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Dr. Shortslef was great to have as a professor, I would definitely take a class with her again!

Dr. Shortslef is a very kind professor who genuinely cares about course content and her students, but this class is SO BORING. Not because of her, but because of Shakespeare. If you don't have a major interest in either Shakespeare or film, you will find yourself very bored. However, Shortslef is nice and the course load really isn't that heavy.

Overall a good Professor, not difficult or anything of the sort. Only qualm is that lectures tend to be boring, and even when content is finished early class is never let out early. If you only have a mild interest on Shakespeare I would not take this class, I do not believe you would enjoy it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great professor, but this is not a film class. You watch the movies on your own time and spend one class talking about it while the other class periods are all about reading the play. If you don't like reading (especially Shakespeare), this is not the class for you. I enjoyed the films but when 3/4 of the class is reading you lose all interest fast

She is amazingly kind and patient. You can tell she really cares about her students' success. A lot of lecture videos and reading for the Shakespeare course, but that is to be expected. She is very smart and you can tell she is passionate about her work! Easy to pass class as long as you do what needs to be done!

My favorite professor this semester BY FAR. She was so sweet, caring, and helpful. You can tell she's genuinely passionate about what she teaches and it makes class so much more interesting. Loved having her and 100% would take a course with her again!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: Dr. Shortslef is the epitome of all caring, intelligent, and well-spoken professors. While the classes were very lecture heavy, and the reading material was extensive, every class was informative and fun to be in! She strives to see each of her students succeed, and makes asking questions in class (no matter how stupid) easy and comfortable!

I loved Dr. Shortslef. She is so compassionate and understanding. Attendance was graded, so I suggest going to classI missed quite a bit and still got an A though. She is a great teacher and will really help you grow. She is also super accommodating, but make sure to do your assignments. There was quite a bit of reading, but thats to be expected.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: Professor Shortslef is truly kind and respecting of her students. She cancels class fairly often so we can work on papers if need be. The class discussion is always really great and she helps to prompt that. Very knowledgeable in her field and can answer most questions you have for her.

Dr Shortslef is the most caring professor I've ever had. She genuinely wants her students to succeed. She's so intelligent and you can tell she's really passionate about literature. She's very well organized and makes it clear what's expected of students. The course content was very difficult, but she made it bearable.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: Dr. Shortslef is so incredibly kind and willing to work with you outside of class. She is one of the most intelligent and well-spoken professors I have ever had the privilege of taking. There is lots of out of class reading, and there are high expectations for papers, but the workload is definitely manageable. She's a gem of a professor!

This course was definitely worth it. Dr. Shortslef is incredibly knowledgeable and pulls many interesting analyses from texts. She is very organized, which I really appreciated, and you always know what to expect from class and when things are due. The amount of work is not too much, and you will do well if you keep up with the reading.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I hated Shakespeare but.... Dr. Shortslef is amazing! She knows what she is talking about and can answer any questions you have. Easy comprehension quizzes and 2 bigger papers. She is always willing to help and talk through paper topics. Participate and you'll really love it and she'll love you and help you out. Few extra credit options.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Smart, engaging, and interested. She made Shakespeare fun. Bit too much group work, but some people like that. Expect easy reading comprehension quizzes and a few short papers. She makes it very clear what students are responsible for. Pay attention, read the text, and do the work, and you'll do well in her class.

Dr. Shortslef is great! I really enjoyed this class. She is very smart and can answer nearly any question you throw at her, which made for some interesting discussions. Classes were a combination of group work and class discussion. Attempt the readings and put forth effort during discussions for a good grade and a very fun/interesting class.

Great professor! Makes class interesting, participation matters, workload is quite reasonable. Doesn't give much feedback for papers, but grades reasonably. She really knows her stuff and wants the students to learn. Another plus: she's quite attractive. What's not to like?

Dr. Brown is great, kind, and willing to work with you. She does force class participation. She knows her stuff and makes a boring class funny and engaging. It is a very discussion-based class so you have to participate and as a class you get to lead the class

I absolutely hated this class and thought it was super boring, but Mrs. Brown was a very nice professor and tried to make it fun as best she could. I was always a little lost with directions for assignments, but she would answer emails very quickly and clarify when I reached out.

There were interesting class discussions every class about the content and how it applied to our lives. I completely missed 4 assignments (got zeros on them) and still ended with a 94. She has been one of my favorite professors in my college career.
well-ordered structure to his lessons
gives tons of extra credit, decent lecturer, very receptive to feedback.
Great professor. Made economics simple

reviews.comment: Dr. Enright herself is incredibly nice, but the class itself is not very useful. If you miss one class, your grade drops 20 points. Mostly reiterated common sense is taught in this course.

Dr. Enright is so kind and helpful! She answers any questions you have quickly and thoroughly, and is very friendly. She's also super lenient with late work and is willing to work with you for pretty much anything if you email and give her a heads up. Definitely take her for CIS 111 if you can!

Dr. Enright is a wonderful professor! She makes an effort to get to know students and is very easy to reach out to outside of class. She's very helpful when it comes to assignments. Can't recommend her class enough!
Very easygoing and lively. She always tried to make class fun and entertaining. She is also very understanding when it comes to missing class or needing an extension. Show up to class though.
Dr. Enright is interesting to say the least. She is a character. Her class is easy if you try but attendance is mandatory and the lectures can be boring. Lots of group work and a few essays.
Love her so sweet and understanding

Dr. Enright is an amazing professor. She cares about her students and has a lot of passion for her job and what she does. I had her for CIS 111 which is a mix of essay writing and public speaking. She grades very well with clear grading guidelines. She is very understanding when it comes to personal limitations.

She cares deeply about what she does. She is very enthusiastic. I enjoyed her a lot. She is a little slow with grading. She wants everyone to succeed. She will not fail any student as long as she sees effort. Very generous grader.

one of my fav profs this semester! she truly tries to make a connection with all of her students and is extremely caring. she is also very understanding and gives extensions if you ask for it. leniant grader and gives good feedback and will sometimes let you redo assignments for a higher grade. attendance required but she lets you have 2 zoom days

Dr. Enright is the best professor I have had. She treats all of her students as equals and genuinely tries to build connections and work with each person. As long as effort is shown, its an easy A. She is overall a wonderful person and I would definitely take one of her classes again just to have her as a professor.

Dr. Enright is caring, funny, & straightforward. The assignments aren't hard and she's a fair grader. Look out for the mini assignments she will create a little advance leading up to speeches and essays they're easy to miss (ex. peer reviews, rough drafts). Gives extensions if needed. Mandatory attendance but gives you two times u can zoom in.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: This is not a difficult class whatsoever. Keep in mind that 93% of your grade will come from exams but they are not difficult. You get what you put in.
