I find this class quite boring, and it is not interactive enough for me to learn any information permanently. It is entirely based on lots and lots of notes that she reads off of a PowerPoint. Each class is the exact same. She seems nice, but her style of teaching is very outdated.

I'm here to review the class that she taught, professor Hapke is amazing but her class is not. I was scam by the reviews! Who said the exam was open notes? Well, not anymore be prepare to memorize the 90 pages of the very details of each definition terms for the exam because it's all look identical and with Lockdown browser+ webcam. Good Luck :)

Hapke is a very nice professor and tries to help the students where she can. I do think that she reads off the slides too much, and the lectures are very dry. The exams are all open note, but I don't feel like I learned a lot from this class.
Great professor who cares about her students. Definitely take her.

Professor Hapke literally reads off powerpoints every class and doesn't elaborate, or to put it simple, teach. Her final was extremely irritating with 80 questions but the irritating part was having some questions being 6 sentences long. If you're going to make your final 80 questions long try not making us read paragraphs for each question.

I struggled with this class a bit because the exams are really short timing. The class itself is a ton of complicated wording in lectures and on tests so it wasn't my favorite. Despite that, she was really nice when I was struggling and came to her for help.

She is a great professor. Our class was hybrid style, so she many in-person attendance optional and gave you 24 hours to complete the questions corresponding to the lecture that day. She provides class notes to be filled in, gives clear answers, and the exams are based on her notes.

This class was super easy! Every homework, quiz, and exam question is on Quizlet. However, if you want to actually learn something, this isn't the class for you. Professor Hapke reads word for word off the PowerPoint and gives little explanation about the content.

Professor Hapke's MKT 300 class is very straight forward: do the homework, review your notes, know the study guides for tests, and you will get an A. Easy class and you will learn a lot! Professor Hapke is also very caring and understanding, I had an injury during the semester and she allowed me time to catch up on work.

Holly is really sweet and I appreciated how well organized her class was. You literally dont have to learn anything in this class because the tests are all on quizlet and very easy. I just found her to be slightly annoying. Shes one of those people that are always just a little too happy and excited about marketing.
Take this class! Easy and Dr. Hapke is so caring and an amazing professor!!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: Super easy class with her. Would take again 9/10.

Course flexibility was excellent by offering different methods, including a textbook, on-demand video, or live video. Very informative and helps relate the material to the real world. Easy to understand the subject matter, gets points and information across quickly and efficiently. Great notes packets provided for tests!
I loved this class. As long as you went to the lectures, which were actually fun to watch, you'll pass. She's really nice and caring so if you have ay problems you will be fine!

Holly was a very easy professor to take online. There was homework every week but it was very easy. Tests could be hard because there was a lot of material but there was no lockdown browser or anything so you could just look everything up. I took this as a summer course and all the lectures were prerecorded so they were boring.

Professor Hapke was a decent professor. Her lectures were really hard for me to pay attention to because she kind of rambles during them and tends to talk to fast. 1 or 2 readings a week which was kind of a lot, especially when you are trying to take notes, too. Exams are of average difficulty- just make sure you study.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: She was awesome. She sent reminders for EVERYTHING which can be annoying but extremely helpful too. She had built in questions to her lectures for grade boosters. Exams were pretty easy and so is homework, lots of chances to understand coursework. She normally teaches online so she was a good selection for this semester.

She is very rude when you have questions she thinks are dumb. Echo and mind tap run the entire class. Almost all answers are on quizlet for exams and homework. Not terribly hard of a class but prof is not very understanding about anything

Holly is always happy and nice during lectures. The class is so big you will most likely never have to talk to her. All hw/ECHO answers are online. Notes are fill in the blank. To pass tests, just memorize each section on the study guide. I just studied hard the night before and got an A on every test. Put in some effort and you will get an A.
Holly is a great and friendly professor. She truly cares about her students and makes lectures as interactive as possible. Super easy going lady and the class is fairly easy as well.

Lots of the reviews on here for Prof. Hapke are ridiculous. Her lectures can get a little boring but they're always based around the concepts you need to know. If you actually care and put effort forward, the class is very easy. Notetaking packet is very helpful for exam prep, and is really the only thing you need to feel ready.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Hapke is super down to earth and funny. The hybrid class is a little confusing at first but then I really liked it. The online homework is really easy and a helpful study tool and the lectures are interesting (if you find marketing interesting) with her inputs. Good class.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: It was a hybrid class, so we were supposed to go one day a week and watch online one day a week. However, if you watch online on the day you are supposed to go at the time your class is, you never have to go because she takes attendance by who is watching live. What she tells you to study for exams is essential because that's what's on the exam.
The class is fine, but the exams are pretty tough. Easy to not pay attention to because homework answers can be found online too.

She is overall a good professor. Her class is very test heavy so if you bomb one exam, it might be hard to bring your grade up. I enjoy how its hybrid class so I only have to go to class once a week and the other day I can watch online. Also, the week before the exam she tells you things that will be on the exam so it helps a lot with students.

I enjoy the style of the class but her tests are HARD. Everything seems like the same thing. if you don't pay attention in the lectures and write down examples, it will be very difficult to differentiate between each term.

Holly is a great character and does a good job at putting all of the content in front of you. I'm in the hybrid MKT 300 class, and my only problem is forgetting to do homework. I recommend reading the book before class and filling out the supplementary course package, and then soak up all of the information during the following lecture.
UGH THE BESTT!! love Hapke!! such an easy A a lot of it is common sense(: 10/10

Some of the negative ratings here are true but way blown out of proportion. She is a really good professor that wants you to understand the material. Her lectures are usually jammed with information, but she clearly explains most everything. The exams are difficult but if you study for them then they aren't too bad.
This class should not be as hard as it is. The tests are all multiple choice, but not easy questions at all. Expected a somewhat easy A but that wasn't the case.
Honestly, Professor Hapke is chill but her exams are HARD. She makes it to where there are 2 possible answers. Other than that, she's pretty cool and flexible.

Holly Hapke is a great professor and will help you in any way that she can. You do have to pay attention in class and study a lot for the exams because they are hard. But she will help you in anyway that she can if you are nice and give effort. I also loved the hybrid format so I didn't have to go to class everyday.

Boring class. She basically reads out of the notebook available for purchase or on Canvas. She is unprofessional. She will talk about students with her microphone on for all 300+ people in a class to hear. The test are the type where two of them are right but one is "more"right. the class is easy-ish but lot of homework.
Worst teacher ever. Boring, rude, and the class is just terrible.

Hapke was a great professor! You definitely need to work for your grade in the class, but she makes lectures interesting and engaging. You must come to every class and do all the homework because they count for pretty good portion of your grade. Exams are difficult so make sure to study!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Really hated this class. I usually dont rate professors but I REALLy did not like her. Her class is so much work. She tries to make too much extra work for this class when her class is not a priority especially when taking other classes like accounting etc.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Oh my dont even get me started on holly. Did not enjoy this class at all. She is seriously the most rude teacher I have ever spoken to at gatton. Her class is pretty easy. Just a terrible teacher.

The class is so much more work than it needs to be. The material itself is not hard but she turns it into so much work by having assignments due everyday before class and questions during her attendance etc.

Wish this class was not a core for the college just for your sake. WORST. CLASS. EVER. IF you can, try not to take a class by this woman. EVER. She is so dull and a waste of time. Makes me want to change my marketing major.

Hybrid course-one day in class, one day online. Lots of definitions to know for exams. I recommend making a quizlet as you fill in your notes so you have a study guide ready for the exams. Hapke is a good teacher, really nice and knows what she is talking about. Go to class as she will mention concepts you need to know for sure on the exams.

Holly is a very nice person. You can tell she cares about her students and the class is overall enjoyable. I really liked the hybrid style class; you only have to show up once a week! However, her exams are tricky. She asks SUPER specific questions and its a lot of material. I dont think its humanly possible to get a 100% on one of her exams
This class is a lot of work. She has homework due twice a week with readings from the chapter. She is just simply not a good teacher. Her tests have a lot more than what she puts on the study guide.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Prof. Hapke is so rude. I wish there were more MKT 300 teachers because I hope you (you who are reading this) never have to take her. Homework and attendance are a HUGE portion of your grade so be sure to turn that in. Exams aren't too horrible.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: She uses something called echo for the class that takes attendance, it sometimes doesn't work. She has homework due at 9 am on the days you have class. Theres so much homework to do and if you miss for any excused absence she still allows no makeup work. I would seriously not recommend her.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: If I had the option to take Prof. Hapke again, I would never do it. She is not a good teacher. She doesn't allow any makeup work, even if you are sick. She is absolutely the worst and I suggest NOT taking her if you dont have to.

This is a Hybrid course, Lecture was one day a week and the other day you watched the lecture online. Very easy homework in the textbook, if you review for a few hours for exams you should get a good grade. Highly recommend taking professor Hapke

I really like and highly recommend Hapke as a person and a professor, but I HATE hybrid courses and I learned this while taking this class. This class utilizes Echo360, and it is slow and constantly disconnects. We spent the first 2 weeks talking about how to use Echo then it almost never worked. Traditional classroom settings are better overall.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Caring

reviews.comment: Only once a week and have to watch and answer questions on echo the other days. The material is a definitional base class. Easy material but a lot for the exams so study in advance and do not underestimate the exams. Easy A if you put the work into it. Holly is an amazing professor and always cares about her students.

Dr. Hapke is an incredible professor - really cares about her students and clearly puts an effort into lectures. That being said, you need to study for the exams and make an effort to learn the material. It being a hybrid class makes it tempting to skip, but you need to at least attend online to understand the topics clearly. Overall, great class.
Holly Hapke is one of the best professors I've ever had. She's so willing to work with students. The homework is easy and if you read and do the homework, tests are easy.
This class is easy. She needs to understand that retail is pronounced reTAIL and not reTELL. Study thoroughly and its an easy A.

This was the easiest class I've ever taken. HW due once a week on Sunday, the midterm was online, and there's so much homework I needed a 50 or higher to keep an A in the class. If you need a GPA booster, take this class.

She is really nice and makes class interesting and fun. The homework is so easy. She gives extra credit points during class. Just study the material by reading the book and her notes and you'll pass, she really cares about her students.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: I did not care for Holly at all. She's very rude and throws too much info at you that you don't retain anything. Her exam reviews are very broad and exams have lots of specific info on them. Definitely need to study. Oh and she will not round anything. I got an 89.9 in the class.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Holly is a really caring and sweet professor. MKT 300 can be a pretty interesting course but it's mostly common sense. It's a hybrid course; you can do the lectures either in class or online. Overall, as long as you do all of the homework assignments (easy) and study what she tells you to study for the exams, you'll have no problem getting an A.

This class was offered as a hybrid so one day a week it had to be attended in person, and the other you got to choose how you attended class (online (live or after) or in person). The homework was heavily based on the reading, and the in-class points were note heavy. Tests were very much like examples she gave during lecture.

I took the online class and loved it. Super easy. One or two lessons a week due every Friday at midnight. Only two tests (midterm and final) & are not very difficult. Shes always available and sends out reminders every week. Just do the work and you should get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I love how easy she is to talk to and how much she cares about her students. But there's SO many notes, and if you aren't into marketing and you are taking it just for credit then you need to study.
Keeps the lecture engaging by using in class activities and having an upbeat personality but i think the exams are unnecessarily specific
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: She is super nice. The class is all online and you have assignments due Friday of every week. You use mind tap and there are usually "unlimited checks" so you will always get a 100%. The exams are hard. I got a 50% on the final without studying one time and still got an A in the class. Do all extra credit opportunities!!!!!!! They help in the end!
I love this class! Lectures are fun. Very nice and bubbly  professor. Exams are easy. Just study what's on the review

Hapke is a great professor. Homework and in-class clicker grades are very easy. Tests are a lot harder than you might think, so you actually have to study. The "hybrid" nature of this class (half online/half in-class) was somewhat difficult, but I ended up just going to class everyday and I found that was much more helpful. Overall great professor.
This class isn't bad. Homework is cake and easy points. Exams can be tough so you need to study. Overall shes pretty clear about everything.

Easy online class, you get as many attempts until you get 100 on homework.  The exams are a little difficult but as long as you have 100 on all your homework you can get an A in the class.  Professor is very nice and answers any questions you have.

I loved Holly! She was super helpful inside and outside class. Listen to the lectures and do the concept questions and the class isn't too bad. Her first 2 exams are kinda tough but the final is a breeze.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Holly is DOPE! She is very energetic in her lectures which make it easy to stay focused. The exams and homework are cake. She's willing to meet with her students and she will talk to you about anything. I love Holly.

This is a hybrid class, so you don't really have to go to class, although ECHO messes up usually. Tests are tough so you need to study before and not cram. She puts up what you need to know for tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: It's a hybrid class so technically you never have to go. Her tests are really hard but there are a lot of easy points to get during class.

She's not too bad of a professor. Her tests are pretty hard, my advice to you is to make friends in that class. The nice thing is it's a hybrid class, I usually go to both classes because she had so much trouble with technology in the beginning. But overall, as long as you take notes and kinda grasp it, youll do okay. She does not curve when needed

Very easy class. Took the class as a hybrid class so only had to show up once a week and then watched the class lecture online the other day. You have to either show up or watch the lecture online because there are always clicker questions. Test are super easy if you just study your notes and do your homework thats due once every two weeks.

Class is easy and can be done online so I never attended, she uses echo. There are questions to go with lecture so you do have to get the participation points from every lecture, but it's not bad. She tells you literally everything that will be on the exams in a review session. Multiple choice tests with a very obvious answer- got 100 on her final.
you have to be in class to get credit, homework once a week -- easy but takes a little while, tests are hard so make sure to study. She is overall super nice and a good teacher

Dr. Hapke is a good professor. Her lectures are pretty good but long. Don't ask for help via email or she will give you the run around and make whatever problem you are having your fault. Tests are not too hard. Homework is just annoying with the program the class uses. Go to class, take the notes, and study some and you will be fine.

Interesting class. Can skip up to 7 classes without it affecting your grade. Clicker questions. Course notebook matches up (for the most part) to past semester's. She's very knowledgable, but just study the notebook and do practice tests online.

She's NOT a good professor.  She IS an easy professor.  Just try and you will not be disappointed in your grade!  She tells you exactly what will be on exam. Learn it! You kind of have to go to class to get clicker credit, but you can chat with friends or play phone/computer games. Attention won't  be rewarded. She can be  annoying and defensive.
great teacher! tests are a little tough, but I loved this class and Prof. Hapke.
People make her seem like shes the greatest prof ever and that is not the case. Her class is easy. Study hard for the exams. Take good notes.

This is an easy class, but she's annoying. She constantly yells at people for talking  and threatened to put us in assigned seats (but it's a class of 600). You have to do clicker questions, so you kind of have to go to class. She tells you exactly what's going to be on the tests and they aren't too hard. The homework isn't helpful at all.

One of the best professors at UK. The class size is big but as long as you go to class and pay attention it is easy.  She is always so cheerful and happy and it was a great start to the day. I would highly recommend taking her because she is very helpful if you have any difficulties.

Hapke's MKT 300 is huge (600 people!), which can be very distracting. Her lectures can be boring if you don't like marketing, but pay attention and study because her exams are difficult, and worth a huge part of your grade. Her clicker questions are for attendance, and build up to be a big part of your grade.

She is such a nice and happy person. She will cheer you up every morning. The in class clickers are easy, the homework assignments are easy, she tells you everything for the exams. Put in an hour or two of studying and you'll get an A. Don't buy the textbook. The notes from Johnny Print are a must though!

Love her. She makes it very easy to do well in her class and tries to make it as interesting as possible. Don't buy the textbook, you get an eBook with your access code and a super helpful note-taking guide can purchased at Johnny Print.

You go to class, do your clicker questions(aka sit there and ask the person next to you the answer), ALL of the homeworks have a "check my work button" before you submit, and you'll pass. the only thing you need to do is study for tests. I haven't don't well on the tests because I'm an idiot, but you'll do really well!!
Such a devoted professor-- genuinely cares about her students
Absolutely amazing person

Holly was a pretty cool teacher man. Honestly, I think her class is set up for you to do well. She drops the lowest 6 clickers (meaning you can miss six classes basically), online homework is a given, she tells you almost exactly what you need to know for exams, three exams (final is optional). There's no way you shouldn't excel. DONT BUY THE BOOK.

Holly Hapke is a great professor. Clicker Quizzes and the answers to notes are an incentive to go to lecture Buying the notes is necessary and tests are directly from them. Attend exam review lectures for test topics and then study those. The exams are easy with the review. Super Easy A!

Started doing online homeworks this year that are bull. Had a homework set due the class after an exam over material we hadn't even learned, and she didnt remind us in the exam class, so I was .02 from an A and she wouldn't round or let me finish the homework. What teacher does that? Bull. Also the most nasal, shrill voice you'll ever hear

Holly Hapke is so nice and helpful. Her class may seem overwhelming at first, but it's not. There are in-class quizzes, homework assignments per chapter (to help your grade), and the exams aren't bad either.  Attend class and the exam review session. No final if you have an A going into the final. Highly recommend.

Not mandatory. It is a MWF class, but almost all Fridays are "virtual"- you have to post something on BB. Very easy tests, she tells you what will be on it. Semester long project; get a good group or it will be hard and time consuming. You have to present 3 WSJ throughout the semester. Easy A, I recommended taking this class.

The lectures are interesting, the lecture packets require you to pay attention to fill them out and seem to vary from page to page which keeps you engaged.  The clicker quizzes are a motivator to get you to attend.  Very helpful, and informative.
Very easy. In-class quizzes, so you must be there. Note packet you fill out in class, she tells you which parts to study. Definitely an "Easy A"

So easy! Great teacher and super nice! Gives you a packet at the beginning for notes and you just fill in the blank. Group project is easy and if you ask her any questions she will help you. Tells you what to study for exams. If you don't get an A then something is wrong.

If you can't get an A in this class you are legitimately brain dead. She makes it as easy as possible, and notes are taken through worksheets she provides at the beginning of class. She literally lets you know every thing that will be asked for on the test. Also, for her MWF class we only met on Friday twice all semester.

Super easy class. You do one clicker quiz per class (5 Q's), but only need 15 for the whole class (she drops the worst 9). Just get a study guide from notehall and you'll Ace the tests (which are insanely easy). Basically no homework, just about 3 very easy, small assignments. Easy A or B. Take this class.
Requires attendence but very helpful, nice prof.
Good!

She's nice... but I really did not enjoy her class.. at all. It was too long and she WILL GO TO THE END. There are daily quizzes but she is really fair with those- she only takes the highest 15 quiz grades. Youll also do just fine on her exams as long as you dont lose your notes and you study.

Great teacher and funny. She gives you an incomplete outline of the book which you fill out in class throughout the semester. Tells you exactly what will be on the tests. Project is broken up into 5 easy sections to be completed throughout the semester.

Holly is an awesome teacher. She is enthusiastic about helping students learn, and her class is very straightforward. The work is helpful, the notes are excellent, and the tests are given and graded fairly. Without a doubt one of the best teachers in Gatton. Those who disagree either had a personal problem or didn't put any effort into the class.

Mrs. Hapke is an amazing teacher! She tells you everything you need to know for the exams and she really cares about her students. She is one of the best teachers at UK. Easy A if you go to class, take notes, and participate!

Hapke is really nice but as far as helping you with your project, good luck.  It seemed that the students weren't her first priority and she would rather spend her time elsewhere.  Class was fun and tests are pretty easy as long as she gives you a study guide.

Hapke is by far my favorite professor at UK. She is extremely nice and she really cares about the students she has. MKT410 was a challenging class, but it wasn't impossible.  The tests are pretty easy, but the projects are a little difficult. But overall, I would recommend any class with her!

Material is challenging if you are not into personal selling, but Hapke is a fantastic teacher.  I would recommend her to anyone I know.  She genuinely cares about her students and wants to get to know everyone.  Best professor at UK!

She is a great teacher and probably the best teacher I have had here at UK.  She makes a point to know everyone's name within the first month of class and gives you exactly what's on the exams.  You HAVE to go to class thou, because she is a stickler on attendence.  But the class is genuinely fun and interesting.  TAKE HER CLASS!!!

AWESOME teacher.  Attendance somewhat required, as "participation" is a big part of grade.  She'll know you by name within a couple months.  Review sessions for exams give you EXACTLY what is on the exam.  Easy A.  Very nice lady.

Absolutely incredible professor, best of the Anthro Department, the class is dense but deeply fascinating, if you are genuinely interested in Evolution, and the statistical side of biology, this is the class for you, come to class, read the book, raise your hand, he will pass you.
Dr. Reyes-Centeno is great. The class is very interesting and interactive. He makes it very clear what is expected on assignments and exams, so as long as you engage, you will do fine.

Dr. Reyes-Centeno is a great guy. With that being said though, I think it is easy to underestimate how much work his class is. The textbook is not great and resulted in me not using it very often. This course was really designed for people with a strong interest in anthropology. Don't take this course because you think it is super easy. Its not.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Reyes-Centeno is a great professor. He offered a hybrid option for his class which was really helpful. He really wants you to participate in lecture to learn the material. His tests are difficult but only if you put zero effort into the class. Grades fairly and curves his exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Reyes-Centeno was great. My class was a once a week, 2 hour session which is always difficult, but it was hybrid so that helped. He wants you to come in person but you can get the lecture recordings if you have a good reason for missing class. Exams are hard, but mostly from the lecture slides.

Dr. Reyes-Centeno was an amazing professor. If you show interest in his class, he will show interest in you. This class was Hybrid, but anyone who came in person had a great time and he was very kind to us. The tests were difficult, but if you took notes you did fine. His practice exams make it impossible not to ace the exams, utilize them!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Test heavy

reviews.comment: Definitely a smart guy but I think because of that his teaching style was extremely difficult to understand. I watched all lectures and took notes and still did terrible on the quizzes- it’s like they weren’t even the same material. Lectures were very boring as well.
Buy book,download readers that don't work, recorded lectures not available, and slideshows have limited information, tests quote directly from book which is not found online
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He was an outstanding teacher.

He is the sweetest little old man. He sometimes goes off on tangents, but he is very helpful and moves at a slow pace, which is good for a 300 level Latin course. He is a bit of a tough grader, but just pay attention in class and reflect that on the tests. He is incredibly sweet and helpful, and while frustrating at times, still a great teacher.

Some of the comments here are too harsh.  I had him for Greek and he is very good with the language and background knowledge.  He's also a thorough, devoted adviser.  Most of all, he is one of the nicest human beings I have ever had the pleasure of knowing.

TRY TO TAKE SOMEONE ELSE FOR THIS CLASS! It is horrific! 3 previous, excellent, semester of Latin were ruined by him. He will give one person credit for something on the exam that another person lost credit for. Latin poetry is especially difficult, but he only made it worse.

One of the best professors I've had at UK. Not an easy prof but he genuinely cares about students, loves what he's teaching, and knows the materiallike you would expect someone who's spent his whole life studying it would.
I wish he would fix his tick, maybe then he could stay on track and finish an assignment
a f#$%ing nightmare.  ou prepare for class to realize that hey, he is going to cover something completely different. the worst class i have ever had

Dr. Martin is an incontrovertible expert in his field, but he takes his digressions a little too far, and can abandon class material during his lectures to the detriment of his students. However, when he does address class material, he is very clear and thorough.

Probably the most organized professor in the department, he provides lecture recordings and slides so you can review at your own pace. He simplifies statistics, making the course enjoyable, engaging, and inspiring. By the end, you'll appreciate statistics and see why he's a truly excellent, born teacher.

As somebody who did awful in Stats in high school this class really helped me understand the basics of Stats, especially geared towards anthropology (my major). Recorded lectures, take some notes but a lot will be reiterated, open-note open book homework, classwork and exam

This class is a pretty easy A as long as you show up and give a little effort. Dr. Hudson definitely cares about student success and wants his class to be as painless as possible. Before the midterm and final he gave us a review sheet with a list of possible test questions so we would know exactly what to expect.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Intelligent guy, very passionate with his work. Holds reasonable expectations for students.

He's a really nice guy, has a lot of knowledge and passion for what he teaches. There is two exams and they are both short answer essay style but he gives you study guides that match up exactly. Great class.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Dr. Hutson is a solid choice for any class he teaches. He's really passionate about his work! He really knows his stuff so he can sometimes go over your head with it, but he is willing to help you work on assignments and talk about grades in his office hours. He loves to know students on a first-name basis which is also admirable.

Dr. Hutson is very passionate about what he teaches. The information is for the most part interesting and well thought out. There are only 2 exams and 1 research paper. He gives you a comprehensive exam study guide, meaning all of the questions on the exam are given to you in advance. The TA, Alex Metz, is terrible! Passive aggressive and rude!
This class was super fun and very interesting. There was readings, but not too much. Only two tests and one paper. Quizzes were exceptionally easy and less than five questions and multiple choice.

Dr. Hutson is animated and clearly passionate about his field, but he really makes you work hard, especially for an intro level class. He assigns assignments at least once a week and gives you little time to complete them. Good guy, just expects a lot from students who are mainly in there to fulfill an elective credit. Don't take for an easy A.

For a UK core class, especially in inquiry in the social sciences, it was extremely interesting and a joy to take. His lectures were  interesting and you could tell he definitely knew what he was talking about. There were only two exams and one easy paper. Attendance was not required except on Fridays. The TA did most of the grading.
Addition to the post below: take home test is hell! I got a high A, but I spent nearly 8 hours sorting through the information and writing my summary.

Amazing lecturer! Keeps everyone involved with hotseat questions and class activities. Many many many assignments. Most are easy, but some are in depth. Tests are fair, but can be tough. Tests mainly from the text and lectures. Assignments are based on additional reading, which there can be a lot of. Excellent Prof. I will take him again.

Dr. Hutson is the most dynamic professor I've had. He is very energetic in class, and I am never bored listening to his lectures. Dr. Hutson will make time to answer your questions after class. He makes sure that you understand the material. The class does cover a lot of information, but the material very interesting!

I had him during his first semester and first year of teaching at UK.  He is a funny fellow and super smart!  I really enjoy his class even though he almost killed me with his awful throws of the M and M bags!  I recommend his class to all majors!

Not a bad class but it's not easy either. For a gen elective it's a little bit of work. I only took it pass fail so i didn't have to do much but I hate reading so I stopped doing that after the first exam... didn't make a difference
Excellent teacher. I would recommend him to anyone. Just take notes. He makes class very energetic and fun. He's very into his subject.
Dr. Hutson is very passionate about the subject and it shows through his teaching. He is definitely willing to help and the tests are pretty much what he goes through in his in-class reviews.

Almost every Ant major will run into this guy. He tries his best to make his subject as interesting as possible. There are alot of in class activities which is great and his tests are based on notes.The cons: his take home exam SUCKS!He grades so hard on it.Also if you miss class he will be against you from the start which can be inconsiderate.

Sadly, I've exhausted all the Hutson classes I can take.  He's a great professor-- I enjoyed going to lecture, he's got a good flow. Hilarious guy and totally sweet.  Wednesday workshops were pretty annoying, but it only takes 3 minutes to do.  Exams aren't difficult at all, just keep up with your notes!  NOTES ARE KEY; readings just complimentary.

Good teacher. Made class interesting though I was already interested. Talks a lot about Chunchucmil... every example is Chunchucmil, but it allows for a real world view of what archaeology can do. GO TO CLASS, he'll secretly hate you if you don't. I read the textbook at first, but he doesn't test over it. For the second test read it though. Nice :]
go to class and do your work, you will get a good grade. he is funny too!

Very funny down to earth teacher. His tests are easy if you spend time preparing for them. The facial expressions he made during the lectures cracked me up the whole class. 3 Tests, 1 group project and a paper. A good class worth taking.

He's very approachable, a complete sci-fi/fantasy nerd, and has a genuine interest in class feedback.  His passion really shows during lecture.  People find his tests challenging-- it's cake if you take good notes, and you can definitely get an A skimming the texts. Oh, he's a total babe, too!  Though I'm not digging the current Don Juan mustache.

if you go talk to Hutson its a HUGE help and he really helps you out. He is a really nice guy and once he sees you care about your grade he does anything to help you out. Even offers 20 points of extra credit. Also grade is 2 test group presentation, and paper pretty easy to get a good grade even if you dont do to hott on the test. Great Class

I never thought I would have much interest in archaeology, but Hutson's lectures are so well presented that you can't help but pay attention.  His genuine delight in teaching is apparent... which is great, because he has a real talent for it.

I never thought I would have much interest in archaeology, but Hutson's lectures are so well presented that you can't help but pay attention.  His genuine delight in teaching is apparent... which is great, because he has a real talent for it.

If you do not take his Introduction to Archaeology class, you are cheating yourself of a great experience. He has hundreds of ways of making the most mundane things interesting. He tells you exactly what will be on the test, the only downfall is they are very long, but he gives partial credit like crazy. Go to class, take notes, you'll be fine!
He is super nice! I learned a lot about archaeology from him. He can be difficult to follow sometimes, but that is only if you have him for a morning class. Oh, and he also has a really nice smile!

If you have a chance to take ceramics with Hunter, do it!! He's so helpful and goes out of his way to make sure you're able to do well and execute your ideas fully. I'm not good at ceramics but I feel like I learned a lot in his class. He's funny and his classroom environment is very welcoming.

Hunter is a great professor! Ceramics was difficult for me, but he helped a lot. He definitely knows what he's talking about and has a lot of knowledge on the topic. Very helpful and understanding as long as you communicate with him. He's a funny guy and keeps the class laughing. Participation isn't required but you need to be there for demos.

I absolutely love Hunter. He is a great teacher! He knows a lot about ceramics and is very helpful with tips and suggestions for your ideas. He's super nice and wants all his students to do well and encourages you to be creative.
Ceramics I is a time consuming course.Would not recommend it if you have a job because it requires for everything to be done outside of class.As far as the teacher goes ...well he tries.

He pretends to know what he's talking about even when clueless about a topic. The class wastes time with videos that aren't really beneficial. Take the other professor, Bobby- you'll get more out of your time.
Class is a waste of time with unnecessary lectures and videos. Both ceramics proffs are useless,don't take ceramics.
No Comment
Terrible teacher,Will tell you to do one thing then ask you why you did it.Hard to trust his opinions.He does try thought .EASY A if you put in the time.

You need to put in time out of class to do well. I enjoyed this class because he knew what he was talking about and really seemed to want the students to understand the world of ceramics. Difficult grader because he knew everyones full potential.
never sure what to think of him.seems fake but he is a nice guy.I got a C but i never came to class.
Very knowledgeable and encouraging, tough but fair grader.

Great professor. Inspires interest b/c he really knows what he's talking about. Class is even better when you've read the stuff. Offers bonus if helps you. Overall great guy, I really enjoyed the class.

Good teacher. Knows his stuff. He makes it kind of hard  to stay awake, but tries to get your input all the time. Easy class for the most part. Just read everynow and then and come to class, not hard at all to pass. Multiple choice quizzes, 2 tests and 1 final
Awesome! Very nice! I learned a lot!
he takes attendance every class, no more than 3 absences. tests are long and somewhat difficult. quizes given frequently.. Never lets us out early. If I didnt have him at 8am it wouldnt be so bad..

This class was pretty good. The quizes over each chapter are really easy and they helped motivate me to actually read the chapter. The tests are super long, but he gives you a study guide and if you read the chapters and paid semi-attention in class you'll get a good grade. There's also a lot of class discussion, so make sure to have an opinion!
he takes attendance every class, no more than 3 absences. tests are hard. quiz given frequently... too much work for gen. ed class

I'm not much of an artsy person, but this class did open my eyes to a new world. Tests are straight forward and cover the material in class. They are fill in the blanks, multiple choice and short answer. Keep up, go to class and study what he gives and you will get an A.
No Comments

She is passionate about media and was well-informed in her video lectures, however, I feel as though online teaching is not her strongest skill. I had no choice but to take this course online and I constantly felt overwhelmed by the sheer amount of content and work that was assigned weekly.

Professor Hunting was one of the professors that decided to make MAS 335 a work at your own pace class. Every week, we had a deadline to read some passages, watch videos, and comment on discussion boards. She really cares about you and wants you to succeed and her lectures were very informative. Overall a great professor. Def recommend.

If you take Dr. Hunting get ready for a ton of work. I took INTRO to Media Industries and while she is a really good professor she makes you work extremely hard. She is extremely accommodating and helpful but that doesn't really matter when you are drowning in work. Her projects are extremely demanding and in the end, I was just trying to survive.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: I loved this class from learning about how I can use my media degree for to a real look into my industry I think out of all of my media professors I would say she has prepared me the most and really helped mold me for this world I think she has a deep care and connection for all of her students and that is what really pushes them to thrive
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Kyra is the heart and soul of UK's MAS program. Transferring in my fourth semester, I was lucky enough to have her throughout my final two years as an A+ prof and advisor. She'll challenge you but do her absolute best to make sure you've mastered the material and done your best with the work. Most caring, insightful, hard-working prof at UK, 10/10.

Very interesting lectures. She's very energetic and definitely knows what she's talking about. She's really friendly too. The in-class activities she comes up with are always fun! My favorite professor this semester by far.

TJ is a great professor. His classes are lecture based but his sense of humor makes it interesting. He doesn't give out homework. Exams are easy if you study the powerpoint slides. One big group project to finish.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Not mandatory attendance but you had to participate inclass 10 times to get full participation credit. The group project was the only annoying part of the class and it was graded hard. The exams aren't very difficult, there is no textbook and all of the questions asked are on the slides he posts from the lectures.

He is hilarious. One of the best management professors ive had. He is a great teacher and person in general. He gives lots of extra credit just for talking in class to the point where it bumped by C to an A. If you take this class, take TJ!!

This is TJ's first year teaching at UK. Overall, he's a pretty laid back professor. He doesn't assign homework, which is good because his class doesn't take up too much time outside of class, but bad because your grade heavily depends on the exams. He does offer extra credit and encourages suggestions on how to improve his class.

He is a very nice guy and definitely knows what he is talking about. He has an accent which can take a little bit to understand, but it's not the worst. The main issue is how boring he makes his lectures that you are required to attend. He read straight from the slides. Tests are easy, no lockdown browser. The TA will grade very strictly on though
Lots of homework but it was easy, all exams were online. He is not very good at giving lectures and he also will call you out by name in class if you miss his classes too many times.

He is a little hard to understand with his accent but after a few classes it won't be so bad. He doesn't grade anything it's all his TA's but he has a very strict guide line and if your answers don't exactly match his you will get points taken off. He also checks attendance at the end of every class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: can't understand him whatsoever, very difficult grader, do not take his courses.

To start it takes a second to comprehend him but like after like a couple weeks you get used to it. But there is like an in class assignment every single day and sometimes he has random assignments on a random day without telling anyone. But the work isn't hard and it doesn't take that long either. So if you get it done your good in the class.
Do not take this class bruh, the TA's are annoying graders and take everything so seriously. The professor has a hard accent and the gives out so much work.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very caring professor. Watch out for weird assignment due dates. As long as you go to class and pay attention to the rather boring lecture, you will have no trouble passing. The textbook is very helpful, but all exam content can be found directly in the lecture powerpoint slides.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Super kind and knowledgeable professor! He reads off slides but also gives real-world examples! Accent is hard to understand but gets easy to pick up on. Tests reflect exactly what the lectures are on so as long as you go to class and take notes you will do well. Attandance is mandatory and will effect your grade by even skipping one class.

Very thick accent and can be hard to understand. Attendance is mandatory and for a grade. Lectures are extremely boring as well and he just reads of a slideshow. Assignments were also due at really odd times, so watch out for the times. Him and his TAs are really tough graders. The exams are challenging and most people score in the 60-75% range.

Was very hard to understand due to his thick accent and his mic never worked so that made it more difficult. Lectures are quite boring because he just reads through PowerPoints. Exams are difficult to prepare for because the study guides are quite vague. Would NOT recommend taking this class.

Absolutely would NOT recommend. Impossible to understand, and reads directly from the PowerPoint. Tests are all "which is NOT correct" multiple-choice questions with all the answers being fairly similar.
Very nice professor. Have homework due every class period. Have to read the book to do well.

Avoid if possible! Although he is nice and he tries it is still nearly impossible to understand him.  Projects are due every week and some times twice.  You can get a B easily enough.  To do well you have to read the book throughly.

A little bit hard to understand because of a language barrier, but he's really nice, tries his best. I'm bored in class, however, this isn't my area of interest. Lectures are powerpoints, read the book (get a cheap older edition), 20 minute oral presentation required by each student.
No Comments

Incredibly knowledgeable about criminology, and has a clear passion for it. Looks at crime from a policing, prosecuting, and theoretical perspective. The exams are more essay-like, which can make them quite tedious. His lectures are great and he gives really good feedback on all assignments.

Show up to lectures, participation matters and he covers a lot of material in class. Tougher grader on the exams, but grades more fairly on papers. Gives lots of class time to work on the final project. Rubrics for papers/projects are very straightforward.

He is disrespectful and far too opinionated on topics rather than showing proper statistics and teaching. I previously enjoyed the classes content and his lectures until I realized that he teaches from his personal perspective and it's not a good one. It's exclusionary  and did not improve my education but rather made me dislike the class, and him.

Took this class as an elective and it ended up being harder then my 400 level classes. Theres 3 exams and 1 large paper that determine your grade. very hard grader. his comments on the paper were rude and not helpful or respectful

Its not surgical school, Chris, its an elective class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: he's ok, his class is also ok, gives ton of material in one week. Doesn't give helpful feedback, grading isn't clear.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: While attendance wasn't mandatory, he graded you off of participation at the end of the semester. I only showed up half of the time and still got full participation because I would raise my hand and ask questions during the times I was there. He gives a LOT of info not provided on the slides by word of mouth so I would recommend showing up.

The exams are very difficult with no guidance. While he makes study guides and does a review before the exam, none of the material he provides is actually covered on the exam. He is very rude and doesn't seem to care if his students succeed. He also never grades anything so you will be waiting for months for grades.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: While attendance isn't technically mandatory, he does grade on attendance and participation. He doesn't often give leeway for students who don't have proof that they were very sick or some other extreme circumstance.

Chris was ok. The online textbook is kind of an awkward topic, and his lectures were dry, but make sure you take notes. The exams were pretty difficult- study guides do not cover everything that ends up on the exams. He's a little odd, but respectful and understanding as long as you communicate (ahead of time if possible).

Chris was a great professor in my opinion. He was very clear with his lectures and offered a lot of opportunities for his students. His grading is fair, but the exams can be a little tricky. It is super important to show up to class because he does a lot of in-class participation you don't want to miss. If you pay attention, it is an easy class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I took 3 of Dr. Huggins' classes in undergrad, and he ultimately wrote me a letter of recommendation for graduate school. He was a wonderful instructor and I would love a chance to take another of his classes. Criminology is interesting to me and he made the material enjoyable.

I truly wanted to like this professor but there were some major problems with the class. We had mini papers due each week except when there were tests, but this did not apply the week we had an eight-page paper due. He also was not clear on the grading criteria both for the weekly papers and the term paper.

He was overall an okay professor. I didn't really have many issues with him. He does not have rubrics for weekly writing assignments, just a loose guide (2-4 sentence prompts) for each one, which kinda tripped me up a bit. Exams were moderately difficult and you really have to pay attention during lectures. Very interesting content though.

Worst professor Ive encountered. Hes rude and doesnt care to help students who have been affected by Covid in any way. The study guides never help with the exams. The entire class did awful on the first exam but did he care? No. 0/10 would recommend. The lectures are boring. Classes were optional over zoom but if you dont go you may be lost.
Didn't give extensions for students that got Covid during the semester

His lectures were a little dull, but very concise and easy to follow. He posts his slides, which is nice for going back and looking at notes. There were frequent (unannounced) in-class assignments for attendance, so definitely go to class! He was really accommodating when I had health issues that kept me from going to class, which I appreciate!

Dr. Huggins is a nice guy who wants people to do well in his class. I took the basic research methods class which was 2/3 lectures and 1/3 a group research project. He chooses interesting reading material and attempts to make the class lectures interesting.

You must come to class because he will not give out the power points, excused or not. The tests are not THAT hard if you study, but you have to study and actually listen in class. The class was pretty interesting and he's super cool. He assigns a lot of reading but he goes over what sections will be on the exam so I never read the req. readings.
Huggins makes the class easier with his slides and examples, plus he goes into detail of every topic. Don't be afraid to raise your hand to ask a question.

He does not take attendance but if you miss you will not get those lectures. His study guides are not very helpful and take a good amount of time to do. If you plan for a fun spring break don't because he will have the hardest exam of the semester the week you get back. He grades tough and you really need to know your stuff. Don't take for easy A.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Really boring class.

Honestly, Huggins is terrifying at first but in the end he is super understanding and nice. If youre sick or going out of town he'll let you make up whatever work thats needed at home. Attendance isnt mandatory. If you read the textbook even if you dont go to class youll most likely wind up getting an A.
It is really hard to do well in this class because you never know where you stand. He takes forever to get assignments back. Boring lectures and acts like he's better than students.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Pretty easy class. Lectures are interesting and prof has lots of good knowledge.

This class focuses more on the criminology aspect of sociology. There are weekly quizzes based on the assigned readings and episodes of The Wire. Exams are pretty hard, but you'll do fine if you study. Two papers over the course of the semester, one on a character from The Wire, the other on something you learned.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: This is a solid choice for SOC101 especially if you like talking about CRIME AND DEVIANCE. Tests are fine but make sure you study. He explains things well and gives lots of good examples.

Good teacher, gives a lot of extra credit and feedbacks. Do good on your weekly quizzes because by the end of the year they are worth the same amount as 2 exams put together. He does not care about attendance. Just take notes and read. It is not worth wasting your time watching the wire.

This class was really interesting & his lectures were almost always interesting. He is a tough grader and kind of picky on papers. You need to attend class most of the time and take notes if you want to come out with an A or a B. He is kind of sarcastic but in a funny way, you just have to accept his humor.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: AVOID THIS CLASS AT ALL COSTS WITH THIS PROFESSOR.   Openly mocks students, tests cover an absurd amount of material and lectures do not help the understanding of the class. This is not a typical 100 level class.

He's decent. Rude, takes forever to grade papers and never gives out study guides that are actually consistent with the exams. He's okay. He grades pretty tough, he's one of those picky professors. Meh.
He does a good job of making class interesting and that readings he assigns are lengthy but usually pretty interesting.
Extremely rude, teaches from his bias (opposes everyone's opinions that he dosen't believe in), calls students out for no reason, takes weeks to get grades back. AVOID THIS INSTRUCTOR AT ALL COSTS.
DO NOT take 101 with this instructor.
a lot of availability outside of class and is very flexible
Great guy. His lectures are interesting and fun. He has weekly quizzes which are difficult to do poorly on. He's funny and likes to make sure students enjoy the class.

Do NOT take his 339 class. The only reason his score is so high is him teaching SOC101, which is an easy class and would be hard to mess up. He had no consistency period. The notes are different from the study guide, study guide different from test, test different from notes. There will be questions not in the notes or study guide but def test.

He lectures the entire class, has poor classroom management skills, allows students to monopolize class & is rude. He is the perfect example of someone with book knowledge that should not be teaching. Little is used from the book, but he will tell you it all comes from it. He lies. Don't trust him. He will test you on what he doesn't tell you.

Great prof! He keeps lecture interesting with cool case studies and always includes some humor in his class. Like others said, he has clicker questions every class which help boost your grade so attendance is definitely recommended.

Professor Huggins is a great teacher! This was one of my favorite classes! Attendance is not mandatory but recommended. You do clicker questions in class for credit and his notes are not posted online so attending class definitely helps. The tests are all multiple choice but you need the knowledge of lecture for the tests.

A good lecturer who is very clear and obviously passionate and knowledgeable about his subject. He was always very helpful if I had a question. There was a lot of outside readings, but they were interesting, including the textbook. The midterms weren't too hard, but they weren't easy either. He can be rude, though

Even though attendance is only a small portion of your grade, you'll need to go to class.  The study guides and book are not consistent with the test material, so you'll need your notes.  He tends to be rude to guests and is not afraid to call people out.  I do not recommend taking him.

He is a good teacher and all, but he is rude and isn't consistent with his lecture material, study guides, and tests. He gives study guides and says knows this you'll be fine. but that isnt true. if you attend class and keep up with the notes, you'll pass with a decent grade. know beforehand not to bother with the book or study guides. just notes.
He kept things interesting. He knows what hes talking about and always provides a little humor to his lectures. He made sociology really cool to learn about and I thought he was a great teacher

Dr. Huggins' lecture is actually really enjoyable and as long as you skim the reading prior to lecture, the lecture will be really clear but if you don't, it'll be kind of confusing, which is a good thing because it forces me to read. He speaks clearly and it's obvious that he knows what he's talking about. Plus, he seems really nice.

Do not take this class if he is the professor. My TA was wonderful and gave me good grades on the papers and weekly writings but Dr. Huggin's test were ridiculous! He doesn't make a new study guide and the test barely compares to the study guide/notes. He does nothing to help prepare you for exams and makes them way to difficult.

"Crime and Deviance" was the topic. Dr. Huggins was a smart/funny guy. LOTS of reading every week, lots of homework, he grades tests very hard (gives questions out ahead of time). Get your papers done early because he grades them hard too. If you keep up with the readings/homeworks you can get a good grade, but procrastination will kill your grade.
Huggins basically just lectures straight from the book. If you get a good TA then you will do well. Tests are multiple choice so just study your notes and do the study guides and you will get an A.

HORRIBLE! The class shouldve been easy but he made it dificult. His lectures were boring and unclear. Recitation was a joke. My TA barely speaks english (she asked us what the word list meant!) ANYONE is better than him.
I don't know if it was that I just don't care for Sociology or the professor. Just sit in class copy the ppt and you should pass, the papers are also easy just do them and you wont fail it.
This class is very easy. If you go to class and pay attention (at least partially) you will get an A. Just study off of your notes and the study guides your TA gives you.

A near impossible class. The subject should have been one of the easiest but he made it a chore. He speaks in a semi-monotone voice that bores you the entire lecture. I learned very little from the class and recitation did nothing to help the lectures. I barely squeezed out with a C. Anyone would be better than him.

Went to lectures at first, but they were incredibly boring. I read the text book chapters that corresponded with chapters on the test and got an A in the class. Just pay attention to what he puts on the study guide. The recitation is a complete joke and the TAs were horrible!
The class is okay. I would recommend you read the book if sociology isn't your thing. You can just go to the lectures and pull of a B in the class.

absolutely awful. his study guides are useless because he doesn't use them to guide the test at all. went to class regularly and read and there was still stuff on the test i had never seen before. not helpful or accessible. he seems to despise women. class is boring and he moves through slides really fast and gets angry when asked to go slower.
Has awful TA's that hold recitations that don't correspond with his lectures.  Should be an A with the studying I did, but the lecture notes and text sometimes contradict each other.
No need to buy the book, attend all classes and all recitations and you should be fine!

If you plan on going to class everyday dont buy the book, he clearly gets the notes right out of it. If you feel like buying it though no need to really go to class. Gives study guides for every exam. Pretty easy. Gives lots of notes though meaning I filled over and entire notebook.
Down to earth and seems like a genuinely good guy. Do not cheat. Trust no one thing.

Prof Hyatt is a great guy.He takes the Database course at UKY and is also an employee at UK IT and therefore brings a lot of real-life knowledge to the class. Midterms and final exams are online and open book/internet and pretty easy to get an A if you put in minimal effort. 30% of final grades are for a group project which is pretty easy as well.

He brings a unique perspective to a class about databases because his daytime job actually involves the databases on campus. Lectures were often drawn out, but attendance was not required and all lectures were recorded. The projects were super helpful and he gave a lot of partial/extra credit. Exams were also open note. It was an easy (but fun) A.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Overall, I've enjoyed having professor Hyatt. The class is fairly slow-paced, and it's not hard to do well in the class without attending lectures. The projects are manageable and due dates are generous for the amount of work assigned.

Mostly all of the information needed is covered in lectures. Projects are graded fairly and assignments and exams are made pretty easy. The class doesn't feel very fast paced. Overall friendly professor

3 Group projects, all were relatively easy and two tests, which were also very easy. He goes over how to do everything in class on his slides. You don't have to go to class, and you can still easily get an A. The guys is pretty great as well. Its a must take.

Definitely cares about his students. Lectures tend to ramble and he doesnt always explain concepts well. He actually works in UK IT, not as a professor, so you get a real world and up to date perspective that is rare in UK CS. Neither the 3 small group projects nor the 2 exams were hard.

TAKE THIS CLASS. Dr. Jeong is amazing, something hard to be during an asynchronous 4-week summer course. This has been no doubt my favorite class at UK. 4 discussion posts, 3 quizzes, and one individual project. The workload is manageable and the content is interesting and meaningful. I really cannot say enough good things about her or the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I had Dr. Jeong for ISC 311 and ISC 441. Yes, she is a little difficult to understand, but she is one of the most caring professors I have had here at UK. She really wants her students to succeed and is very passionate about ISC. It's just an added bonus that her classes are easy!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Took her ISC 321. Most of the class dealt with a group project. She laid out the steps and gave great feedback throughout the semester. She was able to help out whenever we needed help

I had her for both ISC 311 and ISC 321, and for both classes she really goes above and beyond to try and help you understand concepts. She is also very approachable and easy to get into contact with when you have an issue. She was a fantastic professor and would take her class again if possible!

Dr. Jeong is very kind and understanding, but she can be difficult to actually understand. I'm not much of a math/legal guy (lucky me, had her for ISC 311 and ISC 321) so I already didn't care, but her lectures made it harder. However, she is lovely and very easy to work with, so try your hardest, study for the exams, and it'll pay off.

Professor Jeong is a great professor. Her accent isn't hard to understand at all. She really goes above and beyond to help her students and really wants them to succeed. Her notes are easy to follow along with and her tests are very straightforward. You should do well in her class if you pay attention and put in a little effort.

She is very knowledgeable and intelligent, and I thought her class was pretty easy. Fill in the blanks on the Power Point notes, do a group project , take two tests. No BS busy work. Some students have made fun of her thick accent before, but good god, grow up. She isn't that hard to understand.
The course materials are naturally boring but Professor Jeong did a nice job at making her class more interesting and enjoyable!
Great teacher.

Her english is not too good at all. The notes are online but you have to go to class to fill out missing blanks. Notes are very important to doing well in exams. She's very nice just extremely hard to understand. Textbook i irrelevant.
Ian was very chill. As long as you do the assignments and follow the rubrics you will get an A. Ian was a little hard to get ahold of through email though.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Ian is very creative and taught one of my favorite classes ever. I strongly encourage you to take their class. Ian is a great person.

This has been by far my favorite course in college. There truly were no wrong answers and every lecture Ian invited us to think outside of our comfort zones and challenge what we knew. While the readings were difficult none of it felt like real work and I would take this class again and again if I could. I would highly recommend a class with Ian.
Trust me. Take this guy.

Ian was great! They were so good at starting discussion within the class. I really do not think it would possible to get less than a B in this class because of how simple they made it. I was surprised by the other review for them. Easiest class ever. They were also so kind and really cared about us on a personal level. Take their class!
Awful. Do not take his recitation/section. He is a super picky grader and hard to communicate with. Go directly to the professor because Bussan will not answer your question or help you.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: The worst TA I have ever had the experience of being in class with. There were multiple TAs for this class. One of the worst things that happened to me was being put in that section. I loved the professor but every time I have to go into my recitation was always the worst part of my week. I strongly dislike this TA

Worst TA I've ever had. Doesn't give any feedback and grades assignments with unjust intentions. I feel so defeated in his section and my grades do not reflect my work esteem or effort put into this class. DO NOT TAKE HIM, he will set you up for failure
Worst TA at UK. Whatever you do, dont make your life hell by staying in his section.

Mr. Bussan is one of the worst TAs of Dr. Summers. He does not respond to emails and gets frustrated when you ask questions. He also takes over a month to grade anything, all the other TAs get their stuff done faster. If you get him, good luck because he is the toughest grader.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: He is alright.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: He is a very good TA. But, he is a very picky grader.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: His lectures were generally fantastic. My only gripe was that hed occasionally spend TOO much time answering questions. Hes an extremely helpful professor who genuinely cares about his students learning. Homework was rough but doable and only 1 per week Exams were nightmares but he curved heavily

His lectures make the material sound interesting and fun, and he is always willing to help. However, the exams in this class had questions with answers that could not be found in either the textbook or his lectures, and were graded very harshly. The reading is necessary for the lectures, but no amount of reading will prepare you for this exam style
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: He was very helpful to students, always willing to answer questions in a way that clears confusions about topics. He is very kind and very friendly. Definitely would take him as my professor for other courses.

Fantastic professor. He asks thought provoking questions, and wants as many people to participate as possible. Don't be afraid to give wrong answers, you are there to learn. Quantum is not easy, but he is very accessible and helpful during office hours. He gives 10% bonus on HW if you turn it in a class early. READ THE BOOK! It is very helpful.

He does the flipped classroom sort of but not in a bad way. He still sufficiently teaches in class, the book just extremely supplements this learning. He is very passionate about his topic and it makes it a lot easier for the students to be passionate about the learning. He loves to make things relateable, use easy to understand videos, etc.

This man cannot teach. He attempted to use the "flipped classroom" where students are supposed to read the book before class, and the class time was filled with a few abstract, tangential reef polling questions. They take MUCH longer than the 3 minute reef polling time to do. The tests were made with the same idea as the reef polling questions.

He's an excellent professor. He expects you to preview material before class & then he does problems & demos in class. Also, he's a stand-up guy and cares about his students. Yes, he has high expectations & harder exams. But he treats student with respect, literally thanks them for asking questions, & remembers names. More profs should be like him

He's a nice guy for the most part, but he can't explain a concept clearly to save his life. His exams are a lot harder than other professors, and they are just a lot of abstract, trick questions. His PowerPoints are just pictures with no explanation, and he expects you to come to class knowing the material before he even teaches it.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: I love his class. He solves problems I had never dreamed of solving and takes times to answer questions no matter what. His tests are difficult but only because he makes them himself. You are given tools and instead of regurgitating information, you have to critically think in this class.

I read/outlined the book, did the WebAssign, payed attention in class, and studied for DAYS and I still couldnt get the grade I wanted in this class. He writes his own exams (harder than the other profs), lecture is basically an impossible problem that he works through. Is a nice guy but his teaching style is too abstract for me
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: I enjoyed having Dr. Brown as a professor. His lectures were engaging with challenging questions that made you think along with cool demo's each class. His exams were hard and he makes you work for your grade but I respect him for that.

Mr. Brown is a nice guy, but he's not exactly great at portraying the information in class. Other professors used organized PowerPoints to convey the different topics and gave more than just a couple difficult examples per class. Also, if a person has the right answer, he shouldn't discourage them, even if he has "heard from them before."
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Professor Brown was a great teacher this semester. He expects you to read before class, and once I started doing that, this class went from difficult to a piece of cake. His lectures are designed for people that actually try to learn. You can't show up and expect everything to be given to you. If you want that, go back to your liberal arts degree.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: I enjoyed Dr. Brown's. It was difficult, but not overtly so. He expects students to do reading before class and come to lecture ready to discuss. The class was hard, but it's only too hard if you're not prepared to work.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: His exams are very hard, one of them even had 2 wrong answers and I spent 15 minutes wasting time on them.  Do not suggest
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr. Brown does not make his class easy. His lectures are full of mathematical examples but his exams are almost entirely concept-based with tons of tricky questions. He expects you to read before class and will wait all class period for someone to answer his question. He doesn't drop the lowest exam like the other classes. Take someone else.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: This is a hard class, no matter who teaches it, but Dr. Brown does a good job of keeping the lecture interesting.

She is a super sweet person, but makes assignments unclear at times. The class was easy, as long as you do the assignments and show some effort, you'll be fine. She was a little difficult to reach as sometimes she would respond to my email and sometimes not. Overall, she's not bad, the class is an easy A if you just do the assignments decently.
Unhelpful. Will email her and sometimes she won't even respond. Extremely confusing and all over the place. Hated going to this class.
do not take this class with her. class was so confusing, and she is extremely unhelpful. I hated this class and would have gotten a better grade with a different teacher.

Dr. Ike is the best prof. I've had at UK so far. His entrepreneurship class is extremely interesting and he encourages you to actually carry out your projects into the real world. He's very knowledgeable, helpful and willing to meet and talk outside of class.

Absolutely loved taking Ikenna.  I just added on the major to fulfill some hours and ended up loving the class. He is very interesting to listen to as he is very educated in the subject.  Definitely would take him for this class if option is open...you will learn a lot and enjoy it.
Ikenna is a great professor who actually has a lot of connections in the entreprenuer community. he's very knowledgable and helpful. im glad i took this class.
