probably the best professor I have ever had. He actually cares about his students and wants them to learn and be passionate in ways that will help them be successful. he is hilarious and really takes the time to know each individual while having a full plate. take his courses!
Dr. Ingram is a WONDERFUL professor! I am so glad to have had the opportunity to take his class!
Love him, he is the best!

Dr. Bagby is probably one of the easiest professors youll find at UK. He is so nice and funny, and although his lectures might be long, his class is so easy to pass. You can always go to him for extra help and hes good about giving you extra time. His exams are also sooo easy.

Dr. Bagby is incredibly nice and very helpful during office hours. You do have to do the reading and show up to class, but if you do that it's an easy A. He provides accurate study guides for all quizzes. He's a really easy grader for essays as well.

This was a great class. Dr. Bagby gives amazing lectures. Make sure to read the material assigned to prepare you for the quizzes. The essays are very do able and not hard at all. There are many opportunities for extra credit.

Dr. Bagby is a great professor. He's friendly and has interesting lectures, and he even makes study guides for the tests and quizzes. The only criticisms I have are that he calls on people, which I think is uncalled for. Also, even if you study for the quizzes, the multiple choice options are so similar it's difficult to choose the right answer.
He made the class interesting because he was speaking from his own knowledge.

So far at UK I have not had too many professors I thoroughly enjoyed but Bagby changed that. Although he really scared me the first week of class he is a great guy. There is reading every week but it's doable and there are quizzes every few weeks over the reading. If you do the work, an A should be pretty attainable. Extra credit opportunities too

Dr. Bagby is a fair grader and very accommodating. He can be kind of condescending to his students, and will occasionally have a hard time clarifying things. He's also impossible to reach by email. Other than that, he's a pretty good professor: fair, knowledgeable, funny.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: This class was good, not great. Interesting subject matter most of the time, but Bagby tends to drag his lectures on and on. He's generally nice, but at times can be a little condescending to his students. His quizzes are hard to study for (you never know what will really be on them) but pretty easy. Assigns two long papers in the semester.

His lectures can be a little dry and he will likely ask your opinion and tell you that you are wrong. He is very knowledgeable and a very nice man. His expectations are very clear and he is consistent.  You could definitely do worse. Be prepared to spend extra time outside of class. Offers extra credit.

I loved this class! Dr. Bagby makes everything clear and is extremely transparent in his grading. He posts all of his PowerPoints online and gives plenty of time to study for quizzes/complete papers. He also gave plenty of opportunities for extra credit throughout the semester. I would recommend him to anyone!
Bagby is a great professor. Funny guy and makes his subject approachable. If you pay attention to his lectures and assigned reading, quizzes and essays are a breeze.

Bagby is a great professor. Very laid back atmosphere, he's pretty funny. Really makes you see current events in the Middle East with a clear understanding of the background. For the quizzes, memorize the powerpoint slides. 90% of the questions are straight from them, the rest from the readings. Lots to read but I usually just skimmed and was fine.

Super helpful and amazing professor. Makes the content enjoyable and intriguing. There is a decent amount of reading and some quizzes and long papers but nothing is unmanageable and if you complete the assignments given you will do fine.
Fantastic professor. I do strongly advise taking "Islamic Civ" before AIS340. Not an easy class, but definitely one of the best I've taken.

I feel like Dr. Bagby has good intentions and really wants to teach his students about Islam... but his class rarely is fair to your actual intelligence level and his quizzes are impossible unless you prepare to critically read all of the text assigned and all of his lectures. It is possible to get an A, especially if you do the extra credit

The most respectable and informative professor I've ever had. You will leave this class able to fully and confidently argue with your Islamophobic bigot family members. Really puts Islam in a light that makes sense and focuses a bit more on concept using history to demonstrate those concepts.
Nice guy, funny dude. good atmosphere

One of the, if not, the best Professors I have ever had.  He brings Islam to the table in a manner that everyone can appreciate.  Make sure you are a strong writer before you take his classes, especially the 400 level courses he teaches.
Great professor. Nice knowing he is an accredited Islamic scholar and knows what he's talking about when it comes to Islam.
Great prof. easy going. easy to understand. My number 1 prof at UK

Good class; informative and interesting, but not a complete struggle. If you go most of the time and take assignments seriously you will get an A. Also, don't let the presentations scare you away, as they only last a minute or so, if that. Literally, my presentation was 1 min 10 seconds and the guy in front of me spoke for less than 45 sec.
His class was a joke, whenever he actually decided to have class anyway. Honestly I have never had a problem staying awake during class until I met Dr. Bagby.
I have taken all the classes he has offered and would take more
Bagbys got jokes

I love the dude, everyone loves the dude-- you're seriously deprived if you don't have a Bagby class while attending UK.  He's a great professor with a passion for the subject and teaching; every class was interesting and fun.  You will have to lead discussion and make an oral presentation, but it's pretty brief and general-- no sweat.

Extremely cool guy that is able to keep the class fun and interesting.  The workload isn't bad at all a few papers, maybe a take-home final.  The tests are for the most part multiple choice.  Everyone should have a Bagby class!
Makes learning Arabic much easier.  Also very nice and funny.  Very down to earth and knows his stuff.
VERY fun teacher. you learn a lot.
He was great!
Dr.Bagby is the most amazing men I've ever met in my life. He will always crack you up and is really easy to talk to. If you have him then you'll have one of the best professors in UK

He is a really nice guy and easy to talk to, but a lot of the classes dragged on forever because he let group discussions get way off topic. I recommend this class if you have interest in the topic, but if not, definitely stay away.
Class is very interesting and the assignments are easy.  He is such a nice prof. you can't help but like him.
highly recommended, very understanding and nice prof.  assignments not difficult but important, good material

Ingrid is probably the worst grader, and worst teacher, I have ever heard of or seen.  She grades with no respect, or consideration for the student.  She expects perfection in engineering, and doesn't realize she is talking to students, not professionals.   As far as a teacher, she has lied to her students, and blew me off when I politely inquired.

This teacher is absolutely horrible. She takes forever to grade, and she teaches an English class outside of school, and she also mentions her mother was an English teacher, so she grades essays incredibly tough. She doesn't have clear answers to questions. She does a horrible job of explaining assignments and most kids in my class are failing.

She is extremely knowledgeable, yet horrible at teaching.  If you ask a question and forget the terminology of something, she pretends to not understand what you are asking. Unfair grading on tests, which are very hard anyhow. Book was useless. HW took hours, even in groups. Avoid at ALL COSTS!! Vey nice person though

I've never felt worse about my own skill and intelligence than after completing this course. Incompetent grading, MAJOR last-minute additions to the syllabus, and a complete disregard for the people around her all add up to a WASTE OF TIME. If she's teaching this course next spring, consider switching Honors tracks immediately.
She is a knowledgeable professor, and I enjoyed her class discussion. It is a lot of work though.

Class averages on tests were around 60. She did curve but it didn't help much for myself or others. The book is quite terrible. Lectures can border on something of a standoff. If the class doesn't know the answer to a problem, she'll likely wait in silence for a long time till someone attempts it. She is a really nice person, though.
Honestly can't articulate my disgust.  Avoid at all costs.
Worst EVER!!  Lecture is pointless, the book is very poorly written.  Don't take her!!!!! Take Hastings.  Tests are impossible!!

I hated attending class because of how ridiculous and disorganized she was. She is very picky where students sit and does not put enough emphasis on the explanation of projects which is where grade comes from. Instead she wastes time and brings in way to many guest speakers which do not count as anything. No response to emails, boring class.

Although the material in this class was easy, I dreaded going to every single lecture. From the syllabus to class policy to the directions for every assignment, Dr. Adams was horrible at giving clear and concise direction. Because of this, the class was confused often and she was constantly having to go back and modify her initial instructions.
No Comments

Be prepared to do a lot of reading before class and to take 3-minute quizzes based on those readings. The final and midterm also require remembering specific parts from all the readings. Not a hard class, just a lot of outside work required.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I took this class as part of the International Village LLP, so it was a mandatory course. There are indeed a lot of readings, and projects to turn in during the year, but he is a very nice person and will usually give very good grades if effort is shown. I didn't learn much but it's a very easy 3-credit course, with a very sociable aspect to it.
Inoue is a very good speaker and is highly accessible outside of class. He responds to emails and is always happy to help in office hours. Great professor, great dude.

I took the class for the International Village LLP. Inoue is a nice guy who respects his students but I can't honestly say I *learned* anything. Each week is a new topic with surface level discussion at best. To the other reviewer who complained of the assigned readings: respectfully, if you are able to read 10 pages a week then you will be fine.
It's mandatory for the LLP but it's a hard class
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: I took this course that was required for the International LLP but it makes me regret even applying to the LLP. The class comes with so much hw and reading, which was not very interesting to me. Inoue is a very nice professor though, but don't take the class unless you have the motivation to read and do the work.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: make sure you do everything because it will randomly drop. also if you dont show up you will fail

doesn't use powerpoints, you must take notes from him talking or writing some stuff down on the board. Attendance isn't mandatory but it's best to attend to get all the info, he does record his lectures and puts them on canvas. Very nice and adds humor to lectures. Exams are quite hard, class avg was like a C almost D

Inoue is one of the best professors I have had. He is really interesting, and plays guitar which is cool. He responds to emails really quickly and gets grades back in a timely manner. Attendance isn't mandatory, per se, but you won't pass without it. 10/10 would recommend
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: The class itself is quite interesting though sometimes a bit confusing. Marro is really passionate about what he teaches and is incredibly intelligent. He is also respectful and shows a lot of interest in each student's work. 55% of the course grade is based on a semester long project that is somewhat of a headache, but not impossible. No tests.

Dr. Inoue does not use PowerPoints. Be ready to take lots of verbatim notes with little to nothing on the chalkboard. He is lecture heavy, but tries to spice things up with humor. He has VERY clear grading criteria. You will not be at a loss for what to do on a paper. His tests are date and name heavy. Memorize his study guide.

One of the best professors I've ever had and also one of the best guys I've ever met. Extremely passionate about what he teaches and happy to consider all kinds of viewpoints. Heavy workload and oftentimes stressful project, but he'll help you anytime you need it. He'll be on sabbatical next year, but if you have to take this class try to get him.
The tops.
EXCELLENT PROFESSOR!  He cares so much for his student and is the nicest guy!
good teacher

This guy rocks.  He is a very engaging professor with a great deal of passion for the stuff he teaches in this course.  He has an accent, but his English is otherwise virtually flawless.  He gets in a habit of repeating certain bits of information over many lectures, but generally this info is very important, which is why he does so.  Great Class!!

Really great instructor. Lectures are interesting. He really knows how to teach and knows the material. He also incorporates different types of media (e.g. artwork, video clips) into lecture. Major grades consist of a midterm, final, and research paper. His grading is generous and he always answers questions raised in class.

He's nice but he drives me crazy. Lectures are ALL OVER the place. When he handed out the study guide I ended up with 13 full pages filling out the info on it. The test consisted of ONLY 25 QUESTIONS! A lot of the study guide wasn't on the test! There are several extra credit opportunities available. Easy A but sooo frustrating.

Very nice guy. Def wish I would have read the book more and I wouldnt have been so lost if you are looking for a class that you just have to go to and be fine this is not it. Very interesting though and possibility to learn a lot.
Inoue is a great professor, he makes learning fun. He went to Penn for his MA and Duke for his phd, he's one smart cookie. I highly recommend his class, him and Patton are my favorite teachers at UK.
awesome teacher. cares about students and wants you to learn. easy to understand.

Hands-down my favorite teacher of all time. He is absolutely hilarious and so passionate about all of the topics he speaks about, not just topics related to Japan. Unless you are a complete slacker you will do well in his class. Keep an eye out for his unique sweaters and coats...you'll know what I mean when you see them. Hilarious.

He's definitely used to having a bunch of nerds as students.  I thought his lectures were very insightful and kept my interest even though I was mildly interested in Japan.  Tests aren't very difficult, you just basically need to go to class and take notes-- you should do great on the exams.  The paper wasn't all that demanding either.

Great guy, awesome teacher. Although he still has a Japanese accent, his English is very clear, and he probably knows more vocabulary/terms than I do. If you go to class, take notes, and do the readings, there is no reason why you shouldn't easily get an A in his class. Very personable and knowledgeable; I would definitely recommend Prof Inoue.

Great teacher very insightful about Japanese history. He has a good sense of humor as well. Tests aren't necessarily easy, he just grades very hard. Paper was pie. Have to attend class, because his notes are very important.

Great, great teacher.  The class is no joke and if you want to do well, you must attend every class and write notes,  He is really passionate about teaching and is someone that the university needs to keep.  you have to write a 7-9 page paper that is worth 30%, 2 tests, 25% and 20% and going to class is worth 25% of the grade.

1st JP-US Politics seminar he's taught. Overall great class. Smart. Very passionate. However, can get too serious and emotional about Japan. Has many "reservations" about WWII, the "emasculation" of Japanese men and the "feminization" of Japan; constantly accuses you of stereotyping. Because of all this, I found his seminar much less enjoyable.

I wasn't very interested. This was my cross cultural USP and apparently I was the only in this class for that reason. I was very alone in my lack of Japans history. He's a nice guy and probably speaks better english than most of the students on campus but the reading is sucky and you need to really LOVE Japan to get along. Long paper due also.
Uses actual readings instead of text.  I think this is very practical.  He is very understanding.  This class is well paced.
Pretty easy class. He's nice. Easy to get along with. Funny. He speaks english very well though, so don't worry about being able to understand him. I liked the class, the reading sucked though.

Dr. Infanger comes across as really intimidating, but he's actually really nice.  He's opinionated but he likes to have his opinions challenged.  He just likes to know that his students actually THINK about what he teaches.  He has really interesting stories.

I thought Fang was quite informative. I've had several conversation about our lives and interests with him and he is approachable.  He may be incredibly opinionated but it only forces you to strive for your own beliefs.  His classes are incredibly informative but he does ask you to regurgitate facts.

While his lectures are interesting and full of information, Dr. Infanger has zero personality. Of the personality he does have it is mainly rude, condescending, and egotistical remarks. He is overly critical, making him a less than pleasing person to interact with. If he cared about his students half as much as he does playing golf, he'd be A+.

EGR 240 was an easy going class. Everything was pretty straight forward. It was a very interesting class where the professors kept the lecture slides up to date with current world events.Holloway was very nice along with  Ionel. There were two exams and a project, which were not too bad.I definitely recommend either professors and this class!

His lectures are a hit or miss- sometimes helpful, sometimes not. If you don't take meticulous notes, you won't pass. Sheer memorization needed, at least if you're like me and not an EGR major. Not worth the credit, stressed me out so badly

Dr. Ionel is a nice guy, but I feel that he mainly cares about his research and not teaching this class. In lecture he just reads from slides and its kinda boring. If you're looking for an easy global dynamics core, don't take this class, there are easier choices. If you're actually interested in energy issues, then its not that bad I guess.

I would never take this class again and I would recommend anyone looking at taking this class to avoid it. The glass is extremely boring, professor gives lots of busy work, quizzes, and very hard exams
Professoressa is one of the best professors I had during undergrad. I took six different classes with her, and I am grateful to know her.

I greatly enjoyed taking Italian with Professor Larco. She made learning fun, memorable, and meaningful through in class participation and fun Italian culture tidbits. Partner work is really important, and attendance is more mandatory than I realized at first, but it was overall a fun and informative experience.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Would take again

reviews.comment: She is my favorite professor! Before taking her class I did not know any Italian, and now I feel fairly confident I could navigate my way through basic Italian. The first day way scary, she talked in all Italian, but she is hilarious! Lots of partner work. Doesn't grade work book homework. Overall, a blast!
Very helpful instructor. She takes a genuine interest in her students. Her full immersion style of teaching the language really helps if you are going to Italy. Would recommend.

Definitely more difficult than Allaire. If you are taking a 101 or 102, take Allaire. Larco requires a lot of in class participation and speaking in class in Italian. This does help you comprehension though, so if that is what you are looking for, take Larco. Tests are extremely hard, even if you come to class. Attendance policy is very strict.

She's is nice but makes tests harder than needed. She also tends to pick on people who don't come to class and question them a lot. The final is taken with all other sections and the review guide she gave us was nothing like the test. I was over prepared and had trouble doing basic stuff since id over studied it!

Teaches Italian with her heavy Romanian accent. Tests are difficult and she makes the material unclear and makes it much more complex than it should be. Take Allaire. She's kooky and much, much easier.

Absolutely terrible. Never actually taught the material. Used different textbook to teach than what was told to students. Would give class time to do exercises and would just move on if we didn't get it. Gave no alternative explanations for content. When we tried asking her about it, she either blamed other faculty (which isn't true) or blamed us.

Never actually taught, just sped through math equations and then put us into groups to teach each other without examples. Assigned the wrong textbook so that wasn't useful. Never graded anything on time and wasn't kind or understanding when you asked her questions. Didn't know how to to use canvas half the time.

She never actually taught. She sped through math equations, gave no examples, and expected us to teach each other. On top of that, not even nice or understand when you asked her questions. Ruined my semester GPA

Do not recommend at all. Homework would take hours and she would not help. If you have questions, she will not clearly answer. She did help me occasionally with late assignments and questions graded wrong, but overall this was an awful class. Extremely math-heavy and content was provided to help us out, but in class, there was no assistance.

AWFUL PROFESSOR!!! Homework would take at least 3 hours for one assignment. Never answered any questions fully, didn't even try to prepare us for the final. She never actually taught anything, just put students in groups to have us teach each other. Extremely rude through email. Never sign up for a course if she's involved, you'll 100% regret it!!!

Hands down the worst prof i've had so far. Doesn't grade til the end of the year and grades the homeworks as strict as possible. Doesn't even try to teach the material. the whole class was convinced  she didn't even know it. AVOID AT ALL COSTS. Half the class dropped and the other half wishes they did. Just overall horrible prof. don't take

Dr. Voro is a professor full of energy and creativity. Instead of teaching me how to play each note rigidly, she is more about inspiring and guiding me to have the ability to understand and express music by myself. I learned a lot from her classes and enjoyed them a lot.

Didn't teach, instead having students create and give a lecture that related to music in some way (with very little guidance). Class centered on feeling and emotion of playing, but had almost no focus on the structure of the piece. Almost no grading criteria, and overall created a pretentious environment where her artistic choices reigned supreme.

Dr. Voro is not the right professor for everyone. Her emphasis is on storytelling and artistry rather than conventional piano techniques. You won't get away if you're not curious about the sounds you produce on piano or if you're passionless while playing. I think she's a great teacher who teaches you the art of performance without pretentiousness.

I have been a part of Dr. Voro's piano studio for several years now. She is an amazing teacher and genuinely cares about her students. Always gives advice even outside of music. She completely changed the way I play and practice. She is truly extraordinary, I would recommend her to anyone wanting to become a better musician.
Inconsistent, overly critical and never satisfied. If you want your passion for music squashed, Dr Voro is the professor for you.
Very, very creative, very knowledgeable and useful lessons. Dr. Voro gives honest feedback during the semester, but everyone I know gets "A"s as final grades

Great teacher, but tough if you're lazy. Hard to get an "A" when my piano performance doesn't improve. But she encourages negotiation (even for grades!), creativity and team work. Very unusual for piano.  No textbook, but you select a book to present on from her list

I love Dr. Voro- she genuinely cares about her students and wants them to succeed. Not only will you learn how to be an excellent pianist, but you will learn how to be an amazing artist. If you are good at piano then take piano lessons under this exemplary lady.

She was honestly one of my favorite professors I've ever had! She was so helpful and understanding with feedback and homework. I loved the class even though it was hard for me. I have taken two classes with her and both were amazing.

I opened up to her about my mental health struggles and being diagnosed with a disability midway through the year and gives no grace. Told me to drop the class because she can't do anything for me. Is not at all understanding but I'm sure if you don't struggle with anything similar then you'll probably do fine. Very stubborn.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: I absolutely loved profe Irene. I learned so much Bout the Spanish language, even through our online format. She evaluates each student as an individual, so if you come to class consistently and really give all of her assignments a strong effort then you will not have trouble here. She's also an extremely interesting person to talk to.
Don't take her, she's awful. Talks about the most useless things in class and overall isn't a good professor. Stay away

Everyone had her before me and echo the same sentiments; an amazing professor who cares deeply about the subject matter as well as the students in her class. She actively wants to see individuals succeed and is available over email, after class hours, or even during quiet moments in class to answer any and all questions. One of the best at UK.

Easily the best professor I've had at UK. Chico-Wyatt is very intelligent, but she's also easy-going and fun. Her classes involve some work, but stay on top of it and you'll be fine. The best way to describe her: she's the kind of professor that I want to drink wine with and talk about cultural topics.

Loved Irene. Such a nice woman who gives clear, spirited lectures and has an interest in the subject. Her grading will definitely make you learn from your mistakes but it won't kill you. She's very approachable and willing to help. Definitely would recommend!

Stellar professor. Very friendly, reasonable and invested in the students. Her expectations are clear and very doable. You definitely have to go to class, and should do at least most of the homework, but class discussions are fun and you can get an A if you try.

Great teacher! She cares about students and her job. Gives grades based on the amount of work you put it: if you do the work you'll get a good grade. However, there is a lot of work, but it helps you to really understand the subject matter. I definitely recommend her!

Tough grader, seems nice at first but is completely subjective and sometimes simply unfair in her grading, especially the participation grades.  She can be VERY snotty and discouraging at times if you do not understand something due to language difficulty, even on her comments on students' works.

Very clear and concise as a teacher, but a very hard grader. Class is mandatory and also necessary to do well. I would recommend taking her but know that you will have to work on the homework diligently to receive an A. Weird grade weighting also. Everything is 100 pts; homework, tests, and papers are all the same. An A is very possible due to this
Very nice, however she is an extremely hard grader. The readings are really hard but she tries to help you if you ask.

I've had her for 210, 312, 320, and now I'm in her 444 class.  I really enjoy her as a teacher.  She can memorize names and faces almost immediately and knows who hasn't come to class by just looking around... even in a large group... You can count on having to write a long paper (3-10 pages depending on the class level) as a final project.
does not enjoy giving A's. Helpful during office hours but is an unfair grader and very subjective.
Loved the class and loved her.  She gets so excited about her job.

Very entertaining, very easy to work with. She's always willing to help and answer questions. I had her for 210, 211, and 320, and in all of those classes she gave a lot of daily assignments, often busy work, but if you keep up, they will help your grade. Always takes attendance! Her classes definitely require work and participation is a plus.
Very good instructor, works with you but you must work.
