Spielmann is knowledgable and great at explaining difficult concepts if asked to. Don't be shy, study the slides, forget the textbook. Everything needed to do well is in the given slide
He talks extremely fast so be prepared to watch the echo later. He seems kinda cold but just ask him questions after class if you don't understand, I promise he'll explain it thoroughly.

I unfortunately had to drop this course since it was so difficult. Dr. Spielmann is extremely knowledgeable and passionate about biochem, but it was very difficult to keep up with him in class. Sometimes he would go off on random tangents. He was not helpful. The grade in my section was only made up of four exams and clickers.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Despite being very knowledgable he has an EXTREMELY hard time explaining things in a clear and simple manner. He doesn't synthesize the material in a way that makes us students easily understand, but rather he talks very quickly and using a convoluted language. Furthermore, the attendance questions are so intricate that few people get right.

I really enjoyed Professor Peloza for MKT300. His tests had pretty low average and were difficult, but if you study what he tells you, it will be fine. He will drop an exam if you take the final. Attendance isn't mandatory, but you should go because he will give you questions on the exam that only the people who showed up will know. I recommend him

While Peloza knows A LOT about marketing, his lectures were mostly word vomit and hard to follow. Taking notes for exam prep was hard and the exams were more difficult than they needed to be. At least he was super chill in class and did me a solid on my grade when I missed a big assignment due to illness. Grading criteria was not clear either.

Peloza was very disorganized and unapproachable. The class content doesn't connect to MGT352 whatsoever and overall, my least favorite class in the college. However, he was very understanding when I had a personal emergency and bumped my grade to an A. If you can make it through this class, MGT352 is so much better and it's worth sticking with SES!

Peterson is an outstanding teacher who will listen to her students and answer any questions we have from anything lecture related to any troubleshooting with grading. She is very immersed in the topics of the class, and very well prepared and explains everything efficiently.

I've taken Dr. Peterson for JPN languages courses, but she is extra fun in JPN320! Super funny and makes lectures so entertaining. Such an easy A as long as you do the readings and brief discussion boards, plus class is on Zoom so you have a ton of flexibility. There are also many EASY extra credit opportunities.

Dr. Peterson is super funny when it comes to her lectures. It is fully online, though, and it is an hour and 15 minutes. It can get boring, and participation does matter. She will know if you do not read the material, as she asks some specific questions at times about it.
took JPN201 online. it had two professors and she was one of them. she's very nice, patient, and understanding. participation/attendance is part of the grade. homework is not very hard.
Very biased in her teachings and is very hard to reach outside of class. The class is very manageable to get an A as long as you excel in the group projects.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor Phelps is very insightful and cares about her course material. She graded our exams somewhat toughly and did not give us feedback. She also was not easily accessible outside of class from what I heard. However, if you study for exams, attend class, and do your work for assignments and the group projects, you should probably get an A.

Good prof. Be prepared to read a lot as everything taught is straight from the textbook. As long as you read though you should be good. Youll also do some group projects with presentations. She really does just want everyone to succeed and become their best self to their highest potential.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Ms. Shonta was an exceptional teacher. The thing with her is that she focuses on a connection with the students and finds a good balance between coursework and getting to know her students. She is always available to give feedback and help students with their problems or questions on the material. If you have the chance take this course immediately

She takes an intro to business leadership class far too seriously. The exams she gives are impossible (on one the highest score was a low 70). She assumes students will know exactly how to do something and punishes them if they don't do it the way she wants. Overall, just a class that is way more difficult than it should be.

She preached communication, and then she NEVER responded to emails. We were given generalized, unspecific expectations on assignments and tests and then penalized when we didn't just "know" what to do. The tests were consistently un-similar to what was discussed in class. She also would not publish grades until the last possible minute.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Phelps is very engaged in her class and cares a lot about the impact of her course. She wants the best for her students and is a great person. Her tests are pretty hard and mostly rely on applying the textbook to the real world. Regardless, the group projects and other easy grades will help any bad grades you get on a test.

She is a very inconsistent grader and expects too much out of her students. Her exams are entirely too unrealistic and you have to bend over backwards to try and prepare for them just to receive a bad grade. In a class full of honors students, I could count on one hand how many got over an 80%. So many group projects. 100% recommend not taking.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: Grading was entirely inconsistent. I would regularly receive a grade 5 points lower than my groupmates on group projects. She had unreasonable expectations for our final project deliverables. She was out of the room before class started one day, came into class late, and marked me as absent because I was not yet seated. She is ridiculous.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: DO NOT TRUST THE 3.8 . Terrible Professor. There were two tests. That over 50 honors students took. Not a single person got an A. It does not matter how well you do on a group project. Nobody in the class will get over a 93 on it. Her assignments are confusing and she can not write. I am astonished her rate my professor grade is so high.

For the content of the actual class (business leadership), she took it way too seriously and was a harsh grader on simple assignments. The assigned exams were nearly impossible and never lined up with the content of the class. Directions on assignments and projects were extremely vague and due dates were unclear. Great woman outside of class tho!
kinda mid

Difficult to express how strongly I recommend against taking Phelps' class. If possible, give her and her classes a very wide berth. Her exams are impossible (in a group of over 50 honors students in an intro class, not a single one got an A on either), her lectures are obnoxious and insubstantial, and you lose three percent for each missed class.

Prof. Phelps truly cares for each of her students. Her lectures are live and energetic. She loves group projects. The majority of the content from her class is straight from the textbook. Her tests are kind of hard because they are construed from the textbook. She expects lots of time and effort from her students which comes off rudely at times.
Really fun teacher but exams are really hard and confusing. Fun projects but a lot of group work.

Class is entirely about textbook material which seems extremely straightforward and common sense, but somehow exams are nearly impossible. Lots of group projects and presentation skills are important. She is huge on participation and does not grade assignments until the end of the semester. She is a really nice person who cares but expects a lot.

Class is all about the textbook. You can ace the tests by reading the textbook and grinding vocabulary. Most of the lecture/in-class stuff is unneeded aside from one or two topics. Attendance, two group projects, and one end-of-year paper report is the other half of your grade. Show up, participate once or twice a day, and you should get an A.

This class was a little too book heavy. She made all of her lectures about the readings from the book and it never really felt like we learned much. Some students found her teaching methods to be ineffective but I enjoyed her class. Easy A as long as you put in effort.

She expects EVERYBODY to participate, and if they don't then she'll call them out in class and/or deduct points from their grade. She expects lots of participation, and if you don't participate she'll get angry. She also likes having a lot of group projects and presentations. I hated the class mostly, but I think I learned a decent amount from it.

In her class, you can tell she loves and cares about each student. That being said, her class is oftentimes annoying by the fact that your grade is heavily based on attendance and group work. Her exams are impossible, but they aren't weighted heavily so it usually is not a problem.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Shes a great person but not great at teaching. Her class is mostly common sense yet exams are nearly impossible.

She's a great person and you can tell she cares about each student. She gives great feedback and is keen on the importance of individuality. However, at times she seemed disorganized and unprepared in terms of assignments and class lectures. Get ready to do group projects. She's an awesome person, I just wouldn't take her as a professor again.
Fiesty
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: It is possible to do your impact project without money, you just gotta think outside the box a bit. Prof. Phelps may seem like she wants to fail you sometimes but she really is just pushing you to do your best work. She grades fairly as long as you put in the effort. Overall, she's super fun to listen to during lecture.

Group projects. Be ready for them. Professor Phelps is a tough grader but is fair. The criteria is sometimes blurred but she believes honor students should be able to handle it. You will have to do an impact community service project. It is possible to do without spending money so do not fall into that trap.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Love love love Shonta to death, but oh my goodness she makes you work and expects a lot. Not to mention she is probably the worst at putting grades in ever.
She tries to make a difference (but never grades anything ever)
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Good professor and person. Cares about her students, but expects a lot of them. Likes students to be vocal. Always give as much information as possible when doing homework/ group projects. You will get a bad grade if she feels you didn't give enough info. Also, Shonta is very well connected within Gatton so do your best to make a good impression.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Ms. Shonta is a great professor. Tends to be a tough grader, but it was clear it was only to push us to be our best. While many of us left class agitated a lot of days because of heated class discussion, it did stretch our views on some different topics. She isn't afraid to discuss controversial topics if it will build us as leaders.

Shonta is very opinionated and will make sure you know her opinion. She shuts down class discussions as soon as they get good. Sometimes rude. The overall class is very easy, but she is personally challenging.  Very nice outside of class, but sometimes difficult to ask questions to. You never know what hair style she's going to pull out either.
Ms. Shonta is very lively, fun, and friendly.  You learn a lot about groups and types of leadership in this class.  I learned more about myself than anything else.  Take it!

Shonta is a great and fun person! Just make sure that you read all of the homework chapters at the start of the semester, there are reading quizzes. Later on you really don't need to. Her class is a little repetitive and a lot of unnecessary work, but just keep up. Learn to write to her style, for she is a tough grader on papers.

Pretty basic class, but Shonta is a great adviser and a good professor. Class focused on UK resources and adjusting to college (showing up to class etc.) Pretty easy A, but Common Reading Experience paper was graded semi-harshly.
Dr. Phillips is a very nice guy, he is passionate about what he teaches and as someone who isn't majoring in agriculture this class was very easy.

You can tell he is passionate about his job and loves plants! This class was fun and pretty easy. The only homework you do is memorizing/studying for the plant quizzes in labs every week. He grades good and grades fair

This man really loves plants and is very passionate about sharing his knowledge with students. Tim is a very nice guy who has no problem helping students as long as they show they are putting in effort on their end. The class material was not all that interesting to me, and labs were very boring but it is very do-able coursework.

Content was kinda boring since I'm not super interested in agriculture, however, I enjoyed Professor Phillips' class bc he is so passionate about this stuff. He is a really nice and laid back guy as long as you come to class & put forth effort. He didn't take attendance in my class but I'm pretty sure he failed 2 people bc they only showed up twice
As long as you review his powerpoints you will do fine.
kinda boring class but Phillips is really chill
Dr. Phillips is the GOAT, one of the best, nicest and favorite professors I've had.

Doctor Phillips is one of the nicest professors Ive ever had. However, his class is extremely boring. This man knows E V E R Y T H I N G about plants, wondering how he knows all of this information is about the only thing that keeps me awake in his class. Also the man Loves plants, like he LOVES plants. He called a tree sexy in class.

Dr. Phillips is one of the nicest professors I have had. The class itself is really boring if you are not interested in agriculture just because of the nature of the material but Dr. Phillips tries to make it as interesting as possible! Easy A if you just try, quizzes are taken online as homework with two chances and his tests are curved.
Dr Phillips was so knowledgeable about his topic it was fun to learn from him. He is very helpful and although a bit dry sometimes, he can be really funny too. He made this class enjoyable.
Very boring class, he just reads his slides word for word.  (The slides are posted online)  But the tests are easy.  He is a very nice person, and very helpful if you talk to him.
Incredibly nice person, tests are fair.

Perhaps one of the nicest instructors I have ever had.  His lectures are very easy to understand and gives great reviews to study before the tests.  He was very helpful and super nice.  I "Highly" recommend him, but I think he only teaches genetics in the fall.

Took ANT 235 with KCTCS. The class is well structured, grades are posted in a timely manner, and tests are easy. Main issue with Mink is that he never puts feedback on papers. The class has a lot of writing assignments but he never tells you what you are doing right or wrong. I'd take him again - he's a slightly above average professor.

I have a life and 3 other classes in my semester. I read and did the course work but got a D. PP Mink is not helpful and is ridiculous for an introduction course. Find a better professor and stay away from this yoyo
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I don't know who put the negative comments above, but I think they got the wrong professor. This guy is pretty good. I took the Intro to Anthropology and we had nice solid assignments, but there wasn't a lot of them. All in all.. very appropriate for an into class.

Makes you read a lot but only gives you a 10 true or false question quiz. ONLY USE 13th EDITION. He says the 14th is the same but he takes the wording straight from the 13th. If you read the chapters you will be good. He is laid back with due dates but don't slack, hard to catch up on the readings (they are really long).

On-line class, with no discussion groups, and no contact with the Professor. Chapter tests, as outlined in the syllabus, are 10 TF questions. Mid-term and Final follow that pattern. The tests are graded by Blackboard. His input consisted of grading  1 Critical Thinking essay (that took forever to get graded.) Waste of time and tuition.
So I don't know who wrote the above ratings, but he definitely didn't teach Ant345 or Hum221, whatever those classes are. Neither were offered in the Spring at UK.
Took at Lehigh night class. 3 hour block. Class was usually over in an hour or an hour and a half. Practice problems close to exams. Not hard at all. Easy class

He just simply isn't a good teacher. If you are taking him at Lehigh take anyone else but him. He's lazy, is miserable in class, and simply lets students do practice problems while he sits there aimlessly. Had to take his night class which is a three hour block, and most weeks class was over in a hour. Do not take.

This is the most misleading RMP rating. He is awful. I am now in my last semester in high level finance classes and I can confidently say this was my second hardest class in the major. His exams are ridiculous and anyone I talk to does not like him either. I've heard he gives extra credit if you give him a good rating which explains his score.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class kind of sucks. The material is hard to understand, and all the complaints about Trager are valid. But I still liked him. Classes consist of 90% example problems and occasional lecturing. Hes not very good at explaining how to do the questions and just faces the board the whole class and reads off the slides. But hes funny so theres that

DON'T TAKE! I have no idea why his rating is so high on here, I studied 10+ hours for each exam, never missed a class and still couldn't get above an 80 on any. I genuinely felt like he wanted me to fail. He also let half the class get away with cheating on the exams. If you are not comfortable buying a Chegg subscription, take someone else.

Professor Trager was very established in the field of finance. It was clear that he was very aware of the course material and did a very good job of explaining it. The only downside to his courses is the level of difficulty of the exams. Sometimes the study guides wouldn't completely align with the information on the exams making it hard to do well

If you enjoyed Peter for 300, his teaching style for 410 is very different. Lectures are more rare and abstract. His hand-made assignments have no clear grading criteria, are time-consuming, and are graded pretty hard. If you enjoy constantly researching the stockmarket and making trades this class is for you. If you want an easy A, look elsewhere.
One of my favorite professor's I've has during my time at UK. Tells it like it is. Can genuinely help you become a better student of finance, as well as a more accomplished investor.

From someone who went to class everyday, a 4.0 student, and a Finance major, the professor makes the tests extremely difficult for no reason. He puts stuff on the exams, that he does not cover and is extremely rude to his students.

I am a student that attends every class, and this was one of the deepest holes I have had to get out of. I didn't do well on one exam and it screwed me for the rest of the class. He runs through the slides way too fast to keep up with, and jumps from point to point too quickly. Unfortunately there are not many other options for this class.

Lectures consist of him reading off the slides and not giving students time to write things down. His exams are open note, but still unbelievably hard. He seems like a nice guy, but he does not get the content across well. All of the grades come from the exams, so take them seriously, study hard, and go to tutoring/YouTube to learn the content.
Great professor with real-world applications and prepares you well for further finance curriculum.

Ridiculous how people complain about this class. Anyone that struggled with exams simply did not study lol. People that say that exam content wasn't covered during class are wrong, and I guarantee that they didn't put themselves out there and ask a question. The whole point of going to class is to get better, and ask the teacher if you're confused.

One of the best classes within the finance department. Would bring in speakers that are actually relevant to the field, and can give students a good idea of what certain careers look like. Wish I could have taken additional classes with this professor.

No matter what, do not listen to the lower reviews. They're made by students that simply did not try and are just flat out salty that they didn't get an easy A. If you do what's told and listen to the feedback during the course, you should have no problem. This professor is one of the absolute best within the finance department.

Trager is probably the worst professor I've had in college. His exams are 10x harder than the homework and unless you fully understand everything he talks about you're going to have to study for endless hours. His class is doable but unnecessarily difficult especially because most of his students aren't even finance majors.

If you go to his classes you will be able to do the homework easily and understand the material as he has good lectures. However, the exams are way harder and as he says are "conceptual". He is aware students find the exams hard and not similar to the material, but he still won't prepare you for that.

Trager is just meh. The lectures are pretty pointless cause he just reads off the slides. He claims he will never test you on stuff he didn't go over and then proceeds to throw in a couple of questions we never did. Exams are like 80% of your grade too which is so silly for a college requirement. The class isn't hard but harder than it should be

Professor Trager is willing to work with each student as long as they put the effort in. His lectures were very detailed and helped tremendously with the exams. He genuinely cares about his students and communicates well with individual needs. I would definitely take him again!
Attendance wasn't mandatory but lectures really helped with exams, especially the final. Pretty easy to get an A if you pay attention.

Trager made finance fun and interesting. Comes from the industry so he knows what he's talking about. Let us use formula sheets on exams and went through lecture content at a slow enough pace so everyone who asked for help got it. Doesn't take nonsense and calls people out for not paying attention but still cool enough to give bonus for TCE's.

Trager is, nice I guess...His tests are god-awful because of the amount of curveballs he throws. The presentations and the study guides barely matched what was on the exams. The TAs were really nice and helpful though. Just be mindful of the tests that you don't know what to expect from. And yes, I did attend every class.

This is a tough course, but if you apply yourself you'll be successful. Trager wants his students to succeed, and if you ask for help he'll go above and beyond to meet individual student needs. Go to class, read your textbook, ask for help if you need it, and get an A/B.

Professor Trager seems like a cool dude. He has experience working in Finance, and he seems to genuinely want his student to learn. However, his lectures consist of him just reading off slides and doing practice problems. The exams have unnecessarily hard problems, and many of the questions are poorly written and have spelling errors.

Trager is very knowledgeable about finance having experience in-class and in the real world. He reads directly from the slides and always has the best TAs to answer questions middle of lecture and outside. Pretty chill guy. You'll need to buy a calculator for the class, homework and exams aren't bad as long as you ask questions if needed. Take him

He's just mid... not a bad professor by any means and I'll probably take another one of his classes, but nothing especially good ab his teaching either. The only complaint I'd have is that some of his test questions are just out-of-pocket difficult, but overall he's a pretty cool guy and a decent professor! also some advice: use the TA's for help!

It's just not necessary at all to show up to class since he just reads off the already accessible PowerPoint slides. The homework is fairly easy with some hard questions but he gives you two tries. The biggest complaint is the curveballs he throws on the tests. He'll just take certain concepts to the nth degree and catch you way off guard.

Lectures are very tough to sit through. Trager is difficult to reach outside of class and if you are fortunate enough to do so, don't expect more than three words. I don't think he is a bad guy and he is incredibly knowledgeable on all things finance, but I think he would be much better to take in a small class setting.

Professor Trager is great. His nontraditional background as a Wall Street currency trader brings a very different approach to the classroom which I really enjoyed. He has real world knowledge of finance and is super easy to connect with outside of class. He really cares about your success as a student if you are willing to put in the work.

Professor Trager's class was a great intro to finance. He really knows what he is talking about and structured class in a way that allowed everyone to practice and understand the concepts. Attendance is not mandatory, but I would recommend going in person, especially on exam review days as they were extremely useful. The TA's were helpful as well.

Trager is a great professor with loads of work experience on Wall Street as a currency trader.  He's a funny guy who knows what he is talking about and, unlike what others have said, announced when he was going to only hold exam review in class.  As long as you show up to/watch online class, you will be fine in this class.

Says he'll let us watch the class online since it's packed but makes exam reviews in class only without an announcement. Super annoying "learn smarts" that's just copy pasting questions for an hour and has nothing to do with exam content. Dude just seems like a jerk tbh and makes things much harder on students then they need to be

Professor Trager is one of my favorite professors that I have had the chance to learn from. Definitely go to the lectures or take advantage of his Echo Live option. He goes over exact exam problems during lecture and puts a lot on the slides that relate to concept questions on the exams. Put the work in, Easy A for sure!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Professor Trager is a good professor. He knows what he is talking about and tries to make the information understandable. As a finance major I enjoyed the class but if your not a finance major it is still pretty easy. He is very helpful with the calculator and gives lots of time to figure out the info. He goes over lots of review for the exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: From what I can see he has drastically improved his teaching from before. That being said, there is a fall off from his teaching and the students understanding. Use the textbook for concepts and listen to lectures for calculator advice. Everything else he skips past in pwpnt. It would be much better if it was a smaller class size

Overall, Trager is a good professor. He is still fine-tuning his teaching skills since he is a newer professor and has spent a majority of his time working on wall street. Although the content can be difficult and the exams are worded differently than the homework and notes, he makes himself available to help and offers a lot of TA hours.

Professor Trager is a great professor and does a lot to make the class interesting and intriguing to both Finance majors and other Business majors as well. He did go online this semester for some reason but hopefully he's doing all good. Teaches the content well and proficiently while also being funny af. Great guy and great professor!

Trager is one of the coolest professors at UK, but he isn't a great instructor. He just reads off the slides and doesn't explain them. The tests are not representative of the slides. The math/formulas and work on the calculator is really easy and he explains all that clearly, but the vocabulary and info from the book make this class difficult.

Trager is the gets a lot of hate for things that just aren't real. Big trag clearly outlines expectations and assignments and walks you through questions in class that couldn't be closer to assignments in detail. My only critic would be I wish he would care less what students think, his market updates are extremely informative, very impressive prof

Peter's class was hard in my opinion. I am an ACC major so it just seemed backwards. Great lecturer and is extremely fair when it comes to exam issues. He is accommodating as well! I had a personal issue at home & he was very understanding and allowed me to reschedule an exam. Great man & teacher, I just struggled with the material.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Trager is one of the coolest professors I have ever had. If you love the field of finance. You will enjoy the class. One biggest tip I can give is definitely know how to use your financial calculator. The content taught in class helps you learn a lot of basics for future classes. Great guy to have in your network when it comes to finding a job.

Notice how all the 5 ratings are coming up now...? Notice how before them it was all awful ratings? Hmmm wonder WHY... Trager is just a meh prof. Thought he'd be cool, but he's a typical finance-guy-boomer: condescending, self-important. Talks down at students, called us "kids". Gave decent xtra credit, but made things harder than they had to be.

Professor Trager is one of my favorites! I took FIN300 with him and got an A. He is an extremely knowledgeable professor with lots of experience in the finance industry. Trager is very helpful and supportive out of the classroom, so make sure you build a good relationship with him. Talking about the class materials, I can guarantee you a B if you k

Content and the material isnt awful, you earn your grade for sure. Put in the work outside of class and you should be fine. Only problem is his personality. Always felt like he was talking down to us, and acted like hed rather be doing his Foreign exchange stuff instead of teaching. If he had less ego Id take him again.

The class is pretty easy. He tells you what's on the exam and goes over practice problems that are almost identical to what you'll see on the exams. Lectures were straightforward and he does things to break up the monotony like doing class polls and talking about current events.

Professor Trager is great. Finance 300 is a hard class but he does his best to make sure his students succeed. He offers easy extra credit at the beginning of the semester so definitely take advantage of that! The homework can be a little long but it is definitely helpful for exams. If you need help outside of the class he is super easy to contact!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Take him for investment class. Great guy who wants to see his students succeed and learn stuff that is actually important in the real world. No rubric for anything and gives random grades though

If you think professor Trager is hard or condescendingits possible that finance just isnt for you. I had him for both 410 and 300. Thorough lectures and anything that was on the test was clearly covered in class. He is super accommodating and does not make anything more difficult than it needs to be.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Professor Trager is awesome. His grading is fair, and he is always willing to talk about things. His lectures are enjoyable, and he takes a lot of pride in making sure his students know the content. I have never met someone with so many funny stories. He responds near instantly by email. I would recommend him to anyone.

Super nice guy, very willing to do what's best for the class as a whole, very straight forward the only material you see in lectures is what's on the exams. Looking forward to join another one of his classes in the future.

Professor Trager hadn't taught Finance 300 in the past, and with up to 500 students on a zoom call it can be hard to teach that course in a manner that suits everyone. Regardless, he did an excellent job with the material and supplementary information regarding market activity. He's genuine and provides all you need to get an A if you listen.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I had a great time with Professor Trager! If you take notes and spend time working out the problems he gives and homework youll have an easier time. The lectures alone made it easier to do homework. I recommend taking detailed notes, and redoing problems before the exam. DO THE EXTRA CREDIT POLLS. Overall 9/10 I preferred the teaching style
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Trager can be condescending and a difficult person to like, but he is a decent professor. Course expectations and policies are very clear from the beginning, so it's on students if they don't read the syllabus. Exams are right out of the textbook's test bank, so no questions should be at all surprising. He tries his best to make class engaging.
Good teacher, just hard to teach this over zoom. Class is difficult by nature, and is heavily reliant on test grades
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Trager very clearly explained material and hosted helpful exam prep sessions. I was worried about this class because accounting was very hard for me, but if you study adequately for the exams you will be fine. The exams are fair, and they were open note this semester, so really no excuse not to do at least okay. Do the homework.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor Trager is always available for his students and if you care about the content you are learning, you can do well. The grading criteria is not entirely clear, but if you invest yourself and really try to learn, you will earn a good grade.

I've had Prof Trager for both Fin 300 and 410, and he is one of my favorite professors. As long as you study the material, you will be able to get good grades on your exams, nothing confusing or tricky. He makes the class very engaging and makes it fun, not just straight out the textbook lectures. If you have the chance to take him, then DO IT!

Trager teaches my favorite MBA class. His 5 min news and market review at the beginning of his class, is definitely the best part! Clear and organized teaching, very high quality presentations, connections to the real market based on his experience and lots of problem solving in the class. I wish more teachers were like him!

Overall Prof Trager's class was great. The best part of it was the introductory market breakdowns before each class. The FIN 600 material is a bit dry but he adds bits of information here and there that gives meaning behind the concepts. The fact that he is an active trader and has a lot of experience makes the lectures more meaningful.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Trager is one of the best professors I've had during my time at UK. He is an extremely knowledgeable person, and has a very expansive network in the Finance industry. Multiple guest speakers throughout the semester that make this class very fun and engaging. As long as you show up and put forth the effort, this is a relatively easy class
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I had Professor Trager for both FIN 300 and 410. I can say that 410 is my favorite class I've taken at UK. He has a lot of knowledge about finance and incorporates a lot of real world material into the courses. He is very reasonable and willing to work with students if you show you care and are putting in effort.

Prof Trager is the best!! Anyone complaining about him is just bitter that you can't easily cheat your way through his class. He teaches Finance in a way that is actually applicable to the real-world, not just out of the textbook. He is so helpful in and out of the classroom - use him as an asset! He prioritizes being there for students - love him!

Trager is a knowledgeable financier that hasn't perfected the craft of teaching. The first thirty minutes of the class are helpful to traders but unnecessary for most of the class. The worst part about him is his inability to take responsibility for his poor testing structure and constantly be condescending to students who may be struggling.

Trager is an okay professor, but he can be very condescending and he wastes a lot of class time with unrelated news updates and "what's your favorite XYZ" polls. He is a fair grader and exams are directly from the book's built-in test bank, but you will have to teach yourself most content since his class examples rarely explain the actual process.

Prof. Trager, despite the other reviews, is very reasonable and accountable for his work and understands that not all students are financially minded. He has curved tests and modified exam formats to accommodate for complaints; he's adapted to my section quite well and just because he expects the same of us doesn't make him a bad professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Trager is a lecturer who teaches a required course for 600+ and yet still manages to confuse everyone in the class. Instead of teaching he uses poll questions, weekly stock updates and world news to fill class time. He is condescending and blames you for being stupid when you dont know the material. Tests are randomized and hw is nothing like class

This was only his second semester teaching so his testing system is still being refined. As of 2021 his tests are now proctored so no finding them on the internet. He is a really smart guy but somewhat poor at explaining concepts well. Moved through example problems incredibly quick and I didn't feel like I learned the concepts.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Professor Trager is a nice guy and very intelligent in regard to finance and the stock market but the class is way too hard for an entry-level finance class. You better know how to work a finance calculator because you've got 90 minutes to do 70 problems which is utterly ridiculous. Way too many problems per test. You're gonna work for your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: He knows a LOT about finance. The practice problems in class are like the test questions. He's straightforward and understanding. Reasonable speed-wise if you understand basic math and know how to use a TI-84 or finance calculator.

Thank God this class was online and he posted the lectures. Trager is a good professor and explained the material well (I didn't even bother reading the textbook bc it was like deciphering a different language). However, he went a little too fast for people like me who don't have super financial brains so the posted lectures were a lifesaver.

Definitely take Professor Trager. His class is super easy, all the homework and tests are on chegg or socratic. He's super cool and responds fast to emails. He is very accommodating to his students' needs. However, the class would potentially be hard if tests were taken in person.

I learned more Bio. Under Dr Bonner then in my post grad degree as a DMD. I also cloned myson heavy chains for 3 years, which was eventually published, under Dr. Bonner. At the beginning of each semester his lecture hall would have 300 students, however by the end of the semester there may be 15 students left.
Thank you Dr. Bonner.
Doctor. S.
He knows his stuff;however, he does not convey the information in a way you can learn it. The book and internet resources were the most helpful during this class.

He is very passionate about the subject he is teaching. He does get lost in his lectures when he is teaching sometimes, but he is really funny and you are always learning something in his class. Test material strictly from his class notes so it is essential to go to pass the class!! Gives great feedback on what he expects from you.
Nice guy, very respected, but also a very boring lecturer.
Horrible. Tests don't coincide with what he's talking about in class and they're so hard he has to give a 20 point curve. Avoid this teacher at all cost.
HORRIBLE. Good luck staying awake. I got an A and still abhorred this professor.

Dr. Bonner is a nice man but not so great professor. He knows a lot of information and knows biology really well but doesn't know how to teach it very well. Tests are really hard but he does curve them. As long as you get like a 70 with out the curve you should get an A.

Dr. Bonner's class is tough. Be prepared for that. You don't need to go to class since he posts all the lectures online (and you can hear him better this way). The book wasn't beneficial to me because he contradicts it, a lot. Tests are curved hardcore. Wouldn't recommend Dr. Bonner's class because it is so hard. He is a nice guy though.

I recommend his online summer class. Many students who take his in class lecture have such a difficult time. But if you take his online bio class without other classes as a distraction, read the txtbook chapters before the exams, study his lecture material, & use the txtbook as a supplemental on exams, you will get at least a B. Very understanding

Bonner is a quiet, monotoned lecturer and it is really hard to stay awake in his class. He's a really tough homeworktest grader. Homework assignments in his class are essay questions when other Biology professors use MasteringBio or something more helpful as their homework assignments. He doesn't make learning interesting and seems bored himself.

He speaks in a quiet and somewhat monotone voice throughout his lectures.  With a class the size of about 250 students only about 50 attend class regularly, because he puts everything online and his note are pretty detailed.  His tests are very difficult, but he does curve them like crazy.  But, even with the curve, test grades still average DC.

He is a super nice guy, however, his teaching style just isn't one that you'll want! He talks very quietly and tends to spin in circles so at the end of the lecture, you're like, wait: what did I just learn? He gives HUGE curves on tests (for example, our first exam had 20 pt curve) but his exams are so hard, you can do bad even with that!

It seems you must truly learn the concepts to succeed in this course rather than use of simple memorization. Bonner speaks in a low monotonous tone that will make you want to ripe your eyelashes out one by one. Nice guy though, and he definitely knows what he's talking about.

Dr. Bonner is great. However, his class is difficult, simple memorization won't get you through histo lecture. Don't be afraid to ask questions and when you don't understand his answer don't be afraid to ask more lol. Don't be discouraged by low exam scores as the class is curved (I had roughly a D average on exams and ended the course with an A).

Going into this class I was terrified from things I have heard. However, I actually really enjoyed the class. If you pay attention and read his notes, you will do absolutely fine! Every test is curved, so if you get at least a C you will more than likely get an A. Attendance is not taken, but I recommend going. Also, the text book is not needed.
Test are extremely hard ! Even with the huge curves you can still fail
Hard tests, but usually a huge curve. Study early and often and you'll get an A!

I took this class online during the summer. Anyone who is considering this should realize the time commitment. It was a 6-week class with half a textbook covered. Needless to say it took a lot of reading. Bonner's test are extremely difficult, however reading the book then the class notes helped. I ended up with an A thanks to a 5 point curve.

I have gotten A's in all of the science classes at UK (Organic1&2, Calc Physics 1&2, Physical Chem etc.). I have never taken a test that is as confusing as his. His questions are so abstract you really don't know what they are asking. His notes are inconsistent with the book and can even contradict it. No A for me. The material-easy, tests-are NOT

Newsflash, bio 152 isn't easy, and when considering it is a pre-med requisite, it shouldn't be. Personally, I found the course very doable and will probably receive and A. The prof also teaches Graduate level, so he has a wealth of useful, accurate info. You may want to revamp your study habits for this class/prof. Put forth effort, & you'll be ok.

People obviously didn't put a lot of effort into his class. He requires to think outside the box and apply the concepts. Study the book and his lecture notes and you can get an A. Just average a 70 raw score on the exams and you will get an A

This is a tier 2-3 teacher. Lecture is hard to follow but demonstrates scientific thinking. knowing definitions not enough to pass, expects applied knowledge. MC exams. weekly homework assignments in short essay. gives practice exam, expect 3-5 questions on your exam from practice. read text & lecture notes, highlight main points and can pass B+

For the love of God, do not take this man's class for an easy A. In fact, I'm not sure if you could take it for an A at all. He's scatterbrained and difficult to learn from. I'm an A student and I'll be lucky to get a C. Read the book and forget going to class (he doesn't take attendance anyways). That's your only hope of passing, THE BOOK.

READ THE TEXTBOOK. Read the chapters before you come to class. He is approximately 72 years old. Often makes mistakes in lecture. People who don't study get in the 30-40%. People that study get 50-70%. A students get 70-89%. 16 point curves.

So far this is the worst professor I've had in college in terms of actually learning material. I was very much interested biology prior to taking this class. I received a good grade, though he fails to clarify what you will actually be tested on. Just read the book through. Don't take this professor, we can only hope that Bonner quits teaching.

DO NOT TAKE HIM. His class is so hard for being a 100 level course. You never know what to study, and his lectures are all over the place. His exams are beyond hard and the class average was usually 40-50% every time. Skip class, and read the book if you want to do well.

I took his class online over the summer. He never told us what material we should be studying or what topics or when. He just gave a very basic outline and that's all. You we're on your on to learn the material. He wasn't very helpful and the tests we're way hard considering we didn't know what to study.

This man is ridiculous.  He is used to teaching upper and graduate level biology classes, so something like a 100 level is way harder than it needs to be.  A prime example of the faults with tenure.  Avoid if you can, otherwise prepare to be a slave to biology.

If you want to learn a lot and be extremely prepared for medical or dental school, take his histo class! By far the best class I took in undergrad. People who say Dr. Bonner is too hard are too lazy or uninterested to put forth the effort. Fantastic professor!
Ridiculously hard tests.

Bonner is a tough one. He knows the material fairly well but the only grade in his class are the tests, and the tests are extremely difficult. Usually, a class average is in the 60's. He does give curves, but sometimes those aren't even enough to let you pass the exam.

This is not an easy class, it is fairly time consuming and you need to keep up with the reading, but it is not impossible. Difficult subject material for a 100 level class, but Dr. Bonner is very helpful, responds quickly to emails; and fair, gives large curves on the exams.
Worst teacher I've ever had! By far the most boring man you will ever meet. There is no homework and the exams are impossible, although he does give about a 15 point curve on them.

He is a really nice guy who really has a passion for biology. He was always willing to meet with me and explain anything I was confused about. The best way to study for this class is just to read the book and take notes off that. I didn't figure this out until the end and my test grades went up 15%. YOU HAVE TO WORK HARD TO DO WELL IN THIS CLASS!

He is a difficult teacher. Expect large curves on your exams, which will be extremely conceptual. He is a nice guy, but his voice is quite monotoned. For a test, know ALL of the material on the slide notes, lecture notes, AND textbook. I do not recommend taking this professor as a freshman like I did. He is extremely difficult.

DO NOT TAKE! I admit, he is a very intelligent professor, but his tests are ridiculously UNFAIR! i studied ALL of the material every single day and understood it, but still got B's on all the exams. His exams are SO SO tricky that HE even gets some answers wrong when grading them and the students have to argue for points.this will take over ur life

Dr. Bonner is an awesome guy! Class is early and people are sleepy, but lectures are relatively interesting most of the time. His tests are extremely hard, but he is very willing to help. He definitely makes you learn. I wouldn't take with other demanding classes.

Was extremely difficult! Never had problems with biology until the class. Took Bonner against my better judgement and really regretted it! Homework and test questions were very hypothetical and confusing. Curves but it is almost impossible to know where you stand until the very end.

His tests were difficult, but he curves a lot. Sometimes it was hard to pay attention to lectures, but he records everything so I would go back and take very detailed notes from the recording, which is all you need to study. Rarely used the book, except for clarification of something. A really nice guy, truly sparked my interest in the subject.
I thought he made the BIO 152 really interesting!

Honestly if you want good preparation for future biology courses take Bonner. There is a tremendous amount of material you have to cover for tests that only assess about 20% of it, and the multiple choice are sometimes wishy-washy. However the bio courses I've taken since his class have been way easier for me. Read his slide notes!

This clas is VERY hard. Don't exhaust yourself studying because you think it will help you do well, there will always be a lot of obscure, frustrating questions on his tests that you won't know the answers to. He did bump up my average a couple of points so I could get a B in the class, however. He speaks quietly in class and is hard to follow.

Dr. Bonner is BY FAR the worst professor I have ever had should be fired IMMEDIATELY. The final grade in the course is based off of four OUTRAGEOUSLY conceptual, unfair exams.  The exams are curved to a 75% average, but it seems as if the majority of the class still fails them miserably.  For a 100-level biology course, this class is absurd.

My major was biology until I had to take Dr. Bonner's bio class. Now I have changed my major and HATE biology. His class is awful. It is extremely boring and very hard to pay attention to. His only grades in the class are the four tests and they are extremely hard. He favors geniuses and that just is not fair, especially in a 100 level class.

Dr. Bonner is a very, very tough professor.  It is possible to get through his class with an A, but it will take a lot of time.  You have to pay attention in class, read the slide notes, and the book.  The best thing about his class was that he made slide notes and he recorded all his lectures on the internet.  He covers everything on the subject.

Having come into the course not getting an A in BIO 150/152 and ended up pulling an A in 315 tells you something about the course/professor.  VERY hard course with homework assignments but is very fair in grading.  curves to a 75% average (ALWAYS) on everything.  Preps very well for med school/MCAT

I had trouble stay awake in this class, he's pretty boring, but he teaches what needs to be taught, make sure to go over his slide notes, they are a HUGE help for the tests, which can be kind of difficult.

The nature of cell biology is extremely complex and complicated. The professor wasn't much of a help either. He writes conceptual exams that he doesn't even teach in class. He does curve, however, but it wasn't enough. The book was useless, and his lecture notes were useless; basically take this course if you are ok with not passing.

HARD class...need to spend lots of time studying material. read the book read his notes go to class and you still might only get a B and more likely a C. had a 13 point curve on first exam and the final is looking to be very difficult so we will probably have a big curve on it too.

Very hard class! So far our class avg on tests were 58, 58, and 57. Haven't taken the final yet but I hear he gives pretty good curves. The homework is challenging and takes up a lot of time. I do not rec coming to class-use that hour to read the book instead!!! He is extremely boring and goes off on tangents all the time.

It was very hard for me to stay awake in this class. The material covered is somewhat difficult, no matter what professor you have. Study the slide notes he gives you and you should be set for the test. The textbook isn't used very often except for some picture references.

Staying awake during lectures was a challenge for me. Personally, I just started reading the textbook during class and tuning in and out at important points not covered in the text. Emailed him I'd come into office hours to review past exams, he replied he'd be there, and didn't show up. You have to put lots of study time in for a decent grade.

Without question one of the best instructors I've ever had at any level. Tests, indeed, are very challenging, but that is the purpose of an exam - to actually see what it is you know and if you can applied didactic material to other situations. Those that don't like should perhaps re-evaluate why it is they are in college. To learn - take Bonner!

Keep in mind that this is a "weed-out" class for those looking into med school. I would not take this class if you have to take other difficult classes in the same semester. Dr. Bonnner seems like a very nice guy, but I felt like his section of this course was much harder than it needed to be. Tests are EXTREMELY difficult.

He is not the esiest of teachers, but I really didnt think he was that bad. He prepares you ALOT better for the MCAT than the othe rbio 152 teachers do. If your in this class, your probably pre-something, meaning you know how to study. Study, just like any other class, and you;ll get an A. Its not that hard. I would take him over McLet/Debs/Copper

Dr Bonner is a difficult teacher, but that does not mean he is an impossible teacher. I did really badly on the first two tests, but once I realized I need to kick it into high gear, I went to see him. He really helped me understand what I was doing wrong. I ended up getting an A, but I had to work really hard. It's definitely a challenge!

He's better than Gleeson, in my opinion, and is a LOT easier.  My average even without his huge curves was 10 pts higher than in Gleesons half.  The class is difficult because there is a lot of material to cover but as long as you put forth the effort getting an A or B shouldn't be difficult.

i just had bonner for 315...my exam grades were 66, 64, 74, 95 overall on the hw plus whatever i got on the final and got an A.  his multiple choice questions are pretty tough but i always managed to do really well on the essay.  study hard, do ALL the hw, and ask him if you have any questions and you can get an A.

Bonner's class definately requires a lot of time. Go to class, READ THE BOOK, study the slides, and LOOK AT OLD TESTS and you wont have a problem with the class. An A is definately achieveable if you put time in the class.  He tends to go a little fast during lecture, but there is a lot to cover.  He is veryy good at answering emails and is helpful
AVOID!!! Very difficult. Take another teacher or wait until a different semester when a different teacher is available. Tests are extremely difficult. Good Luck!
A really nice guy, but the class is impossible, and he can be difficult to hear/understand. I'd avoid at all costs, but BIO 152 in general seems impossible.
He is the most boring teacher I've had so far, it's very difficult to stay awake in class and his class is rediculously hard.

This class is almost impossible no matter who you take it with. Test are horrible I, didn't make above a 72 on a one. DO THE HOMEWORK, it will save you butt and read the book.  I can't say I gained much from class because he put me to sleep, but I somehow mannaged to get an A... go figure.
Very tough class. He admits that it's far too much material for one semester.  Tests are very hard, but he gives big curves.  Be prepared to study regularly.
He is a horrible teacher, dont take him at all cost find another teacher. His lectures will put u to sleep and then if u do stay awake then u have no clue what he is talking about

Bonner is very random during lectures.  Gets most of his test questions from the book, but they're application questions.  Hard test, but you only have him for half a semester. Try to avoid him.  If a different professor teaches the class, take him/her!

Unbelievably terrible teacher. Bad speaker/aweful lectures which are impossible to follow and take notes on. Ridiculously hard tests with huge curves, but not quite huge enough.  Straight A student until his class, but made a C. He is thinking of changing the grade cutoffs, but probably won't. Do not take him. You will be sorry!

Bonner is a nice guy who will give you help when approached but you can be easily confused during lectures. Countless times he has told the class wrong information. He also designs the tests so that it is impossible to score an A and very hard to even get Bs. He makes up for this though by offering 20 pt curves on all the exams.
Most people don't like Bonner because he makes you actually study very hard. He is an interesting man and eager to help when approached. Be ready to work hard and you'll do just fine.
Awful teacher.  Not very easy to follow and very boring.  Tests are horrible.
He's alright, better in his delivery of content than some of the other biology professors, but then again, that's not saying much.

Do whatever you can to stay away from Bonner...he gives ridiculously hard and impossible tests and then just gives huge curves (somewhere around 15-20 points). Not to mention how incredibly BORING the classes are.

dont take him. seriously. tests are ridiculous. the only good thing about taking him was getting have gleeson during the 2nd half of the course.  Students actually applauded the day gleeson took over.
Try studying and you will be fine.
Horrible...tests are unbelievably hard....20 point curve on last test bc class average was a 50. do NOT take.
He is my advisor too, and he is nice.  He will answer any questions you have and try to help you do better in class.
this teacher is awful GPA butcher.  Dont take
awful, sleep through his class.  Recommend palmer or cooper.  Dropped after two tests with 45 average and 14 point curves.
Large lecture class but seemed easy to talk to. It is important to attend class. Absolutely no use of phones or electronics allowed.
Professor Pittard cares a lot about the subject shes teaching, and can be incredibly engaging. However, she is not accommodating for any absences, and grades harshly.
Great professor! Extremely knowledgeable in English and super smart. TAs were kind of strict, but helpful in feedback on weekly grades. The course did take a lot of time outside of class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Pittard is great! She makes class fun and engaging, and the work in class is easy. There is homework after every class, but it doesn't take long and is relatively fun. Don't take if you plan on skipping.

I love Professor Pittard! She's so funny and engaging. Even though my section is an hour and 15 minutes, it never feels that long. I look forward to coming to class because the material was honestly fun to complete. But if you plan on skipping lectures, this class isn't for you.
She's so awesome and her class is genuinely fun

She knows what she is talking about, and her feedback is some of the best around. She is fairly blunt and can come off as a stickler, but she is funny and clearly cares about helping you become a better writer. Classes are almost entirely student-led, so I did wish that she would spend more time lecturing and helping with form/craft. Amazing prof.

I had Professor Pittard for ENG 207 (not 107), and she is an incredible professor. There were no traditional lectures just lots of writing and thoughtful peer feedback. Her class not only helped me improve as a writer, but it was also so enjoyable. If you participate and show up to class you can easily get an A.

I had Professor Pittard for ENG 207 (not 107), and she is an incredible professor. There were no traditional lectures just lots of writing and thoughtful peer feedback. Her class not only helped me improve as a writer, but it was also so enjoyable. If you participate and show up to class you can easily get an A. I hope to take her again for ENG 407

Pushes you to produce great work. Her workshops are more student-driven than professor-driven, but her feedback more than makes up for it. Very funny, but maybe not the type of humor for the more sensitive folks out there.
I did not find her to be a funny person or the least bit inspiring for those who want to write. She's kind of petty and hyper-self aware

Was on the fence about her personality and professionalism at the beginning of the year but it grew on me. She's a little odd and can be abrasive at times but it aids in her humor. Great feedback though if your actually willing to put in the work and want to become a good writer
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Prof Pittard is great, if not a little blunt. She expects a reasonable amount for a 407 class, but it can occasionally be a lot. She really cares about her students and if you are struggling in any way you can reach out and she will respond well. She does have a particular way of doing things, but she knows what she's talking about.

As long as you turn everything in on time, you will get an A. She assigns a lot of work and only grades like 45% of it, though. She is very respectful during workshop, but struggles to be personal and empathetic at times. She even forgot my name at the end of the semester. That aside, her class is not a struggle at all.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Hilarious--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lectures are fun because she is so freakin funny. LOVE THIS CLASS
I loved Professor Pittard!! ENG 107 is the BEST CLASS for UK core
THE BEST PROFESSOR EVER

Attendance isn't required for lectures, but is for breakout groups on Fridays. The TA tried to pressure you into reading your writing and if you didn't, you received a bad grade for participation. There's a ton of assignments, pretty much one every day. I did not like her, as she was slightly rude and would make condescending jokes in class.

I loved Professor Pittard. I did not like my TA. My TA was very rude and condescending towards me, to the point where I stopped going to my Friday Breakout sessions. Highly recommend Pittard, choose your TA wisely.

Monday and Wednesday class is not mandatory. watch the lecture online which is live or you can watch it at a later date. Friday break out sessions are mandatory. Reading quizzes are online and the answers are directly in the text book. Professor Pittard is amazing and is funny. No tech in the class. We have weekly homework on prompts.

Professor Pittard gives lots of assignments. Class isnt mandatory and you can watch it online. However she gets frustrated easily when people ask questions. If you email her, make sure you are very formal or she will call you out in class.

If you like to write you will not like this class. This class is taught at a beginner's level and you are limited to prompts for writing assignments and expected to complete about ten assignments a week. If you don't like homework and lectures this class is not for you. However, Professor Pittard and the TAs are amazing and can make this class fun!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Although the class is an easy A, I cannot stand ENG107. So much homework-about 10 assignments each week . Prof Pittard just reads off of her slides and class is not entertaining. Lectures this semester do not require attendance, but Friday sessions do. If you do not like writing pointless things do NOT take this class
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Class was usually a rehash of the textbook and almost always ended 10-15 minutes early. Absolutely no tech allowed out. Readings had small quizzes and the big grade was the portfolio at the end. No writing feedback on exercises and only on final project if you meet with her and ask. Textbook required and used. Super funny and makes class fly by.

This class is super easy and fun. It has been my favorite class so far. Lectures are fun because she is so freakin funny. Just go to lecture and breakout (recitation) and do the homework. It is an easy A and an enjoyable class. There are no quizzes or exams, just a final portfolio due at the end of the semester. You'll love her and won't regret it.

Absolutely loved this class and Professor Pittard. Easy A if you show up to class, which you aren't allowed to use any technology in. Homework due before most classes but they are very easy and will help you in the long run. Definitely recommend this class with Professor Pittard!

Hannah is so funny. She has a great sense of humor. Don't walk into class late and NOT expect to get called out like "Oh hey Joe!! Where ya been?". It was a very fun and enjoyable class. She doesn't push expertise and perfection not strenuous work, therefore you can actually enjoy the course.
Best professor! Learned so much from this class, and the work was fun, easy, and minimal! Wish I could take this class again!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: The class was an easy A. Personally, I found the lectures kind of lackluster. But doesn't mean they weren't enjoyable. At times, I thought time was being wasted and that we didn't go over material that was meant to be reviewed. But, again, it's an easy A. Recitation was a waste of time, however. And attendance mandatory with a no phone policy.
I thought I would hate this class but Hannah Pittard made it enjoyable and understandable. The only annoying thing is recitation. But overall I'm glad I took this class with her

I'm a creative writing minor and having personal feedback on the writing prompts was so nice. Pittard is hilarious, she has a really dry humor that makes class so entertaining. I left every lecture feeling so inspired. Attendance for the end of semester during workshop is mandatory but before then missing once or twice won't kill your grade

She is so funny, her lectures are amazing. There is pretty much always homework for her class, but it's usually doable in under 15 minutes. Attendance is part of your grade. I skipped once the whole semester and lost 4% off my final grade. You HAVE to go to class. You also lose points for having your phone out. Definitely recommend her, though.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor Pittard is amazing. She is hilarious, relates to her students and makes class very interesting. You have to show up, attendance is mandatory and she gives homework just like every other class. This has been my favorite class at UK and She is by far the greatest Professor I have ever encountered in College and High School. Take her!!!

Dr Pittard is a really cool professor. She tells stories to her students and makes class enjoyable. Before this class I didn't have much interest in creative writing but now I do. Assignments are easy, main thing is showing up to class. She has an absolute no cell phone policy. Highly suggest taking her.

I loved Dr. Pittard she was hilarious. I would definitely recommend this class and her as a prof to get an easy A and take the work load off from other major classes. There was a textbook but it wasn't expensive and you did have an assignment due before every class but they usually took 5-10 minutes. The final is also easy just a little writing.

Loved this professor! Super funny and makes class interesting! Attendance is mandatory and there is usually a homework assignment due every class day, but they are pretty short and simple. Recommend taking this professor!

ENG107 was a little frustrating because it was a lot of busy work but overall it was super easy. If you have good attendance and don't miss more than a couple of the daily assignments, you'll have no problem getting an A. Pittard is funny and she usually let us our 5-10 minutes early but she doesn't let you use any technology (including laptops)
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Professor Pittard is great. She may seem intimidating on the first day of class, but after that you will be just fine. She lets everyone out early by 5-10 minutes each class. There are 2 assignments online each week that are super early and can be complemented in advance if you need to. This is a good class to take to fulfill arts & creativity

Her sense of humor makes lectures interesting and fun! There are consistent assignments, but as long as you put forth effort, you'll be fine. This is the only class where I don't want to die each day. The TAs are good teachers, too.

Professor Pittard is AMAZING! I fell in love with this class. I came in just looking for a creative writing class as something fun to fulfill a requirement but I am now an English major thanks to this professor! She is nice, funny, and is genuinely interested in her students. If she is teaching 207, I will fight somebody for a seat in that class.

She was extremely funny and will get to personally know you out of 180 people. This class like everyone said is busy work, we had two homework assignments due every Monday and Wednesday. You have to read but usually not a lot. If it is clear in lecture you did not read, you may be threatened with a quiz. Overall, it's very fun and relatively easy.

I felt as if the class was a lot of busy work, but it was almost enjoyable and very easy to do. She's an excellent professor and will not hesitate to help you if you ask.  Your grade is mainly based on attendance and completing the work, so if you can manage that then this class should be an easy A.

I began not enjoying the class but once you understand her and what she expects of you then it becomes fun. I thought the readings were a lot of busy work but I soon realized maybe thats all I wanted to begin with.
Rude, takes days to answer emails, and her class is organized horribly.

I would not recommend taking this course with this professor if you can avoid it. She teaches nothing and relies on the textbook for everything. The lecture videos are from the textbook and not her. She leaves her TA to do everything, but in the case you do ever need to speak to her, she is very rude. She has ZERO flexibility and understanding.

She always gives a Karen and unprofessional vibe. This is the worst online course I have ever taken. She throws everything on your face with very little and poor teaching. The course materials and assignments are very disorganized. Does not have 1% of flexibility. The whole course you need to understand from the homework, and she does NOTHING.

The low rating is pretty unfair, so if you are taking her (especially STA 570) it should not be cause for concern. The class is pretty easy and she or the TA has office hours like 3 times a week, so if you are stuck it should be no problem to reach out. Group project for an online class is a tad odd, though.

She is a good teacher, I have had to reach out to her multiple times for help and she has always been super nice and understanding. As for the class, There is a heavier course load but usually it is all due on the same day once a week. The tests aren't usually too hard but as long as you pay attention to the textbook you should be fine.

Doesn't teach much, just leaves teaching to the textbook and unclear lab assignments. Not a very well organized Canvas page either. I disliked the group project since the class was asynchronous, but it was pretty easy so whatever.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This was an asynchronous online class. Compared to other online classes I've taken I felt that Dr. Pittard did a great job of keeping the course organized and communicating announcements to the class. For labs she always included step-by-step videos and a document with clear and detailed instructions.

Took it as an undergrad and it was a super easy class. Had 1-2 hours of work reading the textbook and doing online homework per week. Labs consisted of following a video on how to write the code line by line. For an online class it was well organized and very manageable. Only 2 exams, a few labs, and online homework each week that you're graded on.

This course is extremely disorganized and poorly executed. As a graduate level course I expected more. You have to teach yourself everything, a majority of your knowledge coming from homework that makes no sense. Dr. Pittard rarely answers her emails and when she does they are very unprofessional. Do not take this class if at all possible.

I took this course over the summer. She is very well organized but does not put up with bs. She is very helpful in office hours and willing to explain things in more detail when needed. Does not accept late work. Overall, she is a good instructor and genuinely cares about her students.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: The class is very disorganized & you learn everything off online textbook/program. The problem comes when you have questions, she NEVER answers emails and I mean NEVER. I hope you dont have any questions for her because it wont get answered. TA isnt the worst but they dont know whats going on either all they do is grade. Avoid if you can.
You have to work in her class, but if you show up and show that you want to learn and do your best she has grace for you.

Lecture was pointless in that she never explained anything in simple or easy to understand ways. The whole class was basically just taught from the book and exam questions didn't match what we had in homework or anything prior.
Good course, great prof.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Had to buy a 60 dollar workbook that was used little. Had to buy access to hw software. Had to buy textbook. Homework due before every class but wasn't difficult. Quizzes every week. Tests were two parts, group and individual. Individual portions were difficult and classroom style did not aid in learning material. Lectures were waste of time.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: In class you learn almost nothing, but tests are difficult. Forces you to buy a second textbook that is hardly used. Unorganized and constant mistakes in her powerpoints. I would recommend avoiding her class!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Even if you understand everything the class is made difficult by her lack of communication. If you check your phone or use your laptop in class you'll lose 90% of attendance points. A lot of group work, be careful what table you sit at.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: She is excellent at explaining concepts and solving problems in class that clarify them. Expect a good amount of group work. The exams are easy if you understand the concepts. Part of projects/exam/quizzes are done in a group you marry. Final exam was a comprehensive project. The class moves deceptively slow so best to avoid irresistible slacking.

One of the worst I've taken. She never emails back, ignored my doctors note on multiple occasions, and thinks the syllabus is just a suggestion because she changes and doesn't follow it regularly. Also assigned projects and homework with contradicting instructions so it was impossible to meet all criteria. Don't get me started on the TAs either.
never expect to get an A in this course, never !
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: One if not THE WORST class and teacher  I have ever seen. Doesn't meet self imposed deadlines. The material in the class isn't that hard to understand, but with all the technology in the classroom she tries to do too much making everything from tests to labs more complicated. She doesn't even know the lab software R.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: Avoid at all costs! It took her 3 weeks to grade exam 1. There were a few major typos on exam 1. On exam 2, she offered extra credit if you could find typos while taking it.
