She has a hard time explaining material and her lectures are very dry. She can't meet self-imposed deadlines. She hardly knows the computer language, R, which is used often.

Good intro to stats. Halfway through though, it seemed like the material got much harder and we had a lot more homework. Make sure you know how to do all the examples because those are basically the tests. I found Rstudio to be a waste of time. She tends to be a bit disorganized but is reasonable when fixing mistakes/adjusting the schedule.

This class was extremely easy up until a couple of weeks before the final. Even then, the material wasn't that bad as long as you practice it. She wasn't the greatest teacher, but DEFINITELY take her for STA 296.

She is just fabulous. Dr. Pittard is a sweet lady that is very knowledgable in statistics. She tries to make the class fun for students, and help them when she can. Best advice - be polite and involved in class, I promise it will pay off. Her tests are not easy.
Is not very responsive to emails so you might as well go ask her in person.

She gives random lecture assignments over things she barely covers and takes them for accuracy. I have a 95.5% on test average but these participation grades are in the low 80s for me. (Also due to a couple of skips). She's vague and skips a lot on topics, but does not matter cause her tests are easy. Would take someone else
She was completely inflexible and rude. Her tests are harder than anything you do in class. Avoid her at all costs.

She didn't really seem to have any clue what she was doing. Our class was built around an online system she didn't seem to know how to use. She promised us so much HW per week, but didn't assign any the whole sem, then assigned 20 long assignments and a major project in the last month. Lectures were long, and sometimes nonsensical and off-topic.

Although attendance isnt mandatory there are clicker questions & quizzes sometimes. They are supposed to be every other class (to help out with giving us more points) but she gets the clicker to work maybe once a month. Literally at least 80% of our test material is on an online system which we cant even use during the test, so tests are very hard

I did not have a good experience with this professor. She seems to have very little experience teaching and it makes it difficult to get through the class. She never actually teaches statistics and tells you to use technology or "StatKey" which you cannot use on the exam. Avoid taking her classes if possible.

The most horrendous professor that I've had at the University of Kentucky. Disorganized, easily flustered, and unwilling to help students. She teaches her classes statistics on a computer program that is not accessible on exams. Little understanding and very little ability to convey concepts to students. I also had her for STA210. Horrible.

I took stats before this class so everything wasn't that difficult for me. If you had never taken a stats class shes not the teacher for you. She goes through everything very quickly. If you don't understand you better ask or you'll fail. Homework is all online, she doesn't explain how to do things on paper so tests suck.

This class used CPR the entire time for every little 10 point assignment. (This is where you have to go online and grade every else's work and pray everything works correctly. Half of the time it doesn't.) It seemed the TA's taught all of the difficult material. The class is easy, but Dr. Pittard is not on top of things. Not hard, but a real pain.
Worst teacher I have had at UK.  Does not explain clearly.  Test make no sense.  Will assign homework at 1pm and say it is due at midnight.

If anything goes wrong in class, she won't hesitate to blame it on something that would imply it couldn't have possibly been her fault.  If she has to explain a concept, it usually ends up with her talking about irrelevant, specific details of an example of that concept, and not how it can derived or applied. Avoid.

She is a horrible professor. Extremely unorganized and not convincing that she actually knows what she is talking about. For a UK required course, she made it very difficult and a lot more challenging than other professors, from people I've talked to in other classes. The CPR grading system is completely ridiculous. She makes everything confusing.

An easy class concept-wise, but the exam questions make absolutely no sense and her 'explanations' are confusing. She is disorganized, and you constantly have to check the schedule she puts up because the due dates for things are never consistent. Good luck and hopefully you get a good TA, who will be the one that really helps you.

She is incredibly apathetic, extremely unorganized, never can keep deadlines for assignments together, and does not really teach anything. Her Prezi's are unhelpful and she pretty much has the TA's do most of the work. Just pray you get a TA that is helpful.

Meh. Nice woman, but this class is annoying. The due dates and locations are never consistent, and the tests are only somewhat related to class content. She will be nice to you, but she won't help you.

Beyond useless in engineering stats. She might be a good teacher in 120 I'm 381 she presents you with a photo copied handout that is never explained and with 5 minutes left in class gives you the answer without the process to arrive at said answer. Her lecture slides are online but formatted so that if you download them they appear as squiggles.

The most useless teacher ever! Lectures make all the material seem easy but when you go to take exam, you find out that 99% was not even mentioned during the lecture. Cannot communicate the material content to students at all! Do not take her! It is like money thrown to the garbage!
This course is useless and so is the professor. Just attend recitation and do hw and you'll get an A.

In my four years at UK, I have never encountered a professor with such a profound sense of entitlement and cynicism comparable to Dr. Pittard's. She is quick to blame her mistakes and lack of understanding on everything and everyone but herself. She is irresponsible, careless, disconnected from reality, & unworthy of receiving your tuition payments
Terrible professor, Condescending, rude and spiteful. Does not understand the material, and creates exams that focus more on obscure facts from the reading that course content.

She is by far the worst teacher I've had during my 2.5 years at UK. She's unclear and attributes any bad performance on exams to the fact that people won't come to class. I attend class 90% of the time and still struggle because she cannot teach the material and I never know what I'm doing. If possible avoid taking her.

This class is extremely difficult for what it is. She makes the class difficult just because she enjoys to see you struggle. HW has to be typed and takes days to do. Tests don't cover what she went over in class and she posts reviews 10 mins before the test. Tests are not curved even when entire class fails.

This was the most useless class I've ever taken. Dr. Pittard's experimental teaching format failed miserably. The large class size made it even worse. Dr. Pittard didn't seem to care.  Skip this if at all possible!

Rarely have I ever had more disdain for such a nice professor. The material was presented using old notes and homeworks from other professors. Rarely did we ever do anything in class. Exams were much harder than homeworks or anything we did in class. Quizes would be returned with just grades and no explanation of what was actually incorrect. Avoid.
Dr. Pittard's apathy is almost admirable. Unfortunately she doesn't appear to know the material well, much less care about it.

Horrible professor. Reads old notes that she doesn't understand and copies old homeworks from previous professors to avoid actually teaching her class. Grades are assigned arbitrarily and nothing is ever done with clarity. Beware.

Easy A but class felt so boring and pointless. She never teaches. You watch a guy talk on a video forever and its obnoxious but its easy. Her test are decently challenging but the homework always makes up for poor test grades. I never got on a personal level with her but she is always clear with what she expects from you.

Seems very nice until you actually talk to her.  She is very condescending and treats you like you're stupid. She is very unorganized, forgetting to assign things and then emailing you the night before she wants it turned in. She grades confusingly and does a mediocre job of explaining things.

Does not teach.  Has you watch someone else's videos.  Puts grades on blackboard to say one thing and gives actual grade that she wants you to have.  Won't grade and return homework so you don't know what you have missed before she gives the tests.  Very, very poor professor. Exam material is NOT covered in videos or workbook.

She was very nice and always explained the content thoroughly. She graded fairly and for the most part everyone got good grades. She's very motherly and never yells at the class regardless of the fact that the class was usually very loud and rowdy. Overall I give a thumbs up

She is such a nice teacher. She's very helpful when you have questions. I personally think the material is boring, but its a required class so as far as this class inconcerned this teacher is pretty good. You do assignments in clss every day and out of class projects every 2-3 weeks. The tests are very reflective of what you learn. Ta's are awesome

Dr. Pittard is great. Not sure what the reviewer below is talking about, but this class was cake. She explains things well, and the recitations are there to help if you don't understand. The pop quizzes hurt my grade, but she offers extra credit every day and participation is easy. I definitely recommend taking her for your gen ed stats class.

Dr. Pienkowski is one of the most passionate professors I have ever had. There is no homework and as long as you go to class and study on your own you will be fine. He goes over about 200-300 slides per exam and a lot of people found his exams difficult, but there are no trick questions and all questions come almost word for word from the slides.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Pienkowski is wise and knowledgeable. His grading is the only thing that "throws you for a loop." His lectures are content-heavy, but he delivers them well. Absorb everything he says, as I truly believe it will be useful later on. He is willing to listen to student feedback so if you are ever concerned, just talk to him.

He is all over the place in lectures/content but it is still a very interesting course. It was hard to know what would be on the exams. He does listen to his students though and answered to a lot of our feedback/requests.

Dr. Pienkowski is a very intelligent and nice man, but it is clear he is much better at engineering than he is at teaching engineering. I took him for BME 201 and your grade was based solely off 3 exams. There also wasnt much of a curve which made the class very frustrating cause if you did bad on one you were screwed.

What can I say that has not already been said, Madame Lodz is a mentor first a French teacher second, and every day you learn and grow and by the end of your course you leave better, happier, and more confident than you could ever imagine. Also. She's hilarious.
best teacher of all time
Madame lodz is one of the few teachers I've met who genuinely cares about her students. Great class dynamic and taking her class has boosted my confidence in languages so much
madame lodz best teacher of all time lets me get away with never doing hw 10/10 would recommend
Lodz is a great teacher, she's sassy yet caring. Made French fun

Lodz is an excellent teacher.  She is always there if you need help, and she genuinely cares about the students.  She is hilarious, and her class was really enjoyable.  I totally recommend her if you can have her!
Very easy going and just there to help. Grades fair, not a hard class
Kind of a rude person. And is very petty. Also terrible at teaching.

Often went over the class time. Most likely because she took a long time to do the attendance quiz. The lectures were easy to understand and the homework wasn't that hard. It's an okay class. But do not skip those lectures. The attendance quizzes are worth a lot.

Dr. Pike overly relies on lecture PowerPoints. I appreciate her enthusiasm for programming. But she overestimates student understanding and bombards you with thick academic language. In the brief minutes that we are coding C++, it doesn't clarify concepts. If you're not a CS major, good luck; class attendance is graded, but not normally helpful.

Dr. Pike cares about student success in this class. She has given a LOT of extra credit opportunity through labs and exams. If you try on all of the labs and complete work, you can get an A. You will need to study for that midterm if you don't have prior coding experience. Lecture quizzes are NOT worth that much idk what the other dude is saying.

She teaches a very detail-oriented class with highly technical and densely written lecture slides that're hard to follow. Her verbal professing isn't that bad, but her analogies are frequently obscure. She clearly cares about her students and that shows during office hours. If you are struggling with the concepts, I recommend you see her in person.

Cons: 
- Talks so much in the lecture 
- Lecture material is already online and in the zy book  (and still requires attendance) 
- Gives paper tests even though it is a CS course (code on paper)

She is a decent professor considering others in the CS department. She really excels at personal teaching during office hours though, so capitalize on those timings whenever you feel stuck on a lesson or project. Only problem is she delays attendance quiz till when class is over.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Dr. Yi Pike is a passionate teacher but she has no respect for your time, often teaching after the end of the class. Her TAs are just "graders" or "observers." They are not typical TAs who help you with your questions during labs.

Dr. Pike is a wonderful professor who really shines during office hours. She is good at explaining difficult concepts and can explain the same concept in many different ways until you have a better understanding. The projects and labs in this class are fun. Exams constitute a large portion of the grade and are difficult to study for.

Dr. Pike means well but she is very unorganized. She'll rush through her slides, poorly explain stuff, and then give the attendance code in the last minute of class when everyone is leaving. But she does do helpful coding demos in class and helps a lot on the labs and goes over them which was nice. Overall nice person but meh teaching.

If you had Pike for CS215 and did well you will also do well in this class. Pretty much the same as 215 just different topics. I found it a little easier but I think that's just because I can understand her accent more. Overall not that bad but also not that good either. The exams are hard though.

Dr. Pike was a caring professor that often had very rushed and sometimes disorganized lectures. The exams are quite challenging and on paper. However, every lab had an opportunity for extra credit. With some extra credit, and doing alright on the exams, it is an easy class to pass. Attendance is also graded every lecture and adds up fast in grades.

CS216 is very similar to CS215. Most of your grade comes from meaningless labs and two paper (!) exams. However, it comes with the added misery that you don't even have a compiler, you write code in notepad on a VM. 

Oftentimes the source code provided is poorly-written or doesn't even work. That's the most difficult aspect of this course.

I've had her for CS 215 and now CS 216. She is nice and does caring. Sometimes it can be hard understanding what she is saying, because she goes very fast, but all of her slides are accessible. She provides lots of extra credit opportunities. There are no group projects, only individual. She is accessible through email and office hours.

CS215 is very weirdly structured, and I don't know how much of that is Dr. Pike vs UK. The lectures and labs often didn't have much to do with each other. The real problem though is the exams- CS exams on paper suck, and a good portion of your grade rides on them.

Dr. Pike's class was pretty easy, especially for a CS professor. Like other CS classes your experience highly depends on your lab TA. My only complaint was the the final was WAY harder than anything in the class. Even though I knew nothing on it, I got a 70, so there must have been a curve. Why not just make a normal final and grade us fairly?

The TA's in the labs should have standardized rubrics for grading. Some TA's let stuff slide, others were hyper pedantic and would quiz you profusely over random methods, lines of code and sometimes even characters which I thought was strange. Overall, considering this is essentially an intro to c++ course it was difficult.

Horrible lecturer but really cares about her students. I went to her office hours weekly and she always gave great feedback. I always learned more in office hours than lecture. Some TAs didn't care if your output was slightly off and would give full credit, but mine definitely did so that sucked. Labs barely count so good luck on the 2 exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Caring--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Her lectures were not at all helpful to me and I actually started doing better in the class when I stopped attending. The number one thing that helped me is actually doing the labs myself. If you want to do good at a coding class actually code the projects instead of asking someone for the answer or using chatGPT. other than that good luck.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Good prof.
Pretty much the exact same as CS215. Daily attendance quizzes, locked by a code that she reveals in class. 3 projects, pretty difficult if you don't have experience.
Easy course if you do the labs and demo to the TA. Exams can be difficult if no prior experience but manageable. Ask for help if needed.

Once you get past the bit of an accent she has, she is a pretty good teacher. She some times helps with labs during lectures, so that is helpful. I would highly recommend going to her office hours if you are struggling, as she is normally pretty helpful and friendly.

Although her lectures aren't great, she would have us program with her during lecture, which is often used for things in the project or labs. She'll sometimes show up to the lab to help. And if you visit her office hours, you'll likely get an experience where she'll walk you everything. She even skipped a meeting to help me on a project.

One of the worst teachers I've ever had, and a massive reason I eventually swapped majors. I had the extreme displeasure of having her for CS215 and CS216. HEAVY accent, unintelligible and annoying, labs and exams don't reflect material at all, and lab instructions are nonsense. Her lectures are empty by the end. If shes the only option, I'm sorry.

All in all she wasn't a terrible instructor. I don't have much to say about her personally because of the size of CS215 classes. Although I will say her lectures were incredibly boring and she mostly just read from the slides and did not give examples of how to use certain logic ideas. Although, the labs did a decent jobs at teaching you.

Don't take this class unless you are required.
1) Accent heavy
2) Expects you to learn from Zybook, Zybook only accepts certain answers
3) Written exam, includes hand-writing code
4) Lab work every week, TA will ask you questions about what certain line of code does
5) Projects/Lab will take up time from you if you are taking other classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Pike is the absolute best, but class was a bit simplistic and felt less like making programs and more fill-in-the-blank files. Still a great class to take

Personally, I feel like there's too much content to effectively teach it all in the amount of time she's given, but she works well with what she was given. Dr. Pike is clearly very knowledgeable about CS and does a pretty good job teaching the content in a short time. I miss ZyBooks, though.

Info from five slides gets stretched into a single lecture, which I don't like. Otherwise, she's fine. She really cares about her teaching. Clear powerpoints. If you actively listen in class, she does fine, but it is possible to learn just by completing the labs as I did. Exam questions are predictable if you look at the sample Q's that she posts.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The only issue I have with her is the fact that she doesnt have all the information on the slides. She puts in a lot of effort and is willing to help however possible. Extra credit is available on most assignments. If you put any effort in, youll get an A. I like that her grading rubrics are exceptionally clear.
class is hard itself. She is the best tho. Good professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Respected

reviews.comment: I don't get why her score is so low. Had her for CS216, she was excellent. Yes, her english isn't the best but she posts all the lecture slides immediately after teaching them, and she is the kindest and most helpful professor I have had while getting my CS degree. During office hours she will explain anything with complete kindness.

The class is Powerpoint heavy, which is not the best way to learn how to code. I succeeded just by completing the Zybook and doing the lab assignments/projects. Some people find it difficult to learn from her because of her accent, but she's genuinely trying to improve. Really, it depends on if you personally need an instructor to learn.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: There are few problems with Yi Pike's course beyond just the accent which is pretty strong. The largest issue that I have is the grading scale. The exams adding up to 45% of your grade is simply ridiculous. There is no reason that a coding class should have exams that come down to vocabulary tests. Great woman but the class could be much better.
Hard to understand accent and moves very fast. Lots of labs, 3 projects, both of which can seem quite unorganized but once you understand what they want you to do, not too difficult.

Don't even bother going to class as she posts the slides that she reads over. Hardly anything learned in class helped me with the lab assignments. If a student with no prior coding experience were to take this class they would struggle to even pass. The exams are also a joke. Gonna need to ask someone who took the class prior about those.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Pike is a great person. However, she tends to go very fast in her lectures and she is very hard to understand. But, at one point, she curved our exam 10 points but did not tell us because she wanted us to have full confidence in our coding ability. Incredible human being, very passionate, but hard to grasp lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I enjoy the course. The lectures can get a bit boring at an hr & 15. I do feel as if I learn more from the Lab, but I feel like thats the nature of computer science. Hands on experience is important! Also, you can earn a ton of extra credit. Studied a normal amount and have gotten 100 & ec on all the Labs, plus 100 on midterm and lab exam.

The midterm exams for this class focused on content that was rarely mentioned in class or just not taught in general. We were not taught the stuff we were asked about on the lab exam, which everyone except the people who have past experience in C++ bombed. Absolutely inexcusable.

She stepped in around halfway through the semester to take over our 215 class, and she was a solid professor. She was clearly knowledgeable about C++, and she had us program along with her during lectures to help with comprehension. She goes through lectures pretty fast, though, and can be tough to understand until you're used to her lecturing.

Yi Pike was super nice and definitely wanted you to pass. The class (CS216) as a whole was relatively easy especially if you did well in CS215. She can be kinda hard to understand at points as she does have an accent and moves quickly, but she will definitely go back and answer questions if you ask.

I can't speak on difficulty because I already had years of C++ experience when I took this class, and I never had CS 215 because I took a bypass exam, but Dr. Pike offers extra credit, and you can turn in assignments a few days late, so I think this class should be pretty easy to get an A in. She's really nice too.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Nothing really extraordinary in this class. Do your work and projects and you'll do just fine honestly. You should be able to pull off a B at least just by doing your work. I didn't get any extra credit for labs and turned most things in late and still pulled off an A
She is TOO FAST! Plus, the exam questions have very little to do with what we talked about in class. I wish there was a textbook so I could have that to help me.

This class was AWFUL. Honestly the biggest waste of my time. While the course is required for engineering, I did not learn anything I didn't already know from previous classes or prior knowledge. You have no need to go to class she only takes attendance once a week through canvas. She gives extra credit on labs and overall should be an easy class.

She is very hard to understand and she will try to help you during the labs and office hours but you normally leave as confused as you were when you went in because shes so hard to understand. She assumes you learned everything in CS 215 (most of us didn't) and did not review, nor does she assign a textbook making learning almost impossible.
This class moves super slowly if you understood CS215. Dr. Pike is really nice and obviously cares about her students. Lectures are decent and she's amazing in office hours.

The lectures are very boring. Not to be mean, but I could not really understand what she was saying. I learned everything that I needed to from youtube. I absolutely love programming, but I could not get behind the lectures. She does care, and she is inspirational to a degree, but I would not recommend. The way she explains things is also unclear.

Mostly reads from lecture notes in class - all of which are posted online later. However, mandatory attendance taken using TurningPoint clickers. Explains concepts well, and is good to talk to outside of class.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: She cares so much about students. Honestly, if you think this class is bad take it with another prof and see what you think. She is total understandable and a little funny on top of that.

Professor Pike cares about her students' success but in this last semester, a lack of teaching within 215 led to a breakdown of the content. Half the semester was review, including the midterm. Most of the second half was review as well. The projects and labs were hard to read and understand. Her lectures were extremely boring. BUT she posts slides

Dr. Pike cares about her students' success. If you ask her for help after class with a project or lab, she will work with you until you get it working. Her lectures are insanely boring, I think I only actually paid attention 2 class periods. Just use that time to work on labs/projects. Sadly, there is attendance. Labs can be very vague sometimes.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: I took Dr Pike for CS 216 in Spring 2017. Dr Pike is a smart woman and she cares about her class, but I think she happens to have some wrong ideas about  how learning should work. She gives endless lectures without any real student participation and gives dull fill-in-the-blank quizzes over those quizzes. The assignments are good, make you learn.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. Pike is extremely sweet. She genuinely cares for each of her students. Every single assignment has extra credit and exams typically do too. Her lectures are quite boring and sometimes she is hard to understand and pay attention to. However, she is very fair on what little she grades and the TA's are typically very lenient on grading.

You get nothing out of her lectures that you wouldnt get from spending a few minutes reading her powerpoints (which she posts online, fortunately), but attendance is mandatory. The code she gives you for projects is also generally hard to read.
Can't understand her half of the time. She teaches straight from the powerpoint. Gives a lot of extra credit though.

Dr. Pike is quite friendly and she obviously cares about her students a lot. She is helpful and gives good feedback. Lectures can be dull but they explain the material clearly and you will learn a lot if you pay attention; she can be pretty funny. I have a lot of respect for Dr. Pike and would gladly take a class from her again.

The absolute worst professor I've ever had. She cannot teach the material at all so you'll have to teach yourself or get outside help. Her lectures are boring, confusing, and do not help with the assignments. The lab assignments and programs are very difficult and the tests do not cover what you did in the labs.

Lectures are boring, but she takes attendance and has pop quizzes. A lot of material is simply not explained, so either go to your TA's office hours or go online. Exams aren't very hard compared to the rest of the course. Don't bother with the textbook.
The lectures were less than helpful and often spent large amounts of time, sometimes weeks, on subjects that were quite simple while not covering things related to the homework being assigned.
You are in for a crazy ride if you do not stay on top of your work, an Youtube will be your bestfriend.

Go to lecture to get an idea of whats going on, then go home and learn the details about it on YouTube. She has absolutely no american accent which makes the lectures a little rough, but you get used to it.
Her lectures and the actual assignments have very little to do with each other

You can get an A if you do well on the programming assignments and projects, which is not a problem if you like to code.  Lectures are straight off powerpoint, so you'll probably get bored.  She tries to break up the pace by asking questions and board exercises.  She's there to help if you have any ?s

Yi Pike definitely tries hard in her pursuit to help you learn programming, however, she isn't really great at it. Her slides sometimes have various typos and the material covered isn't always helpful. Make sure you start labs and projects early, as projects 3&4 and Labs after 9 start to get very, very hard. Hope your TA is helpful!

Her lectures are insanely boring, and while she tries so hard, she doesn't do a great job explaining the material. Class is even easier than CS215 though; most labs are pretty short and most of the essential code for the projects are given in lecture. Exams can be challenging, but if you do well on labs & projects, grades aren't much of a problem.

Dr. Pike is the worst professor I have ever had, and what makes it worse is that she is  trying very hard. Her clarity and comprehensiveness is non-existent. You will have no idea whats happening unless you go home and watch  different lecturer online. Easy grading, but you will waste a year of your college career. She should not teach.

She is a horrible lecturer, so  Expect to learn a ton in recitation!! In the beginning assignments aren't too bad, but make sure you get in a habit of starting the lab assignments earlier, after the first 3 they can be difficult!

Yi Pike is a very hard professor to understand. Her lectures are extremely boring and the PowerPoint will hardly teach you at all. Everything learnt is on your own or peer based. However, her course load is very easy, and she is an easy grader. Besides midterm and final, if your programs work she gives full credit.

If I didn't love programming prior to this class, Yi Pike would've most likely made me change majors. She regurgitates power-points in class. If you manage to understand her through her accent she will just put you to sleep.  A disgrace to the CS department  to have such a boring professor teach what could be such an interesting course.

Only had a midterm and final test.  Gave quizzes randomly in lecture.  At times she was hard to understand and lectures were boring.  Some vital information to do assignments was never taught, so google was a necessity.  At her office, however, she was more helpful than any other professor I have had.  Easy class.

She's nice, but she just reads off slides. It's okay during the first half of the class, which is basically CS115 in C++, but you'll have to Google all of the later material to really understand it. The class itself isn't particularly hard; assignments & exams take thought, but aren't stressful. DON'T buy the book, you'll never use it.
she is tough or she want to be tough. i can't understand what she said. she is one of the worst prof. she did not do any make up or extra grades

Her English is very, very poor.  Gets flustered by simple questions in class.  Even when following her notes, she's not clear.  Fortunately I already knew most of the material in this class.  Tests are pretty annoying "spot-the-error" kind of  stuff.

Worst professor in the CS department, and that is really saying a lot... I have a decent grade, but the class is entirely unhelpful. She covers material from previous courses so no one pays attention, and gives labs that require multiple sessions so that you end up with tons of outside the classroom work. Avoid at all costs.

Easily the worst assignments ever given by a CS teacher at UK. She asks you to rewrite defined standard libraries. Couldn't be more disappointed with a lack of creativity in programming projects. Class is rigid and annoying. Not difficult, but if you are on the border about your affection for programming she will make you absolutely hate it.

Attendance: The quizzes and attendance are random and not daily, so make sure to go to class as missing one day can chunk your grade. Sometimes you will have a lab and a large program due the same day, so WORK AHEAD. Her grading criteria is way more clear than Debby Keen's and it is not hard to get A's if you read directions. Exams are kinda hard.

Programming assignments were EXACTLY like CS215, while this is a follow up class (CS216). She realized this about halfway through the semester and tried to cram the whole semester into a final exam, preparing the class minimally for either that exam or the midterm exam, causing massive drops in grades across the board because of unprepared students
Not a good teacher. Does not cover all course material described on the syllabus. She is extremely easy.

Dr. Pike is a nice woman who tries very hard to encourage student participation and understanding, but her delivery of the material is not effective at all. She reads from pre-made PowerPoint slides and falls apart if you pose a question in class. Lots of graded quizzes, so go to class. I self-taught myself most of the material, which wasn't bad.

He does not assign any homework and his tests are a direct reflection of the class and the  topics covered. He is very knowledgeable of the real estate market, and willing to discuss almost any finance related topic with students outside of class. This is a great choice for one of your finance electives.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Best teacher I have had at UK, knows the topic ridiculously well. Makes sure everyone understands something before moving on, but keeps your interest the whole time. Each exam (2) is over 30% of your grade so if you bomb one you pretty much cannot recover, the rest comes from quizzes. NO TEXTBOOK

He really goes out of his way for students. He'll change due dates if he knows you're busy, and he treats you with respect in the lectures. He also teaches with a lot of examples and gives you time to work them out in class. I definitely recommend taking his class.
easy to understand
One of my favorite teachers. He thinks on a big scale, and teaches students to form a broad view of life.

Very interesting professor, liked to ramble alot during class. He had the TA's grade the papers, so it was confusing what was expected of us. Class discussions were always very interesting, and unlike other professors he facilitated the discussion.
A very dedicated teacher who loves to discuss many topics and has funny stories to share. His downside is that he fails to grade many of the papers when he has a TA who can do them instead.
Menguc is a lot of fun.  He knows a lot about nanotechnology, but is not always clear about what he wants from you.  Many papers were assigned with little direction.

Not at all cool. Dr. Menguç requires every person in the class to say one thoughtful thing each day for mandatory participation, yet spends 30 minutes of a 50-minute class on a rambling, irrelevant lecture, in a class of 20 people. Love the Honors Nanotechnology track, but this class almost killed me. Oh, and expect to read a lot of terrible books.

Great professor. Makes FIN 410 easy to understand. That being said, it is a hard class and showing up for lecture is the only way to get an A. Also cares about his students future success, which is something that isn't always there.

Gives a lot of opportunities for extra credit. No homework so the exams make up 80% of your grade. You do get a note sheet on the exams but they can still be difficult. He is very knowledgeable about the topic and cares about you getting where you want to be. Show up to class and pay attention and you will have no problem. Would take him again.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: You get plenty of opportunities for extra credit. Not a lot of homework, but the exams are pretty difficult even with a cheat sheet. Overall, I would definitely take this class with Pliszka again! Also, he gives you great podcast and book recommendations!

He comes off as a stuck up, typical finance bro -- but you can't help but respect him. He knows what he's talking about, and wants his students to succeed. The course is tough because he stopped giving homework, so ur grade is mainly exams. You do get a cheat sheet on exams, but sometimes its not enough. Just attend class. He gives up to 50 EC pts.

Professor Pliszka is the best professor at the University of Kentucky. You will learn so much about Finance. He truly wants his students to succeed. Several times this semesters he told us that he cares more about us excelling in our careers than in his class, so he spent class time giving us advice about what we can be doing now to succeed.

You will either hate or love this guy, but I loved him. He worked in finance and is very knowledgeable about it, but sometimes his straightforward approach can come off as rude but he really is a nice guy. He stated that he will be moving away from group projects come Fall 2025 as he is teaching in Kincaid, so it will be more exam heavy.

Overall, Pliszka is extremely knowledgable in Finance, but he is not the best professor. Sometimes he struggles to dumb down complex concepts and lectures can be difficult to stay engaged. For exams, you get a cheat sheet, but even with it the exams are very difficult/heavily weighted. The group project isn't to bad if you have a good group.

Knows what he is talking about finance wise, but he is just not a teacher. Lectures are beyond boring and he is very arrogant. If you raise your hand and don't know exactly what you're talking about he will make you look and feel stupid. Sorta nice guy but it's clear he wants you to know how much money he has, was mentioned many times. Finance bro.
He basically reads off the slides and doesn't provide clear instructions for the exam, though he does allow us to use a cheat sheet during the exam. Do not take him if you hate group project.

he is kind when you ask questions, but he is never clear on any of the requirements not even on study guide. He is not a professor so he is not a good teacher. he just reads off the slides and just rambles a whole lot of nothing. if you dont like group work maybe this teacher isnt for you.

He is not the best but also not the worst professor. I was put in a bad group for our Stocktrak project so I had a lot of struggles during the class and he also enjoys rambling during class so he gets into more real-life scenarios. I would have prefer another professor personally as I feel he is not for everyone.

He is a good guy, but sometimes not the best professor. He is super funny and very knowledgeable about Finance, but he sometimes makes it hard to sit through his lectures. The exams come directly from the slides, do not study the homeworks for the exams, the group project is not hard if you plan decently ahead. Do the extra credit he gives.

I'm in my final semester and looking back Pliszka is one of the coolest professors I've had. He has a ton of real world experience since he is actively the president of a wealth management firm and he constantly draws on his personal experience and knowledge to make the class interesting. He treats every student as his equal and with respect.

Every lecture just felt like he wanted to hear himself talk. That said, you get a lot of extra credit opportunities, and his tests aren't hard (you get a front and back note sheet). He was a tough grader on the StockTrak project.

Prof Pliszka is one of the best professors I've had. He takes some getting used to, as he is very knowledgeable about finance and sometimes doesn't explain well or moves too fast. He gives lots of opportunities for grade improvement and is very kind when you have questions. The class isn't hard if you study and just try.

Pliszka is the most real professor I've had. From the very first class, he treats every student as an equal. His lectures always start with real market talk that he allows students to lead. Exams are easy if you go to class and listen. My one major complaint is that homework never matches up very well with class material. Chegg is your best friend.
He is a great professor and wants you to succeed

His lectures are so boring it's almost impossible to stay awake. If you don't already have any coding skills before you enter this class expect to put in more work than other students. I didn't have any experience and struggled. I managed a low B putting in about 6 hours a week on homework.

Paul P is actually kinda funny if you bother to stay awake. Material is super trivial and exams come directly from his notes. He's not trying to make the class hard, if you put the smallest amount of effort in, you'll be fine.

the course was easy but i had knowledge prior, the exams weren't bad, the programs did well to put into practice what we learned in class, but he is the most boring guy ever. i managed to sleep through all the lectures. the labs were better and where most of the learning was done.
super boring.  i had no idea what was going on, if it wasn't for my lab group i dont know what i would've done.

This class taught me a lot and was super easy. My biggest complaint is that the programs were really stupid, I wish the assignments were more interesting and useful rather than card games. He grades really picky when it comes to test cases and designs, but goes easy on programs. Overall, I enjoyed the class. Not time consuming but you still learn.
Knows what he's talking about and is helpful in class. He goes over the homework and quizzes/lab exams so you understand it. I really enjoyed this class!

Lectures could be boring, but it's hard to teach programming in that setting. He always attempted to make things interesting and was helpful when I needed help at one point. Tests reflect what was taught well and are comprehensive. This course requires a lot of work.

The lectures were horrible.  He's not a good public speaker and could barely hear/understand him in the large lecture room.  Without help from my TA I wouldn't have done as well in this course. Sometimes I doubted Piwowarski's actual knowledge of this subject.

Programing is a good class if you are interested. The lecture is good to go to for attendence and doing other assignments for this or other classes. Good professor, its just hard to learn computer stuff from a projector
Good teacher. Straight to the point. Easy tests and quizzes. Will need coffee to stay awake in lecture.

Very sweet man. I always went to class and worked on other hw, but he can answer questions. You're best bet is to read the book, do the assignments before you get to lab, google what you don't know, and then ask questions to get the things finished. Quizzes and final were straight out of his study ?s.

I did(do) not care for this professor. I find that his lectures are less helpful than just reading the book. Actually, attending lecture has left me much less confident on the subject countless times. He can be humorous, but his teaching style is not something that I have been able to mesh with. I recommend someone else.

Very dry, but in my opinion, quite humorous. He is an extremely nice guy. Fairly boring class but his little random jokes keep me interested enough. I would recommend taking this class. If you put forth any effort on the programs, should be an easy A

Very dry, and boring! Taking this class, I had previous programming experience so this class was cake for me, but it you don't he's an O.K. professor. Not the worst at teaching but definitely not the best. Get the textbook for sure because the quiz questions are right from the end of chapter review questions.

Definitely one of the worst professors I have ever came across in academia.  Lab and homework assignments are confusing.  Most material looks as if it was taken from another professor who taught the class.  Avoid him at ALL COSTS!

Good teacher if you have some background with coding, otherwise it's kind of difficult to learn from him. All in all, a nice guy and helpful if you're willing to talk to him. The assignments are not that difficult, and if you're having trouble he's ready to help. He really knows a lot about programming and I'd recommend him for this class.

Worst professor I've ever had. Very easy assignments and tests, but he cannot speak in public. Often comes to class unprepared, with typos in the demos he wants to show. Not knowledgable about programming AT ALL. VERY boring lectures. Continually repeats himself and contradicts himself. If you need an easy A, he's your man. Otherwise, avoid him!
ugh....unless you want to watch your brain ooze out your ears from sheer boredom, STAY AWAY!
Explains clearly, very helpful w/ projects, dryly funny. Projects appropriately challenging. Cares that students learn, but realistic that he can only do so much; students have to put in some effort.

He adjusts his grading scale so that the class is harder.  His tests were fairly confusing, too.  The guy is boring as all hell to listen to, but he can be funny.  The programming assignments were fun.
Very boring class.. but extremely easy.. and he's a pretty funny guy.

He is such a funny old man! His drawings never make sense, but I always got a good laugh out of his class. I do have to say though, if I didn't find humor in his stale personality, it would be an exceptionally boring class...
Hes one of the reasons why i droped out of the CS department.  They really need to re-evaluate their teachers.  Are they trying to kill you with boredom?
A very, very dull class.  My friend and I have dubbed the day we have this class together as Frappuccino Day because we have to make a stop at Starbucks before his class in order to stay awake.

Paul P. has the personality of a wet dish rag. His blandness is the only thing that is really interesting about him - he repeats the same jokes ("It's pronounced just like it's spelled if you are Polish"), notes, and assignments every semester.
It is very hard to stay awake in his class.  He does not explain the material that well.

Pepiwo is nominal. Boring lecture, mildly helpful. Little point in attending lecture because all the notes are online- except he sometimes gives a very few critical notes only in lecture- frustrating.
Had him for a lecture class, but he didnt lecture. so it wasnt that bad... but if you watch when ever you see him standing his hands are tucked under his arm pits...can we say "SUPASTAR!!!"

Oh Brad. This amazing prof cares so much about his students, it's unreal. He intertwines his labs, lectures, and worksheets to maximize student success. I've never had a class so seamless in integrating so many different facets in a way that actually does increase student understanding. His averages for exams are 75-80% because HE TEACHES SO WELL.
Seems to really care about how you do in his class. Gives lots of extra credit and a lot of partial credit on tests. Very good and clear lecturer as well. Definitely recommend for physics 1 and 2!

The class is a hard class and the professor doesn't help at all. lots of group projects. Actual lecture takes about 10 minutes. reviews.comment: Dr. Plaster is a very kind professor. I averaged 75 on the lecture exams and still got an A because of quizzes, in-class worksheets, and lots of bonus points. He is very nice outside of office hours. Definitely take the teal class and know how to solve all the practice problems.

Dr. Plaster has been one of my favorite teachers thus far at UK. I was worried about taking physics due to all the horror stories I had heard, but this class was great. I would definitely recommend taking the teal version of physics because it group work focused and if you get placed in a good group at the beginning you will do fine!

Dr. Plaster is great! This class is perfect for those that have a hard time learning in lecture-style classes. This class is a short lecture then working in small groups through practice problems so that you can really learn HOW to do the problems. Attendance & quiz points are practically given to you, tests are curved, & an 85+ is a an A.

This PHY 211 class was structured as though the students were supposed to teach themselves. Lecture took about 10 minutes tops and then the rest of the time the students worked on worksheets together. As someone who has never taken physics before, this class was SO difficult and stressed me out till I dropped it (& I got A's in CHE 105/107). AVOID!
My mistake was taking physics the same semester as calculus. Do they purposely schedule physics exams to be the morning after calc exams? Plaster is a good teacher though.

I had Dr. Plaster my first semester at UK for PHY 151. The class was difficult, but Dr. Plaster is a very good teacher. Textbook was rarely used and notes are posted on BB. I recommend taking Dr. Plaster if you have to take a Physics class!
This class was so easy! Maybe because the course is the easiest.
An 85% for an A in this class is ridiculous. Class is tough, tests are hard. Plaster is a nice guy though.
Great guy but his tests are very hard and grading scale is unclear. He needs to make an 80 an A in the class.
Dr. Plaster is a great teacher. Very enthusiastic. Really helpful. Astonishing turn-around time for emailed questions.
Great professor！（He graduated from MIT.)The lectures are very clear. Nice person.
This class is so easy it is a joke!
He doesn't teach well, he basically shows you elementary examples in class then assigns 25 of the hardest homework problems.....I would not suggest taking him....
She is very knowledgeable about the subject.

For pre-nursing majors about to come in for their freshman year, this is going to be your hardest class... BUT it is very possible to get an A. Do all the HW's and labs, start studying a week before your exams, and use the HWs for that unit to study for the exams. Dr. Platt is not a mean or even tough professor, but she does expect effort.

reviews.comment: anatomy 109+110 - she's the only teacher. she's been on probation because everyone is failing. its not too bad but you CANNOT study the night before. go get help and study for the tests with friends a week in advance at least. a B/C is manageable

Very hard class. Not everything on the exams is on the powerpoints so good luck. Definitely knows her stuff though. One chance for extra credit my semester but only increased my grade by .4. Won't round an 89 to a 90 no matter how bad your GPA needs it.

reviews.comment: Tough class, but she makes it bearable and is very professional, always wants to make sure the class understands the information and does not talk down on students when they ask embarrassingly simple questions. The class went down the toilet when she went on maternity leave and realized how lucky I was to have her. Stay ahead on assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Kristen is very passionate about anatomy. She makes sure she tells you EVERYTHING about the body systems. She lectures really fast which makes it hard to follow along. Luckily she uses ECHO so that's great. Be prepared to study every day for exams.

It is anatomy. There is little way to may this content easy. If you have to take this class: study hard. The content requires this. You can re-watch the lectures on ECHO and see she makes valuable side comments that she pulls directly for her exams. RE-WATCHING and READING are essential. If you're interested in the content you will do very well.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Tests are tough--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: By far my favorite class this year, but definitely a tough one. Dr. Platt seems incredibly intimidating, but is one of the most approachable people when you actually talk to her. She really goes above and beyond to make sure her students have the materials to pass. Study hard and youll earn an A! Her tests are fair, and she goes over everything
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: This class covers SO much content, so the 60 question exams are tough. Print out the powerpoints before class and invest in some colored pens for drawings in class. Dr. Platt seems intimidating, but she was SO approachable when I went to talk to her in office hours. Just do your best and know HOW and WHY stuff works without looking at your notes.
so hard but if you study hard the tests are fair
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Dr Platt is one of my favorite teachers, She is very caring and is very very approachable. Her class is challenging but if you study hard and keep up with the lecture content, an A is very achievable. I felt the tests were fair and represented her content well. Work hard, Study hard, and you're good to go.

Dr. Platt is a great professor. if you get to know her, there is almost nothing she won't do to go out of her way to try to help you. The material is interesting and presented in an interesting way. They're not always boring power points, there's online videos, guided drawing sessions, and labs are always interesting.

Dr. Platt is by far my favorite professor on campus. Her tests are tough, but if you go to lecture, study hard, and go to office hours for help then getting an A or B is likely. She tries to make lecture as interesting as possible and really cares about her students! Would definitely take this class again.

Dr. Platt is by far my favorite instructor at UK. Rarely do you find a teacher who genuinely cares about the welfare of the students like Dr. Platt. I wish she could teach all of my courses. She is the standard by which all other instructors should be evaluated at UK.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: You get out of this class what you put into it. If you study hard then you will do good and receive good grades on the exams. Her exams are exactly the information she puts in her powerpoints and she repeats key points. You have the ability not to go to class but i definitely would if you are wanting a good grade.

Theres no doubt this class takes effort but does pay off. Dr. Platt is great, she gives heavy lectures that seem overwhealming at first but repeats key concepts over and over until the class seems comfortable. Almost everything you need to know will be covered in class however its YOUR responsibility to learn the material and be able to apply it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Amazing professor! She explains things really well and gives real life examples so you understand better. If you go to the lectures, take notes, do ALL the homework and STUDY; you will do well! She gives you all the tools you need to succeed. Go to lectures!! Don't only watch echos. I promise it helps. Wish she was staying at UK :(

Dr. Platt was incredible. She always explained things as simply as possible, and she was very accessible outside of and during class. She gives the option to ask questions during lecture, so take advantage if you don't understand something. Even though Dr. Platt helps out in lecture, you will not pass if you do not study a lot. Be prepared.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Caring

reviews.comment: Platt was an incredible lecturer and the content was both interesting and relevant. Getting an A takes a lot of hard work and time spent. Dr. Platt is very nice and knowledgeable in the area of anatomy. She does a great job teaching. Classes are recorded and posted online to watch at any time you'd like.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: This was definitely one of the hardest classes I have ever taken. Take every homework assignment and lab seriously from the start because a few points can make a huge difference in the end. You definitely have to put many hours into this class but I found it interesting, although challenging. Definitely does its job as a weed-out for pre-nursing

Dr. Platt is amazing, she wants you to succeed and from day 1, and gives you the tools to do so. She has a point based class so as long as you earn a significant amount of the total number of points through the semester you're okay! Hard to get an A but a B is very manageable especially bc homework and labs help as much as exams do with your grade.

Dr. Platt is an amazing lecturer and gives really good notes- if you are in her section, do NOT skip class. You need the information. Several people came over from the other section of 109 to get her lectures instead of the other prof's and said they got better grades on the exams. You have to work hard for your grade but she is a good prof.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: This is the hardest class I have ever taken and no matter how much I studied I couldn't do well on the tests. The tests are all application and if you can't do well on the tests you better get a 10/10 on just about all the homework assignments or you wont pass.

Dr. Platt is an intelligible professor who is superb at explaining material and breaking it down. There is a lot of material but reviewing lectures, notes, and Wiley chapters makes it easy to comprehend. All material needed for tests is provided to you, so making an A is obtainable.

Dr. Platt is by far my favorite professor I have had while at UK. She is extremely knowledgable and provides many resources for success, many of which other students overlook. It most certainly is not an easy A, but if you apply yourself and are willing to spend time on it you will be very successful in this class.

Dr. Platt is a good teacher and is very knowledgable on what she teaches. You have to put work into this class if you want to do well. A lot of people say this class is hard but if you put the work in it is very possible to do good! She has echo which I listened at least once (usually twice) and took notes on the important things she mentions in her lectures. If you go to class, listen to the echo, take notes, and study at least a week in advance for her tests then you'll be fine!
This class was so hard. Do not take it unless it is required for your major. Good luck. The only thing that saved me was getting 10/10 on almost every homework assignment and lab.

I learned a lot of this stuff in high school and already understand it but the way she explains it confuses students even more which is NOT a god dream. I wish I could say good things about Kristen Platt because she is a nice person but I'm sorry I did not learn well from her teaching techniques.

reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

If you put in the effort you CAN be successful and Dr. Platt is there for help.

Platt is a good professor considering how difficult the material can be to teach and learn. In order to get a good grade, you will need to STUDY! reviews.comment: Dr. Platt is an amazing lecture that cares for your knowledge of anatomy. She is very helpful if you are confusing on any topic and is great on emailing you back. You will have homework and labs are mandatory. Overall great class.

She also is clearly knowledgeable in what she teaches. She gives you everything you need to know, its up to you to put in the time and effort studying.

Great professor, very knowledgable! But you will not pass this class if you don't take it seriously, recommend reviewing everyday!

reviews.comment: Dr. Platt was great, but her class was tough. You get out of it what you put in, so make sure you study, study, study! Go to every class in order to succeed! As intimidating as she looks, she is actually really nice.

Dr. Platt is a very nice lady, but be ready to study!! This class is definitely a weeder class for Pre-Nursing students and is very difficult. reviews.comment: Have to put in lots of work.

I loved Dr Plank- I took this class for fun, and she did not disappoint. Quite a bit of homework, but all of the material was interesting, and she grades very fairly. Amazing lecturer, knows how to keep you engaged, encourages difficult questions. A must take.

Professor Plank's passion for what she teaches definitely helped improve my understanding of the topics. There are two writing assignments that are completed in class, but she gives you everything you will need for them.

Don'' take this class unless you want to be bored out of your mind and have almost your whole grade dependent upon the exams and essays.

Very nice person and very cheerful. Only complaint is the readings/videos were typically really long, but you usually have plenty of time to do them. She is very understanding though and if you were late to class and came up to her after class she would give you the attendance for the day. She is very knowledgeable in the subject.

Professor Plank is very engaging, making her lectures fun. I found anthropology very interesting and she had many personal stories regarding it. Attendance was very important in this class and was a large part of the grade. Her weekly readings were not too difficult.
One of the best professors I've ever had! Dr. Plank has a deep passion for anthropology and truly cares that her students understand the material.

She was a great teacher! A bit slow at responding to emails, but she did have some stuff going on outside of class this semester so that could be an explanation. She really seems to care about her students and loves what she does.
Very good professor, smart in her subject field of Anthropology as well as being a great teacher with not too heavy of a work load
Best professor I've had

I love Dr. Plank so much! She's the best professor I've had at UK and I'm not even in anthro. She's hilarious and makes the lectures so entertaining and interesting. Class is very easy; just have to show up and listen. Readings don't take long. Highly recommend taking this class with her especially if you need your US culture core.

She is literally the best teacher I've ever had. She makes the lectures so interesting and you can tell she really knows what she is talking about. The weekly quizzes are not hard at all and there's only 2 writing assignments for the whole semester.
She's so nice; I highly recommend her. She is down to earth and cares about students and their well-being. I couldn't speak higher of her!

It does not matter what your major is, you HAVE to take this class. This is the best course, best professor I've had by MILES. material is super interesting, Dr. Plank is extremely knowledgeable, engaging, passionate, kind. Only good things to say about the professor and class. PLEASE take this course!
I love Dr. Plank. She is a phenomenal professor, and I wish to take her class again.
Love Dr. Plank :D
great professor, always brings a smile to class and is always ready to listen to what you have to say.

Best anthropology professor I've taken. Very knowledgeable and captivating lectures. Lots of reading for a 200 level anthropology class, but very interesting. Daily participation and attendance required. Good classroom energy and extremely understanding. She clearly cares and wants students to have a good experience.

Plank is an amazing lecturer and pretty easy grader. If you try in this class you will do well. The only bad thing is attendance is a large portion of the grade. While it is still possible to get an A without going (I did) it's a lot more difficult. She also has lots of extra credit opportunities to get your grade up.

Dr. Plank was an incredible teacher, while the course was difficult at times, Dr. Plank posted all her notes and made it easy to catch up, and even with a large amount of homework at times, she made the class incredibly interesting and easy to understand if you were at lecture.

The nicest profesor and one of the nicest people I have ever met. Exams are online and open note and class is very stress-free. She is so nice and a great person. I would 100% take her if you have the chance.

Ms. Plank is an amazing teacher who cares about all of her students.  Her assignments usually took up more of my time than I would like and felt like busy work.  With that being said they were very easy to do but involved lots of reading and writing.  She is so nice and chill I would definitely recommend her.

I cannot stress enough how FANTASTIC Dr. Plank is. This is definitely a course involving high levels of work and commitment, but it is all worth it in the end. I can guarantee that you will learn so much from her, and she is truly a one-in-a-million professor. I highly value her both as a professor and as a person, and I have learned so much.

For somebody who has no interest in Anthropology, I really enjoyed this class and would easily take her again. She has been the best professor I have had so far at my time at the university. Absolutely love her.

This was my second class with Dr. Plank, and she is still amazing. The class was super easy to follow, and lectures were posted online to use if you were confused. Tests were very straightforward, and study guides reflected what was on the exams. Overall, a really great class with a good professor.

dr plank was very very sweet, she is very very passionate about archaeology. she gives excellent feedback and grades fairly easy. there are weekly quizzes and homeworks. i would take her again she is very sweet
I loved Dr.Plank and ANT221. It genuinely made me want to learn the material. The class was structured so well and the assignments were not difficult if you paid attention in class.

Dr. Plank is super nice and very understanding!! All of the quizzes are open from the beginning of the semester, so you can work at your own pace. I felt very prepared for the final, midterm, and semester project and she makes all of her powerpoints accessible after the lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. Plank is amazing. So caring and really wants you to like what she is teaching. The class is interesting and assignments are easy, though a bit tedious. Dr. Plank is one of the best professors I've ever had at UK. Her lectures are so engaging, it doesn't feel like work to learn the content. She's super understanding with her students and truly does her best to work with you. I would 100% take her class again, and I have even since signed up for more of her classes.
Dr. Plank is amazing!!

Dr. Plank is one of the best professors around. She is super understanding and compassionate and seems to actually care about her students. She is passionate about what she teaches and overall just a fun person.
One of the best professors at UK. Shannon is well spoken, extremely intelligent, and has a great personality. Do the work and you will get an A!

reviews.comment: One of the best professors I've had. Good sense of humor who cares about the subject. Do work and getting an A isn't hard.

reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: She works really hard to make the lecture interesting, but there is a daily quiz. She puts the answer for the quiz on the board during lecture, and will notice if someone who isnt present puts in the quiz cod. Also, she expects effort to be put forth for her assignments, and the information for the assignments are usually not on the slides.

I liked Dr. Plank as a professor and she was nice and caring. The midterm was pretty hard just because it covered a lot of material and was timed but it is online. There's also 4 writing assignments but wasn't hard to get a good grade on those. she also offers 2 extra credit papers that aren't hard either.

Dr. Plank is a great lady, and very interesting. However her homework assignments are horrendous. They are by far the most boring, and tedious assignments i have ever done. You are graded as if you should already know everything. She has convinced me that archaeology is a terrible, boring field. Dr. Plank herself is great though.

reviews.comment: Dr. Plank is sweet and funny but 100% expects quality work. The class is interesting and her funny personality makes it easy to stay engaged in conversations. Tons of extra credit available too!!

I had her 4 days a week for two different classes because she has such good ratings. She has always been very into her subjects but after while they get very boring. It is the same things over and over again. She gives a lot of extra credit opportunities and only 2 test. She is overall a well rounded teacher but the subject gets very repetitive.

reviews.comment: She is very passionate about ANT, her lectures are worth going to, she posts powerpoints online. Only two tests (midterm and final) and both are online. Recitation mandatory, just go to it. She is a great teacher!!

Dr. Plank is an energetic knowledgeable professor. Expect long lectures and lots of energy. I'm t taking this class as a major requirement & could care less about the material but she makes it interesting. She does her best to bring the past to life. Definitely take her for any anthropology class.

I loved her as a person, she was kooky and it's clear she's passionate about her field. She graded my writing assignments pretty hard, and her feedback wasn't really clear. She's also pretty absented-minded and took forever to get grades in, like finals week she put in grades from the month before last.

LOVED HER! I totally recommend. If you show up and pay attention, you will pass. A midterm and final, and a paper or too. GOOOO to her extra credit talks she offers! You can get so many bonus points that you will end up with an A
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: I loved this professor! She loves what she teaches, is very well-organized, and cares about the students. Attendance is mandatory and there were weekly online quizzes, midterm and final exam, and a semester-long project. Definitely recommend taking her!

Dr. Plank is one of the nicest professors here. She is so understanding and helps her students in every possible way to make them get a good grade. For our exams she let us fill a note card front and back, which made it super easy. And then if you still messed up she gives a pretty considerate curve. I would 10/10 recommend her if you take ANT.

reviews.comment: Dr. Plank probably has a PhD in power-point making. Seriously. Those things are works of art. ANT101 is a VERY easy class, with a weekly reading and quiz, and several "homework" assignments. This class is super interesting and you'll love taking it. Dr. Plank also really cares about her students.
She's awesome. I dig her.

Dr. Plank cares deeply about the subject matter and her students. You can tell student apathy (of which I must admit I was a part) and the political climate of late have been weighing on her, but she shows up and does a terrific job everyday. Whatever your background, this class will give you a good feel for the current/past Native American plight.
Easy class, awesome professor. All quizzes and exams are online.
Gives over 100pts in extra credit. all assignments and tests (including final) online. Friend misses a test by accident and got an extension with no problems and no lost points.

Dr. Plank is a wonderful archaeologist and professor! She has a great personality, and she never seems to be in a bad mood. She really does care about each of her students, and encourages other points of view. The class itself was not difficult; each week we had a short reading. There were three papers and two online exams. I loved this class!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Caring

reviews.comment: Dr. Plank makes class really interesting. Homework is weekly and super easy, read an article with 10 questions embedded in the reading, one semester research project that is graded with very generous if you meet all the criteria. Exams are not hard either, just study and you should be fine. I have an A and I barely try.

Dr. Plank rocks!  She loves what she teaches and she wants her students to love it too.  I enjoyed her lectures and enjoyed the topic because of her.  She tries to keep things light even though the topic can be a heavy one.  Would highly recommend.

I dread class daily, and the research assignments are downright awful. She expects you to become a Native American expert, basically. I study and always feel very confident during the exams, but do poorly on all of them. I only skipped class once (though attendance isn't mandatory, she's more willing to help you out if you go) and am still lost.

Really enjoyed having Dr. Plank as a professor. She can be funny and is very east to talk to and get help from. Although there was a text book she ended up not using it because it was so hard to comprehend. Enjoyable class although lecture always felt long since it was an early class. Tests are online and open book except for the final.
Great professor. knows what she's talking about. 4 homework, 3 exams.

Great professor, but teaches an almost overwhelming amount of content. Pretty tough grader, has very specific guidelines. If you go to her and let her know you're struggling, she's extremely willing to help. Overall fantastic professor, but class is hard if you're not passionate about native american historyculture. no textbook.
Please take him if you have a choice. He sounds very good and has good communication.
Take his class

Jesus is the best. SO helpful and understanding. He is from Spain, so his pronunciation takes time to get used to. A sweetheart truly. LingroHub, the homework website, is AWFUL and unbearable but this is not Jesus's choice or doing.

Jesus was a TA for this class, but he taught my section. He did a great job considering he had never taught this class before. He is friendly and easy to approach. I do think he was a little harsh on grading at first, but I think he became fairer throughout the semester. He was helpful when questions were asked. I think he is a really nice person!

Jesus taught in a very understandable manner. He is really friendly and loves to talk about Spanish pop culture. His exams were pretty easy and so was the single oral interview at the end of the semester. Participation matters in this course. There is a good amount of homework, but it is all pretty straightforward.

Very good at accommodating to your needs, but still expects you to put in work. You have three skip days, and two oral projects. Tests are straight forward and study guides are accurate. The only thing is that he is not very accessible via email.
Very nice, easygoing guy. Will occasionally give free 100s as a "quiz" grade for attendance. Tests are simple, but he's a little difficult on his essay questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Really nice guy and is always willing to help. His tests are pretty simple and he gives you a good idea of what's gonna be on the test. He knows a lot about the world and he connects the lectures to current events going on. Occasionally has pop quizzes.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Powell is hot.  I didn't care for the subject matter but I always attended class to see what he was wearing.

Great guy and very easyging, but extremely disorganized. Very late on getting grades back and expects you to do a lot of learning on your own- not always clear in class. Definitely need the book. Attendance not always mandatory, but sometimes gives attendance quizzes for grades.

Prof Powell is great but this is not a good class.  The textbook is difficult to understand and there is just too way too much stuff tht is covered.  You really need to attend but he does put powerpoints online.

My 2nd class with him.  Much easier than his 101 class.  His knowledge on the world is CRAZY but he can be all over the place at times.  Some of the readings are repetitive but are otherwise interesting.

I love mr Powell.He flies through lectures, but is very helpful if you have any questions outside of class and since he goes fast you usually get out early. Lectures could go a little slower but hes a good person to take a class with.  I hope he teaches other classes.
big exam curves and basic material. read the review q's and pay attention in class. put in any effort and it should be a cakewalk

this class is ridiculously easy. the easiest class ive ever taken in college. i studied for the first test the night before and got an A. go to class and take notes and look over problems given in the book.
