Grades come from papers and attendance. His lectures are interesting, but there are no tests on any of them.
Great Professor, Understanding and extremely knowledgable in areas of expertise. If you attend UK take him, you won't be dissappointed!
He's a really cool young guy. Very knowledgeable and fair.
Makes you work, but keeps you interested in the assignments.
Best teacher I;ve had so far at UK, makes class interesting and is an extremely intelligent guy. I highly recommend to take him!

I had Dr. Sleep for EGR 101 and 102, he's the best, super funny and nice. I'm not sure how well he actually knows the material lol but its really easy so it doesnt matter, you will look forward to this class every week.
awsome
Love him just think he could make the class a little bit easier.

Dr. Sleep was very friendly and cheerful, which really made EGR102 enjoyable. He explained new concepts in both circuitry and programming very well, and was very available during class to explain anything you missed.
As long as you show that you care, he'll care about you and your grade. He's very nice and supportive and will help if you ask for it. All around very kind, and holds good discussions during class.

This man is such a fantastic professor  He seems to truly care for his students and brings a level of positivity to the lectures. The way he teaches completely new concepts to some students with coding in this course makes it very approachable. He's full of encouragement and if you can take a course taught by him, you should make an effort to.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Dr. Sleep is one of the best professors I have ever had. He is helpful, caring, funny, and understanding. He also responds to emails ridiculously fast, to the point that I'm somewhat concerned about his work-life balance. I had him for EGR 101 and 102, both of which are manageable classes. Make sure to reach out for help on 102 work if you need it.
Hes awesome!
One of the best professors I have had at UK. I highly recommend his class. If you're ever confused, he's very accessable.

I had him as a professor for EGR101 and in EGR 103 now, and I can't recommend him enough. He teaches the material in an engaging way and seems to genuinely care about his students. Additionally, almost every time I've emailed him, I've gotten a response in under an hour. He doesn't grade too strictly, so you'll get an A if you try at all.

Dr. Sleep is the best professor I have ever had in college. He is respectful, helpful, and kind. You will not regret taking his course. This whole course is a group project but he is always available if you need help. He answers emails so quickly; don't be afraid to reach out. If you can, take Dr. Sleep.

He is so awesome! I had him last year and I am glad to have him again! There aren't many lectures since the entire semester is just a giant group project, but he makes sure that the process is smooth and is open to what you have to say to him. If you're looking to see whether to take him or not, TAKE HIM! You will NOT regret it at all!
Dr. Sleep is the goat

Great at explaining the material, understanding when it comes to grading and circumstances, but most of all his jokes had me laughing through the whole class sometimes. Like I just thought of one form last semester now and laughed
Dr. Sleep is the by far the best teacher for EGR101 and EGR103. Makes it really easy to get everything done for all of the group projects.
If you're looking at Rate My Professor while deciding between which engineering professors to choose; I promise you will want Dr. Sleep.

EGR102 is the same across the board, and there is an adequate (not a lot but not insignificant amounts) amount of homework, with a lab each week. While the class itself isn't terribly difficult or confusing, Dr. Sleep makes it enjoyable with a witty and relatable sense of humor and explaining things in a way anyone can understand. Highly recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Aaron was super nice and he helped a lot. A lot of discussions in class and the papers really help you learn the ethics of social work. 10/10

He's a really nice professor and very laid back. He does take attendance but as long as you let him know why you were absent you're fine. He cares a lot about his students and tries to help you with anything you have questions about. He grades fairy easy as well.

Aaron is a really lenient teacher in regards to deadlines and absences. As long as you let him know what's going on he doesn't usually hold it against you. He's a pretty easy grader and most of the classes were discussion based. Would highly recommend.

Great guy, good humor! knows math very well but has a bit of a hard time conveying it to students, tests were extremely easy! i never opened the textbook EVER for his class, homework is online and you have all week to do it, attendance was optional so i only went the day before the test and still got an A in the class

Pretty much the worst teacher I think I've had in my college career.  Gave out assignments that were of no relevance to lectures, and the tests were pretty much the same in regards to the notes.  You'll leave his office more confused than what you were when you went in.
No Comments
Very caring professor

I would highly recommend Dr. Soward for both those looking for an easy A and those interested in the subject. This by far the easiest CS class I've ever taken, there were only 5 assignments and 2 exams which honestly do not require much study because they're online. However, if you are interested in the material, Dr. Soward is also great.
THE BEST!

The best CS professor I have ever had at UKY. We only had 5 coding projects the whole semester, all of them had A LOT of easy extra credit available, online easy going mid term and final exams, I finished this class with 115% grade. I learned A LOT OF STUFF, added all those projects to my portfolio. Dr. Soward is the best professor I have ever had
Attendance not mandatory, super smart guy, easy class, A LOT of extra credit, easy assignments. This class is a must take, with him as a professor.

He's not a very good teacher. Teaches straight from powerpoints, you dont feel like he is really teaching you. I would have done terrible in this class had it not been for the very helpful TA's. He's a nice guy though. It was almost as if he expected you to know things even if they werent taught in 115. Take advantage of TA office hours.
I would not recommend. Grading doesnt appear fair and exams are not reflective of all of the homework
randomly would move homework due date without notice
this class is so hard don't take it. exams are not easy and homework doesn't help prepare
exams don't reflect videos and lectures. be prepared to do bad on exams
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Great professor, had no issues with her whatsoever!

Taking FIN 300 with Professor Song was awesome! They seriously know their stuff when it comes to finance. They made all those complicated concepts seem like a piece of cake. Their teaching style was super engaging and interactive. We had some great class discussions, and they always encouraged us to speak up and ask questions.
The best professor in the UK I've been met !

For this to be her first course taught at UK, Song did a great job. Finance is a tough subject to teach, but she genuinely cared about the success of every student in the class. If you attend class and study for the exams, you'll pass easily. Gives bonus points on exam review days as well.

I had Dr. Slaymaker for JPN 201, 202 and 421G and I loved him. He was very comfortable to work with and I didn't think he was a hard grader at all. For 421G the class was discussion based and we read nine novels. The books were very good however, if you don't want to actually read them don't take the class. I would gladly take more of his courses.

Slaymaker Sensei was very hard to adjust to. He mutters and talks very fast, so it was quite hard to understand him over zoom. And if you can't answer right away he moves onto someone else. I pretty much taught myself Japanese this semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: The class was Japanese Film which wasn't a bad class. I thought it was decently interesting. Slaymaker is a somewhat hard grader though for tests and papers, and watching the movies does take up time outside of class obviously. My only issue was that I felt I couldn't keep up with the discussions because i didn't think that deeply of the movies.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Doug Slaymaker is easily the best professor I've had at the University. He's incredibly intelligent, and it's guaranteed there will always be interesting class discussions. His classes aren't easy A's, for sure, but they are classes where you'll be engaged and interested.
He is a hard grader.  Great professor, don't get me wrong however, the style he grades his papers were unclear.  I've received A's in all my English classes and he gave me C's on all my papers.

Dr. Slaymaker's instruction and "tough love" (=tough grader, strict adherence to class rules) approach to his classes are only fully appreciated in the years after graduation. I was a bit harsh in my evaluations of Dr. Slaymaker during my time at UK, but now realize that I learned more in his class than perhaps any other at UK. Thank you professor!

the class wasn't too hard, but i never understood how he graded papers. he didn't offer much advice on how to improve them and was extremely difficult to see outside of class. there isn't much factual material either, just fiction pertaining to certain times. the novels were good, short readings... not so much. just read soseki & abe on your own.
really hard grader, but you will learn a lot if you do the readings and go to class. only thing is that he is a mumbler, so you can't always catch what he is saying.

Dr. Slaymaker is one of the better teachers I had in my five years at UK. He may not be the easiest A, but isn't that the point of a liberal arts education? To challenge yourself? The important thing is, he's incredibly knowledgeable about Japan. If you're willing to put in the effort, show up, READ, then you'll benefit greatly from his classes.

Dr. Slaymaker is very knowledgeable when it comes to Japan.  But he is ambiguous with all assignments, unwilling to accept opinions not his own, condescending, he is not willing to work with you if you have to miss a class, and his responses for grading never make sense, even if you ask for clarification.  I have nightmares because of him.

Difficult, but not impossible. Quizzes seem hard but you get a better grade than you expected. He likes to stick one Kanji that you don't know in each quiz. He uses Japanese a lot. At first it's intimidating, but in the end it helps. If you work hard and study then you will pass, and it will improve your Japanese all the more.

Professor Slaymaker is really  tough, but not unreasonable. If you do the readings, take notes in class and study for the exams, it's not difficult to pull a good grade. If you don't pay attention, don't do the readings, you WILL fail. Aside from being a brilliant man, he was a pretty good teacher. Tough, but good.

He did not require attendance, yet your grade plummetted if you did not attend. He gave no response as to how he was grading ANYTHING. Also, he is condesending and thrives on girls flirting with him. If you don't flirt, he doesn't care about you or your grade. He expected answers to be perfect, or he took off. He never explained his reasoning.

He is very unwilling to work with you. He is extremely hard to follow. He will also give you a lower grade then you actually have in the class. If you take a class with him please keep all your grades, So that way you can check them at the end of the semester. I am a JPN minor so I have to have him but if you don't need his class don't take it.
Jumped from topic to topic, talked during "quizzes", which wasn't helpful, doesn't reply back to email in a time efficient manner.

Dr. Slaymaker mumbles alot, you will need to contantly ask him to speak up, changes the sylabus weekly, is not flexible. If you have not had a class with him before or not a JPN major I do not recommend taking him.

I love Dr. Slaymaker.  He acted as my adviser and teacher for many many semesters and class with him was always challenging but fun.  Having said that, he does have a tendency to get off topic and go off on tangents.  Also, watch when he speaks, because he does this thing with his hands like he's collecting his thoughts and sorting them into piles

He is always patient when you are trying to say something in Japanese. I think that's really important for learning another language. When you ask questions he always tries to answer to the best of his ability. However, be warned, when he switches to Japanese he is like a flying bullet! So fast!

When I talked to him about how to improve my paper, not very helpful. Grades fairly tough, I thought. Talked about the same thing all semester: trying to find the dichotmies in the essays we read. Didn't use textbooks, printed off essays and read books.
Makes learning Japanese exciting.  Very knowledgeable and often takes side notes that dive into Japanese beyond the language.

only problem i had with him is that when he speaks japanese, he talks a million miles a minute.  kinda hard to work through his accent. some of the ways he said stuff threw me off, but that is about the only complaint i had with him.

Very very very energetic.  Will wear you out with his very presence.  AWESOME knowledge of Japanese and culture, and is a very good model, great accent.  Makes you realize that you CAN learn such a difficult language as an American.

While there is a lot of homework, it is necessary for repetition purposes and not super dense. Sofia was very understanding, caring, and really showed that she wanted her students to succeed. There were tons of extra credit opportunities throughout the semester, and she always found ways to make learning fun.

Sofia is an incredible and caring professor. She is extremely knowledgeable about the language, being a native Spanish speaker, and she is very passionate about teaching the Spanish language and Latin American culture to her students.

Sofia is absolutely amazing!! She prepares you very well for her exams. If your taking Spanish, I definitely advice trying to get a class with her! You will not have a hard time getting an A! Plus she is an amazing professor and cares a lot for her students.

I emailed her for more information on an assignment and sent a snarky reply that I should only ever address her as "Dr. Soto Vega" and not contact her via email. She posts ridiculous assignments with no background or information. Even when the assignment is completed on time, she deducts points if you do not "grade your peers" work.
She wasn't clear with basically every assignment and was very annoying and irrational. Would not take her again but it shouldn't be too hard to get a good grade.

I learned very little in her class. She cares for her students but did not articulate the core concepts of the class clearly. I didn't find the assignments difficult, although some were confused by her ambiguous grading criteria. There was usually one short assignment a week (250 words), with larger assignments being more sporadic.

Vague assignments and does not explain them in a way that makes sense. Class time often feels unhelpful and drags on. She teaches in a way that felt like high school, and her teaching style generally did make me feel like a college student. But she is mostly nice and seems to genuinely care about her students.

She runs this class a lot like a high school English class. She had vague instructions that didn't always match the prompts given on the assignments. She was generally nice and understanding about the students as a whole. Most of the class time is spent listening to her talk about random things. Not a tough grader, but not a clear grader.

Biggest problem with this class is clarity on assignments. The prompt may have one set of instructions and she will say something different in class. Doesn't have clear answer to clarifying questions and it seems she wants instructions to be unclear. Not a harsh grader per se, but will randomly take off 0.1 on assignments and not have a reason why.

Very unclear grading criteria and vague assignments. She's very passionate about the subject, but fails to explain things. Feedback given often doesn't match the grade on the assignment. Sometimes fails to realize the class is a lower level mandatory credit. Will often take .1 points off without a reason.

Dr Soto Vega is an alright professor. I think she is very sweet, but lacks in organizational patterns for her class. Assignments are often very vague and homework is hard to find within Canvas. Lectures are recorded but you need to watch them the day they come out, even if class is asynchronous because there is assignments embedded in them.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr. Soto Vega is a fine teacher. I had her when everything was online. She had never taught an online class and it was extremely obvious. We never could find anything or wanted to constantly watch 30 min lectures every day. I think she would be way better to take in person. Its a credit filler and I don't think she understands that.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr. Soto Vega is extremely helpful outside of class if you have any questions. Instructions for some of her assignments are sometimes unclear and vague, but if you ask for help she will clarify.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I adore this man. He is so sweet and caring. Although the course material can be tough at times, he makes sure that you understand and will help with whatever you need. He is always willing to meet outside of class hours and check your work to help fix any mistakes before turning it in. I absolutely recommend him and the class

Dr. Kim was an incredible professor to have and he really wants you to do your best in the class. It's absolutely necessary you attend class and pay attention to the instructions, otherwise you'll have a hard time with the projects. But Dr. Kim is always there to help when you absolutely need it and was just a fun guy to have as a prof!
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects

reviews.comment: Professor Kim is one of the best professors I've taken as a journalism major, he is super understanding and truly does his best to help students succeed as much as possible. The course is extremely difficult if you are not very tech-savvy, but he still goes above and beyond to make sure all students understand what they are doing!
He is one of respectful professors ever. He also helps those who want to pursue academic career to some extent.

Kim is the man! He's a funny guy who cares about his students success. He knows that photoshop and Dream Waver can be a pain to use and really grades based off basic requirements and effort. If you need to take JOU 330 take KIM!

VERY nice guy and very willing to help his students. JOU 330 is a attendance mandatory class being that he explains something new every class so if you do not show up you will be behind. Highly recommend Professor Kim
he is a nice guy!!!!
Dr. Kim has an exhaustive knowledge of photojournalism. informative, interesting, use of power point was effective, projects were well assigned+ help me learn a lot.
Extremely knowledgeable and very helpful when answering questions. Great teacher, fun! learned a lot
Nice guy though!

I love Yung Soo. He is funny, nice, and grades pretty easily. I've had him in web design and photojournalism and he is laid back, knowledgable, and flexible with deadlines as long as you talk to him. I definitely recommend him.
TAKE HIM!!! IF you need a 300 level he is the guy to take! It was the easiest A I have ever received! He is all about his students and his tests I did not study a single moment for!

Dr. Kim is a sweetheart.  He isn't teaching this class by choice but he still knows what he's talking about and truly wants students to succeed. Easy A if you're moderately interested in making a webpage.

You are better off taking another gen ed course that fufils the requirement. Save yourelf the time and energy and go do something else. If you are not a suck up who Spinks likes, he will not go easy on you. His feedback is borderline un-legible.

Professor Spinks is the hardest grader I've ever had and gives terrible feedback. His "feedback" consist of lines and scribbles on your paper. He gives 6 one page papers the entire semester and one long 5 page paper at the end which you only have 1 week to prepare for. I cried to him about how stress I was about the class and he had no empathy.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: This course is not taught like an "into" level philosophy course. I went to ever class and took notes during class but there is no way to get a good grade in this course if you are new to philosophy. He requires so many papers and never gives anyone an A. My best advice is to drop this class and wait till another section opens up.

This class is way too difficult for a philosophy 100 class and it is not the class it is the professor. I have friends in other philosophy classes that understand the material clearly because the professor actually knows what he's talking about. This professor talks way too fast, doesn't explain anything, jumps from point, and notes are unorganized
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Worst class i have taken in my whole college career. Teacher gets way off topic every time a question is asked, and he doesn't care about anyone's opinion in class but yet tells us to write how we feel...? Also very rude and unaccommodating. would not recommend this teacher to anyone.

Well, where do I start? The class is way too difficult to be a level 100 class. The readingmaterial was VERY difficult. It felt as if I was in church but actually had to do assignments about what I read... Papers are due every two weeks. If you enjoy reading difficult material then this is the class for you. His class made me consider dropping out
Very spastic, never comes to class on time, cancels class constantly, on our final group presentation he never showed up and left the whole class sitting there

I had him as a TA for Phi 343 and it was the only thing that made it bearable. He is passionate, helpful, and very nice. He taught in place of my Prof a few times and it was the only time anyone took something away from lecture. The only complaint is that he slouches a bit which I find distracting.

When I decided to take Philosophy 100, I chose so just to fill up my schedule. In fact, there was only one seat left when signed up. I must say, I am so glad I took this class. Justin is amazing. He is very passionate about his work, and really wants to help students broaden their horizions when it comes to thinking. Now I minor in Philosophy. :)

I don't know why everyone is giving him such bad reviews. He's great and very approachable.  I didn't go to lecture, just recitation, where I learned everything from Justin.  Great T.A. and very knowledgeable.
Justin is passionate about the subject. As a 100 level class grasping the ideas' of the masters of philosophy can be tough. Justin is pretty good at putting it in understandable terms.

Somehow got am A, but only because it was his first semester teaching and I guess he didnt want too make it too tough. Dont get me wrong, the material and readings were very tough to understand and if you zone out in class for 5 seconds you will be lost the remainder of class. Take someone else

I honestly don't think he could have gotten above a C on the proofs exam, as he never did a single example correctly; he would spend 10-15 minutes per proof on the blackboard while talking to himself, only to be corrected by one of the students, at which point he would look up the answer in his instructor's manual and just copy it down.

I did all the readings, went to the lectures, and still didn't learn a thing in this class.  Speaking of reading, that's all you will be doing if you end up with Spinks.  Class discussions over the material could be compared to crickets chirping because no one really understood anything we had to read.  He's a nice guy, but too hard for 100 level.
Very understanding of students and will take the time to help you. You can tell he really knows what he's talking about and is great at explaining topics.

He's nice, but he tends to over-explain. The class could get tedious, but he made sure to keep us engaged. Attendance not taken, but participation matters. Heavily group-based, keep your group accountable. Greenhalgh is always willing to help, but he stresses that you figure it out yourself first. Fair grader, easy class all things considered.
Easy class, Dr. G takes care of his students like I have never seen before. Best professor I have ever had at UK.
the best
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Dr. Greenhalgh really cares about his students. His lectures can be boring, but he includes activities to give students hands-on experience with the topics. His class is very easy and he tries to keep it interesting, so just show up and pay attention and it will be good!

This was his first semester teaching a class in person and I feel like he did great! Obviously wants students to succeed and treated us like adults. Gives you all the resources to do well on exams and is very well educated in Finance. Would definitely recommend taking him over some other FIN professors :)
Great!! Very knowledgeable + helpful. Uses Excel > Calculator. Awesome lectures + is flexible + willing to work with you. Learned a lot and he genuinely cares about the students and the class.

Zero effort put into class. No PowerPoints, no lectures, only online module assignments, basically on your own. Makes you pay for ProctorU for exams when UK already has a free lockdown browser available. The material is easy but no leadership or expectations outlined throughout the semester. 80% of the grade is exams-no curve. Take different prof.

Nice guy but horrible professor. I make As and Bs but I am going to fail his class/withdrawal. Uses another professors lectures, 80% of final grade is exams, gives practice problems for exams but doesn't explain how to do them, hw is nothing like the exam, exams are fill in the blank (not multiple choice), etc. Basically every obstacle. DO NOT TAKE

Dr. Speck is a good professor, and he knows what he's talking about. I loved PGY 206, and honestly it's not that hard as long as you take anatomy before and spend enough time studying. I studied every other day for 1-2 hrs and I got A+ on all of the exams. The key is being focused in class and taking uninterrupted time to think. You'll be fine!

Listen, Dr. Speck is a good professor. But the problem with this class is that there are FIVE different professors who teach it, and they rotate through. It was REALLY hard to adjust to so many different teaching and testing styles over and over again. If it had just been Speck, it might've been ok. But I didn't like how he ran this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Speck and all of the TA's are really good professors. However, the tests are extremely hard and that is 80% of your grade. If you can find old exams I would highly suggest studying those for the exams. Attendance isn't mandatory, I only watched the echo's and still did well in the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Speck is beyond sweet!! The content and exams are incredibly difficult; reviewing old exams is a must to do well. Your grade is based almost entirely on exams so you have to devote the time to studying. Rewatching the lectures can be helpful if you get distracted in class.
reviews.rating_tags: TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Prof. Speck is funny and really wants his students to succeed. His students feel comfortable walking up to him and asking him questions. The content, however, is REALLY challenging. This is definitely the hardest course I've ever taken. Multiple advisors told me not to take this course bc of the difficulty. You must be prepared to work for ur grade
Dr. Speck was a good lecturer. His tests were so difficult. He cares and really wants you to do well. Look at his old exams and take 207 if possible.

He's one of the nicest professors I've ever had, a great guy... but I couldn't pass his exams. If you have had lower level physiology and anatomy you may do okay. For my major they just toss you in upper level physiology, without any prerequisites. This was by far the hardest class I've had. I'd recommend getting this credit at BCTC, if possible.
This class was the most challenging one I have taken so far in college. Using old exams is key for success on tests. Don't skip lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Took this class Fall 2016. GO TO CLASS AND ACTUALLY PAY ATTENTION. Although there is ECHO and he doesnt take attendance, use his lecture time to learn. Dont depend on curves, although he curved for us Fall 2016. His tests are very very challenging and I suggest you study a couple hours each week so you do not cram at the end. Cool guy though.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Tough class. Posts the lectures online so there really is no reason to go to class. Exams are tricky and hard. He didn't curve our tests or our final grade. Most people have old tests, find a friend that does if you don't because everyone that has the old tests will bend the test average higher.
Such an easy class if you can get your hands on the last 3 semesters exams. All of the questions are either reused or rephrased. Easy A in my opinion

Not too bad of a teacher, but could be better. There are different people who teach throughout semester, none of them horrible. Make sure to look at old tests because a lot of questions are reused. Give yourself enough time to study before tests, not an easy A. He can be helpful, but not very lenient with grades. No extra credit or homework.

I had to take this class for my major and it was awful. I don't have much of a bio background so it was a pretty difficult class. Dr. Speck is great but this class has several professors and it makes the class REALLY confusing.
He expected you to know information from the recitation even if you hadn't taken it. He also had you pay for Tophat which had a book, but then he would refer to a different book in his power points.
I struggled a lot in this class. Powerpoint lectures aren't very specific at all and it is very hard to find material to study for the tests. I did not like Dr. Speck at all.

The class is difficult. He is often unclear in teaching &rarely curves exams. Professors rotate for this course so it makes it difficult to get a study technique down for exams, however when it's an exam by Speck it tends to be the very similar to last years so ask around! He's hard to follow and the lectures are boring. Attendance isn't required

Hardest class I have ever taken, but Speck is super helpful. He will help you in any way he possibly can to succeed. May not be my favorite class I have ever taken (actually my least favorite class) but Speck is one of my favorite professors I've ever had.

Dr. Speck is one of the nicest professors I've had.  He will do everything possible to help you understand the material, and his tests are straightforward.  There are guest lecturers for topics throughout the course, all of whom are also very nice and present their material very clearly.

He's clear in his delivery and a nice guy who wants everyone to succeed. Hard class, but my grades improved as I went. I got a 76 on the first test and 96 on the final. I felt bad sometimes because not a lot of people came to class. Study hard, and an A is possible. Don't study and fail.
There are multiple professors for this class but Dr. Speck is the main instructor. He is very friendly and willing to answer any questions raised in class or through email. I'd highly recommend him!
Great teacher! Loves teaching and helping the students as best as he can. It is a very tough course so be make sure to study a lot and always ask questions if you have any!
Good teacher, always very happy and makes class easier to listen too. Material is tough, but can be done. Be sure to read book as well as the things he finds important in lecture.
First test was extremely easy, after that it gets must harder. Be sure to go to class. Other than that its not to bad. Tests are not easy.

Dr. Speck is a great professor!  He kept the class interesting and was always available to clear up any confusion on concepts. You will have to study a decent amount to do well on the tests though but it's definitely possible.  I would take him again in a heart beat, he knows his stuff.

Professor Speck was an EXCELLENT teacher. His notes were great guidelines, and IF you went to class then he explained them in great detail. Attendance is not required, but if you want to learn then you will. Tests are easy if you attend class! I would take any of his classes!

Lecture is a must!!! Explains things that are not clearly spelled out in the notes. Several different teachers for this class and Speck is the best. Others keep updeating notes and printing becomes a pain. Tests are pretty much impossible.Reading the book helps somewhat.

Lecture was very interactive at first- scored a 90 on the first exam, then he switched to powerpoint slides and my interest/grades dropped. Extremely helpful and enthusiastic, but not easy. Exam questions can be pretty tough and very specific.
Great teacher.  Kept things vey clear and and was willing to stop class to clarify any quesiton.  No an easy class but he makes it as easy as possble.  Curves and quizzes worth alot of grade.

As everyone else has said, he is a great teacher. He tries to keep you interested, and at anytime during class will stop to answer your questions. He is also quick to respond to emails. Review sessions are offered before exams... very helpful!!! The class is also taught by four other professors, but he tries to clarify anything you are confused on.

I absolutely love Dex Speck! Taking his physiology class after my terrible experience with anatomy was like a breath of fresh air. He is super dorky but an awesome lecturer. He seems to love his job and loves to help students. The tests are difficult but not impossible. Study hard the couple nights before and you should be fine!

Speck is the best teacher I've had at UK!! He is very friendly and approachable and obviously cares about his students. He is interesting and definitely knows what he is talking about. His tests are hard, so you definitely have to work hard in this class, but he also curves every test. He is very fair. Take speck for pgy!!

Dr Speck is a great teacher! His class is hard (but hey PGY is hard stuff) He really helps out by giving bonus quizzes and lowering the grading scale (an 86 and up was an A). Study hard and attend the lectures and you should be fine

Dr. Speck is a fun teacher. Although the class is very hard and alot of studying must be done, he is such a nice guy and does all he can to make up for the hardness of the test. Some extra credit quizzes were given on blackboard to help raise the grade and a large curve is given at the end.
He was not very good at explain how to do the steps of the equations. He usually went/talked way too fast to keep up. I found that i learned better at the study than in class.

Dr. Spencer is quite possibly the worst professor you could have for a math class. His lectures/notes are generally useless and untimely uploaded to Canvas, he cannot control his classroom, and is generally unknowledgable of the course and its material. His office hours are unwelcoming and he does not understand the homework. Please, stay away.

I like Spencer as a person but, he is very socially awkward and so intelligent that he is unable to explain things in a way that actually makes sense. Don't take him unless you want to teach yourself calculus. All MA123 classes take the same exams and do the same homework but Spencer will not be able to prepare you for either during lecture.

WELL. WHERE DO I BEGIN. Exams are a complete joke. Whatever you learn in class isn't even relevant. All you have to do is study the old exams, but sometimes those are complete garbage as well. Spencer doesn't even teach, he just writes Chinese gibberish and expects you to know it just like that. AVOID THIS MAN.

Patrick Spencer is a really good guy, but he's an awful teacher. He pulls up a pdf during class and just does it expecting us to learn just by watching him. If you are not a math person I would high recommend you stay away.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Class fairly good; he explains how to do problems and then does examples until you feel more confident working them. Homework is very hard, but I think all teachers for 123 are required to have us do the hw. Go to the study or work with a friend and the homework can teach you a LOT. Fair teacher, wants to help his students.

Patrick is an ok teacher. He assigns multiple homework assignments per week however does not actually teach on the topic until after it is due, forcing you to learn the material on your own. The exams aren't too bad, and reflect the practice online. He tends to have a hard time explaining much of the material.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Reads through lecture slides and doesn't explain what he's doing. He does all the problems before class, he even said that himself, and then copies down his work onto the slides. Moves too fast and doesn't teach, just solves problems and expects you to learn from watching him. When asked a question, his answer most of  the time is "I don't know".
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Great with numbers, awful with teaching. He knows how to do it, and expects that just by writing it on the board, without explaining any of the steps, students will understand. Speaks and moves on far too quickly for most students to keep up with. Taught myself the concepts.
One of the best professors I have had at UK.

He is absolutely terrible. He learns the material as he is teaching it. He reads directly off his slides and thinks we will learn that way. He never has any idea what is going on. When you ask him a question his response is usually, "uh I'm not sure, thats a good question, let me get back to you." and then of course he will never get back to you
Do not take her class very difficult to understand grading techniques are hard dry old movies a lot of useless writing DO NOT TAKE CLASS
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: This class was so unorganized. We had 2 professors and they did not seem to know what each other was talking about. There are so many long readings. The papers had no guidelines and are graded hard. We had a book club inside the class, which really made no sense. There is a project that goes along with the book, that doesn't go with the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor Basu was very inconsiderate of other's backgrounds. The grading was tough, she was very unorganized and changed her mind constantly. Lots of group work, and the "large" group project that we spent months on was only worth about 50 points...
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Group projects

reviews.comment: She is very vague on what she wants from assignments. She also takes a long time to get assignments graded. However, she is very knowledgeable and provides great feedback.

Basu is obviously extremely intelligent on the subject matter, however, her class is insanely hard. She usually teaches graduate courses, so it seemed like she forgot that this course was an undergraduate level class. She doesn't give clear grading criteria, so good luck figuring out exactly what she wants from you. But she's really funny and nice.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Tests are pretty difficult because they are all multiple short answers/written response and they take extremely long to review.

He moves really fast and his slides only have pictures on them so you cannot take notes unless you are very quick at writing becuase he does not allow technology. Midterms are all writing, no multiple choice. You must know the who, what, when, where, and how its relevant to the course in order for anything to count.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Taken a few classes with Dr. Summers & enjoy his classes more than other professors. Attendance isn't mandatory, but everything on the tests is in the lectures. He does talk about everything that is on the study guide & tells what won't be on the exams if you go to the review. Still make an A on an exam w/out fully reading books--read summarythough

He gives lots of slides during class to see, the midterms and finals are essays and the recitations are just quizzes that are short essays and essays. He is a tough grader wants names, dates, and all correct history in your answer.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--So many papers

reviews.comment: This class is a class that you have to work very hard in, but if you go to the lecture and take good notes, you will do fine! He is such a fun person to listen to, during lectures he sounds like he's narrating a movie! There is a lot of reading- I just use the textbook for the index and glossary definitions lol, everything else I get from lectures.

Confusing lectures, you have to be able to write two essays with no preparation along with memorizing IDs for every exam. Lots of essays and quizzes. He is nice and does care about the students though.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This dude wants to be the crazy teacher and fun but he is insanely hard and expects simply too much. Im currently a junior and am thinking back to my freshman year and cannot believe how hard he ran this class. The test study guide is simply 200 terms and he picks 20 that you need to know. Insanely hard. Also isn't very nice and not really helpful.

He is very passionate about history but rambles. There are 3 essays and 3 exams. The essays are easy but you need to buy all of the books. His exams are so hard and majority of the people I have talked to do very poorly on them. I got an A in HIS108 but his HIS109 class is hard. His lectures have nothing to do with what is on the exams.

Somehow manages to make lectures about England's thatch roof industry incredibly entertaining. Super energetic and engaging, very knowledgable! He gives you plenty of opportunity to succeed and is very kind to his students.
Dr. Summers teaches history as if he lived it.  He is passionate about his work and has a great desire to pass his knowledge on to his students.
I don't know why everyone likes this guy. Was kinda racist and it was brushed off because he's older. Terrible lecturer, just rambles. Will never take him again.

Dr. Summers (Big Man) teaches a class that is super easy to pass. You just have to attend the lectures (he does put things in Latin on the slides- attendance isn't mandatory, but you won't pass if you don't go). Do the detective assignments- don't worry about reading the book. He never mentions it in class. he talks fast- be prepared to write!

Professor Summers is passionate but can get sidetracked. Lectures are tricky, but slides and study tools like Unstuckstudy make it manageable. Focus on the material, and you'll do well despite the harsh grading.

Professor Summers is obviously very passionate about history, however he tends to get side tracked easily. While I personally think the material itself is not difficult, the way he structures exams says otherwise. I would be sure to study HARD, and know the material. He grades very harshly and hardly lets anyone redo their mistakes.

awful speaker, uses large words in incorrect ways, tries too hard to sound smart.  he is a phony, I knew more about his101 before i took this course, he is filledwith opinions, not facts.  total waste.  avoid him.

Super funny guy, lectures could be better, I never listened to his lectures and only went off his slides and I found that easier, only a few assignments and exams are graded so make sure you know the material
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Hilarious--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very passionate professor who knows what he is talking about. Be prepared to read because there are multiple books with papers that go with them. Exams are only open response so you do need to look at study guides and materials he gives you. Your TA will either make or break this class for you. ASK FOR REVIEW SESSIONS BEFORE EXAMS!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Summers is very clearly passionate about teaching history. His lectures are fun to listen to but are hard to understand and apply. He also jumps around a lot while teaching which made it confusing if you are a linear thinker like me. The exams were rather easy if you know the terms he gives you to study.
If you don't go to his lectures, don't expect to get good notes from the powerpoints as he really just yaps for notes. Lots of essays so be prepared, and the exams are hard
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Take literally any other professor. His lectures are not helpful, just him screaming at the class like a preacher for some reason with slides that are 90% pictures. The entire grade comes from 3 papers (you have to read a 200 or more page book for each) & 3 exams so 1 bad grade & you're done. He's nice but terrible at teaching his material.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Summers was a sweet man who cared about his students. His lectures are hard to follow. He talks fast and crams a lot of information into one lecture. He does post the powerpoints though! As long as you put the effort in and study, this class should be pretty easy!
This course is graded on about 3 assignments, which are all four page essays, and three exams. If you could i 100% take a different course.
reviews.rating_tags: So many papers--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Summers is one of the funniest professor, yet, it comes with a cost. He's very passionate and tends to go on tangents, making it hard to understand. He posts the slides on Canvas so you don't need to go to class. We had to "read" 4 books and write 4 essays along with 3 exams. I think this class is an easy B but a hard A.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He keeps class fun and enjoyable the entire time. If you miss a class however, you have to take your own time to do learn the missed information because it's very lecture heavy. His exams are always identification of terms, short essay questions, and a long essay. The study guides have so many terms and you have to learn ALL of the them.

Dr. Summers is a really funny and smart guy, and he's very passionate about history. But note-taking can be tricky because he just talks the entire time with PowerPoints full of pictures. Based on the exams, it seems best to focus on the list of terms he gives you. There are weekly assignments which aren't hard as well.

Dr. Summers is hilarious and I wish I had taken advantage of interacting with him individually earlier in the semester. He was super enthusiatic about the material and students that show an eagerness to learn. He offers a lot of preperation sessions for exams which are extremely helpful. I would love to find a reason to take another class with him!
He's a great professor! Only thing is that he talks fast, but all the powerpoints are online on canvas!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He pretty much just talks the whole time with powerpoints full of pictures so if you're a visual learner it kinda stinks. A bit of advice for notes is to focus on all the class's terms that he gives you on the first day of class.

The TA I was assigned at first was not good. They were an awful grader. However, I discussed my issue with Dr. Summers and he helped me transfer to another TA who I bonded with better than the one before. The class work isn't hard, you just have to know what you are writing about and read the books. Attend the lectures- he offers extra credit.

Dr. Summers is really passionate about history and definitely wants you to succeed, however there are 6 grades throughout the entire course. If you put in effort you should be fine, however, if you have a bad TA definitely talk to Summers and he will switch you. If you can take a different history I would.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class is a lot of work for a 108 class. There are probably about 6-7 papers, two midterms, and a final exam. It's definitely not an easy A but it's manageable if you put in the work and have a good concept of History. The textbook is "required" but I got easily through the course without opening it once. Dr Summers is a great guy and lecturer.

Doctor Summers is an incredible professor and lecturer. He brings to life American history. As a freshman, he assigned a lot of work that I didn't want to do such as 3 papers, and two midterms. Overall great class! He is very pleasant.
Professor Summers cares about what he is teaching but is very hard to keep up with. If you get a bad TA like I did you will hate this course. Your entire grade is made up of exams and papers.
Don't take him
No
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Dr. Summers is very interesting and involved in his lectures! Never a boring moment. However, he does grade based on detail and does not let a lot of things slide. Overall, if you do the work he assigns, you will pass easily.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --So many papers

reviews.comment: This class contains a lot of outside work. You have to read three outside books for papers, and the TAs do not grade well. You also have another textbook that goes with the lectures you must read, or you will miss stuff on the exams. It is tough to follow in lectures; I recommend a different professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Makes lectures really entertaining, but it can be difficult to take notes if you're someone who solely relies on what is on-screen because he doesn't put much on his slides and he can go fast at times. Asks you to read a handful of books and write essays on them and at the time it kind of felt like a drag but I learned a lot.
Do not take this class. If you do be prepared to write so many papers and read a lot of books. His lectures are interesting but the tests are very hard. I would not recommend this to anyone.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Makes you read 4 books, 4 essay questions (250-300 words each minimum) per 4 test, too much studying, 90% of PowerPoints are just pictures, don't take this class
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Way too much work, if you want personal time don't take this class
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I took this class as an elective but it was one of the hardest classes. He asked about four (essay/short answer) questions per exam when it was on so much information. So you would study so hard to answer a question about like two on vocab and then a very long essay and short answer. It didn't make sense to me at all. At least the TA was helpful.

Mr. Summers is very passionate about history, and that makes his class more enjoyable. However, do not take this class if you are looking for an easy elective. There is a lot of outside reading and papers that are about the readings. There are 3 exams including the final that include a mixture of the readings and the class material.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I loved summers for the lower level history classes, but the colonial course i took was much different. The class had little structure, he didn't post anything to canvas, and everything relied upon a couple exams and a paper. I found it really hard to follow along because it just felt like a story the whole time. 5 stars cuz i love him tho
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Summers is an amazing history professor- but you should only be taking history courses if you love it! They are hard and comprehensive. Summers is an amazing narrator but you may struggle if you can't take notes without words on the screen. Read the books and attend lectures for the best experience .
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Summers is enthusiastic and unique. His lectures are in story-form with many visual aids and little text. His score here is not indicative of his ability to teach and engage students, he is a delight. My advice? Don't take Summers as a freshman, don't take Summers if you don't love history, and don't take Summers if you don't want to read.

Dr. Summers is an excellent professor, but I mostly relied on the book for learning. I missed lecture for the majority of the semester because I personally felt that it wasn't supplemental to my learning, but I still received an A on all of my exams and papers. If you study hard and put in the work outside of class, you will be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr. Summers is the professor that your high school teachers warn you about. He is old and so is his teaching style. You will need to learn how to take notes! He is a genuine person, and wants you to pass though. I agree that his exams are too much for a 108 class, which most are taking as a core class anyway. If you work for it, you will be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: My favorite professor this semester. I enjoyed his lectures, he finds a way to make them interesting by running around the lecture hall and jumping on the desk. If you ask he will give VERY helpful review sessions for the exams. If you start early (two- week and a half early) you will do fine on the exams if you study. I highly recommend this class
Dr. Summers tries to make his lectures interesting but his exams are tough. You will need a lot of books for this course and be ready to memorize terms.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr. Summer is an amazing guy and really enjoys what he teaches. However, as a student, his teaching style is very hard to learn from as he lectures for the entire class. We do not have homework which makes it worse because our grade depends on the three exams we take which are very hard. Your grade really depends on what TA you get.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Your entire grade is based off 2 Midterms, your final exam, and 3 papers. Class was extremely difficult, but the recitation was very helpful! I recommend if youre taking this course, go to all of the study group sessions!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr. Summers is the hardest grader ever. He takes points off for everything on the tests. It doesn't matter how much you study the tests are impossible.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: he tries way too hard in lecture to be entertaining than actually give you information you need. Class is pointless, he talks too fast to write anything down. Recitation for this class is also annoying. EXTREMELY picky on the exams and take off points just because. completely written exams. way to much for a 108 class- take anything else if you can
The best history professor at UK! His lectures are so enthusiastic and well put together, you really learn a ton

This professor is amazing. His lectures are told like story and he incorporates so many visuals. He is such a funny person and cares for his students. There are lectures every class and essay assignments but if you truly enjoy history you should be fine.

I could truly only describe the people that rated this angel poorly, as morons. The same can be said for people who did not get a B or above. Dr. Summers tried his absolute best to make the class as fun and entertaining as possible. I stopped attending lectures after the first month, and only read the text book. Made an A+.

The best professor i've had by far, and im not a history major. His lectures will amaze you, but you need to take notes. He will give you all the time you require for the exams. Take his course once and you will remember him forever.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Summers is very passionate about the topics he teaches and expects you to follow the story line he presents in class on exams and papers. If you go to class and pay attention you will do fine on the exams. Make sure you do the required readings well in advance! He is happy to host review sessions but you have to ask for them in class!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I had the privilege of taking Dr Summers decades ago at UK during my undergrad. I never appreciated how fantastic he was until years later. One of the most amazing professors I've ever taken. He's a treasure.

Professor Summers is very passionate and knowledgeable about everything you will learn about during the semester. The exams are pretty difficult and you have to read 3 books and write papers to go along with them but that is the same across most history classes at UK. Although it was difficult I would not have taken any other professor.

Lectures are incredibly boring and don't teach much. Looking over the study guide for the first exam, I knew literally nothing on it, despite going to every lecture and taking good notes. Also grades impossibly hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: If you have any respect for yourself and your well-being whatsoever, do NOT take Professor Summers. His exams are all writing and he makes you memorize descriptions for over 100 terms when he only has you do SIX on the exam (and you don't know which six, it's completely random). If I could turn back time, I would take literally any other professor.

The TA I had was the worst TA in all of UK. He failed almost our entire class on the first midterm exam. He is a terrible discussion leader. He makes the class feel uncomfortable, and he is very disrespectful towards all students. Dr. Summer's is fine, he's just extremely boring, very knowledgable though.

Your grade is based on 3 exams and 3 essays. the study guides for the exams are made up of 50 ID terms (he picks 6 for the exam), 13 short essays (he picks 1 for the exam), and 5 long essays (he picks 1 for the exam). The TA's are more lenient while grading essays but are harsh on exams. If you don't like history but have to take this, good luck!
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: It makes me sad to discover that Dr. Summers has only been ranked as a 3.8 bc he's a 5.0. He's extremely passionate & absolutely hilarious. His exams are manageable, if you study. The course isn't extremely reading heavy. KEEP TRACK OF KEY TERMS THROUGHOUT THE SEMESTER. If you keep track of those terms, you will learn and easily pass the exams.

Doctor Summers is by far the best professor i have ever had. I enjoyed coming to his lectures to hear the story we turns history into. He includes stories of historical characters and music to bring history to life. He is very passionate about his job and you can easily see he enjoys what he does. After his last lecture the entire class clapped.

Dr. Summers knows his history, but I found his lectures to be very confusing. His lectures tell history like it is a story, which I really hated. Also, we were assigned four books to read which was very extra and attendance was mandatory. If you do everything to get you the participation points, you will easily get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: His lectures can seem a but unorganized at times, but are always entertaining and interesting.
His lectures are fantastic.

He is hilarious. He lectures as if it is a story which is kind've interesting to listen to. The tests are definitions and essays, all written. He does give you all of the possible questions before hand as a study guide. If you raise your hand and ask for a review session, he'll make one. On the last day he dressed up as a colonist. Real Gem.

Dr. Summers is an amazing professor! He is very passionate & enthusiastic about his job. Attendance is not taken in lectures but you should never skip because he covers a lot of information you need to know for exams. There are only 2 exams, a final, and 3 essays to make up your grade. If you even slightly like history you should take his class
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: This class was really tough, but good at giving lectures. He talks very fast, but he presents the material in a way that keeps you engaged. As long as you study, you will do fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Took U.S. History 2 Spring of 1995. I remember he had unique prespectives on the 60's since he went to UC Berkley around then, and he said something about the counterculture not trusting you unless you had a mustache. Played interesting music daily, but remember it not on tests. Required Vietnam and WWII Novels to read. Was an interesting class.

Dr. Summers is the best professor I have ever had and probably will ever have. He is an eccentric storyteller and very passionate about History as well as students learning it. He has a review session before each exam. If you don't finish the exam in the class time, he will take you somewhere else to let you finish.

Dr. Summers is very witty and eccentric. He makes lectures very interesting. That said, his grading methods can be rather unclear and he does not use Canvas, which is inconvenient. His exams are not too hard - just study well and pay attention in class. Overall a fantastic personality but he runs a somewhat disorganized and inconsistent ship.

Even if you hate history any course Dr. Summers teaches is a must! His lectures are witty, funny, poetic, and packed full of information. He plays music, parts of movies, and displays hundreds of often funny pictures, all tying into the theme of the lecture. I can't give enough praise of his lectures. Just pay attention and you will succeed.

Dr. Summers is able to clearly convey information about his subject, and he makes an effort to include everyone in the class. He is accessible, kind, quirky, and funny. He structures his class so that as long as you listen in class and do the reading, you will assuredly succeed. He does not post information on Canvas, though, which is inconvenient.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Such an enthusiastic and entertaining professor who knows his stuff! But lectures are hard to follow. If you are taking this class for a History related major, Summers is great, but for non-majors the class (papers, outside readings, keeping up) can be too time consuming to be worth it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: Summer's is extremely into history! He lectures long and uses a PowerPoint, so you may want to go get the PowerPoints he puts at the library for more notes. DO NOT PLAGIARIZE! He takes that very seriously. Tests are made up of a lot of  concepts so you might want to study days before because you can't cram for it the night before. Great lectures!

Dr. Summers is hilarious and his lectures are like a narrative, very entertaining and informative with beautiful pictures which he ties into the theme of the course very well. One essay, two exams, and small "detective" assignments (which are fun)! He is friendly and is passionate about the history of the West. You MUST read the three books to pass

Lectures are very entertaining but hard to follow sometimes so it makes it essential for you to read the book and go to recitation. Tests are really tough and the TA I had graded all of our papers and tests harshly. Dr. Summers seems like a nice guy and is very passionate about the subject, but his teaching style may not be for everyone.

One of the best History professors I have ever had! Extremely knowledgeable and makes class super fun! Always puts 110% into everything he does and is hilarious. Keeps you attention for the entire class. I would HIGHLY recommend! If I could take him again I would!!
A friendly, knowledgeable professor who likes to teach and makes classes enjoyable.

Dr. Summers is definitely one of my favorite professors I've had during my three year of college. His lectures are interesting and he makes you want to learn the material. You can tell that he is a very educated individual and I highly recommend this class. He provides excellent resources that help you succeed in this class.

This was the most interesting class i've ever taken and would recommend taking this professor.  If you do the work and go then you will definitely have an A. You don't even really need textbook. The best thing for me was having the outline he gives on my computer and then typing whatever i could get down in a different colored text that went along

This was the worst course and teachers I have ever delt with at UK, the teacher just babbles for 50 mins prancing around hoping on the desk, his voice sounds like a narrator on a old tv show, you will not learn from going to class, the book is a must have. DO NOT TAKE THIS TEACHER.

Professor Summers is an interesting man. His lectures go off on tangents and actual course material is not covered. The TA for his class did the same thing. Did not enjoy the class and would advise against it.

The lectures are exciting because Dr. Summers is a goofy person, but it is a big waste of time most days. He gets caught up in his own excitement which causes most of that lecture information to be ignored and some things are not taught. He is clear about what is on tests, but doesn't always teach that, expect to read for a good grade.
Dr. Summers is incredible. A must-take-professor for anyone at UK. He is an asset to UK. He is super funny, super smart, and oh-so-awesome.

This class is a history class so be ready for reading and writing, but Dr. Summers is one of the best lecturers in the department.  He is very amendment about his subject and if you even remotely like history, you will be completely engrossed in his speeches.

Dr. Summers is a really great professor who knows what he's talking about.  The first twenty minutes or so of every lecture are sometimes information that you probably don't need to remember or write down.  Basically, if it's not on his lecture outline, then don't worry about it; he's just setting the context for you.  He's very fair and very good.

Very knowledgeable, but he gets lost in his narrative a lot of times. It is extremely hard to take notes and is even harder to study for the test. However, he doesn't take attendance,  gives you a good study guide for tests, and reading is minimal. If you need a class that attendance isn't required he is your guy. Just be prepared for the tests!
Very knowledgeable but gets lost in his own knowledge during lectures which makes it hard to study for exams.
Exciting lectures! funny guy who plays music for you and makes sure you're listening. Tests are medium hard but require a lot of studying

Dr. Summers is hands down the most exciting lecturer I've had in college. I went to class, not because I needed to for an A (you don't need to), but because he is more entertaining than than skipping class to watch TV. If you enjoy history, you need to experience Dr. Summers at least for a semester.

Totally improvised lectures and no Bb site make attendance absolutely mandatory. Very enthusiastic and knowledgeable. This 500 level class felt like a 200 level, sadly. Very kind and respectful of students. The course's structure felt loose and vague, even with the syllabus. I love him, I just wish the class was more serious and informative.
Seriously loved Summers, easily one of my favorite teachers I have ever had, if you go to UK take this class.

I liked the class. I thought his lectures were interesting and fun. The TA's seemed to do most of the actual grading but if you mess up there are opportunities to redo a test and each paper. He's one of my favorite professors so far.
horrible lecture had to learn on my own try and get  a good ta if you take this class

Dr. Summers is a very enthusiastic and entertaining man, and you can tell he genuinely wants everyone to learn about history, with that said he is not very clear in lectures about what is necessary to know and what is not. The list of IDs is far to long to mememorize all of then and it was never very clear how to write an essay on the exam.

He was very enthusiastic and you could tell he was very knowledgeable on the information, but his lectures were so confusing and the exams were difficult. They were all writing and my TA counted off for the silliest stuff.

I was really nervous at first because I heard Dr. Summers was hard, which he is, but he is the best professor in UK's history department.  I definitely recommend him for at least one class at UK and I wish I could have him again.

I was excited to have him because I wanted an enthusiastic, entertaining professor who enjoyed what he studied but what he was teaching quickly became impossible to follow and I had to rely on the book way more than I wanted. It is story time in lecture, then when the exam comes around you don't remember the story at all.

I don't like how this class is set up. The TA I got is a very tough grader, and isn't very helpful when it came to helping us understand Dr. Summers lectures. He is a great lecturer however he is often doesn't go over material on test.

I heard such great things about Dr. Summers and I was so excited to have him as a professor, but I absolutely hated his class.  His lectures are almost impossible to follow. You pretty much have to teach yourself all of the material on the exams. He seems like a great person and his is very knowledgeable, but his way of teaching is not helpful.

Dr. Summers is wonderful! He knows so much about what he teaches and tells great stories. His lectures are a little hard to follow but if you read the textbook it's extremely easy to do well on the tests.

He is an ok professor. He is very knowledgeable. I even saw him on the history channel! I just don't like the way he lectures or the way the class is set up. There is too much emphasis on the challenging tests.
Dr. Summers is perhaps one of the most knowledgeable professors at UK. He is very eccentric, but his lectures are intriguing and his intelligence is uncanny. Great choice for any UK student.

Great! Knows the history and tells it with a very animated fashion that helps bring history to life. I will base my schedule on what classes he is teaching. I suggest him for all American History students, might be a bit out there for people with no interest in US History. His test were all essay, readings were tested & neither too hard or easy.
There is a reason that I work my scheduled around Summers for each semester and that is because he is one of the best teachers and lecturers in the history department.

Dr. Summers lectures were very interesting and animated, but I probably would not take another of his classes. His exams are a lot of work, as are his detective assignments. He asks questions in a very vague way, so you never know exactly what he is asking and when preparing for exam essays I always felt like I was missing something.

He can sometimes go off the outline, but he is very knowledgable about his stuff.  His test aren't really that hard either.  I would recommend everyone to take him at some point in their college career.

Great teacher! He is very energetic and makes lectures entertaining. I took his class for both 108 & 109 because I enjoyed his class so much.  The TAs are the ones who do the grading so make sure you have a decent TA, they determine your grade. I loved his class and would definitely recommend it to anyone

Dr. Summers was an entertaining Civil War lecturer but impossible to take notes on. He doesn't ask you to keep up with reading, but on exams you are responsible to write essays on the assigned books. He gave us a list of about 100 ID's and said he would choose 10. On the final, only about 3 of the 10 he chose were from that list. Frustrating!!
He made history interesting, best teacher I have had so far.

I really hope there was a way to stop everyone from taking him as a professor. I was so excited for this class, but this professor is madness. VERY difficult to follow & complicated tests with questions based on readings he doesn't even discuss.I LOVE this subject, & it makes me upset that I have a low grade in this class.

Wonderful professor! He is very energetic and makes lectures entertaining. Gives study guides for exams and has exam reviews but ONLY if you ask him to have one. TAs are the ones who do the grading so make sure you have a decent TA. I loved his class and would definitely recommend it to anyone

Tests purely on lecture material.  Take good notes and you will be fine. Lecture style can be scattered.  Uses loads of media to make class enjoyable. Final paper is based on readings. Test questions are tough to decipher at times. Detective assignments can be hard, but he grades on effort, not accuracy.  Great class! Hilarious Prof!
amazing professor take him if you can!

Dr. Summers is a great professor. His entertaining lectures make what could be a very boring class really interesting. Take notes and go to lectures, even though you will still need to read the textbook to study for exams. Your TA does all the grading, so its important to learn what kind of grader the TA is. Overall great class, teacher, and TA.

His lectures are entertaining and extremely informative. Pay attention, take good notes, and you don't have to read the text book. You still do have to read the side books for recitations and papers though. Grading is solely done by your TA, which means difficulty is hit or miss based on which TA you are randomly assigned. Overall, learned a lot.

Going to his class is like story time. He draws you in with his intensity and gets you hooked on to his lecture. He's the most interesting and intriguing man I've run across on UK's campus. Go to class, take notes when you can, read all the books. He's a challenge but really makes you love the class. Highly recommend! =]]
He always makes class interesting, although he's hard to follow. I never took notes in class. I just bought ky class notes and used the study guides from my TA. Made an A on every test and paper.

I had him over 20 years ago.  I thought he was an awesome teacher!  He would at times, dress in clothers from the period, show political cartoons from the time and explain them, and had a great enthusiasm for the subject.  If you like History....he is the teacher for you!
Entertaining, but hard to follow.  Get the KY Class Notes and follow along in class they are extremely helpful

He is hard to understand in his lectures so going to the recitation is extremely important; especially since the TA does the grading. Tests can be hard if you don't study.  There are 3 books to read w/3 papers to follow. As long you do the work you'll be fine in the class.

I've had for 2 classes and if he taught any other classes other than 108 and 109 I would definitely take him again. He will definitely keep your interest in lectures. Its not mandatory to go to lecture but if you don't go you will definitely miss a lot of info. it is vital to go to recitation! great class and teacher!

His lectures are always entertaining and he's very animated, which can make lecture more enjoyable. However, he seems unorganized and is only available through office hours (no email). Would recommend him for 108/109 where the TA does most of the organization. Two exams were IDs/short essay/long essay. One 7-10pg paper. Class not too bad if you study.
One of the best professors at UK in my opinion!  If you want to take a history class make sure you have Dr. Summers.
class was always entertaining and kept your interest. summers would open with music and sometimes a dance. His notes are kind of ineligible, but clear through his lecture

Summers is my favorite teacher at UK. He makes history so entertaining and his lectures are a little hard to follow but definitely won't put you to sleep. For tests, he gives you exactly what he expects of you so as long as you study you should be fine. Seriously an awesome teacher.

Dr. Summers is awesome...he is very energetic about history. Get the KentuckyClassNotes.com and go pick them up the notes go perfectly along with the lecture. TA's grade everything so try and get Andrew Patrick for your TA. Attendance is not mandatory. If you get the KentuckyClassNotes and go to you rec. you should be fine.

Funny man and good historian but terrible teacher.  His lectures are extremely hard to follow because he uses transparencies that he writes himself and is practically illegible and he wears customs and plays music.  Also grades a bit difficultly and appeared to have a somewhat slanted view on the history he was teaching.
