Dr. Frey is a great guy and cares about all his students. He comes up with really creative engagement activities for in class. However he very rarely tells you where and why you got points off on assignments. When he does give feedback, it is helpful, but that frequently doesnt happen. You also dont need to get the books. You never really use them
Kody is a fantastic professor. He always makes his classes enjoyable and fun. He really cares about his students and wants them to succeed. I would highly recommend taking this class over WRD.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I wish I could have Mr. Frey as my professor for the rest of my college career! He's definitely helped me better myself both academically and personally. He's super laid-back and funny but he still teaches you what you need to know. Tough grader, but always provides feedback for how you can improve. Super personable and easy to work with too.

Kody was the best professor for a Communications class ever. He actually cares about his students and is super accommodating if you cant make a deadline for some reason. I wish I could have him for the rest of my college life:( Also he starts every class with a picture of his dog - Pete the Pug.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Group projects--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Mr. Fry is a fantastic instructor. He is very understanding, and his classes are usually fun/interesting. He is a tough grader, but if you are willing to put in the work, then you will get a good grade.

Mr. Frey is an awesome teacher. He is very personal and makes the class very enjoyable. He grades tough, but as long as you follow his directions and do all of the assignments you should be fine. Work is needed for this class, but there aren't a ton of outside assignments and there wasn't a final. Just an informative speech.

Kody (what he goes by) was a great instructor, however, he was tough on grading. I have friends who had other instructors for the same course, put in less work, and received a better grade in the class than me. He is definitely very critical of speeches and all assignments for that matter. Great choice if you're willing to put in a ton of work.

Frey is very laid-back, but certainly makes you work for your grade. However, if you put in effort it is impossible to fail his class. He relates to the students, and he allows 2 unexcused absences before your grade is effected. Not to mention, he starts every class with a picture of his dog (who doesn't love dogs???)
He is considerate, funny, and has a lot of fun activities during class to let you better understand.

Mr. Frey is a younger teacher so he can relate to his students very well. I really enjoyed going to his class every day because he isn't a boring lecturer. He's very approachable and responds to emails asap. The class is not very hard. The class consists of a couple speeches and papers and easy homework assignments. I would take Mr. Frey again.
I took this course online, was very easy. Everything was openbook, so easy A. I would say the lectures are heavy if you actually wanna learn the material.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: one of the best professor at uky. his class is easy. if u put a lil effort you will pass. he did zoom sessions for extra credit. he makes his lectures short and interesting. 10/10. i recommend him for sure.

Dr. Teets is really chill and the class overall isnt bad. You have to read or at least skim to power points to do the weekly assignment but thats pretty much the only homework. There is a group project that isnt the best since its hard to get ahold of people. Overall a pretty good class.

If you're interested in what the class teaches, then the class will be very easy for you. Although there are multiple lectures each week, you are able to put the lecture videos on 1.75x speed and still be able to comprehend them very clearly. The class is very interesting as it also shows multiple YouTube videos as well as personal interviews.

Dr Tunberg is famous in the spoken Latin field, and with good reason. His Latin colloquium class has been so excellent for my Latin abilities. Twice a week, students meet in small groups to speak/write in Latin, and the other two days he discusses our work and lectures; the format made the students close and gave many opportunities to speak Latin.

TT is an amazing Latinist and a really good professor. His courses are my favorite from my entire education at UK. I wish I could have taken exclusively his courses. He is always well prepared, knowledgeable in the specific subject matter from that week, and able to excite meaningful discussion among students.

Dr. Tunberg's Latin is beautiful, his teaching is thorough, his feedback thoughtful and prompt. He will show you the big picture of Latin, the patrimony and all it encompasses. He pushes his students to be better while also allowing them to make mistakes. He is serious but hilarious, rigorous but kind, inspiring but intimidating (in a good way).

Very knowledgeable and passionate. Quite funny. Very flexible with exam times; he cares about quality of translation instead of speed, and will let you take as long as you need to. Grading could be a little frustrating.
Class is super easy. Show uppass. Dr. Tunberg is really boring to listen to and put me to sleep multiple times.
Very knowledgeable-gives great background information about the Greek language-would be a great prof for Latin-tests are hard but fair and attendance is mandatory if you want to learn.

If you are in the Honors track, stay away from this professor. While it is true that he is very knowledgeable and passionate about what he is teaching, it just isn't worth it. His grading is confusing, and you MUST pay attention, or he will dock points from your grade. His tests are long in writing, though you only have 50 minutes to do it.

Clearly compassionate over the subject matter, articulate, and has a very endearing personality. I absolutely adored this class. His 'classics' knowledge is undeniable, and it was an honor to have him as a professor. Not at all difficult but challenging enough to stimulate thought and understanding. Without a doubt would recommend him to anyone.
this class is very low maintenance. just show up every day, look like you're paying attention, and take decent notes. he's a nice guy who seems to really enjoy what he teaches.
Dr. Tunberg is a really cool guy. His class moves slowly and he wants you to get the concepts. Plus he grades papers and tests pretty easily.

A little crazy but he is so knowledgeable and helpful.  I got really sick right around midterms and he was so understanding.  The class was interesting but TAKE NOTES!! write down EVERYTHING the man says and you'll do great!
Great teacher. Can be a very easy class if you put in a little effort.

GRRRR... I hated this class!!! It was sooooo boring and the test were hard. He never graded on accuracy, and you had to list every point that he was looking for. I was so stupid. But it is pver now, and I never have to take a class of his ever again!
by far my favorite honors professor.  i learned a lot in his class and benefited by taking notes and paying attention.  Easy grader and very sweet guy. i would definitely recommend him.
Not an easy class, but by far well worth the effort!
Very great teacher, replies quickly to emails and makes the class interesting.  Always listens to what students have to say, and does not dismiss any comments in class as stupid, even if they are.
optime Latine loquitur
No Comments
Great teacher. Really, really knows his subject, is always willing to give help if asked. Easy class, nice guy to just talk to. Just go to class and you'll definitely get an A.
He is very excited to be teaching this subject.  It definitely shows in his teaching.  It can get boring but his tests are not that hard.

Extremely easy. I think just about the whole class got an A in 101. Lectures are kind of boring sometimes, but he tells you exactly what you need to know for the tests (there are only 2 per semester, not cumulative, with no long essays!). If you take decent notes, this should def. be an easy A.
very boring. difficult for a 100 level class-- tests are very specific...no curve...hate this class with a passion
Class could get pretty boring, but overall, he's a good teacher and does a good job of explaining things.  Tests and papers are relatively rare, and while they aren't easy, they're definitely doable.

2 essays all semester long and one informal one that was essentially completion and between a paragraph and a page. 2 tests and a pop quiz, all fairly easy as compared to my other classes. He speaks very coherently, i've never needed to take notes. He genuinely enjoys his subject and teaching it.

Ok, he is the classic nerd, but he knows his stuff. Just listen carefully to lectures. He posts online notes which help a lot. His tests are fill in the blank and essay, pay close attention to names. He will tell you what is important, but to be safe, know everything! Overall, a good guy.
my first B in college, but still a great experience...he's nice and intelligent.
there's only three tests, and the tests are not multiple choice--which makes it more difficult.  pay attention to names and relationships, plots are secondary

Very good professor. He is very smart and his lectures are sometimes difficult to understand but it's very straight forward what content will be on the exam. There's 3 exams, homework once a week and in class questions for participation. Very good prof and cares about his students.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Gorringe was really a great professor and made physics understandable. While exams can be difficult, they aren't worth a lot in terms of your overall grade. My advice to be successful in this course: do NOT wait until the night before to prepare for exams and take advantage of all opportunities to gain points. Attendance is 10% of your grade.

Professor Gorringe was one of my favorites at UK. Although physics is not my strong suit, he definitely made the class understandable and it was not hard at all to achieve an A grade. The tests are quite lecture heavy but they don't count for a lot in terms of your overall grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Gorringe is awesome. He replies to emails very quickly and wants you to succeed. He is goofy and homework/practice tests/practice problems in the lectures will help you get an A. Learned a lot, especially for the MCAT!!

Overall a very sweet and funny professor, cared about his students a lot. Extremely hard exams and no cheat sheet like the other section of 213 had. However, tests are not a huge part of your grade. Lectures were super boring and he had crazy powerpoint notes, but not horrible to learn from. Use the practice tests to study for the tests!

His lectures were not super helpful and I often felt like I had to puzzle out the information for myself when it came to the homework. He's a nice guy and is funny during lectures, but he does not do enough examples to adequately teach physics. I liked him overall, and he's better than a lot of the other physics professors.
very laid back. homework is easy. lecture slides are boring, but he jokes a lot. homework reflects half of tests and the other half is conceptual. Electrical physics suck but he does a good job.

Dr. Gorringe is fine as none of the physics professors are great. His powerpoint slides are all available on canvas, but they are super distracting. He likes to do examples in class. The tests are not too bad, but don't base it off of the practice exam. Do not wait until the day before to start studying.

Really enjoyed Dr. Gorringe. He is a fair professor and gives okay lectures. He's very easy to talk to if you don't understand something and tests are very straight-forward. Study for a few days before the exams and you'll get an A easy.
Dr. Gorringe is the nicest guy, and makes physics bearable. His sense of humor is subtle and hilarious.  Really good professor, exams are pretty fair.

Dr. Gorringe is the man. He once had a penny collection that consisted of a single penny. But really, he is british, straightforward, and makes his exams fair enough to not need a curve. Go to class, pay attention, do the homework, and study 2-3 days before the exam and an A is attainable.

His tests are difficult, but curved pretty fairly. Didn't do too well in the lecture but did fine in the lab and rec. Definitely was not clear in class. He did very simple examples (that he almost never finished) and my friends and I had to use Yahoo answers for most of the homework questions. Was hoping he'd curve the final grades, but didn't.

A good professor and made class interesting. Really had to study for the test but he gives you practice exams so it makes it a little easier. I liked him as a professor but would consider taking it with other professors as their test are easier and all the same.

He is extremely helpful and fun in class, and has that classic British wittiness. I LOVE going to his lectures. His tests are a bit tough though, with 3-4 problems worth 25 points each. He teaches well but you do have to study a bit to ace his tests.

Good teacher, class wasn't too unbearable.  His tests are tough and there was only 1 curve of 2 points in our class.  We expected he would curve the overall class grades but he did not, I don't know if he is the easiest way out I have heard other physics teachers give huge curves.  But he is a cool guy.
I learned ALOT from Dr. Gorringe, he made physics interesting and fun.  He helped me personally too as I was'nt a physics major and found the subject difficult...
Explains material very clearly. He's also funny, in a dry, British sort of way. Tests can be a bit rough, but they often have a nice curve.

She was very nice and helpful. Her grading scale was different than most classes but lenient. She didn't have a final but instead allowed you to retake your midterm exams for a final to get a better grade. Had in class quizzes however, they were done with a group and were only two question that were copy and paste from the previous nights homework.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: She has an "un-grading" approach that is a bit different. You basically have a homework due before every class, and then a group quiz with the same exact problems in class. As long as you complete so many hws + quizzes (and 70%+ on 3 tests), you get an A. Show up and do the work, and its really an easy class. She is very accommodating as well.

Everything in this class was group work except the exams. Lectures were horrible and barely helped, once people realized no one had to stay for the lectures almost no one did. The grading criteria was very strange and felt like she was just experimenting on us which I did not appreciate as she was the only person teaching this required class.
Fairly graded hw and exams, the first exam was postponed because TA forgot.

Not ready to teach this course yet. Made one too many errors in grading and on the first and second exam questions. Didn't show confidence during lectures and when talking to students. Although can be very lenient if you ask for help, picks and chooses when.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Taylor is a great lecturer and he wants to see you succussed. If you are confused go to office hours!! The first exam is a lot like the notes, the second focus more on the math side of things, and the final is similar to examples he does in class.

Tim Taylor is an amazing and caring teacher. His lectures can get boring sometimes, but he tries to spice them up with humor and good examples. Overall, he's a great teacher. He still offers three extra credit opportunities in each class. He says a textbook is used, but you can find the textbook online.

There's extra credit questions at the beginning of each class that bring up EACH of your tests by the amount of points you get (everyone got 3 chances). He collects some in-class assignments we do for attendance, especially toward the end. He's sweet, pretty easy to pay attention to in lecture, and is a big blue collar guy. Would recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Tests were over notes and lectures, pretty straightforward.
His class is pretty easy, just show up on time and you can get bonus points.  He rarely takes attendance.  He's kind of a bigot though.  The lab is even easier.
He was funny and the class was super easy.  I understand it's not for everyone and he is definitely quirky, but we got to watch an episode of Bluey in class so I can't really complain.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Dr. Minella was a super sweet professor who let students take initiative in discussions. He prepared appropriate coursework, but kept the workload light. Taking a field trip to the special collections library and relating Bluey to our topic of the day were some of the highlights!
Dr. Minella is quirky in a good way. I think most of the negative reviews are just people who don't want to take the mandatory honors classes and decide to take it out on him.
Dr. Minella was a great professor! His 140 class was primarily discussion based, so be sure to participate when you can. He was flexible and lenient with grading.

Awesome professor, seems to genuinely care about who we are and where we're going, realizes that his class is not the only one we have. I looked forwards to this class. Genuinely wants the best for us, always there if we need to reach out to him, no complaints at all

Minella is the best professor I have had. He shows so much respect to his students. Class was solely discussion based, but it was pretty easy to talk about the course topics. He graded very leniently and was always generous with extending deadlines. I always left class with a smile and in a better mood than before. Truly the best.
He’s so funny! He’s a little bit of a tough grader but if he knows you’re trying he is willing to be easier on you. Participate in class!

Contrary to most of the reviews on here, Dr. Minella is one of the most understanding professors on campus. He is very fair with his grading and even offers extra credit. If you put in the effort, you will get an A. Class is discussion-heavy, so he makes it much more enjoyable than a typical lecture. 10/10 recommend taking him
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: This professor was the most awkward professor I ever had. It just made the entire class feel uncomfortable. Sitting in class, everyone would just wait until we could go because it was that boring. The longest hour and 15 minutes of my life. I learned absolutely nothing. I would take a different section of HON-252 if you can. However, its and easy A

Minella was not afraid of awkward silences. Most classes just felt like forced conversations in order to fill the time. Ive never had a teacher so picky about grammar. Overall not too bad, but the class definitely could have been a lot more interesting
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Minella is extremely disrespectful to students. He yelled at a student in class because she had a different opinion even though the course is discussion based and different opinions are suppose to be welcomed. He doesnt have any clear grading criteria and gets extremely defensive when asked about it. Your grade in the course depends on his mood.

Dont take Minella. Not a bad guy, but definitely not who you want for a discussion-based class. His expectations are unclear and he has specific preferences, but no rubrics. His voice is awful- super gravelly and annoying. He starts sentences without having a point and comes off extremely awkward. Nice, but among the worst choices for HON101.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--So many papers

reviews.comment: Hear me out. Minella starts off quite awkward at first, but once your class gets more comfortable together, it becomes VERY enjoyable! He was always willing to laugh at my jokes and gave me an A on an assignment I did about how much I hated the Whitehall stairs. Doesn't care too much about due dates or word counts and graded very easy in my opinion

Rreally not as bad as everyone says. If you aren't confident in your writing ability, then try to get somebody else. But, if you're a decent writer, you'll survive. Grade averages & distributions are always high, no matter the assignment. If you reach out to him to ask for help or an extension, he is very flexible and helpful.

DO NOT TAKE MINELLA FOR THIS CLASS! Every other honors class receives high A's and my class is averaging C's and B's. He grades insanely hard and does not have any form of rubric or justification for your grade. DONT DO IT.

tough grader and doesn't lay out his expectations for assignments clearly. HON 101 is supposed to be an easier introduction into the Honors college but he makes everything way more difficult than it should be.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Minella is a tough grader and can be a bit awkward, but he does seem to genuinely care about his students and is willing to help if you go to office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Tough grader

reviews.comment: This is the most boring teacher I have taken at UK. He always starts his sentences without knowing where he is going with them. There are many awkward pauses during class because of this. I dread going to this class every day.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I fell asleep every single class: its that boring. Still got a B without showing up to half the classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: This class is primarily discussion based. If you think that it's the professor's job to facilitate discussion and baby college students, then don't take Minella. If you're willing to open your mind, read the assigned articles, and participate, his class will be fine and you might even enjoy it. He grades tough but it is an honors class. No surprise
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: He gives awful grades and the class is 100% discussion so if you do not show up you're screwed (I have an 8am). The class is full of very awkward pauses. Do not take him for HON 101 and do not take it at 8am. He grades all the papers way too hard and participation is a huge part of your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Professor Thompson was professional and well informed. His lectures were clear and easy to follow. His tests are very hard and difficult to pass; be prepared to study. Attendance and homework were most of the grade and that made passing easier.

He reads off of his presentation slides and it feels like he doesn't even know what he's saying. When students ask questions he doesn't know how to answer in a clear way. He overcomplicates things which makes it confusing. Lectures & homework don't match with exams. Exams are tough and he has a 65% average. Homeworks help a lot, so get all points.

Decent at best boasts he has a 65% test average. Half the information on test were not in lectures or homework. I'm disappointed in his availability outside of class to get clarification on some topics. Gives miss information during lectures and test review. 

STUDENT BEWARE!!!!

Attendance is mandatory but course is kind of easy overall. 3 exams and a project but exams are easy to learn and project doesn't take long. Mr. Thompson is very understanding and gives you many chances to succeed.

His handwriting is hard to read at first, and he moves very quickly. You reach a point where you do recognize what he is writing, but it is annoying at first. I struggled with math in this class because sometimes the content is not taught thoroughly enough compared to the exams. Just go to class, you'll be fine.

Mihai knows the topics very well but is not great at explaining them. His accent isn't really an issue but he does have very poor handwriting that can make some things hard to understand. He explains some topics very well but some topics very poorly. He is also willing to help outside of class but isn't the best lecturer.

I actually took MA113 with him. I really liked his lectures. It is clear he knows what he is talking about, and he always posts his notes on canvas to look at after. His handwriting can be a bit hard to understand at first but then you start recognizing it. Also, his accent doesn't really affect that much but can affect a word or two.

Class was actually MA 113. He seems to be a very nice guy, but he can go a little quick in lectures and he writes his notes straight from textbook so some things are worded weird. His hand writing can be a little confusing at times, but the more you show up and take notes you can get the hang of the way he writes.
He is super sweet! He does go a little fast in lectures but if you go to his office hours he explains everything  very good.

[MA 471G] I had to go to office hours every week to get help on homework, which really helped. Lectures went very fast and I found myself just copying information instead of actually learning. Doesn't interact with class much during lectures, but textbook was very helpful. I would make sure to take MA 261 before this- lots of proof writing.
[MA 113] Calc I can be hard no matter how you slice it. Mihai can be hard to understand at times, and handwriting is pretty bad, but they have taken steps to make it more readable.

(Course is actually MA 471) - Mihai moves quickly through the lectures and rarely stops to check for understanding. The lectures align perfectly with the textbook, so you could get by through reading the book and not attending lecture. The exams are 70% of your grade, and the homework is 30%. Prepare to do most of the learning on your own.

Mihai has a very thick accent so if you're bad at understanding accents, do not take this class. He goes very fast through the lectures and explains things in the most convoluted way possible. He also writes very fast and his handwriting is not great. He is very funny but the content is just a little too hard to have all the other cons on topof it.

Exams should be worth the majority of your grade but the 86% weight of the exams in the course was extreme considering the other portion of the grade was not just participation.

No one I knew made an A, even with 85-90+ scores on all exams. Also, no curves were given! As a professor, you should be looking out for your students! 

Do better.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Tohaneanu was an excellent professor. Cal III is hard any way you slice it, but the lectures covered the material that showed up on exams and he made class time to review before exams. His explanations of new concepts were pretty good.
This professor teaches horribly. He explains the topics in the most convoluted ways possible, and rushes through everything
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Mihai is very effective at delivering the content in an entertaining and meaningful way.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Hilarious--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Great professor
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Great professor. Lectures are clear and to the point. Plenty of examples and explanations for theorems. Weekly quizzes and homework, but not too bad.

Dr. Draper was overall a awesome professor, but the pacing of his lectures was hard to follow. I took physics in HS, and the content of this course was nearly identical, with a tiny bit more calc related.  He has great demos, but the caveat I have is the i-clicker grade, which counts as attendance.  All exams online over zoom, and no patrial credit

Draper's lectures were hard to understand and keep up with. He knows the topic so well, that he explains it on a higher level than we understand. All homework and exams are online and require specific inputted answers to be considered correct. Overall, Draper is a nice guy, he just knows physics too well to effectively convey it to his students.

Daily attendance is based on small quizzes; if you answer incorrectly, you receive a 70% participation grade, which can be frustrating. Homework and exams are taken on a website; decent feedback is given on homework, but it's difficult to gain partial credit on exams, which are 50% of the final grade. Also, the textbook isn't needed.

Dr Draper is a very good teacher! Lectures are worth going to even though you can complete IClickers from home. At home exams are also a bonus and you get a formula sheet. Lots of fun demonstrations in lecture to keep you engaged. Overall a great guy.
Exams from home. Easy content. good professor. Just a lot of stuff to do. I hate expertTA.
Awesome professor. Physics sucks but hes awesome

If you're taking a physics class, I would highly recommend Professor Draper. He is a good lecturer, a fair grader, and is generally very accommodating. The amount of homework in PHY 231 can seem daunting, but as long as you reach out for help when necessary, an A or B isn't too difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Draper makes physics very enjoyable by using a lot of active examples and demos. Still, the material can be challenging and you will have to keep up with a rather fast pace.

Explains well and the demonstrations are often hilarious. Only need the textbook for webassign access. Exams are 75 points multiple choice, 25 open response. Final reuses questions from midterm exams so you don't find out what you did wrong on the midterms unless you go to office hours.
Best Physics professor there is. The nature of the class is hard but Dr. Drapers makes learning physics enjoyable and inspirational
In class he goes far in depth in everything he does and does lots of examples. He leaves the powerpoints up, and is just a very good person. Best physics class I've had

Amazing and well respected professor. His lecture 'demos' are amazing and will leave you loving physics and wondering how you entire life has been a lie. Gives you practice exams that are almost the same as the real exam, so study those and you will be fine. Always get the extra credit for the homework! It will seriously help your grade in the end.

It's easy to do well in this class if you learn Physics how Draper wants you to learn Physics. He will teach EXACTLY to his exams. He goes really fast when lecturing sometimes and is a bit intimidating in office hours.

Lots of demos, good explanations. Very organized. Figure out the quizzes BEFORE class (in the lecture slides), they can make the difference in the end. Also they show up on tests. Tests are tough but not impossible. Do the homework early for extra credit! From what I've heard about the other physics teachers, Draper is the only real choice.

Dr. Draper is easily the best professor the UK physics department has to offer. If you take him for PHY 231 be prepared to have fun learning physics. His demonstrations and explanations help make sense of the crazy world of physics, and his attitude about class makes you want to come every day.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: I hated physics in high school and I never understood the content, but that changed after this class. Draper's lectures are very clear and he has organized the course such that every assignment will contribute to your learning of the material. Highly recommended.
He is the best.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: hes funny

Amazing Physics professor. Gave clear lectures and example problems for WebAssign. He made class fun, and I really enjoyed physics because of him. The tests were not very hard, and even if you do badly on one the class structure made sure you had a cushion to prevent your grade from dropping.
Dr. Draper was FANTASTIC! If you have the chance to take him, despite your proficiency in Physics, do so IMMEDIATELY. You'll thank me later :)
Draper is a little dry when it comes to lectures, but he has good demonstrations and makes physics as easy as it can be. The tests are a lot easier than the homework. Overall good professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--Caring

reviews.comment: Prof. Draper is a very good lecturer, and explains complex concepts very well to students with no experience. He does plenty of awesome demos in class as well. He is very helpful in office hours and drops by recitation occasionally. His one fault is that he does not often explain his intermediate steps when performing example problems in lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Dr. Draper is the best. The class itself is hard, but he's polite, patient, and very caring with his students.  Dr. Draper once sat with me for half an hour on his own time in order to fix a software problem I had with my exam.  Sweetest prof I've ever had.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Difficult material, but Draper conveys it pretty well. Doesn't do many examples of practice problems but is very good at explaining the concepts with a ton of cool demonstrations. His lectures are pretty funny too, so he keeps a dry subject fairly interesting. Far from an easy class, but do the work and it's not too hard to get through it.

very good teacher.  He is very clear and detailed in lecture.  As long as you pay attention and do the hw you will be fine.  Physics is not my thing but he made it enjoyable.  is really funny in lectures.  does a lot of demonstrations
Very clear in lecture.  Willing to help answer any questions or understand concepts during office hours.

Absolutely an amazing professor. He really cares about teaching and has a knack for it. I personally don't like physics, but he's very clear and conveys the material very well. Only bad part is clicker questions are tough, but the exams are much easier than the homework. You can get an A. Absolutely take him over anyone in the physics department.
I actually looked forward to going to his morning lecture which is saint a lot. His tests are really easy as long as you do the practice exam he provides.
Best teacher through 2 years of engineering, great lectures and very helpful
Best teacher through 2 years of engineering, great lectures.

The first test is THE hardest test in the class but the final had the biggest curve.  So has does curve the test and is pretty fair that way.  IF you have any access to his old tests USE THEM HE RECYCLYES PROBLEMS!!!

Dr. Draper is one of the best professors at UK. He clearly knows what he is doing as he has been here for, I think, over 20 years. He does a very good job at explaining class materials. He will clarify any questions you have during his office hours if you are confused. If you were to take Physics, must take it with him!
never look to any other professors if you want to take physics.

Good at explaining, but he talks quietly, so don't sit in the back.  Shows us lots of examples to help explain the material.  Fair exams and grading.  All exam material is taught in class, so don't bother with the textbook

Dr. Draper has been one of my favorite teachers so far. He gives interesting lectures and he can be pretty funny. The tests are really similar to the practice exams and easier than the homework. If you go to class and keep up with the material, it is not hard at all.

He speaks very clearly when he presents information. Not hard at all to understand him. He'll be happy to answer your questions if he sees you raise your hand, but he usually doesn't stop to see if anyone has any; he just keeps moving. He should get a record for doing the most demonstrations. Every lecture, he does at least 2 or 3 demonstrations

Professor Draper is a great guy.  He is extremely intelligent and very clearly explains physical concepts through his words and demonstrations.  You will have to do one or two quiz questions with a clicker for each class, and this can get annoying. All in all, he is a good teacher and I would take him again.

Overall,this class wasn't too bad. The lectures are boring and you might not get much from them, but draper and his T.A's are extremely helpful if you talk to them. Also,the grading scale is awesome. Show up to recitations, study the concepts,and you'll do great.

Dr Draper is an awesome guy! He is very funny and likeable and wants to see everyone do well. What made the class that much better was the fact that there was a NotTerryDraper Twitter account and someone in my class was always tweeting like they were him. Overall a great class!
T. Drapes is the MAN. Loves Demos. Gives practice exams that are 75% same as real exam. Extremely easy to get a B. not hard to get an A. Glad I took calculus based physics.

Doctor Draper was among my favorite professors (next to Dr. Ovall for Calculus I/II). He was clear in lecture, his lectures weren't boring (to me, at least!), and he made sure his students knew the subject well. He was very straight forward and his teaching followed a rigid schedule. He was very organized. Because of this, his exams were also easy!

Topics are difficult, and lectures are bland, but Dr D does a really good job of trying to keep our attention with demos, video clips, etc. I really like his tests because he gives partial credit of mcs, and the questions are easier than the homework. The class just takes alot of time.

He really does want to see students succeed. The material is boring, but he does his best to make it interesting with lots of demos. The book isn't too much help, but can be useful if you really need it. I even overslept the first test and he still let me come in later and take it for full credit. Very understanding
Great teacher! Very knowledgeable about the subject matter, easy to follow, and very funny.

I'd never taken a physics class before, so this was the hardest class I'd ever had to take. I'll probably end up with a C and I've been a 4.0 student my whole life. Physics doesn't click with me. Read the book and study homework questions for exams. And good luck.

Super nice teacher, rather boring, but so is the subject matter. Always willing to help a student, remembers you even out of big classes, and is extremely willing to help you succeed. That rates a 10.

A really nice prof, but one of the only prof I struggled to pay attention to.  He uses lots of demos, but his fast PP notes makes it hard to take down notes. Book is a paper weight, useless. His exams are either pleasantly easy or crushingly hard.  Online HW is extensive and constant. The exams/HW stress the math, but the lectures don't prepare you

Good guy. Not the easiest class ever but hey, it's physics. It's not really supposed to be easy. He made me much more interested in physics than before his classes. Plus physics is pretty much applicable to everything so the class is useful in the real world.

He is a wonderful lecturer, but you feel highly unprepared for exams. He teaches outstandingly when it comes to the conceptual understanding of the subject, but his exams completely blindside you. You understand WHAT is happening, but lack the ability to use that information mathematically. If you have him, be prepared to use your book...a lot.

Good entertaining teacher who uses humor and in-class demonstrations to elucidate on topics.  His lectures are fairly easy to follow, but it is necessary to pay close attention.  Tests are straightforward and reasonable, but you must know the material very well. the practices tests are in a slightly different format, but same content. Good teacher.

His exams barely at all resemble the practice tests he gives. His tests are hard. Lecture is boring enough to make you want to chop your nuts off, yet it is mandatory. Between him and steve ellis, the physics experience for moststudents leaves you with a lower gpa and a deep hatred of anything physics. I praise God everday I am not ina physicsclass
Good guy.

Very nice guy, but the class is impossible. He mostly does demonstrations in class, and his powerpoint notes are totally useless. He does provide formula sheets for the exams, but they are almost too lengthy to be helpful. Exams are all in-class and are long. Most test questions come straight from examples in the book and quizzes from class.

This class was very hard for no reason. I had taken physics in high school, knew most everything already, and I was in calc 3, so I had a leg up on most students and I STILL struggled greatly in this class. He gives lots of demonstrations, but that doesn't help you solve a homework problem. The final had questions unlike anything discussed in class
He teaches you concepts in a way that makes you interested in what he is saying.

Cool guy! but extremely boring. If i didn't have physics before his class then i believe things possibly could have been a little unclear. But its not his fault because the course is designed to go that fast.
great teacher. the practice exams go right along with the actual exams.
I really did not like him. He gave these "practice tests" that were NOTHING like the actual tests. I really understood the material, and my grade did not reflect it because of his ridiculous tests.

Draper's lectures are very interesting and he will work to help you understand physics, despite his large class sizes. You must study nearly every day to keep up with the clicker and recitation quizzes, but the tests are doable.

Definitely a hard class in its own right, but Draper certainly doesn't do anything to make it easier.  He had great demonstrations and tolerable lectures, but he has very hard tests.  Also, his attendance questions test us on concepts that we have not even learned prior to the question.  I would look for a different proffesor if you can.

draper is a great prof. he's also just so darn NICE- gave me 3 extensions on internet homework this semester, and let me make up one exam too. only complaint i have is the in class quizzes. i think that it should be up to me whether i need to be in class to learn the material, but missing class hurts your grade because of the quizzes. not cool.

He's an EXTREMELY nice guy! ...And he really cares if his students are progressing on each exam, if you go to his office he is ALWAYS willing to help you and he'll remember you too! So if you come back next time he WILL check up on your progress in class. His demos make class really FUN! And he ALWAYS helps/gives a hint to the clicker quizzes! :)

He's got 3 or 4 demonstrations to illustrate each concept... I think that's one of his best qualities.  I'm really glad I had him this semester.  There are 1-3 in class quizzes each day where you answer using a remote control clicker... there's a ton of them, but if you don't take them seriously, they'll hurt your final grade.
draper is one of my favorite teachers at uk, period
I have taken other adv. physics courses, so this material is pretty much review, but this guy manages to make it so confusing and boring for other students.
Kind of boring, but he is a good teacher. He explains everything nicely.
He gives clear examples and goes over them alot. Also puts notes on the internet. Exams are standard physics exams with 2 multiple part questions and 8 multiple choice questions.
Nice, but all he does is demonstrations.  The class is unbearably boring, and he will spend a whole class period on one example. His tests are multiple choice, but that means no partial credit.

Pretty good, considering physics isn't exactly an easy subject.  Gives notes on projectors, makes them available in library too if you miss a class.  Tests are multiple choice.  Uses the UT online homework system.  Gives detailed explanations and demos.
Great professor with fair grading.

If you have to take 407, take it in person. He is much more generous with grading and exams!!! This class is nothing like actually preparing taxes because in the tax world, you use software, and it calculates it for you. Lewis a very understanding professor and super smart. His exams are just kinda hard.

Professor Lewis is a great professor, and he tries his best for everybody to understand his class material. But this class is still really hard. The questions on the exams are so tricky! I also liked the way he brought in, his law and CPA knowledge into this class!

There are very few really great teachers on college campuses. Lewis is one of them. Professional, extremely smart, very nice and funny. Do yourself a favor and please take him if you have the opportunity. Difficult class but he has a pretty generous built in curve to the tests which makes it doable if you put in the work.

Don't get me wrong, this class sucks. However, I enjoyed professor lewis's teaching and actually found myself enjoying learning about taxes? He's an incredible professor and tries to make the class interesting. Generous built in curves on exams (you only have to answer about 80% of the questions) and very accessible outside of class.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Tax sucks, T Lewis makes it suck a little less. It's a hard class and he knows it, he does his best to make the material understandable and is always willing to answer questions. Great prof and the class isn't half as bad as you'd think as long as you put some effort in and use the study guides.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great professor. Really enjoyed his class. It is tough, but manageable.

Dr. Lewis is a great professor. His lectures were extremely boring. The content he teaches comes straight from the textbook. In his lectures, he provides some clarifying examples and makes jokes to keep his class light-hearted. He truly cares about the success of his students and even offered extra study class sessions prior to exams.

Great ACC 201 teacher. His lectures are boring, but he has funny jokes he chops up inbetween long slides to make class go by faster. His tests aren't the worst if you study. The homework he gives, while tedious, is very effective in teaching you the documents you will have to fill out on the tests.

Tom Lewis is a funny and likable professor. His lectures can get boring sometimes, but it's mostly the content and not the professor. He lets you skip a couple of questions on each exam. He treats his students like adults and doesn't care if you go to lectures or not. If I took another accounting class, I'd want Tom Lewis.

Tom Lewis is probably the most loved professor on campus. Everyone in my class enjoyed his jokes. He truly cared about teaching us the material but also giving us the grades that we needed. I cant say enough good things about him.
Excellent professor, explains the concepts in a way that are easy to understand. He lets you skip a few questions on tests and there's always bonus. Really cares about his students
Professor Lewis is a good teacher imo. His lectures are boring (I mean it's tax) but he is the best dressed professor I've ever had. Read the textbook. It's key to do well on the exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Before each test, he would give out and outline of what exactly would be on it, but would also say to read the book to get the rest. He is a CPA, so when he puts the math stuff into study make sure to review it, those were the short answer questions normally. group project is a pain if you have lazy group members. Just focus on the test you'll be ok.

This course is all about the textbook. There are no notes or PowerPoint presentations posted online. You have to read the textbook and preferably attended the lectures. Exams are nothing surprising but the group projects are a lot of work and the usual pain in the rear end because of having bad and lazy team members. That sums up the course.

Boring. You need to go to class to get the notes. He is really nice with exams though, you can skip a ton of questions and he gives you an outline of exactly what will be on it. He's just way too monotone for me.

Rarely went to class, he took attendance twice all year. He tells you exactly what is on the exam the class before and I used my textbook to study and got A's. He is an interesting and funny guy and very to the point. Final project is kind of annoying, but not too hard.

Class is easy if you take the notes. gives an outline for the tests that helps a lot. group project is difficult if you get the finance section. overall, decent class. don't need the textbook, his slides are directly from it. takes attendance really randomly.
Class is extremely boring and the exams are very challenging, but not impossible if you study a lot. Must attend class to get the notes.

He gives 3 tests worth 100 points each and takes attendance worth 30 points (he's only taken it twice).  Tests are pretty hard but not impossible, just study the night before a lot. You can make a cheat sheet and he puts 65 questions on the exams  and you can pick the 50 that you want.  I have over 100% in there right now.  Some extra credit.Boring
class was so boring and his exams were impossible
makes the material somewhat interesting. tests are almost the exact same so get a copy of the old ones and you will get an a without a problem.
Fantastic professor!! Knows his stuff and is very good at explaining it. Highly recommend his class.

Great Teacher! Very thorough in explaining corse material. Even if you don't have an old test, Tom tells you EVERYTHING that will and wont be on the test. If you understand all the points he covers the class before the test you will get an easy A. Take Tom!

Tom is the man! He is better than all of the other ACC professors.  He uses the same tests every semester, so if you can get your hands on an old test, you are golden.His tests are hard like all other ACC tests, but if you have last semesters test you will get an A on his tests.He looks sort of dorky, but is really funny and doesnt care about much.
Tom Lewis is the only way to go, if you're taking ACC 201.  His tests are all the same, and while he is somewhat dry, he tries to be funny.

This was an exceptional class. Tom is an awesome teacher, very easty to understand. Quizzes are simple and tests are too...especially if you get hold of an old exam...they're almost exactly the same, even the numbers and multiple choice answers.

Pretty easy class...he's a really good teacher. His exams are hard though, but he doesn't change them so if you get an old one, you're good as gold. Very helpful, and VERY willing to work with schedule conflicts.

Tom Lewis is a tax attourney who teaches night courses.  He is definitely a good teacher and if you go to class there is literally no way to not get a B minimal.  Plus his exams are all the same, so if you can, get an old exam and study it to a T.

Unorganized. Got 5 different syballuses over the course of the first month, somehow still managed not to follow it whatsoever. Showed up late to class almost every time and didn't show up once without sending out an email. Good luck trying to figure out what your grade is because there is no canvas. I could go on and on without a character limit.

I've had the opportunity to take several classes with Dr. Marksbury, including WRD 112 (my freshman year), History of Hip-Hop (WRD 305), and Introduction to Documentary-all of which I earned A's in. He is incredibly sweet and genuinely cares about all of his students. 

If you ever get the chance to take a class with him, do it!

Dr. Marksbury is very sweet and supportive of his students! His class is centered around a variety of readings and documentaries, so be prepared to read or watch materials for in-class discussion. His grading is very fair, but scores are handed out in person and aren't visible on Canvas. He is understanding and flexible with deadlines as well.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Assigns things to watch/read before class but it is just for discussion and there will be easy short answer questions about them on exams. Grades easy and very flexible with deadlines. HORRIBLE with technology though. Great guy

Dr. Marksbury is very wise and full of information to share, but sometimes, his information comes across as disorganized. He doesn't know how to work with Canvas, so we often didn't know our course grades. He handed out grades per assignment on paper. However, he is very responsive over email and cares a lot about students' well-being.

This class only had 5 or 6 graded assignments, though these were larger assignments like papers. Out-of-class readings and movie watching are typical to prepare for class. Dr. Marksbury is very understanding and flexible in regards to completing assignments. If you want an interesting, quirky professor, Dr. Marksbury is the way to go.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I really enjoy Dr. Marksbury's eccentric personality and it is certainly reflected in his class. This is an easy course if you watch the weekly documentaries and you're prepared to speak in class. He is not very tech savvy and not good at grading things quickly, so if you need that to be successful in a course, maybe look for another teacher.

Thomas Marksbury is no doubt one of the best professors you will have during your time at UK. He is extremely flexible and cares about his profession, students, and department on a deeper level than a paycheck. I enjoyed every second of his class and would take it 50 more times if I could. This course is a bit content heavy, but super interesting!

Dr. Marksbury was incredibly flexible and let me write essays instead of giving speeches. Always email him if you need help, he's super understanding. He assigned a lot of reading/watching films. There was a textbook but you can find all the readings online. He did not have great organization and didn't use canvas so it was hard to find assignments

I love Dr. Marksbury and he is a wonderful guy to be around. This class has a lot of easy work like watching movies, but it adds up to a lot. I had a lot of fun with it and I think Marksbury gave great advice and feedback if you are interested in movies or media. Make sure you are tech savvy, because he isn't.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: good guy but uses all examples from when he was younger so nothing is relevant to us. this class took up more time outside of class than any others. have to listen to songs, read stories, and watch 3 hours documentaries every week. very disorganized class structure and no real rubrics for work. great guy and ideas tho

Dr. Marksbury is a very nice person, but is all over the place. Hed show up to class late, not post any assignments through Canvas and didnt keep you updated on your grades. The best way to reach him is to stay after class. If youre okay with being a little lost at times but have little work, than you will be fine.

This was my favorite class, and I am an engineering major. He is so funny and all over the place but has awesome stories to tell. He is genuinely trying to foster thought and doesn't care if you aren't the best writer. Easy class as long as you show up, are respectful, and participate in discussion.
Dr. Marksbury can tend to go off book or get off schedule, but overall he is easy to work with and cares about your success
Really interesting guy. Can be a bit unorganized but you will learn a lot in this class

A textbook is required, but not used a lot. Mr. Marksbury is a pretty easy going guy. The tests are not hard and there is no final. At the beginning of the year, you watch some movies and you do have to write some papers, but they're not hard. The syllabus looks hard and intimidating, but he basically lets you write about whatever you want.

Class wasn't organized, but other than that, it was really great to be in Prof Marksbury's class. He's a very kind person and he cares about his students. The class was designed to be decently easy, so long as you put in the effort. He makes an impact on students beyond teaching.

Nice enough guy but if you want a structured class, do not take. Absolutely must attend because the few exams you do take are based on things he discusses or shows you in class. Will definitely work with you about deadlines and project ideas.
reviews.rating_tags: Tests? Not many--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: The best professor I've ever had. He shaped the way I viewed the world my freshman year. I made this account just to give him major props. This man is great and the awards he's received have been earned. He helped me realize the person I want to become and taught me so much. He also made me want to become an English major.

Very liberal views.  But if you can put up with that, then he's pretty good.  Pay real close attention to everything he says in class, and remember it so you can put his main points into your exam essay answers.  Half of my class failed his first exam because they weren't expecting him to grade so harshly.  Write long essays for every question

A nice guy I'd like to have a beer with and talk about music. Infinitely interesting experiences and opnions to share. Would love to take all of his classes. Only 2 assignments and 2 tests the entire semester.
Awesome class and he is a great instructor.

I took his documentary film class and I loved it. He is very laid back and easy to talk with, and he provides good feedback. Not the clearest as as far as grading goes, but his class is pretty easy. He really listens to and cares about his students. Would recommend.
One of the easiest professors out there, he is extremely laid back. However, read the textbook to pass the midterm exam.
nice guy... heavy reading... be prepared 2 bring book w/ u to class... grading may be surprising.... think about what else ur taking w/ his class...

Hands down one of my favorite professors. Laid back and knows his films. Assignments were straight-forward and a final wasn't even given. Always gave helpful advice on papers and presentations. Great guy.

I didn't find him to be a hard grader at all, and his tests have both a take home and in-class section, so you have a fair shot at doing well. I didn't like all the movies, but he does a great job of creating discussions and I really enjoyed talking about all of the movies.
Had him for screenwriting. Great prof. He grades well, and he has awesome stories about hanging out with Hollywood stars. He also wrote the first documentary on Hunter S Thompson. Very down to earth.

I loved the freedom he gave us on the papers - it definitely prompted more effort on my part and it was fun writing about two of my favorite films (and after watching them repeatedly for material, I now appreciate them even more).

Marksbury is awesome.  he knows his movies, but some of the films we watch are boring and hard to get into.  His tests are graded hard and he really wants you to go in depth when you write for the test.   overall hes a cool dude.  u can tell back in the day he was a "hip" dude.

Had him during the second summer session and loved him. Movies were interesting and watched out of class, we had a couple of exams but he gave us a list of questions and told us he would pick a few, so exams weren't awful. Also had to write a couple of papers but he was very helpful. I really enjoyed having him and loved the class!! Take him! :)

Ok obviously he LOVES movies... films are watched outside of class, so throughout lecture what exactly was he talking about? Hard to follow at certain times.. and take home essays were very hard to understand what he wanted exactly.

Marksbury is a great teacher and he's really up to date on pop culture. He doesn't do the whole "Lets tear the book apart and find out what the writer is really saying!" thing, which is very refreshing in college level english classes. Marksbury loves movies so if you can hold a conversation about film with him you're golden.
I love Dr. Marksbury.  He reminds you of the "Fear and Loathing in Las Vegas" characters, and he's just so laid back.  He actually makes the course fun!

This is my favorite professor in my college career.  Was incredibly helpful and motivating; was always open to further discussion and different opinions; inspired intelligent discussion on topics not limited to the immediate subject, and aided student sucess outside the classroom and in.  Tom Marksbury is a true asset to UK's faculty.
Most favorite college professor thus far.  YAY!!!

Will write 3 stories and a portfolio (including, but not limited to the three stories) of a minimum of 25 pgs. on the stories, u wont be graded below a b. Doesnt read u'r stories very deeply. U wont get below a b on any of the stories and not below a b overall unless u don't turn in the portfolio.
Interesting teacher and is open to most any topic for writing papers.  Good guy.  Definetly recommend him!!

Not a bad guy but is pretty cold in terms of personality. Seems nice, but never really opened up which would make the class a lot more fun. 3 very vague tests throughout the year and thats it. expect 8 pages per test (take home) and a 20 Q in class portion. Better than an alternative
FABULOUS teacher! he gave me As on all of my papers. He's a really interesting guy and is willing to help whenever you need it. i totally recommend taking his classes if you can.

Great teacher. Very interesting to listen to his lectures and the class is almost always an open discussion. He helped me with my writing and kept me interested because he used pop culture to get his points across. Not a very intense class because he opens the class up to discussion.

On the first paper he may scare you with a low grade, but dont worry. I got a D on my first paper, and wound up with an B in the class, and i never went. He really helped me out with my writing the times i went.
Very strict

He is knowledgeable and funny during lectures. His tests are very difficult and the google earth assignments are extensive. For the final exam he allows you to use all of your google earth work. Attendance is mandatory and he asks written question to turn in at the end of class. He has extra credit opportunities and is open to help with anything.

I've taken Dr Stalins class twice each time he's been great, His tests are super long but it's open book and mainly over PowerPoints. The only thing I don't like about his class are the weekly reading quizzes I didn't gain any new information about them but other than that he's a pretty solid professor and loves what he teaches.
VERY long tests every week. Very hard grader and does not elaborate on the grading scale. Have to go to recitation on Fridays or you will get a bad grade. Do not recommend!!!!

Literally half my class wound up going to the head of GEO/ENS because this class was THAT bad last semester. He verbally degraded me to the point of tears and made several other students cry with unnecessary comments and accusations about attendance. Tests were impossible, tough grader... BEWARE. Still have nightmares about this class.

He's is a really knowledgeable and passionate professor and the course is not "challenging," but there is a lot of busywork, reading, and weekly quizzes. Be prepared to work outside of class. It's an easy A if you just do the work.

He is very passionate about the topics presented which made this class better. Very test-heavy grading but answers come from powerpoints. An A is possible for sure but definitely felt harder and had more work than a class that is taken for core credit should be. Wouldn't want to take this class again, but the information presented was kinda cool.

Tony is one of my favorite professors at UK! He's very caring and loves talking to his students! Lots of group projects and collaboration, which I personally liked because I got to meet new people in the class. He gives weekly quizzes on the readings, but they are usually super easy as long as you actually do the readings. Overall great guy!

Professor Stallins is a down to earth guy with a big heart. He is very passionate about what he teaches. This class specifically has four tests total. The first two are easy and the last two were more difficult. He gives weekly reading quizzes which arent that bad. Overall, you just have to put in effort and try and he will work with you.

Professor Stallins is one of the most caring professors I have ever had. His class is very easy if you keep up with the work. There is a weekly quiz on news articles but they are very easy. The entire class you work toward a big group project, so participation is necessary for that, but that is only on recitation days. He is also very flexible!

Every single assessment/exam is a group project. He also very clearly has his bad days and unfortunately takes this out on students by leaving condescending feedback on assignments. He has very unclear expectations on assignments; no one ever knew what he wanted. I would literally change my minor if I had to take him again.

Tony is one of the few profs I've met that actually really, truly cares about his students a LOT. He is always willing to meet with and work with students to help them get through his classes, and when tests don't go so well he encourages students to come to his office for help and they can work through it together to get more points back.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: This class was great! It was my favorite because of how interesting it was. Tony is awesome. He is my favorite professor that I've had. Yes there are a lot of videos you have to watch but every one is interesting and you'll learn something cool every time.

I found his class to be informative and interesting. There are 8 tests, several quizzes on articles and documentaries (you might have to rent/buy). His powerpoints can be lengthy, so pay attention to what he discusses during lecture. Also in sections, be prepared to be in groups for assignments/projects/UKCore project.

He is a good professor and is very insightful about his field, and the topic was interesting. However, this class was harder and more detailed than I expected for a 100-level class. There were 8 tests in total and many online quizzes. Most of the quizzes required us to watch long documentaries that we sometimes had to pay a small price to rent.

THIS CLASS IS UNNECASSARILY HARD. The tests are so specific and there's one every other week. There's no final which is a plus but there are a 8 tests. HW is a ridiculous amount of documentaries that you take quizzes on after you watch. I spent $50 on videos because they weren't on Netflix. Don't take this class as a core pick an easier class.
I loved this professor!

There are a lot of tests, but he provides detailed study guides that cover all the questions on the exam. You really learn a lot in this course and the professor is very understanding of students who commute. This class is an easy A for anyone that attends and pays attention. The exams only require 2-3 hours of solid study for a high A average.

Professor Stallins is a good professor, but he treats his 100 level classes like 400 level classes when it comes to the exams. Difficult, but if you go to class and ask questions when you're confused the class is passable. Probably would not take again..

I am a freshman and I can honestly say I spend more time on his class than I do all my classes combined. Decided to drop a class (was taking 17 credit hours) just to focus more time on his class. Great guy/material. LOTS of work.
Don't take Geo with him, it treats his 100 level classes like 300 level classes.

Too many tests. 8 tests and a quiz every day. Can not fall behind at all or you pretty much stay behind. Not a recommended class for upperclassmen with larger workloads in more important classes. Typical "Welcome To College" freshman class with an intense workload and occasional 100+ page readings. Readings and Videos must be watched everyday.

There are a lot of tests (8semester), but they're easy if you go to class, do the readings, and watch the movies. They're non-comprehensive, too. The readings are usually 5-10 pages and apply directly to the lecture. Movies are to be watched on your own time and there are generally easy quizzes assigned with them. Easy A if you pay attention.

He's a great teacher and realy cares about what he talks about. He is also helpful. If you take this class to fill the core req then try your best to take him. Shows a lot of videos and movies, no textbook and no final. Awesome class

Do NOT take him for GEO 130 if you're looking for an "Easy A." Somehow he made that freshman level class hard - and I took it as a sophomore. Terrible teacher, ridiculous tests. Go take underwater basket weaving instead.

Loves his subject...and that's it. He can't reach or engage students in anyway. He takes random attendance and ridiculous pop quizzes. His tests are difficult and his organization is sub par at best. He needs to put the bong down and pick up a teaching guide. Don't take him do Geo 130.  He treats it like a 300 level course

Dr. Tsang is one of the nicest professors out there, but that is it. He is one of the worst lecturers I've had the displeasure to sit through, his homework will take days, and his tests are far too difficult and long for the allotted 50 minutes. On top of that, there's a strong accent that almost no'one grasps. His classes are a difficult chore.

Great person, extremely lovable, awful professor. Lectures are incoherent mixtures of nonsense and semi-related material. Regularly starts early and somehow still goes over on time. Gives quizzes/exams on content never mentioned in class that we "should have known anyway". Like I said, great person. Terrible professor. Avoid if you can.

I had Dr. Tsang for several CME course at UK, and I think he's fantastic. He is hard to understand,  and in all honesty his lectures can be rather hard to follow so make sure to read ahead in your textbook. That being said, he's great at helping students during office hours and grades pretty easy. Brownie points if you mention Manchester United.

Very project heavy class. While not difficult, I have taken much easier classes at UK. There's a ton of video and audio projects to do in this class. However, they aren't very hard to do. Just time consuming and annoying. He takes attendance and the attendance is worth a lot, so go to class. Or better yet, take it online.

If you're looking to pick up a random elective, ICT200 with Cooper would be my #1 choice. Quite literally the easiest class I've ever taken. Fully online, no lectures, about one assignment every other week. He posts stuff that he tells you to read, but trust me, you don't have to read anything. Also, you can turn in anything late with no penalty.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Really nice professor, he really cares about his students. Attendance is mandatory and apart of your grade but assignments are pretty easy
Other than he take a long time to grade he is wonderful
When he responds to emails, he is faster than cheetah. All joke aside, he is the best.

Dr. Cooper is my favorite instructor so far. Do what the rubric says and he will never disappoint you. I spent about an hour or two every week to finish his assignment. I will recommend you his online class.

Since this was an online class, I really didn't interact with Professor Cooper that much. The lectures are all just reading on the Canvas shell. Do the assignments with some effort, and you'll do well. It can be super boring sometimes, but it is an easy class.

He was a great instructor that was willing to work with me on anything I needed. The rubrics were very clear on what the expectations were and he explained what he was looking for thoroughly on the papers but let you have freedom. If I emailed him with any questions he responded quickly. His comments on the assignments were always helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr Cooper responds promptly. His course is very structured! Follow the grading rubric and you will do fine. He seemed fair and understanding throughout the course.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Easily my favorite professor so far! Assignments are clear and he's always willing to help. His main goal is to help students improve as a writer/speaker so you're in good hands.

I took Dr. Cooper's online class for a Core Requirement. One of the easiest classes I've taken at UK! The class is interesting and as long as you participate in discussions and turn in work on time, you're good!

Very caring professor and allows class to be more free-flowing instead of lecture-heavy. Tests are not bad at all, although a fairly small part of class. Papers were not too long and the group project on crisis management was a good experience.

Dr. Cooper is a great guy. He gets the class involved in discussion so you're able to get to know one another. Come to class because he gives you credit for it. You have two papers that aren't a big deal and one group project. Find your friends early and you won't have to worry about the project.

Dr. Cooper is a solid guy. You get points for just for showing up and he grades pretty fairly. The group project kind of stinks depending on your group members and you have to write a decently long paper but nothing too bad.

Professor Cooper's goal was to see his students improve on their public speaking. He cared about his students' progress. He gave good feedback after each speech. We tended to work in groups a lot during class. This was good because we had the opportunity to get to know each other better.
This teacher involves students in every lecture making the class interesting no matter what your major is. Great guy!

This class was interesting and he gives great lectures. There is not much homework in this class and I overall really enjoyed the class and how Dr. Cooper taught. He is a fairly easy grader , you can't go wrong with taking his class ! He is also a really nice guy and very understandable. He also calls class off several days throughout the semester.
Great person and teacher, one of my favorite teachers so far
Great class and awesome professor
class is relaxed and makes you feel comfortable. Grades rather easily and is understanding if you are late or have to leave early.  Really cool dude, taking him again for 112.
Great teacher, helped a lot. Recommend everyone taking him.

great professor who helps build confidence for you if you are shy about public speaking. yes you have to challenge yourself to do everything but he doesnt pressure you to go beyond your limits. instead he focuses on helping you develop your strengths. highly recommended
Probably one of the best teachers I've ever had. He's an extremely nice guy who knows how to bring out the best in his students through meaningful assignments. Highly recommended.

Mr. Cooper was a good teacher.  Fun class, kind of nerve-racking with the few speeches, so if you don't like public speaking take word.  He makes it easy though, and it really helped my confidence.  Small class. Didn't use textbooks. I recommend it, it'll be fine.
Great professor!  Grades super easily and is extremely helpful.  Doesn't really care if you show up late or not but he does take attendance.  But overall one of my favorite professors at UK so far.

Nice guy. Gives you projects that actually have some relevance to things you will need to do in life. Also, you do these fun exercises in class that everyone loves. It's a nice way to make friends. And the textbook is interesting, but pretty much useless, as we never had quizzes about any of our reading.

He is super cool and laid back. You only have to read the first weeks of class because of easy simple quizzes that fall of during the semester. After that, the books are useless. Extremely easy teacher and easy to get an A.

Dr. Trask was arguably the most difficult professor I've had, however, he will help you out if you ask. His grading is what I had the most trouble with as there are no rubrics and most grading seems to be entirely opinion based with no clear or expectations. The overall content can be confusing with lectures consisting of rambling for two hours.
Class was just him rambling for an hour and 15 minutes. Don't understand what the point of the class was. It never made sense and was all over the place.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof. Trask's class is interesting but sometimes hard to follow and disorganised. He likes what he teaches but it's often just him discussing the novels and not actually teaching.The books to be read are announced at the beginning of the year, and the schedule is normally respected.

I would have taken Trask again if I had found out about him sooner. I liked his personality and found his lectures helpful. Take good notes (my final was open-notes and I got a perfect score). Class is lecture heavy and participation isn't mandatory but it gets boring if you don't.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: it's too bad that Dr. Trask requires attendance because you could literally miss every class except on quiz days and still pass his class. He spends the whole class just talking about irrelevant info about the book we're reading and doesn't care if you participate or not. Write good papers on the books and you'll get an A with no problem.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: this is such a random class, it can't not be interesting. super easy. definitely recommend it to everyone. I took it as a core class, maybe spent 2 hours a week on it? mostly just reading the books but you could definitely do fine just reading spark notes
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Trask is a great professor! His class requires you to read, and he expects more analysis than just what is obvious. Discussions are always interesting if the class is participating.

I loved Dr. Trask! He's an honest, sympathetic person with a good sense of humor, and he picks out interesting texts to read. I was going through a really tough time towards the end of the semester, and he was very helpful and supportive.
